            assert!(out.contains(pane), "{pane} is missing from:\n{out}");
        }
        assert!(out.contains("stopped") && out.contains("idle") && out.contains("never-launched"));
        // The pane id is what a director types, so it is never truncated — the column grows to fit.
        let header = out.lines().next().unwrap();
        assert!(header.starts_with("PANE       "), "column widens to the longest id: {header:?}");
    }

    /// The tally states the thing that scrolls off: 38 stopped rows above the fold read as a healthy
    /// fleet. Each non-running state names the move that clears it — and the two moves differ, so a
    /// never-launched stream must not be pointed at `wake`.
    #[test]
    fn the_summary_counts_the_states_and_names_the_move_for_each() {
        let rows = vec![
            row("nm:director", "director", membership::State::Running, true, true),
            row("nm:api", "worker", membership::State::Stopped, false, false),
            row("nm:ui", "worker", membership::State::Stopped, false, false),
        ];
        let s = summarize(&rows);
        assert!(s.contains("3 pane(s)"), "{s}");
        assert!(s.contains("1 running") && s.contains("2 stopped"), "{s}");
        assert!(s.contains("bsc fleet wake"), "a stopped worker's move is named: {s}");
        assert!(!s.contains("bsc fleet start"), "nothing is unlaunched here: {s}");

        // An all-running fleet is told to do nothing — the hints are for the states that need one.
        let quiet = summarize(&[row("nm:director", "director", membership::State::Running, true, true)]);
        assert!(!quiet.contains("bsc fleet wake") && !quiet.contains("bsc fleet start"), "{quiet}");

        // A planned stream that never ran has no session to wake; it needs a launch.
        let unlaunched = summarize(&[row("nm:docs", "worker", membership::State::NeverLaunched, false, false)]);
        assert!(unlaunched.contains("bsc fleet start"), "{unlaunched}");
        assert!(!unlaunched.contains("bsc fleet wake"), "{unlaunched}");
    }

    /// The tally is only useful if it reaches the table. `done/total` beside each row is what turns
    /// "38 stopped" into "34 finished, 4 stalled at the start".
    #[test]
    fn the_table_carries_each_streams_progress() {
        let mut finished = row("nm:api", "worker", membership::State::Stopped, false, false);
        finished.member.progress = membership::Progress::tally(vec!["verified", "complete"]);
        let mut barely = row("nm:ui", "worker", membership::State::Stopped, false, false);
        barely.member.progress = membership::Progress::tally(vec!["open", "open", "complete"]);
        let director = row("nm:director", "director", membership::State::Running, true, true);

        let out = render_plan_table(&[director, finished, barely]);
        assert!(out.contains("ISSUES"), "the column is labelled: {out}");
        assert!(out.contains("2/2") && out.contains("1/3"), "{out}");
        // The director owns no stream, so it gets no ratio — a `0/0` there would read as no progress.
        let dir_line = out.lines().find(|l| l.starts_with("nm:director")).unwrap();
        assert!(dir_line.contains(" - "), "a streamless row shows `-`: {dir_line:?}");
    }

    /// `done/total` cannot show a stuck issue: 2/7 reads the same whether the other five are
    /// untouched or blocked. The streams are NAMED under the table rather than left to be counted.
    #[test]
    fn stuck_issues_are_named_by_stream_under_the_table() {
        let mut stuck = row("nm:api", "worker", membership::State::Stopped, false, false);
        stuck.member.progress =
            membership::Progress::tally(vec!["complete", "blocked", "blocked", "failed"]);
        let clean = row("nm:ui", "worker", membership::State::Running, true, true);

        let s = summarize(&[stuck, clean]);
        assert!(s.contains("stuck issues"), "{s}");
        assert!(s.contains("nm:api"), "the stuck stream is named: {s}");
        assert!(s.contains("2 blocked") && s.contains("1 failed"), "{s}");
        assert!(!s.contains("nm:ui"), "a stream with nothing stuck is not listed: {s}");

        // No stuck work anywhere ⇒ no line. The exception report must stay an exception.
        let quiet = summarize(&[row("nm:ui", "worker", membership::State::Running, true, true)]);
        assert!(!quiet.contains("stuck issues"), "{quiet}");
    }

    /// `--json` is what a director reads programmatically, so the joined fields must be on the wire
    /// under stable camelCase names — and `stream` in particular, since the table drops that column.
    #[test]
    fn the_json_row_carries_the_joined_shape() {
        let mut r = row("nm:api", "worker", membership::State::Stopped, false, false);
        r.member.stream = "api".into();
        r.member.launched = true;
        r.member.ledger_status = "running".into();
        r.member.launched_at = 1000;
        r.member.last_seen = 2000;
        let v = serde_json::to_value(&r).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(v["paneId"], "nm:api");
        assert_eq!(v["stream"], "api");
        assert_eq!(v["role"], "worker");
        assert_eq!(v["state"], "stopped");
        assert_eq!(v["live"], false);
        assert_eq!(v["launched"], true);
        assert_eq!(v["ledgerStatus"], "running");
        assert_eq!(v["launchedAt"], 1000);
        assert_eq!(v["lastSeen"], 2000);
        assert_eq!(v["issues"]["total"], 0);
        // A pane with no session has no pid; the key is absent rather than a misleading 0.
        assert!(v.get("pid").is_none(), "{v}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn roster_is_optional_and_tolerates_a_ragged_row() {
        // A missing roster must not fail the command — it just loses the stream/role columns.
        assert!(read_roster(Some("no/such/file.tsv")).is_empty());

        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("bsc-fleet-cli-{}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let p = dir.join("fleet.roster.tsv");
        // Row 2 is short (no role) and row 3 is blank — neither may panic or produce a junk pane.
        std::fs::write(&p, "p:a\tstream-a\trepo\tbr\tworker\np:b\tstream-b\n\n").unwrap();
        let rows = read_roster(Some(&p.to_string_lossy()));
        assert_eq!(rows.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(rows[0].role, "worker");
        assert_eq!(rows[1].role, "", "a missing column reads empty, not a panic");
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod director_tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Build a plans DIRECTORY the way the real one looks: several stores, only some with a director,
    /// plus the scratch/abandoned ones that accumulate in `plans/` and must be skipped silently.
    fn seed_plans_dir(name: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("bsc-fleet-plans-{}-{name}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();

        // alpha — a director both PLANNED and LAUNCHED, with issues.
        {
            let s = plandb::Store::open(&dir.join("alpha.db")).unwrap();
            s.fleet_set(&serde_json::json!({"director": {"enabled": true}, "streams": []})).unwrap();
            s.fleet_session_upsert(&plandb::FleetSession {
                pane_id: "alpha:director".into(),
                role: "director".into(),
                status: "running".into(),
                launched_at: 10,
                last_seen: 20,
                ..Default::default()
            })
            .unwrap();
            for (r, st) in [("a", "verified"), ("b", "open"), ("c", "blocked")] {
                s.upsert(&plandb::PlanIssue {
                    r#ref: r.into(),
                    title: r.into(),
                    status: st.into(),
                    ..Default::default()
                })
                .unwrap();
            }
        }
        // beta — a director PLANNED but never launched.
        {
            let s = plandb::Store::open(&dir.join("beta.db")).unwrap();
            s.fleet_set(&serde_json::json!({"director": {"enabled": true}, "streams": []})).unwrap();
        }
        // gamma — a real project with a fleet but NO director. Not part of this tier.
        {
            let s = plandb::Store::open(&dir.join("gamma.db")).unwrap();
            s.fleet_set(&serde_json::json!({"streams": [{"id": "api", "repo": "o/r"}]})).unwrap();
        }
        // scratch — an empty store, the kind `plans/` accumulates. Nothing planned, nothing launched.
        plandb::Store::open(&dir.join("scratch.db")).unwrap();
        // Not a store at all — the scan must not choke on it.
        std::fs::write(dir.join("notes.txt"), "not a db").unwrap();
        dir
    }

    /// The scan reports a project whose director is NOT running, skips projects that have no director
    /// at all, and does not choke on the junk that shares the directory.
    #[test]
    fn the_scan_finds_every_project_with_a_director_and_only_those() {
        let dir = seed_plans_dir("scan");
        let rows: Vec<_> = {
            std::env::set_var("BSC_PLANS_DIR", &dir);
            let r = scan_directors();
            std::env::remove_var("BSC_PLANS_DIR");
            r
        };
        let keys: Vec<&str> = rows.iter().map(|r| r.project_key.as_str()).collect();
        assert_eq!(keys, vec!["alpha", "beta"], "gamma has no director; scratch has nothing");

        let alpha = &rows[0];
        assert!(alpha.planned && alpha.launched);
        assert_eq!(alpha.pane_id, "alpha:director", "the id `brief` is typed against");
        assert_eq!(alpha.ledger_status, "running");
        // The ledger stamps its OWN launched_at/last_seen on upsert, so the values are whatever it
        // wrote — what matters is that the scan carries them through rather than zeroing them.
        assert!(alpha.launched_at > 0 && alpha.last_seen > 0, "the launch times survive the scan");
        // The PROJECT's tally, not a stream's — 1 of 3 done, 1 blocked.
        assert_eq!(alpha.progress.cell(), "1/3");
        assert_eq!(alpha.progress.blocked, 1);

        let beta = &rows[1];
        assert!(beta.planned && !beta.launched, "planned, never launched");
        assert_eq!(beta.progress.cell(), "-", "no issues at all");
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }

    /// THE SIDE-EFFECT GUARANTEE. The architect's listing is READ-ONLY, and a scan that migrated
    /// every store would write to thirty plan.dbs it does not own — some open under a live fleet.
    #[test]
    fn the_scan_does_not_write_to_the_stores_it_reads() {
        let dir = seed_plans_dir("readonly");
        let before: Vec<(std::path::PathBuf, u64, std::time::SystemTime)> = std::fs::read_dir(&dir)
            .unwrap()
            .filter_map(|e| e.ok())
            .map(|e| {
                let m = e.metadata().unwrap();
                (e.path(), m.len(), m.modified().unwrap())
            })
            .collect();
        assert!(!before.is_empty(), "the seed produced something to compare against");

        std::env::set_var("BSC_PLANS_DIR", &dir);
        let rows = scan_directors();
        std::env::remove_var("BSC_PLANS_DIR");
        assert_eq!(rows.len(), 2, "it did read them");

        for (path, len, mtime) in &before {
            let m = std::fs::metadata(path).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(m.len(), *len, "{} changed size", path.display());
            assert_eq!(m.modified().unwrap(), *mtime, "{} was rewritten", path.display());
        }
        // No new plan STORE was minted. Scoped to `.db` deliberately: a read-only query on a WAL
        // database creates its `-wal`/`-shm` coordination files (measured — see
        // `a_read_only_query_creates_the_wal_sidecars` in plandb), so asserting "no new file at all"
        // would be asserting something SQLite does not offer. What the architect's read must never do
        // is change or create a project's DATA, and that is what these two checks cover.
        let dbs = |d: &std::path::Path| -> std::collections::BTreeSet<std::path::PathBuf> {
            std::fs::read_dir(d)
                .unwrap()
                .filter_map(|e| e.ok())
                .map(|e| e.path())
                .filter(|p| p.extension().and_then(|x| x.to_str()) == Some("db"))
                .collect()
        };
        let seen: std::collections::BTreeSet<std::path::PathBuf> =
            before.iter().map(|(p, _, _)| p.clone()).filter(|p| p.extension().and_then(|x| x.to_str()) == Some("db")).collect();
        assert_eq!(dbs(&dir), seen, "the scan minted a plan store");
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }

    /// A missing plans dir is an architect with no projects, not a crash.
    #[test]
    fn a_missing_plans_dir_scans_to_nothing() {
        let missing = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("bsc-fleet-noplans-{}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&missing);
        std::env::set_var("BSC_PLANS_DIR", &missing);
        let rows = scan_directors();
        std::env::remove_var("BSC_PLANS_DIR");
        assert!(rows.is_empty());
    }

    fn pane(id: &str, live: bool, busy: bool) -> PaneLive {
        // `agent` mirrors `busy` in these fixtures: they were written when the two were one signal,
        // and the cases here are about JOINING liveness onto membership, not about telling them apart.
        PaneLive { pane_id: id.into(), live, busy, agent: busy, working: busy, pid: if live { Some(7) } else { None } }
    }

    /// The table must show a stopped director as a ROW — that row is the point — and say plainly how
    /// many of them a brief can actually reach.
    #[test]
    fn the_directors_table_shows_the_unreachable_and_counts_what_a_brief_reaches() {
        let mut rows = vec![
            membership::DirectorMember {
                project_key: "alpha".into(),
                pane_id: "alpha:director".into(),
                planned: true,
                launched: true,
                progress: membership::Progress::tally(vec!["verified", "open"]),
                ..Default::default()
            },
            membership::DirectorMember {
                project_key: "beta".into(),
                pane_id: "beta:director".into(),
                planned: true,
                launched: true,
                ..Default::default()
            },
        ];
        // Only alpha is up.
        let res = FleetResult { panes: vec![pane("alpha:director", true, true)] };
        let live_of = |r: &membership::DirectorMember| {
            res.panes.iter().find(|p| p.pane_id == r.pane_id).map(|p| (p.live, p.busy))
        };
        membership::sort_directors(&mut rows, |r| r.state(live_of(r)));

        let out = render_directors(&rows, &res);
        assert!(out.contains("beta") && out.contains("stopped"), "the stopped one has a row:\n{out}");
        assert!(out.contains("alpha") && out.contains("running"), "{out}");
        assert!(out.contains("2 director(s) — 1 reachable"), "{out}");
        assert!(out.contains("quietly missing"), "the consequence is stated: {out}");
        assert!(out.contains("1/2"), "the project's progress is carried: {out}");
        // Unreachable first — those are the rows an architect must act on.
        let first = out.lines().nth(1).unwrap();
        assert!(first.starts_with("beta"), "the actionable row leads: {first:?}");
    }

    /// An all-running tier is told nothing extra, and an empty one says why it is empty rather than
    /// printing a bare header a reader would take for a failure.
    #[test]
    fn a_healthy_tier_gets_no_warning_and_an_empty_one_explains_itself() {
        let rows = vec![membership::DirectorMember {
            project_key: "alpha".into(),
            pane_id: "alpha:director".into(),
            planned: true,
            launched: true,
            ..Default::default()
        }];
        let res = FleetResult { panes: vec![pane("alpha:director", true, true)] };
        let out = render_directors(&rows, &res);
        assert!(out.contains("1 reachable") && !out.contains("quietly missing"), "{out}");

        let empty = render_directors(&[], &FleetResult::default());
        assert!(empty.contains("no project has a director"), "{empty}");
    }

    /// The pane id one spelling, used by create / list / brief alike — a second spelling would create
    /// a director the `directors` read could not see.
    #[test]
    fn the_created_pane_id_is_the_one_the_read_looks_for() {
        let id = crate::director_pane_id("studio-code");
        assert_eq!(id, "studio-code:director");
        assert!(id.ends_with(DIRECTOR_SUFFIX), "the `directors` filter must match what `new` creates");
        assert_eq!(director_project_key(&id), "studio-code");
    }

    /// `stop` is refused with the REASON, not with a generic unknown-command error. An architect that
    /// tries it should learn the asymmetry is deliberate rather than assume a typo.
    #[test]
    fn there_is_no_director_stop_and_the_refusal_says_why() {
        for verb in ["stop", "kill", "end"] {
            let args = parse_args(vec!["director".into(), verb.into(), "studio-code".into()]).unwrap();
            let err = cmd_director(&args, "bsc fleet").unwrap_err();
            assert!(err.contains("no `bsc fleet director stop`"), "{verb}: {err}");

        }
    }

    /// A missing key fails BEFORE any request is written, and points at where the keys come from.
    #[test]
    fn a_missing_project_key_is_a_usage_error_naming_where_keys_come_from() {
        for a in [vec!["director".into(), "new".into()], vec!["director".into(), "new".into(), "  ".into()]] {
            let args = parse_args(a).unwrap();
            let err = cmd_director(&args, "bsc fleet").unwrap_err();
            assert!(err.contains("usage:"), "{err}");
        }
        let args = parse_args(vec!["director".into(), "new".into()]).unwrap();
        assert!(cmd_director(&args, "bsc fleet").unwrap_err().contains("bsc project list"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_unknown_director_subcommand_points_at_new() {
        let args = parse_args(vec!["director".into(), "restart".into()]).unwrap();
        let err = cmd_director(&args, "bsc fleet").unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("unknown director command 'restart'"));
        assert!(err.contains("director new"));
    }

    /// The two outcomes must read differently in PROSE too, not only in the JSON — and the
    /// already-running line has to point at BRIEFING rather than leaving the caller to retry, because
    /// retrying is how a project ends up with two coordinators.
    #[test]
    fn the_outcomes_read_differently_and_already_running_points_at_the_brief() {
        let mk = |o, w| DirectorNewResult {
            project_key: "studio-code".into(),
            pane_id: "studio-code:director".into(),
            outcome: o,
            kickoff_written: w,
        };
        let created = describe_director(&mk(DirectorOutcome::Created, true));
        let kept = describe_director(&mk(DirectorOutcome::Created, false));
        let running = describe_director(&mk(DirectorOutcome::AlreadyRunning, false));

        assert!(created.contains("seeded with the discovery"));
        assert!(kept.contains("kept the existing"), "a planner kickoff is not silently overwritten");
        assert_ne!(created, kept, "which director you got is visible");
        assert!(running.contains("already has a running director"));
        assert!(running.contains("bsc plan brief"), "the alternative to a second director is a brief");
    }

    /// The kickoff is what makes creation carry context. It must name the requirement FIRST (the thing
    /// the director is accountable to), cite sources as COMMANDS, and never inline a body.
    #[test]
    fn the_kickoff_names_the_discovery_sources_as_commands() {
        let k = crate::discovery_kickoff("studio-code");
        for needle in [
            "bsc plan requirement get",
            "bsc plan stage list",
            "bsc plan feature list",
            "bsc plan fleet get",
            "studio-code",
        ] {
            assert!(k.contains(needle), "the kickoff must cite `{needle}`");
        }
        // The director's lane, stated — it coordinates and never writes feature code.
        assert!(k.contains("do not write feature code"));
        // The empty-requirement case is called out: an architect may still be sealing it, and a
        // director that invents scope to fill the gap is worse than one that waits.
        assert!(k.contains("do not invent scope"));
    }

    /// The wire shapes round-trip verbatim — a rename on either side would surface as "the app did
    /// nothing" rather than as a parse error.
    #[test]
    fn the_director_wire_contract_round_trips() {
        let req = DirectorNewRequest { project_key: "studio-code".into() };
        let back: DirectorNewRequest = serde_json::from_str(&serde_json::to_string(&req).unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(back, req);

        let res = DirectorNewResult {
            project_key: "studio-code".into(),
            pane_id: "studio-code:director".into(),
            outcome: DirectorOutcome::AlreadyRunning,
            kickoff_written: false,
        };
        let json = serde_json::to_string(&res).unwrap();
        assert!(json.contains("\"projectKey\""), "camelCase on the wire");
        assert!(json.contains("\"already-running\""), "kebab-case outcome");
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<DirectorNewResult>(&json).unwrap(), res);
    }

    /// One channel, routed by kind — the third fleet key must not collide with its siblings.
    #[test]
    fn the_director_routing_key_is_distinct() {
        assert_eq!(DIRECTOR_KIND, "fleet-director");
        for other in [KIND, WAKE_KIND] {
            assert_ne!(DIRECTOR_KIND, other);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn reads_the_project_key_out_of_a_director_pane_id() {
        // The pane id carries its project, which is why `directors` needs no roster — the architect
        // does not sit in a project hub and has no fleet.roster.tsv to read.
        assert_eq!(director_project_key("studio-code:director"), "studio-code");
        assert_eq!(director_project_key("a-b-c:director"), "a-b-c");
    }

    #[test]
    fn leaves_a_non_director_id_alone_rather_than_mangling_it() {
        // Defensive: the filter should never hand this a worker id, but silently returning a truncated
        // key would be worse than returning the id — a wrong project name reads as real.
        assert_eq!(director_project_key("studio-code:api"), "studio-code:api");
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_suffix_match_does_not_catch_a_worker_stream_named_director() {
        // `<key>:director` is the director. A worker stream could legitimately be called something
        // ending in "director" (e.g. `art-director`), and `ends_with(":director")` is what keeps that
        // out — the colon is load-bearing, so this pins it.
        assert!("studio-code:director".ends_with(DIRECTOR_SUFFIX));
        assert!(!"studio-code:art-director".ends_with(DIRECTOR_SUFFIX));
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod clone_credential_tests {
    use super::*;

    /// The failure a maintainer actually met, twice read as a missing PERMISSION.
    ///
    /// Git does not say "unauthorized" when it has no credential — it tries to PROMPT and fails on
    /// the absent terminal. The message must name the cause (no credential) and both ways out.
    #[test]
    fn a_credential_prompt_failure_names_the_cause_and_the_ways_out() {
        let raw = "Cloning into '/hub/repo'...\nfatal: could not read Username for \
                   'https://github.com': No such device or address";
        let m = explain_clone_failure("bsc fleet", "acme/private", false, raw);
        assert!(m.contains("no GitHub credential"), "names the cause: {m}");
        assert!(m.contains("acme/private"), "names the repo: {m}");
        assert!(m.contains("Settings → GitHub"), "names where a token comes from: {m}");
        assert!(m.contains("$GH_TOKEN"), "says the token reaches a session automatically: {m}");
        assert!(m.contains("--source"), "names the no-network way out: {m}");
        assert!(m.contains(raw) || m.contains("could not read Username"), "keeps the original: {m}");
    }

    /// HAVING a token and being REFUSED is a different problem with a different fix, so it must not
    /// tell the reader to go connect an account they already connected.
    #[test]
    fn a_refusal_with_a_token_in_hand_reads_differently() {
        let m = explain_clone_failure("bsc fleet", "acme/private", true, "fatal: Authentication failed");
        assert!(m.contains("refused the credential"), "{m}");
        assert!(!m.contains("no GitHub credential"), "must not claim there is no token: {m}");
    }

    /// Anything that is NOT an auth prompt passes through untouched — a disk-full or bad-path clone
    /// failure must not be relabelled as a credential problem.
    #[test]
    fn a_non_auth_failure_is_not_dressed_up_as_one() {
        let m = explain_clone_failure("bsc fleet", "acme/pub", false, "fatal: destination path exists");
        assert_eq!(m, "bsc fleet clone: fatal: destination path exists");
    }

    /// A set-but-blank variable is how a shell says "no token"; passing it on would rebuild the
    /// anonymous URL this fallback exists to avoid.
    #[test]
    fn a_blank_env_token_counts_as_absent() {
        // Distinct names per case: nextest gives each test its own process, but these still must not
        // depend on each other's ordering within one.
        std::env::set_var("BSC_TEST_TOKEN_BLANK", "   ");
        assert_eq!(env_token("BSC_TEST_TOKEN_BLANK"), None);
        std::env::set_var("BSC_TEST_TOKEN_REAL", "  ghp_example  ");
        assert_eq!(env_token("BSC_TEST_TOKEN_REAL").as_deref(), Some("ghp_example"));
        assert_eq!(env_token("BSC_TEST_TOKEN_ABSENT_XYZ"), None);
    }
}

//! The component-library CLI (#2281) — the shim over the shared verbatim-JSON-per-id store CLI
//! ([`bsc_json_store::cli`], #2158). TWO collections: the **components**
//! (`~/.base-studio-code/components/<id>.json`) and the **kits** (`~/.base-studio-code/kits/<id>.json`),
//! each list/get/set/remove-able from a session's own shell — the same store the desktop Component
//! Library pane reads/writes and an agent reaches to reuse a proven component instead of re-inventing it.
//!
//! **Mounted under `bsc ui` (#2469)** — the one UI-design-surface command: `bsc ui <cmd>` operates on
//! components; `bsc ui kit <cmd>` operates on kits (`bsc_ui::cli` delegates the store verbs here via
//! [`run`], composing [`command_docs`] into its merged help tree). `bsc component …` remains a thin
//! DEPRECATED alias for one release (the umbrella `bsc` prints a stderr pointer, then delegates here
//! unchanged — the #1721 `bsc plan integration` → `bsc data connector` pattern). Per-command help
//! (#1762):
//!   bsc ui help          # the merged UI-surface commands
//!   bsc ui kit help      # kit commands
//!   bsc ui set help      # detailed help for ONE command
//!
//! Each collection resolves via `--dir <path>` or its env var, defaulting to `~/.base-studio-code/<seg>/`.

use bsc_cli_util::CmdDoc;
use bsc_json_store::cli::CliSpec;
use std::io::Read;

const TAGLINE: &str = "the component library — proven components in technology-scoped kits (#2281)";
const KIT_TAGLINE: &str = "the component library's kits — technology-scoped component namespaces (#2281)";

/// The data-shape vocabulary (#2475 + `series` #3517) — the seven canonical shapes a feature's data
/// can take, each with the one-line description `bsc ui shapes` prints. A component's optional `shapes`
/// JSON field stamps the shapes it is an IDEAL rendering for; the CLI computes the index from those
/// fields verbatim (no Rust schema — the store stays verbatim JSON). Mirrors `DataShape` in
/// `src/features/designs/lib/model.ts`.
const DATA_SHAPES: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
    ("list", "a flat, ordered collection of homogeneous items"),
    ("linked-list", "a sequence whose items chain by explicit next/prev links"),
    ("tree", "a hierarchy — every item nests under a single parent"),
    ("graph", "nodes joined by arbitrary edges (many-to-many)"),
    ("table", "homogeneous records with fixed, aligned columns"),
    ("key-value", "one record's named fields — a label → value map"),
    ("series", "an ordered axis + one or more aligned numeric value series — a time-series (LineArea · Bars · Spark)"),
];

const COMPONENT_COMMANDS: &[CmdDoc] = &[
    CmdDoc {
        name: "list",
        summary: "every component's {id, name, kitId, role, group, shapes} (JSON; --graph for the graph projection)",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui list [--kit <id>] [--shape <shape>] [--feature <f>] [--tags a,b] [--graph] [--full] [--pretty] [--raw]

Prints every component's { id, name, kitId, role, group, shapes } as JSON (compact; --pretty for indented).
--shape filters to the components whose `shapes` field stamps <shape> — the kit's IDEAL renderings
for that data shape (#2475/#3517; one of list · linked-list · tree · graph · table · key-value · series — see
`bsc ui shapes`). --full emits the COMPLETE component objects (variants + props + composes + guidance
+ source + …) as a plain array — the full-fidelity read the desktop library hydration needs.
--graph (#4072) emits { id, name, kitId, role, group, used, composes } — EXACTLY what the Design
Studio's composition graph renders: the node card plus the field its edges derive from. It exists
because --full is 1.72 MB over 321 components (77.6% of it `srcText`, which no node reads) and the
page blocked up to 8s on it; the graph projection is 33 KB. Reach for --full only when you need a
component's source/variants/props — and prefer `get <id>` for ONE component over the whole library.
--raw (#3166) drops the JSON entirely and prints ONE id per line, raw UTF-8, LF-only — byte-clean for
`for id in $(bsc ui list --raw)` / `while read id` (no CRLF or cp1252 traps; honors --kit/--shape, ignores --full/--pretty).

THE TWO AXES A WORKER SEARCHES BY, and they answer different questions:
--feature <f> is OWNERSHIP — which feature owns the component, and so which worker may WRITE it
  (`bsc ui features` reports and backfills it). It worked before this and appeared in no help text.
--tags a,b is SUBJECT — what the component is ABOUT. An AND: a component must carry EVERY tag named,
  because a second tag is how a search NARROWS and a union would widen it. An untagged component is
  never a match, so the filter is purely additive. The tags that exist are `bsc ui tags` — a tag
  cannot be searched for until it can be discovered, which is why the pair ships together.",
    },
    CmdDoc {
        name: "shapes",
        summary: "the data-shape vocabulary → each shape's ideal components (#2475)",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui shapes [<shape>] [--pretty]

Prints the seven-shape data vocabulary — list · linked-list · tree · graph · table · key-value · series — as a
JSON array of { shape, desc, components }, where components are the stored components whose `shapes`
field stamps that shape (the kit's IDEAL renderings for it, as lean {id, name, kitId, role, group, shapes}
rows). With <shape>, prints just that shape's entry. An EMPTY components array means the kit has no
ideal layout for that shape yet — a genuine gap to record, not a fit to force. Read-only: how the
planner picks a layout — derive the data's shape, then `bsc ui shapes <shape>` (or the equivalent
filter, `bsc ui list --shape <shape>`).",
    },
    CmdDoc {
        name: "get",
        summary: "print one component (JSON, verbatim) or null — or ONE field with --field (#3162)",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui get <id> [--pretty] [--raw] [--out <name>] [--kit <kitId>]
  bsc ui get <id> --field <json-pointer> [--raw] [--pretty] [--out <name>] [--kit <kitId>]

Prints the stored component JSON for <id> verbatim, or `null` if absent. --raw (#3166) writes the
record as raw UTF-8 bytes, LF-only (CR-stripped), no locale layer — safe for `VALUE=$(bsc ui get <id>
--raw)`; a missing id prints NOTHING (empty capture) rather than the literal `null`. With --field
(#3162), prints just the value at the RFC-6901 JSON pointer <json-pointer> (e.g. `/name`, `/props/0/req`,
`/srcText`; a leading `/` is optional) — errors when the component OR the field is absent; --raw unwraps
a string value (no quotes/escaping) via the SAME raw printer, so a shell `$(...)` capture is clean (a
non-string value prints as compact JSON), and without --raw the value prints as JSON (--pretty indents).

--out <name> (#3713) writes the SAME bytes to a BARE-named file in the session's $BSC_SCRATCH dir instead
of stdout, then prints that path. Use it to review a LARGE value (e.g. a big `srcText`) a restricted
session would otherwise truncate on stdout — the scratch file is a confinement-allowed path, so Read/Grep
open it in full. <name> must be bare (no '/', '\\', '..' or ':') and $BSC_SCRATCH must be set. With --out,
a missing id/field ERRORS (there is nothing to write) rather than emitting an empty capture.

--kit <kitId> (#3729) DISAMBIGUATES — the store is keyed by id ALONE, so there is exactly one record per
id; this asserts WHICH kit it belongs to, erroring (naming the actual kit) on a mismatch. Note: writing a
component whose id already lives under another kit OVERWRITES it — `bsc ui set` now warns about that.",
    },
    CmdDoc {
        name: "log",
        summary: "a record's change history — the current stamp + the per-write log (#3164/#3568)",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui log <id> [--kit] [--dir D] [--pretty]

Prints the record's provenance AND its change history as JSON —
{ id, rev, updatedAt, updatedBy, history: [ { rev, at, by, note?, changed, dropped? } ] }. The top-level fields are
the current stamp (#3164): `rev` is the monotonically-increasing revision (a record never stamped, or a
legacy one, reads as rev 0); `updatedAt` is the last write's ISO-8601 UTC timestamp; `updatedBy` is the
writer tag (`bsc ui set --by <tag>` / $BSC_UI_WRITER, else \"unknown\"). `history` (#3568) is the per-write
log, NEWEST-FIRST, one entry per write: its `rev`, `at` (ISO-8601), `by` (the writer), an optional `note`
(`bsc ui set --note <text>`), and `changed` (the top-level fields that moved, `[\"created\"]` on the first
write). An entry also carries `dropped` (#4197) — the fields that write REMOVED — but ONLY when it
removed some, so a destructive write is legible at a glance instead of hiding inside `changed`.
An entry that MOVED `srcText` also carries `prevSrc` — the source it replaced — which is what makes the
write revertible (`bsc ui revert`). Retained on the most recent 5 such entries only: srcText is 77.6% of a
record's payload, so keeping it for all 30 would multiply the store. The metadata log still runs the full
30, so an aged-out entry reads as a write with no `prevSrc`, never as a write that changed nothing.
Capped to the most recent 30 writes. Review it before editing so you know what changed and why.
--kit logs a KIT record instead of a component. Read-only. Use the `rev` to guard your next write:
`bsc ui set --if-version <rev>` refuses to overwrite if the record has moved on.",
    },
    CmdDoc {
        name: "revert",
        summary: "restore a record's srcText from the retained change history — undo a bad write",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui revert <id> [--to <rev>] [--kit] [--by <tag>] [--dir D] [--pretty]

Restores `srcText` to a version the change log retained (`prevSrc`, see `bsc ui log`). With no --to it
undoes the LAST write that moved the source; `--to <rev>` restores the source as the record held it at
that revision.

WHY IT EXISTS. Recovery from a bad write used to be \"re-seed from the packaged seed\", which is no
recovery at all for a record that has no seed — and 25 of 47 `role: page` records had none. A designer
session that rewrote five rendering-critical records at 01:39 left three of them with the broken version
as the only copy that had ever existed, because the log recorded THAT `srcText` changed and never what it
was. This is the way back.

The revert is itself a WRITE: it stamps a new rev and its own history entry (noting where it came from),
so the version it replaced becomes revertible in turn and a mistaken revert is not a second unrecoverable
act. It restores ONLY `srcText` — every other field is left exactly as it stands, so a revert of a bad
source never also rewinds a good `composes` edit.

A revision whose source has aged past the retention cap is REFUSED, naming the revisions that are still
reachable. It never falls back to a nearer version: silently reverting to bytes the record never held at
the revision you asked for is worse than refusing. A ui-scope MUTATION.",
    },
    CmdDoc {
        name: "set",
        summary: "MERGE component JSON from stdin into the record (stamps rev/updatedAt/updatedBy); prints id(s)",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui set [--by <tag>] [--note <text>] [--if-version <n>] [--clear a,b] [--pretty]   # component JSON (one object or an array) on stdin
  bsc ui set --file <name> [--by <tag>] [--note <text>] [--clear a,b] [--pretty]        # ...or the same JSON from $BSC_SCRATCH/<name>
  bsc ui set --replace …                                                                # verbatim WHOLE-record write (see below)
  bsc ui set --force …                                                                  # store a `role: page` the gate would refuse (a deliberate spec)

Upserts each component by its (required, non-empty) \"id\" field. Prints the id(s) written — how an
agent (or the pane) authors/updates a component in the shared kit.

A write is a MERGE (#4197): the fields you send are overlaid on the STORED record, and every field you
did NOT send is PRESERVED. So `{\"id\":\"fleetpage\",\"srcText\":\"…\"}` changes the source and leaves the
kit, role, `composes` edges, `src`/`folder` provenance and `props` exactly as they were. This matches
`bsc graph impl set` (#4154) — the two stores answer a partial write identically. It used to REPLACE,
which silently deleted every field a write did not restate; that cost a 16-entry reorg on the algorithms
side, and here it can be unrecoverable (`fleetpage` has had no source file since #3636, so the record is
the only copy of that UI).

Removal is therefore EXPLICIT, two equivalent ways: --clear a,b removes those fields, or send JSON
`null` as the field's value. `id` can never be removed (it is the store key). Each removal is recorded
in the change history as `dropped` — separate from `changed` — so `bsc ui log <id>` tells a write that
DELETED fields from one that merely edited them.

--replace opts back into the verbatim whole-record write for a caller that genuinely holds the whole
record: the app's write-through bridge, `bsc ui import`, and the seed reconcile's authoritative reset
(which a merge would stop from ever converging back on the seed). It is the ONLY mode that can still
delete a field by omission, so it WARNS on stderr naming each one. --clear with --replace is refused.

--file <name> reads the SAME payload from a bare-named file in the session's $BSC_SCRATCH dir instead
of stdin (#3373). It exists because a heredoc cannot be permitted in a restricted session: newlines are
command separators, so the JSON body parses as its own (unmatchable) subcommands. The name must be
BARE — no '/', '\\', '..' or ':' — and $BSC_SCRATCH must be set, or the flag is refused.

Every write STAMPS provenance (#3164): it auto-bumps the record's `rev` integer, sets `updatedAt`
(ISO-8601 UTC), and records `updatedBy` — the writer tag from `--by <tag>`, else $BSC_UI_WRITER, else
\"unknown\". --if-version <n> is OPTIMISTIC CONCURRENCY: the write is REJECTED (non-zero exit, nothing
stored) unless the record's CURRENT rev is exactly <n> — so a background rewrite can't silently clobber
your edit. Read a record's current rev with `bsc ui log <id>`; --if-version takes a single record on stdin.

An optional `group` field is the component's FOLDER PATH within the kit — a nested, `/`-delimited path
(`shared/ui/controls`, `features/github`) that organizes the kit like a completed project's folders
(#3579). Orthogonal to `role` (the arch tier), organizational only (`composes` still resolves across the
whole kit). `bsc ui refolder` re-derives it from `src` for the whole store; the harvest seeds it too.",
    },
    CmdDoc {
        name: "remove",
        summary: "delete a component (no-op if absent)",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui remove <id> [--pretty]

Deletes the component keyed by <id>. A no-op (not an error) when it does not exist. NOTE: a PACKAGED
BUILTIN comes back on the next hydrate (the seed re-adds it) — use `suppress` to remove it permanently.",
    },
    CmdDoc {
        name: "suppress",
        summary: "PERMANENTLY remove a packaged builtin component — it won't re-seed (#3725)",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui suppress <id> [--superseded-by <new-id>] [--force] [--pretty]

Writes a `{ id, suppressed: true }` TOMBSTONE for <id>, so the frontend seed-reconcile stops re-adding
the packaged builtin (a plain `remove` re-seeds on the next hydrate). The library and the doctor both
skip a tombstone. Use for a builtin you never want back; `unsuppress` restores it (re-seeds from source).

THE CLAIM IS NEVER ORPHANED SILENTLY. A tombstone is `{ id, suppressed: true }` — it carries no
`provides` — so suppressing a record that CLAIMED a specifier drops the claim. If something still
imports that specifier, the suppression is REFUSED (the error names the importers), unless you either
name the replacement with --superseded-by, in which case it INHERITS the claim, or pass --force to
orphan it deliberately. Nothing fails at build time when a claim is orphaned: the loader declines the
whole closure at MOUNT time and the page renders its fallback, which is how four records went dark in
one consolidation and stayed dark until someone opened the page.

--superseded-by <new-id> records WHAT replaced this one, on the tombstone — the one record the
seed-reconcile never overwrites, so the fact survives every hydrate. Use it when retiring a wrapper into
its replacement, so the consolidation is still readable months later. The target must EXIST (a dangling
pointer is refused, not stored) and cannot be the id itself.
A ui-scope MUTATION.",
    },
    CmdDoc {
        name: "unsuppress",
        summary: "remove a suppression tombstone so the builtin re-seeds (#3725)",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui unsuppress <id> [--pretty]

Removes the `{ id, suppressed: true }` tombstone written by `suppress`, so the next hydrate re-seeds the
packaged builtin from its source. Errors if <id> is NOT a tombstone (use `remove` for a real component).
A ui-scope MUTATION.",
    },
    CmdDoc {
        name: "export",
        summary: "dump every component to a folder tree — <dir>/<group>/<id>.json, lossless (#3606)",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui export <dir> [--dir <store>] [--pretty]

Writes each stored component VERBATIM to <dir>/<group>/<id>.json, nesting by its `group` folder path
(#3579) so the tree mirrors a project's folders. The seed half of components-as-data: round-trips
through `bsc ui import`. Files are written pretty (readable diffs); --pretty also indents the report.
A READ — no `ui` write scope required. `--dir` overrides the STORE location, not the output <dir>.",
    },
    CmdDoc {
        name: "parity",
        summary: "does the app RENDER what it SHIPS? store vs seed, per record (#4246)",
        usage: "USAGE:
  bsc ui parity <seed-dir> [--role <role>] [--strict] [--dir <store>] [--pretty]

Compares each seed record's `srcText` against the STORE copy the app actually mounts. `--role page`
scopes it to the pages, which is the sharp version of the question: a page record IS the page, so a
diverged store copy renders source nothing has ever checked.

Three existing guards all read the SEED — `graphParity` globs it, the ratchet lists its exclusions, and
`reconcileSeed` returns early for any record with no `builtin`. None of them looks at what renders.
This does, and it lives here because the store is SQLite behind this binary: vitest cannot read it,
which is exactly why every other guard ended up seed-side.

Reports and exits 0 by default; `--strict` exits non-zero on any drift. A guard that lands red protects
nothing — see `record-link-debt`, where a red parity test sat unnoticed for weeks. Use `--strict` once
the known set is adjudicated. `delta` is SIGNED: the drift runs both ways, and a positive delta is the
store holding source the seed never had. A READ — no `ui` write scope required.",
    },
    CmdDoc {
        name: "sync-seed",
        summary: "write a store record's current body back into its packaged seed file, by id (#139)",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui sync-seed <id>… --seed-dir <dir> [--dir <store>] [--apply] [--pretty]

The store-to-seed sync `bsc ui parity` diagnoses and nothing could act on: an edit to a component
record lands in the store, and the app keeps SHIPPING the seed's old body until something writes the
seed back. `export` dumps a record VERBATIM (by design, so it round-trips through `import`) — including
store bookkeeping (`history`/`rev`/`updatedAt`/`updatedBy`/`builtin`/`seedHash`/`used`/`usageAssessed`/
`version`) no seed file has ever carried — so its output can't be dropped straight into <dir>. This
strips those fields and writes the rest over the EXISTING seed file matching <id> (found by walking
--seed-dir and reading each record's own `id`; a kit bundle with no top-level `id` is not a target).

Deliberately BY ID, never a sweep — seed and store drift both ways, so a mass re-stamp would as often
overwrite real seed content with stale store content. Dry run by default; pass --apply to write. Skips
(reported, not erroring) an id absent from the store, an id with no matching seed file (that is a
PROMOTION — a new file — not a sync), and an id already identical. A READ of the store — no `ui` write
scope required, since only the on-disk seed file changes (like `bsc ui export`).",
    },
    CmdDoc {
        name: "promote",
        summary: "write a genuinely NEW store record into its own file under the packaged seed (#162)",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui promote <id>… --seed-dir <dir> [--dir <store>] [--apply] [--pretty]

The counterpart `sync-seed` explicitly declines to be: syncing an id with no matching seed file needs
PROMOTING (a new file), not syncing (an existing one), per `sync-seed`'s own report. Without this,
authoring a genuinely new component in the store had no path to git except hand-writing the seed json —
exactly what request #162 hit authoring NetworkArchitectMount.

Strips the same store bookkeeping `sync-seed` strips (`history`/`rev`/`updatedAt`/`updatedBy`/`builtin`/
`seedHash`/`used`/`usageAssessed`/`version`), then writes what remains to <seed-dir>/<folder>/<id>.json,
nested by the record's own `folder` (mirroring `bsc ui export`'s nesting; a folder-less record lands at
the seed-dir root). Mirrors `bsc graph promote`'s shape — an explicit, gated verb landing a runtime
record into the committed store — ported to this store's one-file-per-record layout.

Refuses (reported as `alreadySeeded`, never overwritten) an id that already HAS a seed file — that
drift is `sync-seed`'s job, by id, drift-aware; this verb is not. Dry run by default; --apply writes. A
READ of the store — no `ui` write scope required, since only the on-disk seed file changes (like `bsc
ui export`/`sync-seed`).",
    },
    CmdDoc {
        name: "import",
        summary: "load a folder tree of component records into the store — the seed half (#3606)",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui import <dir> [--dir <store>] [--pretty]

Walks <dir> recursively for *.json and UPSERTS each into the store, keyed by the record's own `id`. A
file that is a KIT BUNDLE ({\"components\":[…]}, e.g. react-ui.json) is exploded — every component in it
is imported. A missing <dir> is empty, not an error. A ui-scope MUTATION. The load half that pairs
with `bsc ui export`; boot-seeding imports the packaged `data/components/` tree the same way.",
    },
    CmdDoc {
        name: "rename",
        summary: "rename a component in place — sweeps every composes/rules reference (#3576)",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui rename <id> <NewName> [--by <tag>] [--note <text>] [--dir D] [--pretty]

Renames the component keyed by <id> to <NewName> in ONE operation. <id> is the STABLE store key (frozen at
creation, never re-derived), so only the display/code NAME moves — nothing keyed by id (the store key, the
change history #3164/#3568, tokens, the cross-graph URN) is disturbed.

Because the composition graph is NAME-keyed, a rename rewrites, scoped to the component's OWN kit (kits
never cross):
  • the record's `name`, and the identifier in its `srcText` (+ `source` if present) — `export function
    <Old>` and self-`<Old>` → `<New>`, matched on whole-identifier boundaries so `IconButton` /
    `ButtonGroup` are never touched;
  • every sibling's `composes[]` entry == <Old>, and every `rules[].use` == <Old>, → <New>.

Every touched record gets a change-history entry (#3568); `--note` overrides the default
\"renamed <Old> → <New>\" summary. Prints { id, from, to, kit, updated: [ids], referencesUpdated }.

REFUSES when <NewName> is not a PascalCase identifier, equals the current name, or already names another
component in the same kit (which would make `composes` ambiguous). A ui-scope MUTATION.",
    },
    CmdDoc {
        name: "merge",
        summary: "combine a duplicate INTO a survivor — repoints every reference, then removes it (#3592)",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui merge <from-id> <into-id> [--by <tag>] [--note <text>] [--dir D] [--pretty]

Folds the component `<from-id>` INTO `<into-id>` (the survivor) in ONE operation — the ACT step that closes

  • every `rules[].use` == <from>'s name → <into>'s name.

    CmdDoc {
        name: "backing",
        summary: "which component record backs a file — and the gate that keeps edits going to the record",
        usage: "USAGE:
  bsc ui backing <path> [--json|--pretty]   # the record(s) whose `src` names this file
  bsc ui backing gate <path>...             # exit 1 if ANY path is record-backed (the landing gate)
  bsc ui backing audit [--json|--pretty]    # records whose `src` names a file that is NOT here (#4223)
  bsc ui backing reconcile [--json] [--apply] [--annotate] [--retire]
                                            # the SEED-side provenance reconcile (#records)

The graph is the source of truth and a component's file is the EMITTED ARTIFACT, so a fix belongs in the
record: edit it with `bsc ui set`, then `bsc ui emit component <id> <dir>` and the file follows. Editing
the file directly loses the change — the record keeps the old body and the app renders the record (#4193).

`backing <path>` answers whether a file has a record before you touch it. It reads the store's own `src`
provenance, so it covers EVERY component, not only the pages in the migration catalogue. Prints
`{ path, backed, records: [{ id, kitId, src }] }`.

`backing gate <path>...` is the landing check: run it over the files your change touches (e.g.
`git diff --name-only`). It exits 1 and names the record + the two fix commands for every backed path, and
exits 0 when none are backed. Rejecting rather than warning is deliberate — a warning here becomes noise.

`backing reconcile` is the SEED half, and it is a DIFFERENT POPULATION from `audit`: `audit` reads the
STORE (what the running app renders), this reads `data/components/app/**` (what ships to a fresh install),
and the store carries harvested and de-seeded records the seed has never held — so a fix to one leaves the
other wrong. It is the gate in front of the whole file-retirement track: deleting a migrated file whose
record is the OLDER copy is a silent revert of real work, and when the two disagreed the FILE was the newer
copy in NINE OF NINE cases measured (#4235).

Six verdicts — `ok` · `null-src` (no `src` at all, the convention for a record with no file counterpart) ·
`stale-pointer` (`src` names a file that is not here) · `moved` (`src` resolves, but the record's SYMBOL is
not in it — re-point, do not refresh) · `drifted` (symbol present, bodies disagree) · `intentional`
(drifted, with an evidenced `srcDivergence` saying why, so the reason lives where a future sweep reads it).

It REPORTS on every run and writes only under a flag: `--apply` re-points what is UNAMBIGUOUS and never
guesses, `--annotate` records why a difference is by construction, `--retire` moves `src` to `srcRetired`
where the file is gone and nothing matches. So the same command answers \"what is wrong\" and \"fix what can
be fixed mechanically\", and answers the first one again afterwards.

SCOPE: components only. An algorithm record is a function LIFTED OUT of a file and several share one
`src` (#4192), so a path-based gate cannot be honest about them yet.",

    CmdDoc {
        name: "test",
        summary: "materialize a record + its CLOSURE + its paired tests into an EMPTY dir and run them there — a pass proves every dependency is a record or the declared platform",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui test <id> --out <dir> [--run]         # one record + its closure
  bsc ui test --all --out <dir> [--run]        # every record carrying a paired test, each in its own dir
  bsc ui test <id> --out <dir> --records-only  # is every dependency a RECORD yet? (migration progress)
  bsc ui test <id> --out <dir> --no-closure    # the STRICT form: the record utterly alone
  bsc ui test <id> --out <dir> --repo <dir>    # where the boundary's real files live (default: cwd)

The components twin of `bsc graph test`. Materializing OUT OF THE REPO is what makes the run mean
something: inside the repo every import resolves whether the record declares it or not.

What goes in with the record is its RECORD CLOSURE — every record its code imports, transitively
(materialize-a-records-record-closure). Components COMPOSE components, so a strict one-record
materialization can only ever verify leaves, and most of a UI library is not leaves. The closure resolves
the way the running app resolves: a `@/components/<id>` sibling, then a component whose `provides` is the
specifier, then an algorithm impl's. Members are written into a `_closure/` MIRROR of `src/` that `@` is
aliased to, so each sits at its real position and its own imports resolve with no source rewriting.

The loader's OTHER half comes in too: a dependency may be a record, or a module the PLATFORM REGISTRY
(`platform-modules.json`) declares. The two are supplied differently on purpose — a record is COPIED out
of the store into the mirror, a boundary module is ALIASED to the app's real file, one exact alias per
specifier actually reached. Never a blanket `@` onto `src/`: that would resolve everything and leave the
run proving nothing.

What is withheld is still APP CONTEXT — the repo tree, the app's aliases, the store. An import that is
NEITHER a record nor declared is left out and the run FAILS on it, even when the file is sitting right
there. Every run reports `closure` (records that came in, and from which store), `boundary` (what the app
still supplies from a FILE — this IS the per-record migration list) and `missing`.

The record under test is JUDGED; the boundary is SUPPLIED, not judged. Inside a boundary module the app's
own resolution applies, so its imports are followed whether declared or not, and those are reported with
`registered: false`. Judging the platform's internals would fail records over modules the app resolves
perfectly well — measuring the registry instead of the record.

--records-only empties the registry, so the run answers the MIGRATION question instead: is every one of
this record's dependencies a record YET? That is the progress measure, and it is a different question
from whether the record works.

--no-closure restores the strict one-record form: a pass there proves the record is a LEAF, importing no
other app module at all. That is the RETIRABILITY signal, and it runs opposite to usefulness — the
records that verify alone are the primitives everything imports.

The directory gets its own `vitest.config.ts`, or vitest walks UP, finds the repo's, and lends the record
the aliases and setup file isolation exists to withhold. The component file takes its ORIGINAL basename,
because the paired test imports it the way it always did (`./WorkerModals`, not `worker-modals`).
`environment` follows the test — jsdom when it reaches for @testing-library or `document`, node otherwise.

A record with NO paired test is refused rather than reported green: a vacuous pass would claim `verified`
about a record nothing checks. A test that reaches other app modules is not paired onto the record at all
— it belongs on an edge. `--all` exits non-zero when any record fails, and COUNTS the ones it skipped.",

    CmdDoc {
        name: "doctor",
        summary: "graph-health report — orphans, dead branches, duplicates, cycles, unbuildable + self-referential components (#2678)",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui doctor [--kit K] [--json] [--pretty]              # the health report (read-only)
  bsc ui doctor --category cat[,cat…] [--kit K] [--json]   # NARROW the report to one or more categories (#114)
  bsc ui doctor --sound-kit id@version [--json]            # judge @bsc/sounds/… against a PINNED sound kit (#3412)
  bsc ui doctor --motion [--kit K] [--json]                # ALSO run the four mechanical MOTION checks (#3163)
  bsc ui doctor --runtime [--kit K] [--json]               # ALSO report what the app OBSERVED while running
  bsc ui doctor --imports [--kit K] [--json]               # ALSO walk each record's import CLOSURE for a symbol the target never exports (#149)
  bsc ui doctor --fix [--kit K] [--yes]                    # OPTIMIZE: merge byte-identical dups + prune dead roots (dry-run unless --yes)

--category (#114) narrows the report to the named categories after every lens has contributed — so it
composes with --motion/--runtime/--imports rather than pre-empting them. Comma-separated for more than
one (`--category dangling-branch,orphan`); an unknown category name simply matches nothing, same as an
unknown --kit. Use it to check one category's status out of a 200+ finding report without a helper
script or re-parsing --json by hand.

--sound-kit (#3412) names the project's PINNED sound kit (its blueprint's `soundKit`, as `id@version` in the
`bsc sound release` store), so a `@bsc/sounds/<cue>` reference is judged against the kit the project actually
adopted — the same target the Design Studio's preview resolves. Omit it for an unpinned project and the
packaged default kit is used. A ref the store does not hold is a hard ERROR, never a quiet fall back to the
default: a pinned project reported against the starter kit would call broken sound references clean.

--motion (#3163) ADDS four mechanical animation checks to the report: MOTION-DEAD-SELECTOR (an animation
`selector` whose class hook the component's source never renders — it matches nothing), MOTION-DASH-NO-
PATHLENGTH (a stroke-dash(offset|array) keyframe on a component that sets no `pathLength` — a draw needs a
known path length), MOTION-TRANSFORM-ATTR (a CSS `transform` keyframe on a component using an SVG
`transform=` ATTRIBUTE — the two don't compose), and MOTION-NAME-COLLISION (an inline animation NAME
declared by 2+ components in the same kit — their keyframes clobber). They scan each component's INLINE
animation defs (a name-ref string points at the kit's shared library and is not checked).

--runtime (#doctor-reads-the-runtime) ADDS the findings this report structurally cannot reach, read from
runtime.db — what the RUNNING app observed rather than what the graph's shape implies. RUNTIME-DECLINED (the
loader refused the record and served the bundled platform module instead — the record is inert while the app
looks fine), RUNTIME-NEVER-RAN (no attestation at all; the honest superset of ORPHAN, which only sees
`composes` edges), RUNTIME-STALE (the record's current source has never run — an unexercised edit is where a
broken record hides), RUNTIME-FELL-BACK (an older version rendered instead), RUNTIME-RENDER-THREW (mounted,
then threw), RUNTIME-RECOMPILE-LOOP and RUNTIME-SLOW-COMPILE. With no attestations recorded it emits ONE
finding saying so rather than calling every record dead — an empty store means nothing was MEASURED, which
is not the same as nothing having run.

--imports (bsc request #149) ADDS UNRESOLVED-IMPORT-SYMBOL: `unresolvable-import` above only asks whether a
`@/…` specifier resolves to SOME record; this asks the sharper question — once it resolves, does the target
actually EXPORT the name being imported? Follows `export * from` barrels (and `export type * from`) through
the SAME resolution chain `bsc ui test`'s closure walker uses (sibling by id → component `provides` → algorithm
impl `provides`), and reads every comma-separated declarator in a `const`/`let`/`var` export, not just the
first — a checker that stops at either of those reports a record clean on exactly the drift that breaks it at
runtime with no typecheck error and no failing test (tsc/vitest compile the SEED file; the app loads the STORE
record, and the two can drift apart). Skips a specifier that resolves to no record at all — that gap is
UNRESOLVABLE-IMPORT's finding, not this one's, so the two never double-report the same defect.

Traverses each kit's composition graph (nodes = components, edges = `composes`) and reports the
dead/duplicated design a growing kit accumulates: CYCLE (a composes loop), DANGLING-BRANCH (an unused
root that still pulls in dependencies), DUPLICATE (two components wrapping the same intrinsic, or
byte-identical source), NO-IMPLEMENTATION (a component the Design Studio preview can't build — a spec,
not code; a built-in whose real source lives in the packaged artifact is NOT flagged), and ORPHAN (an
isolated, never-referenced primitive/composite). \"Unused\" = no composer AND used = 0; a page/layout
with used > 0 is a legit entry point, never flagged. Ranked most-severe-first; --kit scopes to one
kit; --json emits the findings array (LLM-consumable).

PROPS-METADATA-MISMATCH (#88) diffs each record's `props` against the prop signature parsed from its own
source, naming the missing and extra props. The preview's sample-data synthesizer reads `props` and
NOTHING else, so an EMPTY `props: []` on a component with a real typed signature silently leaves it
nothing to sample and the component renders with every prop undefined. Run kit-wide, it partitions a
render-error backlog into the crashes a `props` edit fixes and the ones that need a real change. It
reports only what it can read off the source — an imported props type or a `memo(…)` wrapper yields
nothing rather than a guess — and cedes the \"metadata names props the source never uses at all\" case to
UNWIRED-PROP, which already owns it.

DANGLING-COMPOSES-REFERENCE (#89) is the standard the designer doc always stated and nothing checked: a
`composes` entry naming no component in the kit, by name OR id. Both edge builders DROP an unresolved
name, so the graph reads as complete while the reference names nothing. One finding per MISSING
component, listing every composer — the fix is one record, not one per site — and it distinguishes the
two cases, whose fixes are opposites: the name exists NOWHERE (a forward reference to an extraction
never done ⇒ author the canonical record it already names) versus the name exists in ANOTHER kit
(`composes` only resolves within one kit ⇒ reach the record that exists; do not write a second copy).
Neither fix is a merge: `bsc ui dupes` used to report such a pair as a near-duplicate whose \"merge X
into Y\" the preview sandbox makes impossible, so that proposal now leads with the extraction instead.

SKIPS-FAMILY-SHELL (#87) is the question `dupes`/`similar` structurally cannot answer: which members of a
FAMILY do not compose the shell primitive the rest of it does. A family is a folder or a trailing-
PascalCase-word group of 6+ in one kit; a shell is any component 85%+ of that family composes AND its kit
composes widely (10+ composers), and the finding names the minority — at most three, or it is a split
rather than an outlier. Fuzzy name + prop-contract distance CANNOT see this: a toggle card has
`enabled`/`onToggle` and an info card has `value`/`label`, so siblings sharing a shell never meet in a
dupes report. It is a REPORT, not a rule — an outlier may be a deliberate exception.

--fix is the mechanical, SAFE OPTIMIZE (#3089): (1) MERGE byte-identical-source duplicates — fold each
group into the most-`used` canonical and repoint composers to it (lossless; only byte-identical, never a
same-`wraps` dup; a merged-away `builtin: true` dup gets a suppression tombstone instead of a bare delete,
same as `bsc ui merge`, so it survives the next hydrate — #96), then (2) PRUNE the GUARDED dead roots — the
ROOT of each orphan/dangling-branch finding (never a used > 0 node). DRY RUN by default (prints what WOULD
change); pass --yes to apply. Cycles and same-`wraps` (differing-source) duplicates are NOT auto-resolved —
they need a semantic call. Branch descendants are left for the next pass (one might be shared) — re-run to
clean them.

The PRUNE GUARDS (#3087) — the dead-root heuristic is a good REPORT and a dangerous auto-DELETE, so three
classes of candidate are named, then held back: a `page` (a page is a root BY DEFINITION — nothing composes
a page, so the heuristic condemns the whole pages tier), a `builtin: true` packaged seed (shipped on
purpose; the seed reconcile re-adds it), and EVERY candidate while the usage index is unpopulated (no
component in scope carries used > 0, so `used = 0` means UNKNOWN, not unused). A held-back candidate is
still REPORTED by `bsc ui doctor` — only the automatic removal is withheld. #2678/#2679/#3089/#3087.",

    CmdDoc {
        name: "dupes",
        summary: "the whole-library duplicate report — exact + fuzzy NEAR-duplicates (name + contract distance), propose-only (#3544)",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui dupes [--kit K] [--threshold 0..1] [--explain] [--json] [--pretty]

The DEDUP surface. Reports the EXACT `duplicate` findings the per-kit analyzer emits (two components sharing
a `wraps` intrinsic, or byte-identical source) PLUS the FUZZY near-duplicates it structurally misses —
`Donut`≈`DonutChart`, `Bars`≈`BarChart`, `Legend`≈`ChartLegend`, and cross-kit `Card`/`Grid`/`KeyValueList`
repeats a growing multi-kit library accumulates. Each near-duplicate is scored by NAME distance (normalized
token-set + edit distance; `Chart`/`View`/`Bsc` affixes stripped, names singularized) and CONTRACT/body
distance, combined 0.5·name + 0.5·contract. Cross-kit by design — the whole point is consolidating
overlapping kits into one.

CONTRACT TERMS (#4138): prop-signature · source shingles · `src` (same file — a strong PRIOR, not a verdict:
several components are legitimately extracted from one module) · `folder` · `composes` · `shapes` ·
`whenUse`/`whenNot` guidance · variants · tags · colocated `tests` · `wraps` · role. A term with NO signal on
either side is DROPPED, never scored 0 — two prop-less primitives must not read as identical for both
lacking props.

A pair is contract-scored when its NAME is near OR it shares a hard co-location signal (same `src`, folder,
`wraps`, `provides`, shape or test file). Before #4138 a dissimilar name alone skipped the pair entirely, so
`Donut` vs `PieChart` — the duplicates you cannot grep for — were invisible unless byte-identical.

Also reports `provides-collision`: several records overriding ONE platform specifier. Not a similarity
score — the loader resolves it to one record, so the rest are dead overrides that still read as live.

SUPPRESSED RECORDS ARE NOT SCORED, here or in `bsc ui similar`. A tombstone keeps its id and loses every
content field, so every contract term drops for want of signal and NAME similarity alone is left carrying
the pair — and ids retired together are named alike by construction. Left in, one batch consolidation
mints a mutually near-duplicate clique out of the records it just retired: the live store's largest
cluster was 31 `settings-*card` tombstones proposing the consolidation that produced them, with 41 of the
store's 58 tombstones somewhere in the report, sitting on top of the live clusters. Asking about a
tombstone BY id still answers — it is ranked against the live library, and `similar` says the record is
retired so a thin result is not read as `nothing resembles it`.

A SHARED FORWARD REFERENCE is not shared code (#89). `composes` is a raw string-set match that never asks
whether a name resolves, so two records both naming a component nobody has authored score 1.0 on that term.
Where that fabricated agreement is the only thing carrying a pair over the bar, the pair is DROPPED — the
signal is `bsc ui doctor`'s `dangling-composes-reference`, not a duplicate. Where the pair stands on real
evidence anyway (same `src`, same folder, overlapping bodies), it is still reported, but the proposal leads
with AUTHORING the record both already name: that extraction is the consolidation, and a literal merge is
not available, because the preview sandbox forbids the first-party import it would need.

--explain prints each pair's per-term contributions (`term=value×weight→contribution`) and the terms dropped
for lack of signal, so the ranking is auditable and the weights are tunable against real output.

--threshold tunes the fuzzy bar (default 0.55); --kit scopes to ONE kit (which drops cross-kit near-dups);
--json emits the findings array (LLM-consumable), each `{ category, severity, kit, nodeIds, nodeNames, why,
suggestedAction }`. PROPOSE-ONLY: there is no `--fix` here — a near-duplicate is a WEAKER signal than a
byte-identical dup and the merge is a semantic call, so use these proposals to guide a manual/designer merge.
Inspect one component's neighborhood with `bsc ui similar <id>`. #3544.",

  bsc ui similar <id> --shape [--top N] [--threshold 0..1]   # rank by STRUCTURE only (#90)

different question, so it returns different columns — `{ composes_similarity, skeleton_similarity }`.

        summary: "determine each component's usage from composes + host mounts + `provides`, over a DECLARED corpus (#3888)",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui usage-scan [--kit K] [--root DIR]... [--apply] [--json] [--pretty]

The producer for `used`, which has never had one: measured 2026-08-24, 0 of 552 components across all
four kits carried `used > 0`. So doctor's dead-root rule (`in-degree 0 AND used == 0`) collapsed to
\"nothing composes it\" and flagged every entry point by construction.

THREE SOURCES, because usage has three shapes: `composes` (another record in the kit composes it) ·
`mount` (a `<GraphComponent id=\"X\">` literal names it) · `provides` (its specifier is imported).
Each row says WHICH source answered, so a count is never a bare number you have to trust.

THE CORPUS IS DECLARED AND INCLUDES THE STORE. `--root DIR` adds a tree (repeatable); the kit's own
records are ALWAYS in it and are named in the report. That is not a convenience — post-#3604 a
`GraphComponent id=` sweep of `src/` finds ONE hit (the literal `id=\"x\"`), while all ten real mount
sites live inside record `srcText`. A corpus that is only the repo tree reports every migrated page

that belong to `Card` — its props type, its variant enum, a `useCard` hook. It does not export

record.

--all is deliberately UNBOUNDED, with no threshold: over the records that carry source, ~37% export more
than one name and ~20% more than one item, and that shoulder — a component plus one domain type it

        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui patterns [--kit K] [--threshold 0..1] [--min N] [--json] [--pretty]

`bsc ui similar <id> --shape` answers `what is built like THIS?` from a seed the caller must already
have — so a pattern can only ever be CONFIRMED by someone who already suspects it. This is the other
half: it sweeps every LIVE record pairwise on the shape score and returns the groups themselves.

The one sweep that already existed, `bsc ui dupes`, structurally cannot find these: it is blended
(0.5 name + 0.5 contract), and a differing NAME halves a pair however identically it is built. Six
settings cards composing [Card, ToggleRow] around one skeleton score 34% blended and never meet.

Each cluster carries three things beyond its member list:

  signature   what every member SHARES — the composes entries and the rendered tags common to all of
              them. A member list says WHICH records are alike; the signature says WHAT they are, which
              is what a pattern needs before anyone can name it.
  cohesion    the WEAKEST pairwise score inside the cluster. Connected components CHAIN — A~B and B~C
              group all three even when A and C are unalike — so a cohesion well under the threshold
              means `related`, not `uniform`, and the row says CHAINED. At cohesion 1.00 the cluster is
              an exact equivalence class.
  kits        every kit represented. Cross-kit by design, like `dupes`.

--threshold sets the bar (default 0.90, MEASURED — see the constant); --min the smallest cluster
(default 2; a pair is a legitimate pattern-of-two); --kit scopes; --json emits the clusters; --pretty
indents. The threshold and the counts are always PRINTED before the rows, because a sweep whose bar is
invisible reads as `this is everything`.

Suppressed records are excluded, as everywhere on this surface. A READ — never scope-gated.

NOT a dedup proposal. Two records sharing a shape are usually SUPPOSED to: that is what a pattern is.
Reach for `bsc ui dupes` when the question is `should these be one component?` and this when it is
`what conventions does this library already have?`",

USAGE:
  bsc ui pattern list [--json] [--pretty]
  bsc ui pattern get <id> [--json] [--pretty]
  bsc ui pattern new <id> --from <member-id> [--name \"...\"] [--threshold 0..1]
  bsc ui pattern of <component-id> [--json]
  bsc ui pattern remove <id>

`bsc ui patterns` (plural) FINDS the library's structural conventions. This names one. A cluster is a
report — recomputed every sweep, with nothing to point at — so the only way to author into an existing
convention is to find a sibling and copy it, which is how the convention drifts and how a fifth copy
gets written by a session that believed it was writing a first.

An id changes the request: `author a telemetry settings card` becomes `add a member to
settings-toggle-card`, and a pattern you are INSTANTIATING is not one you can duplicate.

  new     PROMOTES the cluster containing --from <member-id> into a named record. Any one member names
          the cluster, so there is no positional index to go stale. It reuses the same sweep at the same
          bar, so a promoted pattern's members are the cluster that was reported.
  get     the signature + its members, recomputed LIVE. Points at an exemplar to read, which is what a
          session should copy FROM.
  of      the REVERSE lookup — which convention does this record already belong to? The read to make
          when you have a component in hand rather than a pattern.

MEMBERSHIP IS COMPUTED, NEVER STORED. A frozen member list is wrong the moment anything is authored,
which is exactly when the question is asked. The record keeps its `exemplars` (the evidence it was
promoted from) and nothing else about membership.

TWO KINDS OF PATTERN, tested differently, and the record says which (`signatureSource`):

  derived    promoted from a real cluster, so members define it. A record conforms when it SCORES at or
             above the pattern's threshold against an exemplar — the same measure the cluster was drawn
             with.
  declared   named by an author before any member exists. Nothing to score against, so a record
             conforms by CONTAINING the signature. That is LOOSER — anything holding those parts
             matches — and every member row carries `basis` so the caller is never guessing which test
             produced the answer.

--dir is the COMPONENT store (what conformance is computed against), as everywhere else; the pattern
records have their own --pattern-dir. Suppressed records are never members. A READ except for `new` and
`remove`.",

/// The component collection's knobs over the shared CLI. Lean `list` projects id/name/kitId/role +
/// the data-shape axis (`shapes` rides the projection verbatim, #2475).
const COMPONENT_SPEC: CliSpec = CliSpec {
    noun: "component",
    dir_env: "BSC_COMPONENT_DIR",
    dir_segment: "components",
    tagline: TAGLINE,
    commands: COMPONENT_COMMANDS,
    // `domain` (epic-the-graphs-are-split-by-feature-over-a-core) is the FEATURE axis, beside `folder`
    // rather than replacing it: folder is derived from `src` and names emit paths, domain is stored and
    // says what the record belongs to. It rides the lean projection so "what is in this feature" is one
    // read, the same shape `bsc graph impl list` already answers for algorithms.
    meta_fields: &["id", "name", "kitId", "role", "folder", "feature", "shapes"],
    // #4072 — exactly what the Design Studio's composition graph renders: the node card
    // (name/role/group/×used) plus `composes`, which `buildComposesEdges` turns into the edges.
    // Deliberately NOT `srcText` (77.6% of the full payload) / `tests` / `history` / `props`: the
    // graph reads none of them, and the page was blocking up to 8s fetching them.
    graph_fields: &["id", "name", "kitId", "role", "folder", "used", "composes"],
    // #4107 slice B: `group` -> `folder`. 351 stored records predate the rename and there is no
    // migration pass, so every projection reads the legacy key when the current one is absent.
    // #4107's `("folder", "group")` alias is GONE (finish-the-4107-group-to-folder-shim). It existed
    // because 351 records predated the rename; `bsc ui refolder` has since migrated the last of them,
    // and the packaged seed never carried the legacy key at all. Its removal is what makes `bsc ui list`
    // and `bsc ui get --field folder` agree again — projecting through an alias while `get` read the raw
    // record is why those two disagreed for a year.
    field_aliases: &[],
};

/// A non-blocking `kit set` advisory (#3040): the Design Studio places a kit in its rail by two axes —
/// `tech` (technology slug) + `style` (visual language) — so a kit missing either shows under the
/// trailing "other" head (e.g. "other/other"), which is almost never intended. Warn (stderr) per such
/// kit, but NEVER reject: both axes are OPTIONAL in the model (`Kit.tech?`/`style?`, back-compat with
/// pre-#2487 stores), so this only nudges. `stack` is a display label, NOT a substitute for either.
fn warn_kit_axes(items: &[serde_json::Value]) -> Result<(), String> {
    for it in items {
        let id = it.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("<no id>");
        let present = |k: &str| it.get(k).and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).is_some_and(|s| !s.trim().is_empty());
        let missing: Vec<&str> = ["tech", "style"].into_iter().filter(|k| !present(k)).collect();
        if !missing.is_empty() {
            eprintln!(
                "warning: kit '{id}' has no {} — the Design Studio groups kits by tech + style, so it will \
                 show under the \"other\" bucket. Add e.g. \"tech\":\"react\",\"style\":\"studio\" (stack is a \
                 display label only, not a grouping axis).",
                missing.join(" and no ")
            );
        }
    }
