    Ok(())
}

/// The component-surface command catalog, exposed so `bsc ui` (#2469) can compose it verbatim into its
/// merged help tree AND gate which verbs it delegates here (unknown verbs stay `bsc ui`'s, so its
/// error shows the MERGED overview rather than this partial one).
pub fn command_docs() -> &'static [CmdDoc] {
    COMPONENT_COMMANDS
}

/// Whether `args` is one of the store's MUTATING verb invocations — `set` / `remove` on either
/// collection (`… set|remove` or `… kit set|remove`) or the component-animation writers
/// (`define-animation` / `remove-animation`, #2869) — gated by the session's runtime `ui` scope
/// (#2470). The trailing `help` form (`set help`, `kit set help`) is NOT a mutation: help must stay
/// reachable from a read-scoped session. Read verbs (`list`/`get`/`eslint-preset`/`usage`/
/// `list-animations`/`kit list|get`) never gate.
fn is_scoped_mutation(args: &[String]) -> bool {
    let (verb, next) = if args.first().map(String::as_str) == Some("kit") {
        (args.get(1), args.get(2))
    } else {
        (args.first(), args.get(1))
    };
    matches!(
        verb.map(String::as_str),
        Some("set") | Some("revert") | Some("remove") | Some("rename") | Some("merge") | Some("define-animation") | Some("remove-animation") | Some("refolder") | Some("features") | Some("import") | Some("suppress") | Some("unsuppress")
    ) && next.map(String::as_str) != Some("help")
        // `usage-scan` is a READ until `--apply`, which writes `used`/`usageAssessed` onto every examined
        // record. Gate on the flag, not the verb, so the diagnosis stays available to a read-scoped session.
        || (verb.map(String::as_str) == Some("usage-scan") && args.iter().any(|a| a == "--apply"))
}

/// Every LIVE record whose source imports `spec`, excluding `skip_id` and any tombstone.
///
/// Matches the specifier QUOTED (`"spec"` or `'spec'`), never as a bare substring: `@/x/Foo` is a
/// prefix of `@/x/FooBar`, so a `contains` would report the wrong record as an importer and turn a
/// harmless suppression into a refusal nobody can act on. Covers `import … from`, `export … from` and
/// `require(…)` alike, because all three are just the specifier in quotes.
fn live_importers_of(store: &bsc_json_store::Store, spec: &str, skip_id: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let needles = [format!("\"{spec}\""), format!("'{spec}'")];
    let mut out: Vec<String> = store
        .list()
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|raw| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(raw).ok())
        .filter(|r| r.get("suppressed").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_bool) != Some(true))
        .filter(|r| r.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) != Some(skip_id))
        .filter(|r| {
            let src = r.get("srcText").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
            needles.iter().any(|n| src.contains(n.as_str()))
        })
        .filter_map(|r| r.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).map(str::to_string))
        .collect();
    out.sort();
    out
}

/// `bsc ui suppress <id>` / `bsc ui kit suppress <id>` (#3725) — write a `{ id, suppressed: true }`
/// TOMBSTONE into the collection's store, PERMANENTLY removing a packaged builtin: the frontend
/// `reconcileSeed` sees the tombstone occupying the id and never re-seeds the builtin (a plain `remove`
/// comes back on the next hydrate). A ui-scope MUTATION (gated by [`is_scoped_mutation`] before this runs).
fn cmd_suppress(
    args: &[String],
    open: impl Fn(&Option<String>) -> Result<bsc_json_store::Store, String>,
    noun: &str,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let kit_prefix = if noun == "kit" { "kit " } else { "" };
    let SuppressArgs { positionals, dir, superseded_by, force } = parse_suppress_args(args)?;
    let id = positionals.first().ok_or_else(|| format!("usage: bsc ui {kit_prefix}suppress <id>"))?;
    let store = open(&dir)?;
    // Read BEFORE the tombstone replaces it — the claim being retired is only visible here.
    let current = current_record(&store, id)?;
    let mut inherited_by = None::<String>;
    let mut tombstone = serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "suppressed": true });
    // `--superseded-by` (#a-tombstone-can-name-what-superseded-it) — WHAT replaced this record, stored on
    // the tombstone because the tombstone is the one thing the seed-reconcile never overwrites. A
    // consolidation that retires 45 wrappers into composed widgets is otherwise unauditable a month later.
    if let Some(new_id) = superseded_by {
        // REFUSED, NOT STORED, on a dangling or self pointer — the same discipline `bsc project architect
        // set` applies to an unknown persona. A pointer to nothing is worse than no pointer: it reads as
        // provenance while naming a record no one can open, and the tombstone is durable, so the lie
        // outlives everyone who could correct it.
        if new_id == *id {
            return Err(format!("'{id}' cannot supersede itself"));
        }
        // `current_record` returns Null for a missing id rather than Err, so ABSENCE is the Null check —
        // `.is_err()` here would never fire and the guard would be decorative.
        let target = current_record(&store, &new_id)?;
        if target.is_null() {
            return Err(format!(
                "--superseded-by '{new_id}' is not a {noun} in the store — author it first, or omit the flag"
            ));
        }
        // A target that is ITSELF a tombstone is dangling in the way that matters: the pointer names
        // something no one can open, which is the whole failure this guard exists to prevent.
        if target.get("suppressed").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_bool) == Some(true) {
            return Err(format!(
                "--superseded-by '{new_id}' is itself suppressed — a retired {noun} cannot be the replacement"
            ));
        }
        tombstone["supersededBy"] = serde_json::Value::String(new_id.clone());
        inherited_by = Some(new_id);
    }

    guard_provides_claim(&store, id, &current, inherited_by.as_deref(), force, "Suppressing")?;

    stamped_set(&store, id, tombstone, &crate::record::resolve_writer(None))?;
    // A suppressed component carries no live preview — clear any stale render-error keyed to it (#3707).
    if noun == "component" {
        let _ = crate::preview_errors::clear(id);
    }
    println!("suppressed {noun} '{id}' — the packaged builtin will not re-seed (`unsuppress` to restore)");
    Ok(())
}

/// `bsc ui unsuppress <id>` / `bsc ui kit unsuppress <id>` (#3725) — remove a suppression tombstone so the
/// next hydrate re-seeds the packaged builtin from its source (no data loss). REFUSES on a non-tombstone
/// id: a real record must go through `remove`, never this.
fn cmd_unsuppress(
    args: &[String],
    open: impl Fn(&Option<String>) -> Result<bsc_json_store::Store, String>,
    noun: &str,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let kit_prefix = if noun == "kit" { "kit " } else { "" };
    let (pos, dir, _pretty) = parse_anim_args(args)?;
    let id = pos.first().ok_or_else(|| format!("usage: bsc ui {kit_prefix}unsuppress <id>"))?;
    let store = open(&dir)?;
    let existing = current_record(&store, id)?;
    if existing.get("suppressed").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_bool) != Some(true) {
        return Err(format!(
            "'{id}' is not a suppression tombstone — nothing to unsuppress (use `remove` to delete a real {noun})"
        ));
    }
    store.remove(id)?;
    println!("unsuppressed {noun} '{id}' — it re-seeds on the next hydrate");
    Ok(())
}

/// The `bsc ui merge` result object — extracted so the CONTRACT is testable without capturing stdout
/// (`cmd_merge` prints with `println!`, which the shared capture sink does not see).
///
/// `retired` NAMES what happened, and `removed` is the id ONLY when the record is genuinely gone.
/// Reporting a tombstone as `removed` is what sent designer request #102 hunting a missing delete call
/// through 32 ids that were every one of them behaving exactly as designed.
fn merge_report(
    from_id: &str,
    into_id: &str,
    kit_id: &str,
    repointed: &[String],
    retired: Retired,
) -> serde_json::Value {
    serde_json::json!({
        "from": from_id,
        "into": into_id,
        "kit": kit_id,
        "repointed": repointed,
        "retired": retired.as_str(),
        "removed": match retired {
            Retired::Removed => serde_json::Value::String(from_id.to_string()),
            Retired::Tombstoned => serde_json::Value::Null,
        },
    })
}

/// THE SPECIFIER MUST NOT BE ORPHANED — the one guard every retirement path shares.
///
/// A tombstone is `{ id, suppressed: true }`; it carries no `provides`. So retiring a record that
/// CLAIMED a specifier drops the claim, and if no successor picks it up, every importer of that
/// specifier resolves to nothing. The record still compiles, so nothing fails at build time; the loader
/// declines the whole closure at MOUNT time and the page renders its fallback. That is how four records
/// went dark in one consolidation and were not noticed until someone opened the page, and it is why
/// `branchesview` needed the same repair before them.
///
/// **It lived inside `cmd_suppress` and nowhere else, which is the bug moving it here fixes.** `bsc ui
/// merge` and `doctor --fix`'s dup fold retire records through [`retire_component`], which wrote the
/// same tombstone with none of this checking — so the guarded verb refused while the unguarded ones did
/// it silently. On 2026-08-24 a designer session merged 34 module records away and orphaned 34
/// specifiers, taking Settings, Glance and Accessibility off the store's resolution graph one `merge` at
/// a time. Its output looked right because `merge` repoints `composes`, by NAME — and `composes` is not
/// what an import resolves through.
///
/// `verb` is the gerund naming the action in the refusal ("Suppressing" / "Merging"), so the message
/// describes what the caller actually did rather than what this function is called.
fn guard_provides_claim(
    store: &bsc_json_store::Store,
    id: &str,
    current: &serde_json::Value,
    successor: Option<&str>,
    force: bool,
    verb: &str,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let Some(spec) = current
        .get("provides")
        .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)
        .map(str::trim)
        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
    else {
        return Ok(());
    };
    let importers = live_importers_of(store, spec, id);
    match (successor, importers.is_empty(), force) {
        // Nothing imports it — orphaning the claim costs nothing, so this stays quiet.
        (_, true, _) => Ok(()),
        // Deliberate: the operator said orphan it.
        (_, false, true) => {
            println!("warning: '{spec}' is imported by {} record(s) and no longer resolves — --force", importers.len());
            Ok(())
        }
        // A successor was named: it INHERITS the claim, which is what the consolidation meant.
        (Some(new_id), false, false) => {
            let mut target = current_record(store, new_id)?;
            let held = target.get("provides").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").trim().to_string();
            if held.is_empty() {
                target["provides"] = serde_json::Value::String(spec.to_string());
                stamped_set(store, new_id, target, &crate::record::resolve_writer(None))?;
                println!("'{new_id}' inherited provides '{spec}' — {} importer(s) keep resolving", importers.len());
                Ok(())
            } else if held != spec {
                // Two claims, one successor. Guessing which wins is how a WRONG module starts answering
                // a specifier, which is worse than the specifier answering nothing.
                Err(format!(
                    "'{id}' provides '{spec}' ({} importer(s)) but '{new_id}' already provides '{held}' — \
                     one record cannot answer both. Re-point the importers, or clear `provides` on \
                     '{new_id}' so it can inherit '{spec}'.",
                    importers.len()
                ))
            } else {
                Ok(())
            }
        }
        // No successor and live importers: refuse. The list is what makes it actionable.
        (None, false, false) => {
            let mut shown: Vec<&str> = importers.iter().take(5).map(String::as_str).collect();
            if importers.len() > shown.len() {
                shown.push("…");
            }
            Err(format!(
                "'{id}' provides '{spec}', which {} record(s) still import ({}). {verb} it orphans that \
                 specifier and every importer's closure goes unsatisfiable at MOUNT time, not at build \
                 time. Name the replacement so it inherits the claim, or --force to orphan it deliberately.",
                importers.len(),
                shown.join(", ")
            ))
        }
    }
}

/// What [`retire_component`] actually did. A tombstone and a delete are not the same event, and a caller
/// that reports one as the other makes the store look broken: designer request #102 spot-checked 32 ids
/// `bsc ui merge` had called `"removed"` and found all 32 still gettable. They were tombstoned, by design
/// (#3725/#96) — only the WORD was wrong.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum Retired {
    /// Deleted outright — a non-builtin, with no packaged seed to come back from.
    Removed,
    /// A `{ id, suppressed: true }` tombstone replaced it, so the packaged seed will not re-add it.
    Tombstoned,
}

impl Retired {
    pub(crate) fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Retired::Removed => "removed",
            Retired::Tombstoned => "tombstoned",
        }
    }
}

/// Retire a component `id` whose references have already been repointed away — the shared tail of
/// `merge` and `doctor --fix`'s byte-identical dup fold. A packaged BUILTIN gets a suppression
/// TOMBSTONE (the same `{ id, suppressed: true, supersededBy }` shape `bsc ui suppress` writes) instead
/// of a bare delete: the frontend seed-reconcile only skips re-adding a builtin when it finds one of
/// these occupying the id (#3725), and a plain `store.remove` leaves the id looking merely ABSENT —
/// which is "missing" to the reconcile, so it comes back on the very next hydrate. That is exactly
/// designer request #96: `bsc ui merge`/`doctor --fix` folding a builtin duplicate away never stuck,
/// because neither wrote the tombstone `suppress` does. A non-builtin has no packaged seed to come back
/// from, so a plain remove is enough and never leaves a stray tombstone behind.
fn retire_component(
    store: &bsc_json_store::Store,
    id: &str,
    builtin: bool,
    superseded_by: Option<&str>,
) -> Result<Retired, String> {
    // The claim check comes FIRST and applies to BOTH arms — a bare delete drops a `provides` exactly as
    // a tombstone does, so gating it on `builtin` would leave the same hole for the other half. See
    // `guard_provides_claim` for what this cost before it was here.
    let current = current_record(store, id)?;
    guard_provides_claim(store, id, &current, superseded_by, false, "Merging")?;
    if !builtin {
        store.remove(id)?;
        return Ok(Retired::Removed);
    }
    let mut tombstone = serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "suppressed": true });
    if let Some(b) = superseded_by {
        tombstone["supersededBy"] = serde_json::Value::String(b.to_string());
    }
    stamped_set(store, id, tombstone, &crate::record::resolve_writer(None))?;
    // A suppressed component carries no live preview — clear any stale render-error keyed to it (#3707),
    // same as `cmd_suppress`.
    let _ = crate::preview_errors::clear(id);
    Ok(Retired::Tombstoned)
}

/// The component-verb entrypoint: `args` is everything after the mount point (`bsc ui`, or the
/// deprecated `bsc component` alias — `prog` is that display name for help/errors). `<prog> kit …`
/// routes to the KIT collection; everything else to the COMPONENT collection — each is the shared
/// verbatim-JSON store CLI over its own dir.
pub fn run(args: Vec<String>, prog: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    // Runtime `ui` scope check (#2470, defense-in-depth): refuse the mutating verbs when the
    // session's `$BSC_SCOPES` doc scopes `ui` to read/none — BEFORE any store is touched. Guarding
    // here (the verb dispatch this crate owns) holds under BOTH mounts of the store CLI (`bsc ui`
    // and the deprecated `bsc component` alias, #2469). Absent env ⇒ unrestricted (hand shells);
    // NOT a security boundary — the launch-time deny rules are (see `bsc_cli_util`).
    if is_scoped_mutation(&args) {
        bsc_cli_util::require_write_scope("ui")?;
    }
    match args.first().map(String::as_str) {
        Some("kit") => {
            let kit_prog = format!("{prog} kit");
            match args.get(1).map(String::as_str) {
                // The kit-scoped animation authoring verbs (#2942): a kit owns its motion library.
                // Custom reads/writes over the KIT store; the two writers are already ui-scope gated by
                // `is_scoped_mutation` above (the `kit` prefix → args[1] check), BEFORE any store touch.
                Some("define-animation") if args.get(2).map(String::as_str) != Some("help") => {
                    cmd_kit_define_animation(&args[2..])
                }
                Some("list-animations") if args.get(2).map(String::as_str) != Some("help") => {
                    cmd_kit_list_animations(&args[2..])
                }
                Some("remove-animation") if args.get(2).map(String::as_str) != Some("help") => {
                    cmd_kit_remove_animation(&args[2..])
                }
                // #3163: the COMPILED-motion emitter — a custom read over the kit + component stores.
                Some("emit-motion-css") if args.get(2).map(String::as_str) != Some("help") => {
                    cmd_emit_motion_css(&args[2..])
                }
                Some(v @ ("define-animation" | "list-animations" | "remove-animation" | "emit-motion-css")) => {
                    print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(&kit_prog, TAGLINE, KIT_COMMANDS, v));
                    Ok(())
                }
                // `kit set` is intercepted here (#3164) so it stamps rev/updatedAt/updatedBy + honors
                // --by/--if-version — the shared store CLI's parser would reject those flags and never
                // stamps. `kit set help`, `kit list/get/remove` still fall through to the shared CLI
                // below (which fires the "kit" ui-touch on remove). Already ui-scope gated above.
                Some("set") if args.get(2).map(String::as_str) != Some("help") => {
                    cmd_set(&args[2..], open_kit_store, warn_kit_axes, "kit")
                }
                // #3725: permanently remove a packaged builtin KIT (its shell survives a plain `kit
                // remove`, re-seeded on hydrate). ui-scope gated above (the `kit` prefix → args[1] check).
                Some("suppress") if args.get(2).map(String::as_str) != Some("help") => {
                    cmd_suppress(&args[2..], open_kit_store, "kit")
                }
                Some("unsuppress") if args.get(2).map(String::as_str) != Some("help") => {
                    cmd_unsuppress(&args[2..], open_kit_store, "kit")
                }
                Some(v @ ("suppress" | "unsuppress")) => {
                    print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(&kit_prog, TAGLINE, KIT_COMMANDS, v));
                    Ok(())
                }
                // Emit a `ui-touch` for the Design Studio's live-focus (#2525) after each kit set/remove
                // write lands — WITH the "kit" collection context (bsc-json-store has none). A no-op for
                // read verbs (the hook only fires inside set/remove) and for non-designer sessions.
                _ => bsc_json_store::cli::run_hooked_validated(
                    args.into_iter().skip(1).collect(),
                    &kit_prog,
                    &KIT_SPEC,
                    Some(&|id: &str| bsc_util::emit_ui_activity("kit", id)),
                    // Non-blocking nudge (#3040): a kit with no tech/style buckets to "other/other".
                    Some(&warn_kit_axes),
                ),
            }
        }
        // `eslint-preset` is a custom read (store → eslint config), not a CRUD verb, so it's handled
        // here before delegating to the shared store CLI.
        Some("eslint-preset") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "eslint-preset"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_eslint_preset(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        // `usage` is the consumer index (kit_usage) — a flat edge store, not a per-record CRUD (#2277).
        Some("usage") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "usage"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_usage(&args[1..], prog)
            }
        }
        // `shapes` is the data-shape picker (#2475): the vocabulary + each shape's ideal components,
        // computed from the stored `shapes` fields — a custom read, so it's handled here.
        Some("shapes") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "shapes"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_shapes(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        // `backing` (#4193) — which record backs a file, and the landing gate built on it.
        Some("backing") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "backing"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_backing(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        // `library` (bsc request #118) — verify a `doctor` @bsc/algorithms/<name> finding from inside
        // the designer's own `bsc ui` confinement, never touching the librarian's `bsc graph` surface.
        Some("library") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "library"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_library(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        // `doctor` (#2678) is a custom read — the graph-health analyzer over the component store.
        Some("doctor") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "doctor"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_doctor(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        // `dupes` / `similar` (#3544) — the fuzzy DEDUP surface over the whole library (name + contract
        // distance), the LLM-native "what should I merge?" / "does this already exist?" reads. Propose-only.
        // `test` (component-records-need-a-test-runner) — the components twin of `bsc graph test`.
        // 131 records already carry paired tests and nothing ran any of them.
        Some("test") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "test"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_component_test(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        Some("dupes") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "dupes"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_dupes(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        Some("similar") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "similar"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_similar(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        // `usage-scan` (#3888) — the `used` producer. A read unless `--apply`, which `is_scoped_mutation`
        // gates like every other write.
        Some("usage-scan") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "usage-scan"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_usage_scan(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        // `used-by` (#3584) — the graph-usage read (composes-inverse); a READ, never scope-gated.
        Some("crossgraph") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "crossgraph"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_crossgraph(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        Some("used-by") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "used-by"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_used_by(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        // `refs` (#113) — literal srcText cross-references to a component's NAME; a READ, never scope-gated.
        Some("refs") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "refs"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_refs(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        Some("exports") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "exports"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_exports(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        Some("pattern") => cmd_pattern(&args[1..], prog),
        Some("patterns") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "patterns"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_patterns(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        // The component-animation authoring verbs (#2869): motion as DATA on a component record. Custom
        // reads/writes over the component store (validate → upsert into `animations`), so they're
        // handled here rather than via the shared verbatim-JSON store CLI. The two writers are already
        // ui-scope gated by `is_scoped_mutation` above, BEFORE any store is touched.
        Some("define-animation") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "define-animation"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_define_animation(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        Some("list-animations") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "list-animations"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_list_animations(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        Some("remove-animation") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "remove-animation"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_remove_animation(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        // `preview-props` (#3165) — the preview harness's schema-derived sample props for <id>, per
        // data-state. A custom read (pure sampler in `crate::preview_props` mirrors the TS twin).
        Some("preview-props") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "preview-props"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_preview_props(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        // `scan-cache` — the preview sweep's durable memory. Like `preview-error` this is a diagnostic
        // /cache channel rather than a store mutation, so it is intentionally NOT ui-scope gated: it can
        // only ever save the app work, never change what a component IS.
        Some("scan-cache") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "scan-cache"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_scan_cache(&args[1..], prog)
            }
        }
        // `preview-errors` (#3165) — tail the captured preview runtime errors (read).
        Some("preview-errors") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "preview-errors"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_preview_errors(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        // `preview-error <id>` (#3165) — the frontend's append path (message on stdin). A diagnostic
        // append, NOT a store mutation, so it is intentionally NOT ui-scope gated.
        Some("preview-error") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "preview-error"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_preview_error(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        // The granular writes (#3162): a one-field edit that skips the whole-record stdin round-trip.
        // `set-src` (replace only `srcText`, through the same #2928 syntax gate) and `patch` (set one
        // field by JSON pointer) are ui-scope MUTATIONS — each honors the runtime `ui` write-scope
        // BEFORE touching stdin/the store (in its own fn, like `doctor --fix`), and stamps the write
        // (#3164) via the shared `stamped_set` boundary.
        Some("set-src") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "set-src"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_set_src(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        Some("patch") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "patch"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_patch(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        // `refolder` (#3579) re-derives every stored component's `folder` as a nested path from its
        // `src`, and carries a srcless record's legacy value across — a ui-scope MUTATION (gated above),
        // so a kit organizes like a completed project's folders.
        //
        // The `regroup` ALIAS IS RETIRED (finish-the-4107-group-to-folder-shim). It was kept because the
        // old name was "named in prose the designer/librarian may have memorised" — but the concept it
        // named is gone from the store now, and an alias that outlives its field is how two names for
        // one thing stay alive indefinitely. `unknown_command` names the near miss, so a session that
        // types the old verb is told the new one rather than left guessing.
        Some("refolder") if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) != Some("help") => cmd_refolder(&args[1..]),
        Some("features") if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) != Some("help") => cmd_features(&args[1..]),
        Some("refolder") => {
            print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "refolder"));
            Ok(())
        }
        // `export`/`import` (#3606) — components-as-data round-trip: dump the store to a folder tree under
        // `data/` and load it back. `export` is a read; `import` is a ui-scope MUTATION (gated above).
        Some("export") if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) != Some("help") => cmd_export(&args[1..]),
        Some("parity") if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) != Some("help") => cmd_parity(&args[1..]),
        Some("sync-seed") if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) != Some("help") => cmd_sync_seed(&args[1..]),
        Some("promote") if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) != Some("help") => cmd_promote(&args[1..]),
        Some("import") if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) != Some("help") => cmd_import(&args[1..]),
        Some(v @ ("export" | "import" | "sync-seed" | "promote")) => {
            print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, v));
            Ok(())
        }
        // `get --field <json-pointer>` (#3162, ONE field), `get … --out <name>` (#3713, spill to the
        // scratch dir), OR `get … --kit <kitId>` (#3729, disambiguate) — all intercepted here (the shared
        // store CLI rejects the extra flags), and handled by `cmd_get` (which also emits the whole-record
        // `ui-focus` the plain path does). A plain `get <id>` (incl. the whole-record `--raw`, #3166) still
        // delegates unchanged. A read verb.
        Some("get") if args.iter().any(|a| a == "--field" || a == "--out" || a == "--kit") => cmd_get(&args[1..]),
        // `log` (#3164) is a custom read — the record's history stamp (rev/updatedAt/updatedBy).
        Some("log") => {
            if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("help") {
                print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "log"));
                Ok(())
            } else {
                cmd_log(&args[1..])
            }
        }
        // `set` (#3164) is intercepted here — it stamps rev/updatedAt/updatedBy + honors --by/--if-version
        // (the shared store CLI never stamps and its parser rejects those flags). `set help` still prints
        // the doc. The scope gate above already refused a read-scoped session before we got here.
        Some("set") if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) != Some("help") => {
            cmd_set(&args[1..], open_component_store, validate_component_batch, "component")
        }
        Some("set") => {
            print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "set"));
            Ok(())
        }
        // `revert` — restore `srcText` from the retained history. The recovery path a record with no
        // packaged seed had no way to reach. The scope gate above already refused a read-scoped session.
        Some("revert") if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) != Some("help") => cmd_revert(&args[1..]),
        Some("revert") => {
            print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "revert"));
            Ok(())
        }
        // `rename` (#3576) — id-stable rename that sweeps the NAME-keyed composes/rules references across
        // the kit + stamps history. The scope gate above already refused a read-scoped session.
        Some("rename") if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) != Some("help") => cmd_rename(&args[1..]),
        Some("rename") => {
            print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "rename"));
            Ok(())
        }
        // `merge` (#3592) — fold a duplicate INTO a survivor, repointing the NAME-keyed composes/rules
        // references then removing it. The ACT step of the optimize loop. Scope gate above applies.
        Some("merge") if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) != Some("help") => cmd_merge(&args[1..]),
        Some("merge") => {
            print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "merge"));
            Ok(())
        }
        // `suppress`/`unsuppress` (#3725) — permanently remove a packaged builtin component (a plain
        // `remove` re-seeds on the next hydrate). Scope gate above applies.
        Some("suppress") if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) != Some("help") => {
            cmd_suppress(&args[1..], open_component_store, "component")
        }
        Some("unsuppress") if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) != Some("help") => {
            cmd_unsuppress(&args[1..], open_component_store, "component")
        }
        Some(v @ ("suppress" | "unsuppress")) => {
            print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, v));
            Ok(())
        }
        // `list --shape <shape>` (#2475) filters to one shape's ideal components — intercepted here
        // (the shared store CLI rejects unknown flags); a plain `list` still delegates unchanged.
        Some("list") if args.iter().any(|a| a == "--shape") => cmd_list_shape(&args[1..]),
        // #4158 (designer request #44): `list --kit <id>` filters to ONE kit. Intercepted here for the
        // same reason `--shape` is — the shared store CLI rejects unknown flags — and a plain `list`
        // still delegates unchanged. Without it, comparing two kits' membership meant a full-store dump
        // (tens of KB) and grepping the auto-persisted tool-output file for `kitId`.
        Some("list") if args.iter().any(|a| a == "--kit") => cmd_list_kit(&args[1..]),
        Some("list") if args.iter().any(|a| a == "--feature") => cmd_list_feature(&args[1..]),
        // `list --tags a,b` (`the-graphs-cannot-be-searched-by-the-axes-they-store`) — the SUBJECT
        // axis, intercepted for the same reason `--shape`/`--kit`/`--feature` are: the shared store
        // CLI rejects unknown flags. `feature` says who may WRITE a record; `tags` says what it is
        // ABOUT, and a worker looking for what it NEEDS is asking the second question.
        Some("list") if args.iter().any(|a| a == "--tags") => cmd_list_tags(&args[1..]),
        // `tags` — the vocabulary, the same discover-then-search pair `features` already forms with
        // `list --feature`. A tag cannot be searched for until it can be seen.
        Some("tags") if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) != Some("help") => cmd_tags(&args[1..]),
        // A plain `get <id>` (read) FOCUSES that component in the Design Studio preview (#3545) — a
        // `ui-focus`, so the preview follows Claude's working focus as it INSPECTS each node, not only
        // when it writes one. Distinct from the write `ui-touch`: a read triggers NO library re-hydrate.
        // `get --field`/`get help` fall through unchanged (the id guard excludes a flag or `help`).
        // #doctor-reads-the-runtime: `get <id> --metrics` JOINS the runtime attestations at read time.
        // Intercepted here for the same reason `--shape` and `--kit` are — the shared store CLI rejects
        // unknown flags. Deliberately a JOIN and not a field ON the record: writing metrics there would
        // make every boot a record write (filling `bsc ui revert` history with timing noise instead of
        // authorship), vendor a second copy of a constantly-changing number — the drift #4191 forbids for
        // algorithm bodies — and ship one machine's numbers to another inside a seed or a snapshot.
        // `feature rename <from> <to> [--under <folder-prefix>] [--apply]` — the algorithms twin
        // (`the-graph-vocabulary-is-the-plans`). `features` DERIVES from the folder, which is what
        // produced the divergence in the first place, and never overwrites a feature already set — so
        // it cannot perform a reconcile. This can.
        Some("feature") if args.get(1).map(String::as_str) == Some("rename") => cmd_feature_rename(&args[2..]),
        // A plain `get <id>` (read) FOCUSES that component in the Design Studio preview (#3545) — a
        // `ui-focus`, so the preview follows Claude's working focus as it INSPECTS each node, not only
        // when it writes one. Distinct from the write `ui-touch`: a read triggers NO library re-hydrate.
        // `get --field`/`get help` fall through unchanged (the id guard excludes a flag or `help`).
        // #doctor-reads-the-runtime: `get <id> --metrics` JOINS the runtime attestations at read time.
        // Intercepted here for the same reason `--shape` and `--kit` are — the shared store CLI rejects
        // unknown flags. Deliberately a JOIN and not a field ON the record: writing metrics there would
        // make every boot a record write (filling `bsc ui revert` history with timing noise instead of
        // authorship), vendor a second copy of a constantly-changing number — the drift #4191 forbids for
        // algorithm bodies — and ship one machine's numbers to another inside a seed or a snapshot.
        Some("get") if args.iter().any(|a| a == "--metrics") => cmd_get_metrics(&args[1..]),
        Some("get") if args.get(1).is_some_and(|a| !a.starts_with('-') && a != "help") => {
            // #91: resolve the handle to a real id BEFORE delegating, so `get <Name>` works and a miss is
            // an ERROR rather than a bare `null` on stdout. The shared store CLI cannot do this — it backs
            // every `bsc <store> get` and knows nothing about a `name` field — so the rewrite happens here
            // and the delegate still prints the stored bytes verbatim (the #3166 `--raw` contract).
            let dir = args.iter().position(|a| a == "--dir").and_then(|i| args.get(i + 1)).cloned();
            let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
            let id = resolve_component_handle(&store, &args[1])?;
            let mut args = args;
            args[1] = id.clone();
            emit_component_activity(&store, false, &id);
            bsc_json_store::cli::run_hooked_validated(
                args,
                prog,
                &COMPONENT_SPEC,
                // The kit is read AFTER the write lands, so a record whose kit this call just set (or
                // changed) reports its NEW kit — which is the one the Studio should follow.
                Some(&|id: &str| emit_component_activity(&store, true, id)),
                Some(&validate_component_batch),
            )
        }
        // The COMPONENT collection's list/get/remove (set is intercepted above, #3164). Fire the
        // live-focus `ui-touch` (#2525) after a component remove write lands, with the "component"
        // collection context.
        _ => bsc_json_store::cli::run_hooked_validated(
            args,
            prog,
            &COMPONENT_SPEC,
            Some(&|id: &str| bsc_util::emit_ui_activity("component", id)),
            Some(&validate_component_batch),
        ),
    }
}

// ── record history / attribution / optimistic concurrency (#3164) ────────────────────────────────
//
// Every `bsc ui` write STAMPS provenance so a background rewrite can't silently clobber a record with
// no trace: `rev` (auto-bumped integer), `updatedAt` (ISO-8601 UTC), `updatedBy` (writer tag). The
// stores stay verbatim JSON, so the stamping lives here (the crate owning the record shape), on the
// write boundary shared by `set`, the animation authors, and doctor `--fix` — see [`crate::record`].

/// The record's CURRENT stored `rev` (0 when absent or never stamped — the backward-compat contract),
/// read straight from the store so a stamp/version-check always compares against what's on disk.
/// `bsc ui get <id> --metrics` — the record, plus what the RUNNING app observed of it.
///
/// `metrics` is `null` when nothing has been measured rather than a zeroed object: zeros would read as
/// "this ran nowhere and cost nothing", which is a claim the store cannot support. Null says it has
/// nothing to say, which is the same honesty `bsc runtime summary` leads with.
fn cmd_get_metrics(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let handle = args
        .iter()
        .find(|a| !a.starts_with('-'))
        .ok_or("usage: bsc ui get <id> --metrics")?;
    let dir = args.iter().position(|a| a == "--dir").and_then(|i| args.get(i + 1)).cloned();
    let pretty = args.iter().any(|a| a == "--pretty");
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let id = resolve_component_handle(&store, handle)?;
    let raw = store.get(&id).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?.ok_or_else(|| format!("no component '{id}'"))?;
    let mut record: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

    let metrics = bsc_runtime::default_db_path()
        .and_then(|path| bsc_runtime::Store::open(&path).ok())
        .and_then(|s| s.list(&bsc_runtime::Filter::default()).ok())
        .map(|rows| bsc_runtime::doctor::metrics_for(&rows, &id))
        .filter(|m| m.sessions > 0)
        .and_then(|m| serde_json::to_value(m).ok())
        .unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null);
    if let Some(obj) = record.as_object_mut() {
        obj.insert("metrics".into(), metrics);
    }
    let out = if pretty {
        serde_json::to_string_pretty(&record)
    } else {
        serde_json::to_string(&record)
    };
    println!("{}", out.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

#[cfg(test)]
fn current_rev(store: &bsc_json_store::Store, id: &str) -> Result<i64, String> {
    Ok(crate::record::read_rev(&current_record(store, id)?))
}

/// Emit a component live-focus event carrying the record's KIT (#live-focus-is-kit-filtered).
///
/// The Design Studio filters its `.working` pulse, its auto-pan and its Inspector subject by the
/// SELECTED kit, so a touch it cannot place in a kit is discarded. It can resolve the kit from its own
/// hydrated copy for anything it already loaded — but that misses exactly the interesting case, a
/// record written seconds ago, so the kit rides the event instead.
///
/// Reads the stored record to find `kitId`. Best-effort in the same spirit as the emit itself: a miss
/// (absent record, unreadable store, no `kitId`) degrades to the historical 5-column line rather than
/// failing, because activity signalling must never break a store mutation.
fn emit_component_activity(store: &bsc_json_store::Store, kind_is_write: bool, id: &str) {
    let kit = current_record(store, id)
        .ok()
        .and_then(|v| v.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).map(str::to_string))
        .unwrap_or_default();
    if kind_is_write {
        bsc_util::emit_ui_activity_in("component", id, &kit);
    } else {
        bsc_util::emit_ui_focus_in("component", id, &kit);
    }
}

/// The record's CURRENT stored JSON (`Value::Null` when absent), so a write can carry its change history
/// forward and diff what changed (#3568). Malformed stored JSON reads as absent (fail-safe: the write
/// still lands, just starting a fresh history rather than erroring on a corrupt row).
fn current_record(store: &bsc_json_store::Store, id: &str) -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> {
    Ok(store.get(id)?.and_then(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&j).ok()).unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null))
}

/// Stamp `value` for a write (bump `rev`, set `updatedAt` + `updatedBy`), then upsert it by `id`. The
/// single write boundary EVERY non-`set` writer funnels through (the animation authors, doctor `--fix`
/// repoints), so they all get a consistent rev bump + attribution; `writer` is the resolved tag (see
/// [`crate::record::resolve_writer`]).
fn stamped_set(
    store: &bsc_json_store::Store,
    id: &str,
    mut value: serde_json::Value,
    writer: &str,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let prior = current_record(store, id)?;
    crate::record::stamp_with_history(&mut value, &prior, writer, &crate::record::now_iso(), None);
    store.set(id, &serde_json::to_string(&value).map_err(|e| format!("set: {e}"))?)
}

/// Read the `set` payload — a single record object OR an array of them — into a `Vec`.
///
/// Two channels, identical semantics (#3373): stdin, or `--file <bare-name>` resolved inside the
/// session's sealed `$BSC_SCRATCH` dir. The file form exists because a heredoc cannot be allow-listed
/// (newlines are command separators), which left a restricted studio session unable to author at all.
/// `bsc_cli_util::read_payload` owns the resolution + the traversal defence.
fn read_set_items(noun: &str, file: Option<&str>) -> Result<Vec<serde_json::Value>, String> {
    let raw = bsc_cli_util::read_payload(file)?;
    let where_ = if file.is_some() { "in --file" } else { "on stdin" };
    let value: serde_json::Value =
        serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|e| format!("{noun} JSON {where_} is invalid: {e}"))?;
    Ok(match value {
        serde_json::Value::Array(items) => items,
        other => vec![other],
    })
}

/// How a `set` combines the incoming record with the stored one (#4197).
///
/// The DEFAULT is a MERGE ([`crate::record::merge_over`]): unsupplied fields are preserved, and removal is
/// explicit (`--clear a,b`, or a JSON `null` in the payload). That mirrors `bsc graph impl set` after
/// #4154 — the two stores answer a partial write identically, which is the whole point: a worker told to
/// "edit the RECORD, then re-emit" (#4193) must not lose the fields its edit never mentioned, and for a
/// page whose source file is gone (`fleetpage`, since #3636) the record is the only copy.
///
/// `replace` (`--replace`) restores the verbatim whole-record write, which three callers genuinely need:
/// the app's `pushComponent`/`pushKit` bridge, `bsc ui import`, and — the load-bearing one —
/// `reconcileSeed`'s seed-authoritative path (#3723), which forces a diverged builtin back onto its seed
/// copy. Under a merge that push could never converge: a store-only field would survive every reset, so
/// the record's content hash would stay off the seed's and the reconcile would re-fire forever.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
struct WritePlan<'a> {
    replace: bool,
    clear: &'a [String],
}

/// The warning for a write that removes a field WITHOUT BEING ASKED TO (#4197) — `None` for every
/// merging write (which removes only what `--clear`/a `null` names) and for every `--replace` that
/// restates the whole record, so the common paths stay silent and the warning keeps its meaning.
///
/// It exists for the one remaining way to lose data silently: `--replace` with a partial payload. An
/// explicitly cleared field is NOT reported — the caller asked for it, and a warning about a deletion you
/// just requested is the noise that trains people to ignore the real one (the removal is still recorded
/// in the history's `dropped`, so `bsc ui log` shows it either way).
///
/// PURE so the decision is under test rather than tangled in the write loop; the caller prints it. It
/// names each field, because "this write is destructive" without a list is not actionable — the reader
/// needs to know whether it dropped `srcText` or a `folder` tag.
fn destructive_write_warning(
    id: &str,
    noun: &str,
    prior: &serde_json::Value,
    effective: &serde_json::Value,
    clear: &[String],
) -> Option<String> {
    let dropped: Vec<String> = crate::record::dropped_fields(prior, effective)
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|f| !clear.iter().any(|c| c == f))
        .collect();
    if dropped.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    Some(format!(
        "warning: this write REMOVES {} field(s) from {noun} '{id}': {}. \
         --replace writes the record VERBATIM — drop --replace to MERGE (unsupplied fields are kept), \
         re-send them, or `bsc ui log {id}` to see what was there.",
        dropped.len(),
        dropped.join(", "),
    ))
}

/// The merging, stamped, version-aware `set` core (#3164/#4197): for each item, read the current stored
/// record, enforce `--if-version` (reject a stale overwrite), combine it with the stored one per `plan`
/// (a MERGE unless `--replace`), stamp (`rev+1` + `updatedAt` + `updatedBy`), upsert, and fire the
/// ui-touch hook. Returns the written ids in input order. Split out of [`cmd_set`] so the merge +
/// concurrency + stamping logic is unit-testable without a drivable stdin. `--if-version` takes a
/// SINGLE record (a lone version number is meaningless across a batch).
/// Apply a relink plan's writes (#4223) — a MERGING, stamped write of just `src`/`folder`.
///
/// Exported because the relink verb lives in `bsc-ui` (it needs the harvest, which sits a crate above
/// this one), while the write must still go through the same stamped path every other component write
/// uses — so a re-point bumps `rev`, records attribution, and lands in `bsc ui log` like any edit.
pub fn apply_relink(store: &bsc_json_store::Store, writes: &[serde_json::Value]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(None);
    set_stamped(store, writes, None, &writer, "component", Some("relink: re-point a stale src"),
                WritePlan { replace: false, clear: &[] })?;
    Ok(())
}

/// Apply a module LIFT's write — a MERGING, stamped write, so a lift bumps `rev`, records attribution
/// and lands in `bsc ui log` like any other edit.
///
/// Exported for the same reason [`apply_relink`] is: `bsc ui lift` lives in `bsc-ui` (it needs the
/// harvest, which sits a crate above this one), while the write must still go through the one stamped
/// path every component write uses.
pub fn apply_lift(
    store: &bsc_json_store::Store,
    writes: &[serde_json::Value],
    by: Option<&str>,
    note: &str,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(by);
    set_stamped(store, writes, None, &writer, "component", Some(note),
                WritePlan { replace: false, clear: &[] })?;
    Ok(())
}

/// Apply a per-record `tests` write (#166) — a MERGING, stamped write of just `tests`, so `bsc ui tests
/// set` can pair ONE record without a whole-tree `harvest` re-mirroring every other paired record (and
/// dragging along whatever a stale re-read of an UNRELATED record happened to hold — the `terminalhost`
/// `provides` loss #166 was filed against: a re-emitted record carried an explicit `null` for a field a
/// concurrent write had since given a real value, and `merge_over` honours an explicit `null` as
/// "remove this", #4197).
///
/// Exported for the same reason [`apply_relink`] is: the verb's file read lives in `bsc-ui` (a crate
/// above this one), while the write must still go through the same stamped path every other component
/// write uses — so a per-test pairing bumps `rev`, records attribution, and lands in `bsc ui log` like
/// any edit. `Err` when `id` names no existing record: this PAIRS a record, it does not create one.
pub fn apply_tests_set(
    store: &bsc_json_store::Store,
    id: &str,
    tests: serde_json::Value,
    by: Option<&str>,
    note: Option<&str>,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    if current_record(store, id)?.is_null() {
        return Err(format!(
            "no component with id '{id}' — `tests set` pairs an EXISTING record, it does not create \
             one; check the id with `bsc ui get {id}`, or author the record first with `bsc ui set`"
        ));
    }
    let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(by);
    set_stamped(
        store,
        &[serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "tests": tests })],
        None,
        &writer,
        "component",
        Some(note.unwrap_or("tests set: pair one record's colocated test")),
        WritePlan { replace: false, clear: &[] },
    )?;
    Ok(())
}

fn set_stamped(
    store: &bsc_json_store::Store,
    items: &[serde_json::Value],
    if_version: Option<i64>,
    writer: &str,
    noun: &str,
    note: Option<&str>,
    plan: WritePlan<'_>,
) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
    if if_version.is_some() && items.len() != 1 {
        return Err(format!(
            "--if-version guards a single {noun} write, but stdin held {} records — send exactly one record when using optimistic concurrency",
            items.len()
        ));
    }
    let now = crate::record::now_iso();
    let mut ids = Vec::new();
    for item in items {
        let id = bsc_json_store::cli::id_of(item, noun)?;
        let prior = current_record(store, &id)?;
        // WHICH records this session may write (`a-worker-writes-only-its-own-feature`).
        //
        // Here rather than at the verb dispatch, because THIS is the funnel: `set` takes its records
        // from stdin, so the id is not in argv and a dispatch-level guard could not see it. Every
        // component write lands here, so a verb added later is confined without remembering to be.
        //
        // The PRIOR record's feature governs. A payload carrying `"feature": "mine"` against a
        // component owned by `core` is the move confinement exists to stop, and reading the submitted
        // value would wave it through — the record would simply change hands. A record that does not
        // exist yet is judged on what it claims, so a new one cannot slip in unowned.
        if bsc_cli_util::session_features().is_some() {
            // A missing record reads as `Value::Null`, whose `get` is None — so the fallback to the
            // SUBMITTED feature is the new-record case, expressed without a second existence check.
            let owner = prior
                .get("feature")
                .or_else(|| item.get("feature"))
                .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)
                .unwrap_or_default()
                .to_string();
            bsc_cli_util::require_feature_write(&id, &owner)?;
        }
        let prior_rev = crate::record::read_rev(&prior);
        if let Some(n) = if_version {
            if prior_rev != n {
                return Err(format!(
                    "version conflict on {noun} '{id}': its current rev is {prior_rev}, not {n} — it changed since you read it. Re-read (`bsc ui log {id}`) and retry."
                ));
            }
        }
        // #4197: a `set` MERGES over the stored record, so a write that restates only `srcText` keeps the
        // kit, role, edges and provenance it never mentioned — the same semantics #4154 gave
        // `bsc graph impl set`. `--replace` opts back into the verbatim whole-record write the app bridge
        // and the seed reconcile need; only that path can still delete by omission, and it says so.
        let mut stamped =
            if plan.replace { item.clone() } else { crate::record::merge_over(&prior, item, plan.clear) };
        if let Some(msg) = destructive_write_warning(&id, noun, &prior, &stamped, plan.clear) {
            eprintln!("{msg}");
        }
        crate::record::stamp_with_history(&mut stamped, &prior, writer, &now, note);
        store.set(&id, &serde_json::to_string(&stamped).map_err(|e| format!("set: {e}"))?)?;
        bsc_util::emit_ui_activity(noun, &id);
        // #43: editing a COMPONENT invalidates the last preview render — clear any stale `render-error` so
        // `bsc ui doctor` doesn't keep reporting the pre-edit throw for source that just changed. Best-effort
        // (a diagnostic side-effect must never fail the write); a no-op unless this id currently has an error.
        if noun == "component" {
            let _ = crate::preview_errors::clear(&id);
        }
        ids.push(id);
    }
    Ok(ids)
}

/// `set [--by <tag>] [--note <text>] [--if-version <n>] [--clear a,b] [--replace] [--dir D] [--pretty]`
/// (#3164/#3568/#4197) — the STAMPING upsert for a collection. Parses the ui-write flags, reads the
/// record(s) from stdin, runs the domain batch `validate` (the component srcText gate / the kit-axis
/// nudge), then MERGES + stamps + upserts each via [`set_stamped`], which also appends a change-history
/// entry (`--note` is its summary; `bsc ui log <id>` reads the log). Prints the written id(s). Shared by
/// the component and kit collections (`open` + `validate` + `noun` differ). Already ui-scope gated in
/// [`run`]. See [`WritePlan`] for the merge/`--replace` split.
fn cmd_set(
    args: &[String],
    open: fn(&Option<String>) -> Result<bsc_json_store::Store, String>,
    validate: fn(&[serde_json::Value]) -> Result<(), String>,
    noun: &'static str,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut pretty, mut by, mut if_version, mut file, mut note) =
        (None::<String>, false, None::<String>, None::<i64>, None::<String>, None::<String>);
    let (mut replace, mut clear) = (false, Vec::<String>::new());
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            // #4197: the write MERGES, so a value can no longer be removed by omitting it — removal is
            // explicit. Mirrors `bsc graph impl set --clear` (#4154) so the two stores read the same.
            "--clear" => {
                let raw = it.next().ok_or("--clear needs a comma-separated field list, e.g. --clear folder,src")?;
                clear.extend(raw.split(',').map(str::trim).filter(|f| !f.is_empty()).map(str::to_string));
            }
            // #4197: opt back into the verbatim whole-record write — for the app bridge, `bsc ui import`,
            // and `reconcileSeed`'s seed-authoritative reset, which a merge would stop from converging.
            "--replace" => replace = true,
            // #3849: store a record the write-time gate would REFUSE — the deliberate spec-only escape.
            // Carried in a process-global rather than a parameter because `validate` is a shared `fn`
            // pointer used by every store's `cmd_set`; threading a flag through would change that
            // signature for stores that have no gate to bypass. One-shot CLI process, set once here,
            // read once in `validate_component_batch`.
            "--force" => FORCE_WRITE.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
            // #3373: read the payload from a BARE-NAMED file in $BSC_SCRATCH instead of stdin, so a
            // restricted session can author multi-line records at all (a heredoc cannot be allow-listed
            // — newlines are command separators). Resolution + the traversal defence live in bsc-cli-util.
            "--file" => file = it.next().cloned(),
            "--by" => by = it.next().cloned(),
            // #3568: a human-readable summary of WHY this write happened, recorded in the change history.
            "--note" => note = it.next().cloned(),
            "--if-version" => {
                let raw = it.next().ok_or("--if-version needs an integer revision (see `bsc ui log <id>`)")?;
                if_version = Some(
                    raw.parse::<i64>()
                        .map_err(|_| format!("--if-version '{raw}' is not an integer"))?,
                );
            }
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            other => {
                return Err(format!(
                    "unexpected argument '{other}' — `set` reads the record(s) from stdin, or from                      --file <name> in $BSC_SCRATCH"
                ))
            }
        }
    }
    // The two are contradictory: `--replace` writes the payload verbatim, so there is nothing left for
    // `--clear` to remove. Refusing beats silently honouring one of them.
    if replace && !clear.is_empty() {
        return Err(
            "--clear and --replace contradict each other: --replace writes the record VERBATIM (a field \
             absent from the payload is already gone), while --clear removes fields from a MERGE. Pick one."
                .to_string(),
        );
    }
    let items = read_set_items(noun, file.as_deref())?;
    let store = open(&dir)?;
    // VALIDATE WHAT WILL BE STORED, not what was typed (#3849's hole).
    //
    // A write has MERGED by default since #4197, so a payload carries only the fields being changed —
    // `{"id":"githubpage","srcText":"…"}` is the ordinary shape. Validating the raw payload therefore
    // judged a record by fields it never restated: `validate_component_batch` reads `role` to decide
    // whether the page gate applies, so EVERY partial write slipped past it and a `role: page` record
    // that cannot render could be stored by any of them — the exact thing #3849 exists to prevent. It
    // also emitted the preview-oracle warning at a page, which is the visible half of the same bug and
    // how this was noticed.
    //
    // Under `--replace` the payload IS the record, so there is nothing to merge and the raw items are
    // already what will be stored.
    let validated: Vec<serde_json::Value> = if replace {
        items.clone()
    } else {
        items
            .iter()
            .map(|item| {
                let id = item.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
                match store.get(id) {
                    Ok(Some(raw)) => serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&raw)
                        .map(|prior| crate::record::merge_over(&prior, item, &clear))
                        .unwrap_or_else(|_| item.clone()),
                    // Unknown id (a create) or an unreadable row — the payload is the whole record.
                    _ => item.clone(),
                }
            })
            .collect()
    };
    validate(&validated)?;
    // #3729: a component store is keyed by id ALONE — writing an id that already lives under a DIFFERENT
    // kit silently OVERWRITES it. Warn (never reject) so a promote-over-a-builtin clobber is visible.
    if noun == "component" {
        warn_cross_kit_collision(&store, &items);
        // Deliberately over `items`, not `validated`: this warns the AUTHOR about source they just
        // wrote, at the moment they can still choose differently. A partial write that never restates
        // `srcText` gets no warning — re-reporting an import the caller did not touch is noise, and
        // noise is what made 53 GraphHost findings unreadable.
        warn_unresolvable_imports(&store, &items);
    }
    let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(by.as_deref());
    let plan = WritePlan { replace, clear: &clear };
    let ids = set_stamped(&store, &items, if_version, &writer, noun, note.as_deref(), plan)?;
    let json = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&ids) } else { serde_json::to_string(&ids) };
    println!("{}", json.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// The cross-kit id-overwrite warnings for a `set` batch (#3729) — PURE so the decision is under test;
/// the CLI prints each to stderr via [`warn_cross_kit_collision`]. The component store is keyed by id
/// ALONE (not by `(kit, id)`), so writing `fleetpage` under kit `harvested` SILENTLY OVERWRITES a
/// `fleetpage` already stored under `base-studio-code` — that bit a designer promoting a harvested page
/// over a builtin of the same name (they believed the two coexisted). One message per colliding id.
fn cross_kit_collision_warnings(store: &bsc_json_store::Store, items: &[serde_json::Value]) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for item in items {
        let (Some(id), Some(new_kit)) = (
            item.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str),
            item.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str),
        ) else {
            continue;
        };
        let prior = current_record(store, id).unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null);
        let prior_kit = prior.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
        if !prior_kit.is_empty() && prior_kit != new_kit {
            out.push(format!(
                "warning: component '{id}' already exists under kit '{prior_kit}' — this write (kit '{new_kit}') \
                 OVERWRITES it, because the store is keyed by id, NOT by (kit, id). Rename one of them if you \
                 meant to keep both, or ignore this if the re-home is intended."
            ));
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Print each [`cross_kit_collision_warnings`] message to stderr. Non-blocking (never rejects) — a
/// deliberate re-home is legitimate and the write still lands.
fn warn_cross_kit_collision(store: &bsc_json_store::Store, items: &[serde_json::Value]) {
    for w in cross_kit_collision_warnings(store, items) {
        eprintln!("{w}");
    }
}

/// Every `@/components/<id>` specifier `src` imports, in source order, deduped.
///
/// A deliberately narrow scan: only this ONE specifier shape is checked, because it is the only
/// internal form whose resolvability is decidable entirely inside the store. The preview also accepts
/// PLATFORM modules (`@/shared/ui/…`, `@/store`) — the declared boundary the bundler stubs — and those
/// are enumerated in TypeScript; duplicating that list here would create two copies to keep in sync,
/// and a stale copy would warn about imports that are perfectly fine.
fn component_specifiers(src: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut out: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for (i, _) in src.match_indices("@/components/") {
        // Bounded by the quote that opened the specifier — a specifier is a string literal, so the
        // closing quote is the terminator regardless of which quote style the author used.
        let rest = &src[i..];
        let end = rest.find(['"', '\'', '`']).unwrap_or(rest.len());
        let spec = rest[..end].trim_end();
        if spec.len() > "@/components/".len() && !out.iter().any(|s| s == spec) {
            out.push(spec.to_string());
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Which `@/components/…` specifiers in a `set` batch resolve to NOTHING (#73, designer request).
///
/// `bsc ui set` only syntax-checks `srcText`, so a write naming a component that publishes no such
/// specifier is accepted and the break surfaces two tool-calls later at `bsc navigate` time — after
/// which the usual recovery is to inline the widget and lose the composition. Five components were
/// reverted that way in one session.
///
/// Resolution mirrors the preview resolver (`componentPreview.ts`, `siblingIndex` + its internal-spec
/// gate): a specifier resolves when some record `provides` it EXACTLY, or when some record's `src`
/// minus extension equals the specifier's path. Anything else makes the importer unbuildable — the
/// build genuinely refuses rather than quietly substituting a stub.
///
/// WARNS, never rejects: 30 of the 94 `@/components/` imports already in the store resolve to nothing,
/// and a hard refusal would make those records unsaveable on their next edit. The point is to tell the
/// author at the moment they can still choose differently, not to relitigate what is already stored.
fn unresolvable_component_imports(
    store: &bsc_json_store::Store,
    items: &[serde_json::Value],
) -> Vec<String> {
    let published = published_specifiers(store, items);
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for item in items {
        let Some(id) = item.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) else { continue };
        let src = item.get("srcText").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
        let missing: Vec<String> = component_specifiers(src)
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|s| !published.contains(s))
            .collect();
        if missing.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let list = missing.join(", ");
        let target = missing[0].trim_start_matches("@/components/");
        // The suggested command is the MERGE write (#4197) — `set` reads its record from stdin and has
        // no `--provides` flag, so the obvious-looking `bsc ui set <id> --provides <spec>` is rejected
        // twice over (unknown flag, unexpected positional). Naming a command that errors would make
        // this warning worse than silence, so the exact form here is covered by a test.
        out.push(format!(
            "warning: '{id}' imports {list} — no record publishes {}, so the preview will refuse to \
             build it (an unresolvable internal import is not stubbed). Fix by making the target \
             publish the specifier: echo '{{\"id\":\"{target}\",\"provides\":\"{}\"}}' | bsc ui set",
            if missing.len() == 1 { "that specifier" } else { "those specifiers" },
            missing[0],
        ));
    }
    out
}

/// The `@/components/…` specifiers the store resolves — every record's `provides`, plus the implied
/// specifier for a record whose `src` (minus extension) is itself a `components/<id>` path. `items` is
/// folded in so a batch that introduces BOTH the importer and its target validates as a unit rather
/// than warning about a specifier the same write is publishing.
fn published_specifiers(
    store: &bsc_json_store::Store,
    items: &[serde_json::Value],
) -> std::collections::HashSet<String> {
    let stored = store.list();
    let parsed = stored.iter().filter_map(|r| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(r).ok());
    let mut out = std::collections::HashSet::new();
    for rec in parsed.chain(items.iter().cloned()) {
        if let Some(p) = rec.get("provides").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) {
            let p = p.trim();
            if !p.is_empty() {
                out.insert(p.to_string());
            }
        }
        if let Some(s) = rec.get("src").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) {
            let base = s.trim().rsplit_once('.').map_or(s.trim(), |(stem, _)| stem);
            if base.starts_with("components/") {
                out.insert(format!("@/{base}"));
            }
        }
    }
    out
}

fn warn_unresolvable_imports(store: &bsc_json_store::Store, items: &[serde_json::Value]) {
    for w in unresolvable_component_imports(store, items) {
        eprintln!("{w}");
    }
}

/// A valid component NAME — a PascalCase identifier: an uppercase ASCII first char, then ASCII
/// alphanumerics. React cannot treat a lowercase name as a component, so the capital is a real rule, not a
/// style one; alphanumeric-only keeps the derived `--<name>-<token>` conventions and JSX tag clean.
fn is_component_name_ident(name: &str) -> bool {
    let mut chars = name.chars();
    matches!(chars.next(), Some(c) if c.is_ascii_uppercase()) && chars.all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric())
}

/// Replace WHOLE-IDENTIFIER occurrences of `old` with `new` in `text` — `old` must be bounded on both
/// sides by a non-identifier char (or the string edge), so renaming `Button` never rewrites `IconButton`
/// or `ButtonGroup`. Identifier chars are ASCII alphanumeric, `_`, and `$` (the JS identifier set).
/// Component names are ASCII, so matching on char boundaries is safe. Used to rewrite the renamed
/// component's own `srcText`/`source` identifier.
fn rename_ident(text: &str, old: &str, new: &str) -> String {
    if old.is_empty() {
        return text.to_string();
    }
    let is_ident = |c: char| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_' || c == '$';
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len());
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < text.len() {
        if text[i..].starts_with(old) {
            let before_ok = i == 0 || !text[..i].chars().next_back().is_some_and(is_ident);
            let after = i + old.len();
            let after_ok = after >= text.len() || !text[after..].chars().next().is_some_and(is_ident);
            if before_ok && after_ok {
                out.push_str(new);
                i = after;
                continue;
            }
        }
        let ch = text[i..].chars().next().expect("i is a char boundary");
        out.push(ch);
        i += ch.len_utf8();
    }
    out
}

/// `rename <id> <NewName> [--by <tag>] [--note <text>] [--dir D] [--pretty]` (#3576) — rename a component
/// in place. `id` is the STABLE store key (frozen at creation, never re-derived), so only the NAME moves:
/// the record's `name` + the identifier in its `srcText`/`source`, and — because the composition graph is
/// NAME-keyed (`model.ts`) — every sibling's `composes[]` + `rules[].use` that named it, swept across the
/// SAME kit only (kits never cross). Every touched record gets a change-history entry (#3568). Everything
/// keyed by id (store key, history, tokens, cross-graph URN) is untouched. A ui-scope MUTATION.
fn cmd_rename(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut pretty, mut by, mut note) = (None::<String>, false, None::<String>, None::<String>);
    let mut positionals: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            "--by" => by = it.next().cloned(),
            "--note" => note = it.next().cloned(),
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            positional => positionals.push(positional.to_string()),
        }
    }
    let id = positionals
        .first()
        .ok_or("usage: bsc ui rename <id> <NewName> [--by <tag>] [--note <text>]")?;
    let new_name = positionals
        .get(1)
        .ok_or("usage: bsc ui rename <id> <NewName> — the new PascalCase name is required")?;
    if !is_component_name_ident(new_name) {
        return Err(format!(
            "'{new_name}' is not a valid component name — a component is a PascalCase identifier ([A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*)"
        ));
    }

    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let target_raw = store.get(id)?.ok_or_else(|| {
        format!("no component '{id}' in the store — nothing to rename (ids are stable; see `bsc ui list`)")
    })?;
    let target: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&target_raw)
        .map_err(|e| format!("stored component '{id}' is not valid JSON: {e}"))?;
    let old_name = target.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string();
    if old_name.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!("component '{id}' has no `name` to rename"));
    }
    if old_name == *new_name {
        return Err(format!("component '{id}' is already named '{new_name}' — nothing to do"));
    }
    let kit_id = target.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string();

    let records: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
        store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok()).collect();
    // Collision: `composes` resolves by NAME within a kit, so two same-named components in one kit make it
    // ambiguous. Refuse before writing anything.
    let collides = records.iter().any(|r| {
        r.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(kit_id.as_str())
            && r.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(new_name.as_str())
            && r.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) != Some(id.as_str())
    });
    if collides {
        return Err(format!(
            "kit '{kit_id}' already has a component named '{new_name}' — a rename would make `composes` ambiguous (it resolves by name within a kit). Pick another name."
        ));
    }

    let now = crate::record::now_iso();
    let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(by.as_deref());
    let default_note = format!("renamed {old_name} → {new_name}");
    let note_str = note.as_deref().map(str::trim).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).unwrap_or(&default_note);

    let mut updated: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for mut rec in records {
        // The sweep is bounded to the renamed component's OWN kit — kits never cross, so a same-named
        // component elsewhere is a different component and must NOT be touched.
        if rec.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) != Some(kit_id.as_str()) {
            continue;
        }
        let rid = match rec.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) {
            Some(s) if !s.is_empty() => s.to_string(),
            _ => continue,
        };
        let mut changed = false;

        if rid == *id {
