            rec["name"] = serde_json::Value::from(new_name.as_str());
            changed = true;
            // Rewrite the identifier in the component's own source (usage snippet + any vendored module).
            for field in ["srcText", "source"] {
                if let Some(s) = rec.get(field).and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) {
                    let rewritten = rename_ident(s, &old_name, new_name);
                    if rewritten != s {
                        rec[field] = serde_json::Value::from(rewritten);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        // Every record in the kit: rewrite composes[] + rules[].use references to the old name.
        if let Some(arr) = rec.get_mut("composes").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_array_mut) {
            for e in arr.iter_mut() {
                if e.as_str() == Some(old_name.as_str()) {
                    *e = serde_json::Value::from(new_name.as_str());
                    changed = true;
                }
            }
        }
        if let Some(rules) = rec.get_mut("rules").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_array_mut) {
            for rule in rules.iter_mut() {
                if rule.get("use").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(old_name.as_str()) {
                    rule["use"] = serde_json::Value::from(new_name.as_str());
                    changed = true;
                }
            }
        }

        if changed {
            let prior = current_record(&store, &rid)?;
            crate::record::stamp_with_history(&mut rec, &prior, &writer, &now, Some(note_str));
            store.set(&rid, &serde_json::to_string(&rec).map_err(|e| format!("rename write: {e}"))?)?;
            bsc_util::emit_ui_activity("component", &rid);
            updated.push(rid);
        }
    }

    let references_updated = updated.iter().filter(|u| *u != id).count();
    let out = serde_json::json!({
        "id": id,
        "from": old_name,
        "to": new_name,
        "kit": kit_id,
        "updated": updated,
        "referencesUpdated": references_updated,
    });
    let text = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&out) } else { serde_json::to_string(&out) };
    println!("{}", text.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// `merge <from-id> <into-id> [--by <tag>] [--note <text>] [--dir D] [--pretty]` (#3592) — fold the
/// component `from` INTO `into` (the survivor) and remove `from`. The ACT step of the optimize loop
/// (`dupes`/`similar` only propose). `into` stays authoritative; every same-kit `composes[]`/`rules[].use`
/// that named `from` is repointed to `into` (deduped; a self-reference the fold would create is dropped),
/// then `from` is deleted. Every repointed record gets a change-history entry (#3568). Scoped to the kit
/// (`composes` is name-keyed; a cross-kit merge is refused). A ui-scope MUTATION, gated in [`run`].
fn cmd_merge(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut pretty, mut by, mut note) = (None::<String>, false, None::<String>, None::<String>);
    let mut positionals: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            "--by" => by = it.next().cloned(),
            "--note" => note = it.next().cloned(),
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            positional => positionals.push(positional.to_string()),
        }
    }
    let from_id = positionals.first().ok_or("usage: bsc ui merge <from-id> <into-id> [--by <tag>] [--note <text>]")?;
    let into_id = positionals.get(1).ok_or("usage: bsc ui merge <from-id> <into-id> — the survivor id is required")?;
    if from_id == into_id {
        return Err(format!("cannot merge '{from_id}' into itself"));
    }

    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let load = |id: &str| -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> {
        let raw = store
            .get(id)?
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("no component '{id}' in the store (see `bsc ui list --raw`)"))?;
        serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|e| format!("stored component '{id}' is not valid JSON: {e}"))
    };
    let from = load(from_id)?;
    let into = load(into_id)?;
    let from_name = from.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string();
    let into_name = into.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string();
    if from_name.is_empty() || into_name.is_empty() {
        return Err("both components must have a `name` to merge".to_string());
    }
    let from_kit = from.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
    let into_kit = into.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
    if from_kit != into_kit {
        return Err(format!(
            "'{from_id}' is in kit '{from_kit}' but '{into_id}' is in '{into_kit}' — `composes` is name-keyed WITHIN a kit, so a cross-kit merge is unsafe. Move one into the other's kit first, or merge within a kit."
        ));
    }
    let kit_id = from_kit.to_string();

    let now = crate::record::now_iso();
    let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(by.as_deref());
    let default_note = format!("merged {from_name} → {into_name}");
    let note_str = note.as_deref().map(str::trim).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).unwrap_or(&default_note);

    let records: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
        store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok()).collect();
    let mut repointed: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for mut rec in records {
        // Only same-kit records reference `from` by name; and the `from` record itself is being removed.
        if rec.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) != Some(kit_id.as_str()) {
            continue;
        }
        let rid = match rec.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) {
            Some(s) if !s.is_empty() && s != from_id => s.to_string(),
            _ => continue,
        };
        let own_name = rec.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string();
        let mut changed = false;

        if let Some(arr) = rec.get_mut("composes").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_array_mut) {
            let mut seen: std::collections::BTreeSet<String> = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
            let mut next: Vec<serde_json::Value> = Vec::with_capacity(arr.len());
            let mut any = false;
            for e in arr.iter() {
                let Some(orig) = e.as_str() else { continue };
                let mapped: &str = if orig == from_name.as_str() { into_name.as_str() } else { orig };
                if orig == from_name.as_str() {
                    any = true; // a from → into repoint
                }
                // Drop a self-reference the fold would create, and dedup (a component that composed BOTH
                // `from` AND `into` must not end up composing `into` twice).
                if mapped == own_name.as_str() || !seen.insert(mapped.to_string()) {
                    any = true;
                    continue;
                }
                next.push(serde_json::Value::from(mapped));
            }
            if any {
                *arr = next;
                changed = true;
            }
        }
        if let Some(rules) = rec.get_mut("rules").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_array_mut) {
            for rule in rules.iter_mut() {
                if rule.get("use").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(from_name.as_str()) {
                    rule["use"] = serde_json::Value::from(into_name.as_str());
                    changed = true;
                }
            }
        }

        if changed {
            let prior = current_record(&store, &rid)?;
            crate::record::stamp_with_history(&mut rec, &prior, &writer, &now, Some(note_str));
            store.set(&rid, &serde_json::to_string(&rec).map_err(|e| format!("merge write: {e}"))?)?;
            bsc_util::emit_ui_activity("component", &rid);
            repointed.push(rid);
        }
    }

    // Retire the merged-away component LAST, once every reference is repointed. A packaged BUILTIN gets
    // a suppression tombstone rather than a bare delete, so the fold survives the next hydrate (#96) —
    // see `retire_component`.
    let from_builtin = from.get("builtin").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_bool) == Some(true);
    let retired = retire_component(&store, from_id, from_builtin, Some(into_id))?;
    bsc_util::emit_ui_activity("component", from_id);

    let out = merge_report(from_id, into_id, &kit_id, &repointed, retired);
    let text = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&out) } else { serde_json::to_string(&out) };
    println!("{}", text.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// `regroup [--kit <id>] [--dir D] [--dry-run] [--pretty]` (#3579) — re-derive every stored component's
/// `group` as a nested `/`-delimited FOLDER PATH from its `src` ([`crate::group_from_src`]), so a kit
/// organizes like a completed project's folders (`shared/ui/controls`, `features/github`). Rewrites ONLY
/// the records whose derived group differs (each write stamped + logged via [`set_stamped`]); a record
/// with no usable `src` is left untouched. `--kit` scopes the pass to one kit; `--dry-run` reports the
/// moves without writing. Prints `{ scanned, changed: [{ id, from, to }], applied }`. A ui-scope
/// mutation, gated in [`run`].
/// A record's FOLDER, accepting the legacy key (#4107 slice B).
///
/// The store holds records written under `group`, and the component seed dir is skipped by
/// `ensure_seeded`, so there is no config-mirror pass to migrate them. Every READ therefore accepts
/// both names while every WRITE emits only `folder`: a record migrates the first time it is rewritten,
/// and `bsc ui refolder` does the whole store in one pass. Nothing needs migrating before this ships.
pub(crate) fn record_folder(rec: &serde_json::Value) -> Option<&str> {
    rec.get("folder")
        .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)
        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
}

fn cmd_refolder(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut kit, mut dry, mut pretty) = (None::<String>, None::<String>, false, false);
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--kit" => kit = it.next().cloned(),
            "--dry-run" => dry = true,
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other => {
                return Err(format!(
                    "unknown flag '{other}' — usage: bsc ui regroup [--kit <id>] [--dry-run] [--pretty]"
                ))
            }
        }
    }
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let mut scanned = 0usize;
    let mut changed = Vec::new();
    let mut updated = Vec::new();
    // `Store::list()` yields each record's VERBATIM JSON (NOT its id) — parse each directly; the id is
    // the record's own `id` field (which `set_stamped` also keys the write off).
    for raw in store.list() {
        let mut rec: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&raw)
            .map_err(|e| format!("a stored component is not valid JSON: {e}"))?;
        if let Some(k) = &kit {
            if rec.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) != Some(k.as_str()) {
                continue;
            }
        }
        scanned += 1;
        let src = rec.get("src").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
        // The legacy key, read HERE and nowhere else. `record_folder` no longer knows it (#4107's alias
        // is gone), and this is the one place that still must: a migration verb is the last reader of
        // the name it is retiring.
        let legacy = rec.get("group").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).filter(|v| !v.is_empty())
            .map(str::to_string);
        let derived = crate::folder_from_src(src);
        // WHY THIS IS NOT JUST `let Some(new) = derived else { continue }`:
        //
        // `folder` derives from `src`, so a record with NO src was skipped outright — and every one of
        // the 19 components still on `group` at 2026-08-25 was srcless. The only verb that could finish
        // #4107 structurally could not touch the records that needed it, which is why the rename stalled
        // at 19 and the compatibility shim stayed load-bearing for a year. (4118 recorded exactly this
        // trap for the ALGORITHMS store — "refolder counts all 75 as srcless and skips every one" — and
        // nobody noticed it was equally true here.)
        //
        // A srcless record carrying `group` is migrated BY VALUE: its folder is curated (`app/console`,
        // `features/planner/fleet`) and no `src` could reproduce it, so carrying the value across is the
        // only correct move as well as the only possible one. Re-derivation stays what it always was for
        // a record that HAS src.
        let new_folder = match (derived, &legacy) {
            (Some(d), _) => d,                      // has src: re-derive, unchanged behaviour
            (None, Some(g)) => g.clone(),           // srcless + legacy key: carry the value across
            (None, None) => continue,               // nothing to derive and nothing to carry
        };
        let old = record_folder(&rec).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
        if old == new_folder && legacy.is_none() {
            continue;   // already correct AND already migrated off the legacy key
        }
        let id = rec.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
        changed.push(serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "from": old, "to": new_folder }));
        rec["folder"] = serde_json::Value::String(new_folder);
        // Drop the legacy key so a rewritten record carries ONE name for its folder — otherwise a stale
        // `group` lingers beside the new `folder` and the two can drift.
        if let Some(o) = rec.as_object_mut() { o.remove("group"); }
        updated.push(rec);
    }
    let applied = if !dry && !updated.is_empty() {
        let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(None);
        // #4197: the write MERGES, so dropping the legacy `group` key above is no longer enough — a
        // merge would carry the stored one straight back. Name it as an explicit clear, which is also
        // what puts it in the record's history `dropped` instead of leaving the removal implicit.
        let clear = ["group".to_string()];
        let plan = WritePlan { replace: false, clear: &clear };
        set_stamped(&store, &updated, None, &writer, "component", Some("refolder: folder path from src"), plan)?;
        true
    } else {
        false
    };
    let report = serde_json::json!({ "scanned": scanned, "changed": changed, "applied": applied });
    let out = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report) } else { serde_json::to_string(&report) };
    println!("{}", out.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}


/// `bsc ui features [--kit <id>] [--apply] [--pretty]` — the FEATURE-axis backfill
/// (`epic-the-graphs-are-split-by-feature-over-a-core`), and the report of what it would do.
///
/// DRY BY DEFAULT, the inverse of `refolder`'s `--dry-run`. `refolder` re-derives a field it already
/// owns; this one INTRODUCES a field across the whole store on a mapping a human has to agree with
/// first, so the safe direction is opposite: you read the plan, then pass `--apply`.
///
/// It reports three groups, and the third is the point:
/// - `changed`  — records whose domain would be set (or corrected), with from/to.
/// - `byDomain` — the resulting per-domain counts, so the shape of the split is visible BEFORE it lands.
/// - `unmapped` — records the mapping cannot place, listed by id and never given a default.
///
/// The unmapped list is why this is not a sweep. 44 of 448 records are hollow — no folder, no `kitId`
/// and no `name` — and a backfill that quietly bucketed them would bury a data-quality problem inside a
/// migration and call it done. They surface here, every run, until someone decides what they are.
///
/// A record whose stored domain already matches is left alone, so re-running is a no-op.
fn cmd_features(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut kit, mut apply, mut pretty) = (None::<String>, None::<String>, false, false);
    let mut seed_dir: Option<String> = None;
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--kit" => kit = it.next().cloned(),
            "--seed-dir" => seed_dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--apply" => apply = true,
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other => {
                return Err(format!(
                    "unknown flag '{other}' — usage: bsc ui features [--kit <id>] [--apply] [--pretty] \
                     (reports only unless --apply)"
                ))
            }
        }
    }
    // `--seed-dir <dir>` — backfill the PACKAGED SEED directly, deriving each record's feature from
    // its OWN folder rather than from the store's copy.
    //
    // WHY IT EXISTS. The normal path reads the store and syncs onward, and that covered 294 of 306
    // packaged components. The other 12 are records whose STORE copy is hollow — no folder, no kitId,
    // no name — while the seed file holds the real record, folder and all. That is the store-vs-seed
    // drift this repo has both ways, and it meant the ownership gate (which reads the seed, because a
    // rule that depends on whose machine ran it is not a rule) could never reach full coverage through
    // the store.
    //
    // Deriving from the seed's own folder needs no store at all, so a hollow store copy cannot hide a
    // record from the rule. Same never-overwrite contract as the store path: a feature already written
    // is a decision, not a starting point.
    if let Some(seed_dir) = &seed_dir {
        let root = std::path::Path::new(seed_dir);
        if !root.is_dir() {
            return Err(format!("not a directory: {seed_dir}"));
        }
        let (mut scanned, mut already) = (0usize, 0usize);
        let (mut changed, mut unmapped) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
        let mut by_feature: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, usize> = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
        let mut stack = vec![root.to_path_buf()];
        while let Some(d) = stack.pop() {
            let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(&d) else { continue };
            for e in entries.flatten() {
                let p = e.path();
                if p.is_dir() {
                    stack.push(p);
                    continue;
                }
                if p.extension().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) != Some("json") {
                    continue;
                }
                let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(&p) else { continue };
                let Ok(mut rec) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&text) else { continue };
                // A kit bundle has no top-level `id` and is not a record.
                let Some(id) = rec.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).map(str::to_owned) else { continue };
                scanned += 1;
                let old = rec.get("feature").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
                if !old.is_empty() {
                    already += 1;
                    *by_feature.entry(old).or_default() += 1;
                    continue;
                }
                // Fall back to deriving from `src` when the record carries no `folder`. Not a guess:
                // `folder` IS derived from `src` (`bsc ui regroup` re-derives it), so a record with a
                // src and no folder is one nobody has re-foldered — not one whose home is unknown.
                // Without this the last packaged component stayed unplaced for want of a cached value
                // the record already carries.
                let folder = record_folder(&rec)
                    .map(str::to_owned)
                    .or_else(|| rec.get("src").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).and_then(crate::folder_from_src))
                    .unwrap_or_default();
                let Some(new) = crate::feature_from_folder(&folder) else {
                    unmapped.push(serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "folder": folder }));
                    continue;
                };
                *by_feature.entry(new.clone()).or_default() += 1;
                changed.push(serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "folder": folder, "to": new }));
                if apply {
                    if let Some(o) = rec.as_object_mut() {
                        o.insert("feature".into(), serde_json::Value::String(new));
                    }
                    let out = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&rec).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
                    std::fs::write(&p, format!("{out}\n")).map_err(|e| format!("cannot write {}: {e}", p.display()))?;
                }
            }
        }
        let report = serde_json::json!({
            "seedDir": seed_dir, "scanned": scanned, "alreadyCorrect": already,
            "changed": changed, "unmapped": unmapped, "byFeature": by_feature, "applied": apply,
        });
        let out = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report) } else { serde_json::to_string(&report) };
        println!("{}", out.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
        return Ok(());
    }
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let (mut scanned, mut already) = (0usize, 0usize);
    let (mut changed, mut unmapped, mut updated) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new(), Vec::new());
    let mut by_feature: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, usize> = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
    for raw in store.list() {
        let rec: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&raw)
            .map_err(|e| format!("a stored component is not valid JSON: {e}"))?;
        if let Some(k) = &kit {
            if rec.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) != Some(k.as_str()) {
                continue;
            }
        }
        scanned += 1;
        let id = rec.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
        let folder = record_folder(&rec).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
        let old = rec.get("feature").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
        let Some(new) = crate::feature_from_folder(&folder) else {
            // Report the folder we could not place ALONGSIDE the id: "which records are unmapped" and
            // "what shapes is the mapping missing" are different questions and this answers both.
            unmapped.push(serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "folder": folder }));
            if !old.is_empty() {
                *by_feature.entry(old).or_default() += 1;   // an already-set domain still counts
            }
            continue;
        };
        *by_feature.entry(new.clone()).or_default() += 1;
        // NEVER OVERWRITE a feature already set. The derivation is a starting point, not an
        // authority: a record deliberately placed by hand — `toggle` is `DeployToggle`, owned by
        // `core` because four other features compose it, while its FOLDER stays the planner tree it
        // was lifted from — must survive every later re-run. Without this the backfill silently undid
        // curation on each invocation, which is how it was found: a hand placement reverted one
        // command later.
        if !old.is_empty() {
            already += 1;
            continue;
        }
        if old == new {
            already += 1;
            continue;
        }
        changed.push(serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "folder": folder, "from": old, "to": new }));
        // Submit ONLY {id, domain}, never the round-tripped record.
        //
        // The write MERGES, so the two are equivalent — right up until a stored field is `null`. A
        // resubmitted explicit `null` reads as a CLEAR, so round-tripping the whole record deletes
        // every null field it carries. Measured on the real store before this line existed: 448
        // records went in, 401 fields came out where 402 should have, and the missing one was
        // `terminalhost.provides` — a stored null, silently dropped by a backfill that was only
        // supposed to ADD a field.
        //
        // Sending just the delta makes that unreachable: a field this command never names is a field
        // it cannot lose.
        updated.push(serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "feature": new }));
    }
    let applied = if apply && !updated.is_empty() {
        let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(None);
        let plan = WritePlan { replace: false, clear: &[] };
        set_stamped(&store, &updated, None, &writer, "component", Some("features: ownership axis from folder"), plan)?;
        true
    } else {
        false
    };
    let report = serde_json::json!({
        "scanned": scanned,
        "alreadyCorrect": already,
        "changed": changed,
        "unmapped": unmapped,
        "byFeature": by_feature,
        "applied": applied,
    });
    let out = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report) } else { serde_json::to_string(&report) };
    println!("{}", out.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}
/// `bsc ui export <dir> [--dir <store>] [--pretty]` (#3606) — dump the component store to a folder tree,
/// `<dir>/<group>/<id>.json`, so components-as-data round-trips: the seed half `bsc ui import` reads it back.
/// Files are written pretty (readable git diffs); `--pretty` also indents the stdout report.
fn cmd_export(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut out, mut dir, mut pretty) = (None::<String>, None::<String>, false);
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other if !other.starts_with("--") && out.is_none() => out = Some(other.to_string()),
            other => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}' — usage: bsc ui export <dir> [--dir <store>] [--pretty]")),
        }
    }
    let out = out.ok_or("usage: bsc ui export <dir> [--dir <store>] [--pretty]")?;
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let out_root = std::path::Path::new(&out);
    let mut ids = Vec::new();
    for raw in store.list() {
        let rec: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|e| format!("a stored component is not valid JSON: {e}"))?;
        let id = rec.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).ok_or("a stored component has no `id`")?;
        // `folder` is a `/`-delimited FOLDER PATH (#3579) → nest the file, so the tree mirrors the
        // project. Read through `record_folder` so a record still carrying the legacy `group` key
        // exports into the same tree rather than silently flattening to the root.
        let folder = record_folder(&rec).unwrap_or("");
        let mut path = out_root.to_path_buf();
        for seg in folder.split('/').filter(|s| !s.is_empty()) {
            path.push(seg);
        }
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&path).map_err(|e| format!("cannot create {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
        path.push(format!("{id}.json"));
        let text = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&rec).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        std::fs::write(&path, text).map_err(|e| format!("cannot write {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
        ids.push(id.to_string());
    }
    let report = serde_json::json!({ "exported": ids.len(), "dir": out, "ids": ids });
    let s = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report) } else { serde_json::to_string(&report) };
    println!("{}", s.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// `bsc ui import <dir> [--dir <store>] [--pretty]` (#3606) — load a folder tree of component records into
/// the store (the load half of components-as-data). Each `*.json` is UPSERT by its `id`; a KIT BUNDLE
/// (`{"components":[…]}`, e.g. react-ui.json) is exploded so every component in it imports.
/// `bsc ui parity <seed-dir>` — compare what the app RENDERS against what it SHIPS (#4246).
///
/// ## Why this exists
///
/// Three guards already watch the graph and none of them looks at the thing that renders:
///
/// ```text
/// graphParity.test.ts   globs data/components/app/**       -> the SEED
/// GraphComponent.tsx    useAppStore(s => s.components…)    -> the STORE
/// reconcileSeed         store <-> seed, but returns early for a record with no `builtin`
/// ```
///
/// So a record whose store copy has drifted from its seed renders source nothing has ever compared
/// against anything. Measured on this machine: 8 of 22 `role: page` records differ, `skillspage` by 9137
/// characters — and two of those eight drifted because a seed fix landed and the store never followed,
/// which is #4207 in miniature.
///
/// ## Why a CLI verb and not a test
///
/// The store is SQLite behind this binary; vitest cannot read it, which is precisely why the existing
/// guards are all seed-side. Putting the comparison where the store already lives is the only place it
/// can be honest. It reads the seed with the SAME folder walk `bsc ui import` uses, so the two verbs
/// cannot disagree about what "the seed" means.
///
/// ## Reporting, not gating, by default
///
/// Exits 0 unless `--strict`. A guard that lands red protects nothing — it just teaches everyone to
/// ignore it (`record-link-debt` is this repo's worked example: a red parity test sat unnoticed because
/// CI is disabled). `--strict` is for a caller that has adjudicated the known set and wants the next
/// drift to fail.
fn cmd_parity(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut inp, mut dir, mut pretty, mut strict, mut role) =
        (None::<String>, None::<String>, false, false, None::<String>);
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            "--strict" => strict = true,
            // Scope to one role — `--role page` is the #4246 question, since a page record IS the page.
            "--role" => role = it.next().cloned(),
            other if !other.starts_with("--") && inp.is_none() => inp = Some(other.to_string()),
            other => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}' — usage: bsc ui parity <seed-dir> [--role <r>] [--strict] [--dir <store>] [--pretty]")),
        }
    }
    let inp = inp.ok_or("usage: bsc ui parity <seed-dir> [--role <r>] [--strict] [--dir <store>] [--pretty]")?;
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;

    let mut files = Vec::new();
    collect_json_files(std::path::Path::new(&inp), &mut files).map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {inp}: {e}"))?;
    files.sort();

    let mut same = 0usize;
    let mut drift: Vec<serde_json::Value> = Vec::new();
    let mut missing: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for f in &files {
        let raw = std::fs::read_to_string(f).map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {}: {e}", f.display()))?;
        let seed: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|e| format!("{} is not valid JSON: {e}", f.display()))?;
        let Some(id) = seed.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) else { continue };
        if let Some(want) = role.as_deref() {
            if seed.get("role").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default() != want {
                continue;
            }
        }
        let Some(stored_raw) = store.get(id)? else {
            // In the seed, absent from the store — it has never been hydrated here. Reported separately
            // from drift: "not yet seeded" and "seeded then diverged" need different remedies.
            missing.push(id.to_string());
            continue;
        };
        let stored: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&stored_raw)
            .map_err(|e| format!("stored record '{id}' is not valid JSON: {e}"))?;
        let s_txt = stored.get("srcText").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
        let d_txt = seed.get("srcText").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
        if s_txt == d_txt {
            same += 1;
            continue;
        }
        drift.push(serde_json::json!({
            "id": id,
            "role": seed.get("role").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default(),
            "store": s_txt.chars().count(),
            "seed": d_txt.chars().count(),
            // Signed, because the drift runs BOTH ways and "the store is stale" is the wrong summary:
            // a positive delta is the store holding source the seed has never had.
            "delta": s_txt.chars().count() as i64 - d_txt.chars().count() as i64,
            "builtin": stored.get("builtin").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_bool).unwrap_or(false),
            "stamped": stored.get("seedHash").is_some(),
        }));
    }

    let report = serde_json::json!({
        "seedDir": inp, "role": role, "same": same,
        "drift": drift.len(), "missingFromStore": missing.len(),
        "records": drift, "missing": missing,
    });
    let s = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report) } else { serde_json::to_string(&report) };
    println!("{}", s.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    if strict && !drift.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!(
            "{} record(s) render source that differs from what ships — `bsc ui parity {inp} --pretty` names them",
            drift.len()
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn cmd_import(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut inp, mut dir, mut pretty) = (None::<String>, None::<String>, false);
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other if !other.starts_with("--") && inp.is_none() => inp = Some(other.to_string()),
            other => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}' — usage: bsc ui import <dir> [--dir <store>] [--pretty]")),
        }
    }
    let inp = inp.ok_or("usage: bsc ui import <dir> [--dir <store>] [--pretty]")?;
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let mut files = Vec::new();
    collect_json_files(std::path::Path::new(&inp), &mut files).map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {inp}: {e}"))?;
    files.sort(); // deterministic import order (stable across platforms)
    let mut ids = Vec::new();
    for f in &files {
        let raw = std::fs::read_to_string(f).map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {}: {e}", f.display()))?;
        let v: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|e| format!("{} is not valid JSON: {e}", f.display()))?;
        // A kit bundle → import each of its components; anything else is a single record.
        let records: Vec<&serde_json::Value> = match v.get("components").and_then(|c| c.as_array()) {
            Some(arr) => arr.iter().collect(),
            None => vec![&v],
        };
        for rec in records {
            let id = rec
                .get("id")
                .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)
                .ok_or_else(|| format!("a record in {} has no `id`", f.display()))?;
            store.set(id, &serde_json::to_string(rec).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?)?;
            bsc_util::emit_ui_activity("component", id); // Design Studio live-focus (#2525) re-hydrates
            ids.push(id.to_string());
        }
    }
    let report = serde_json::json!({ "imported": ids.len(), "dir": inp, "ids": ids });
    let s = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report) } else { serde_json::to_string(&report) };
    println!("{}", s.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// The store's bookkeeping fields a packaged SEED never carries (#139, verified against all 73
/// `features/settings/cards/*.json` seeds): the change-history stamp (`history`/`rev`/`updatedAt`/
/// `updatedBy`, #3164), the reconcile fingerprint (`seedHash`), and the runtime-computed flags
/// (`builtin`/`used`/`usageAssessed`/`version`). `bsc ui export` dumps a record VERBATIM (by design —
/// it round-trips through `bsc ui import`), so its output carries every one of these and cannot be
/// dropped straight into `src-tauri/data/components/app/**`; `sync-seed` strips them before it writes.
///
/// #158 — the list was short by `usageAssessed` (stamped by `usage-scan --apply`, see its own doc
/// comment) and `version` (a store-only defaulted key), so a `sync-seed --apply` after either had run
/// wrote both into the seed file and `seedRoundTrip.test.ts`'s "carries only fields the projection
/// preserves" case failed on the very next `terminalview.json` sync.
const SEED_BOOKKEEPING_FIELDS: &[&str] =
    &["history", "rev", "updatedAt", "updatedBy", "builtin", "seedHash", "used", "usageAssessed", "version"];

/// `bsc ui sync-seed <id>… --seed-dir <dir> [--dir <store>] [--apply] [--pretty]` (#139) — the
/// store-to-seed sync `bsc ui parity` diagnoses (123 of 337 drifted, measured) and nothing could act on:
/// `export` dumps EVERY field, including store bookkeeping no seed file has ever carried, so its output
/// can't be dropped into the packaged tree. `sync-impl-seed.mjs` already solves this for algorithm
/// IMPLEMENTATIONS, one id at a time; this is that fix's counterpart for COMPONENTS, mounted on `bsc ui`
/// instead of left as a script per this repo's rule that a capability lives on the `bsc` surface.
///
/// Deliberately BY ID, never a sweep — `parity`'s `delta` is signed because drift runs BOTH ways, so a
/// mass re-stamp would as often overwrite real seed content with stale store content as the reverse. A
/// read-only DRY RUN by default (matching `sync-impl-seed.mjs`'s own default); `--apply` writes. A READ
/// of the store — no `ui` write scope required, since only the on-disk seed file changes (exactly like
/// `bsc ui export`, which also writes files under a read-only gate).
fn cmd_sync_seed(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut seed_dir, mut dir, mut apply, mut pretty) = (None::<String>, None::<String>, false, false);
    let mut only: Option<String> = None;
    let mut ids: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--seed-dir" => seed_dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--apply" => apply = true,
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            // `--only <field>` — write exactly ONE field onto the seed record, leaving the rest as the
            // seed has it. Without it this verb is whole-body, and store and seed drift BOTH ways (its
            // own help says so), so syncing a NEW facet across many records would drag that unrelated
            // drift along under cover of the change. The algorithms side needed the same flag for the
            // same reason when the `feature` axis landed.
            "--only" => only = it.next().cloned(),
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            other => ids.push(other.to_string()),
        }
    }
    let usage = "usage: bsc ui sync-seed <id>… --seed-dir <dir> [--dir <store>] [--only <field>] [--apply] [--pretty]";
    let seed_dir = seed_dir.ok_or(usage)?;
    if ids.is_empty() {
        return Err(usage.into());
    }
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;

    // Index the seed tree ONCE by id. A kit BUNDLE (`{"components":[…]}`, no top-level `id`) is skipped —
    // this fix targets the one-record-per-file layout `bsc ui export`/`import` already use.
    let mut files = Vec::new();
    collect_json_files(std::path::Path::new(&seed_dir), &mut files)
        .map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {seed_dir}: {e}"))?;
    let mut seed_by_id: std::collections::HashMap<String, std::path::PathBuf> = std::collections::HashMap::new();
    for f in &files {
        let Ok(raw) = std::fs::read_to_string(f) else { continue };
        let Ok(v) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&raw) else { continue };
        if let Some(id) = v.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) {
            seed_by_id.insert(id.to_string(), f.clone());
        }
    }

    let (mut synced, mut up_to_date, mut missing_from_store, mut missing_from_seed) =
        (Vec::new(), Vec::new(), Vec::new(), Vec::new());
    for id in &ids {
        let Some(raw) = store.get(id)? else {
            missing_from_store.push(id.clone());
            continue;
        };
        let Some(path) = seed_by_id.get(id) else {
            // Mirrors `sync-impl-seed.mjs`'s own SKIP wording: a record with no seed file needs
            // PROMOTING (a new file), not syncing (an existing one).
            missing_from_seed.push(id.clone());
            continue;
        };
        let mut stored: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|e| format!("stored record '{id}' is not valid JSON: {e}"))?;
        let obj = stored.as_object_mut().ok_or_else(|| format!("stored record '{id}' is not a JSON object"))?;
        for field in SEED_BOOKKEEPING_FIELDS {
            obj.remove(*field);
        }
        let seed_raw = std::fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
        let seed: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&seed_raw).map_err(|e| format!("{} is not valid JSON: {e}", path.display()))?;
        // ONE field onto the seed record: everything else stays exactly as the seed has it, so no
        // unrelated drift rides along with the facet being synced.
        let stored = match &only {
            None => stored,
            Some(field) => {
                let mut merged = seed.clone();
                match (merged.as_object_mut(), stored.get(field)) {
                    (Some(m), Some(v)) => { m.insert(field.clone(), v.clone()); }
                    (Some(m), None) => { m.remove(field); }
                    _ => {}
                }
                merged
            }
        };
        if seed == stored {
            up_to_date.push(id.clone());
            continue;
        }
        if apply {
            let text = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&stored).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            std::fs::write(path, format!("{text}\n")).map_err(|e| format!("cannot write {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
        }
        synced.push(serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "path": path.display().to_string() }));
    }

    let report = serde_json::json!({
        "seedDir": seed_dir, "applied": apply,
        "synced": synced, "upToDate": up_to_date,
        "missingFromStore": missing_from_store, "missingFromSeed": missing_from_seed,
    });
    let s = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report) } else { serde_json::to_string(&report) };
    // Through the SHARED emitter (unlike `export`/`parity`/`import`'s plain `println!`) so a warm `bsc
    // serve` child can answer this read too, and so the report is capturable in tests.
    bsc_util::emit_line(&s.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// `bsc ui promote <id>… --seed-dir <dir> [--dir <store>] [--apply] [--pretty]` (#162, request from
/// kevin) — writes a genuinely NEW record's content into a NEW file under the packaged seed. `sync-seed`
/// deliberately declines exactly this case (its own report calls it out: "an id with no matching seed
/// file — that is a PROMOTION — a new file — not a sync"), so authoring a new component in the store had
/// no path to git — the request's evidence is a hand-written
/// `src-tauri/data/components/app/features/studio-sessions/networkarchitectmount.json`. `bsc graph
/// promote` does the analogous move for algorithm records, but its shape doesn't transplant here as-is:
/// that store is one committed `algorithms.json`, so "promote" there means writing a JSON *field* into
/// one file, while the component seed is a file tree of one-record-per-file, so promoting here means
/// creating a new *file*, nested by the record's `folder` (mirroring `bsc ui export`'s own nesting).
///
/// Deliberately narrower than `bsc graph promote`'s bare-refresh + `--id`-adopt shape, and on purpose:
/// an earlier in-flight attempt at a full store↔seed reconciler (`bsc ui promote --check`, never merged)
/// surfaced that the store is POORER than the seed for a real, non-empty set of existing records —
/// `provides` synthesised as a fallback that stops resolving, `srcText` that is simply older than what
/// shipped — so overwriting an EXISTING seed file from the store risks regressing landed work. This verb
/// never does that: an id that already has a seed file is left untouched and reported as
/// `alreadySeeded`, pointing at `sync-seed` (the by-id, drift-aware verb for that direction) instead. By
/// id, never a sweep — same reasoning as `sync-seed`. Dry run by default; `--apply` writes.
fn cmd_promote(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut seed_dir, mut dir, mut apply, mut pretty) = (None::<String>, None::<String>, false, false);
    let mut ids: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--seed-dir" => seed_dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--apply" => apply = true,
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            other => ids.push(other.to_string()),
        }
    }
    let usage = "usage: bsc ui promote <id>… --seed-dir <dir> [--dir <store>] [--apply] [--pretty]";
    let seed_dir = seed_dir.ok_or(usage)?;
    if ids.is_empty() {
        return Err(usage.into());
    }
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;

    // Index the seed tree ONCE by id, same walk `sync-seed` uses, so the two verbs cannot disagree
    // about which ids already have a seed file.
    let mut files = Vec::new();
    collect_json_files(std::path::Path::new(&seed_dir), &mut files)
        .map_err(|e| format!("cannot read {seed_dir}: {e}"))?;
    let mut seeded: std::collections::HashSet<String> = std::collections::HashSet::new();
    for f in &files {
        let Ok(raw) = std::fs::read_to_string(f) else { continue };
        let Ok(v) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&raw) else { continue };
        if let Some(id) = v.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) {
            seeded.insert(id.to_string());
        }
    }

    let (mut promoted, mut already_seeded, mut missing_from_store) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new(), Vec::new());
    for id in &ids {
        let Some(raw) = store.get(id)? else {
            missing_from_store.push(id.clone());
            continue;
        };
        if seeded.contains(id) {
            // Refuse rather than overwrite — that is `sync-seed`'s job, and it is drift-aware where
            // this verb (by design) is not.
            already_seeded.push(id.clone());
            continue;
        }
        let mut rec: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|e| format!("stored record '{id}' is not valid JSON: {e}"))?;
        let obj = rec.as_object_mut().ok_or_else(|| format!("stored record '{id}' is not a JSON object"))?;
        for field in SEED_BOOKKEEPING_FIELDS {
            obj.remove(*field);
        }
        // Nest by `folder`, exactly like `bsc ui export`, so a promoted record lands where the rest of
        // the tree would put it rather than flattening to the seed-dir root.
        let folder = record_folder(&rec).unwrap_or("").to_string();
        let mut path = std::path::Path::new(&seed_dir).to_path_buf();
        for seg in folder.split('/').filter(|s| !s.is_empty()) {
            path.push(seg);
        }
        path.push(format!("{id}.json"));
        if apply {
            if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
                std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).map_err(|e| format!("cannot create {}: {e}", parent.display()))?;
            }
            let text = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&rec).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
            std::fs::write(&path, format!("{text}\n")).map_err(|e| format!("cannot write {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
        }
        promoted.push(serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "path": path.display().to_string() }));
    }

    let report = serde_json::json!({
        "seedDir": seed_dir, "applied": apply,
        "promoted": promoted, "alreadySeeded": already_seeded,
        "missingFromStore": missing_from_store,
    });
    let s = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report) } else { serde_json::to_string(&report) };
    bsc_util::emit_line(&s.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// Recursively collect every `*.json` under `root` (a missing dir ⇒ empty, matching the store's leniency).
fn collect_json_files(root: &std::path::Path, out: &mut Vec<std::path::PathBuf>) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    if !root.exists() {
        return Ok(());
    }
    for entry in std::fs::read_dir(root)? {
        let path = entry?.path();
        if path.is_dir() {
            collect_json_files(&path, out)?;
        } else if path.extension().is_some_and(|e| e == "json") {
            out.push(path);
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// `log <id> [--kit] [--dir D] [--pretty]` (#3164) — print a record's history stamp
/// (`{ id, rev, updatedAt, updatedBy }`). A read verb (never scope-gated). `--kit` logs a kit record.
fn cmd_log(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut pretty, mut kit, mut id) = (None::<String>, false, false, None::<String>);
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            "--kit" => kit = true,
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            positional => id = Some(positional.to_string()),
        }
    }
    let id = id.ok_or("usage: bsc ui log <id> [--kit]")?;
    let store = if kit { open_kit_store(&dir)? } else { open_component_store(&dir)? };
    let raw = store
        .get(&id)?
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("no record '{id}' in the store — nothing to log"))?;
    let record: serde_json::Value =
        serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|e| format!("stored record '{id}' is not valid JSON: {e}"))?;
    let out_val = crate::record::log_value(&id, &record);
    let out = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&out_val) } else { serde_json::to_string(&out_val) };
    println!("{}", out.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// `revert <id> [--to <rev>] [--kit] [--by <tag>] [--dir D] [--pretty]` — restore a record's `srcText`
/// from the retained change history. The recovery half of the 02:00 incident: before this, `bsc ui log`
/// recorded THAT a write moved `srcText` and never WHAT it replaced, so a bad write on a record with no
/// packaged seed had no way back and the designer's version was the only copy that had ever existed.
///
/// No `--to` reverts the LAST write that moved the source. `--to <rev>` restores the source as the record
/// held it at that revision. Either way the revert is itself a WRITE — it stamps a new rev and its own
/// history entry, so the version being replaced becomes revertible in turn and a mistaken revert is not a
/// second unrecoverable act. A ui-scope MUTATION.
fn cmd_revert(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut pretty, mut kit, mut id) = (None::<String>, false, false, None::<String>);
    let (mut to, mut by) = (None::<i64>, None::<String>);
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            "--kit" => kit = true,
            "--by" => by = it.next().cloned(),
            "--to" => {
                let raw = it.next().ok_or("--to needs a revision number")?;
                to = Some(raw.parse::<i64>().map_err(|_| format!("--to '{raw}' is not a revision number"))?);
            }
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            positional => id = Some(positional.to_string()),
        }
    }
    let id = id.ok_or("usage: bsc ui revert <id> [--to <rev>] [--kit]")?;
    let store = if kit { open_kit_store(&dir)? } else { open_component_store(&dir)? };
    let raw = store
        .get(&id)?
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("no record '{id}' in the store — nothing to revert"))?;
    let record: serde_json::Value =
        serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|e| format!("stored record '{id}' is not valid JSON: {e}"))?;

    let reachable = crate::record::revertible_revs(&record);
    // No `--to` ⇒ undo the last write that moved the source, which is the newest anchor.
    let target = match to {
        Some(r) => r,
        None => *reachable.last().ok_or_else(|| {
            format!(
                "'{id}' has no retained earlier source — nothing to revert to. Only writes made since the \
                 change log started retaining source can be undone, and the most recent {} are kept.",
                crate::record::PREV_SRC_CAP
            )
        })?,
    };
    let restored = crate::record::src_at_rev(&record, target).ok_or_else(|| {
        let offer = if reachable.is_empty() {
            "no revision's source is retained".to_string()
        } else {
            format!(
                "revertible revisions: {}",
                reachable.iter().map(i64::to_string).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")
            )
        };
        format!("'{id}' cannot be reverted to rev {target} — its source is no longer retained ({offer})")
    })?;

    let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(by.as_deref());
    let from_rev = crate::record::read_rev(&record);
    let mut next = record.clone();
    if let Some(obj) = next.as_object_mut() {
        obj.insert(crate::record::SRC_TEXT.to_string(), serde_json::Value::from(restored.as_str()));
    }
    let note = format!("revert: srcText restored to rev {target} (was rev {from_rev})");
    crate::record::stamp_with_history(&mut next, &record, &writer, &crate::record::now_iso(), Some(&note));
    store.set(&id, &serde_json::to_string(&next).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?)?;

    let out_val = serde_json::json!({
        "id": id,
        "revertedTo": target,
        "fromRev": from_rev,
        "rev": crate::record::read_rev(&next),
        "srcTextChars": restored.len(),
    });
    let out = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&out_val) } else { serde_json::to_string(&out_val) };
    println!("{}", out.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// Write-time gate for a `bsc ui set` batch (#2928): for each record whose `srcText` claims to be a
/// module (`looks_buildable_module` — the preview's own buildability test, modulo the #3470 elision
/// accuracy fix), run the module-syntax check and reject the whole batch on the first defect — so a silently-corrupted source (an unterminated string
/// from an escape-collapse) can't be stored. A record with no `srcText` is fine.
///
/// A `srcText` that is NOT a module is still stored (a spec-only record is legitimate), but that is now
/// a STATED outcome rather than a silent skip (#3470): it warns on stderr, naming every reason. The old
/// shape inverted the gate at the edges — the source least like a module (one keeping its unresolved
/// `@/…` imports) made the predicate false, which skipped the syntax check ENTIRELY, so it stored with
/// zero complaint and only surfaced much later as a `no-implementation` finding in `bsc ui doctor`, far
/// from the write that caused it.
///
/// ALSO (non-blocking, #3065): warns on stderr for a bad INLINE animation def on the record's
/// `animations`, but never rejects over one. The srcText Err semantics are unchanged; both warnings are
/// pure side-effects. Driven directly by tests.
/// `--force` on this process's `bsc ui set` — see the flag's arm in [`cmd_set`] for why it is a global.
static FORCE_WRITE: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool = std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false);

fn validate_component_batch(items: &[serde_json::Value]) -> Result<(), String> {
    for item in items {
        // `requiredBy` — the USAGE mirror of a plan feature's `requires`. Validated HERE so a malformed
        // entry is refused at the door: an entry must be `<projectKey>:<feature>`, because a bare slug is
        // ambiguous across projects and a stored ambiguity is the thing the qualification exists to stop.
        if let Some(rb) = item.get("requiredBy") {
            let entries: Vec<String> = rb
                .as_array()
                .ok_or("`requiredBy` must be an array of `<projectKey>:<feature>` entries")?
                .iter()
                .map(|v| v.as_str().unwrap_or_default().to_string())
                .collect();
            bsc_util::required_by::normalize_required_by(&entries)?;
        }
        // #3065: non-blocking — runs for EVERY item, BEFORE the srcText early-continue below, so an
        // inline-animation warning surfaces even on a component whose `srcText` isn't a buildable module.
        warn_component_animations(item);
        // #3709: same — a JSX-text unicode-escape leak surfaces on any item with source, even a spec.
        warn_jsx_text_escapes(item);

        let src_text = item.get("srcText").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
        if src_text.trim().is_empty() {
            continue; // no source to judge — a record can legitimately carry none.
        }
        // #43: a graph-source component (carries `provides`) is a real app primitive whose `@/` imports the
        // runtime loader — and the now provides-aware preview build/doctor — resolve. `looks_buildable_module`
        // treats ANY `@/` import as unbuildable, so it emits a FALSE "unresolved first-party @/" warning for
        // it. Skip the buildability advisory for these (buildability is judged by `doctor`); the syntax check
        // below still runs, so real corruption is still caught.
        let provides = item.get("provides").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
        // A STATEFUL record must not claim a REGISTERED platform specifier. `bsc graph impl set` has
        // refused this since the 36-shadow sweep, but the component store never did, and component
        // records carry no `moduleState` field to refuse on — so the whole tier was ungoverned. 88 of
        // the double-covered specifiers come from component records, and one was already wrong:
        // `plan-relationship-graph` holds a top-level `let _ctx` and provides
        // `@/features/planner/relationship/RelationshipGraphView`, registered at
        // `features/planner/bodies/graphPlatform.ts:90`.
        //
        // `provides` BEATS the registry, so this vendors a second copy of live state to every graph
        // consumer — and unlike a broken override, which declines and falls back visibly, a stateful
        // shadow WORKS, just against the wrong copy. Detected from `srcText` with the graph crate's own
        // detector rather than a second rule here, so the two stores cannot disagree about what state is.
        if !provides.trim().is_empty() && bsc_graph::is_registered_platform_module(provides) {
            let tsx = src_text.contains('<') && src_text.contains("/>") || src_text.contains("</");
            let state = bsc_graph::extract::module_state_of(src_text, tsx);
            if !state.is_empty() {
                let id = item.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("<no id>");
                return Err(format!(
                    "'{id}' cannot provide `{provides}`: that specifier is a REGISTERED platform module \
                     and this record holds module state ({}). A record wins over the registry, so this \
                     would vendor a SECOND copy of that state to every graph consumer. Drop the \
                     `provides` (the record stays for provenance), or move the state out of the module.",
                    state.join(", ")
                ));
            }
        }
        // #3470: not-a-module is REPORTED, never an unchecked skip. Still permissive — it stores.
        // …and ask the LOADER's oracle before warning. The `provides` skip above is a band-aid
        // `runtime_module_defects` already names as one: it silences the advisory for a record that
        // CLAIMS a specifier, when the thing that actually matters is whether the loader can resolve the
        // imports. Dropping a stateful record's claim (just above) exposed that immediately —
        // `plan-relationship-graph` lost its `provides` and instantly drew "unresolved first-party
        // `@/features/planner/relationship/relationshipGraph`", an import the loader resolves fine.
        //
        // So warn only when BOTH oracles object. Strictly fewer false positives, and it cannot create a
        // new one: a record the loader cannot resolve still warns exactly as before.
        if provides.trim().is_empty()
            && !crate::graph_health::looks_buildable_module(src_text)
            && !crate::graph_health::runtime_module_defects(src_text).is_empty()
        {
            // #3849: for a `role: page` this is FATAL, not advisory. A page record IS the page — there is
            // no `.tsx` behind `fleetpage` at all — so storing one that cannot render ships a blank
            // screen, and the failure surfaces at mount, far from the write that caused it. Every other
            // role stays permissive: a spec-only primitive is a legitimate thing to store.
            //
            // Gated on the defects being TRUSTWORTHY, which is why the false-positive fix had to land
            // first: rejecting on a liar would just teach everyone to pass `--force`.
            // A PAGE is judged by the LOADER's oracle, and ONLY by it. It is mounted by the runtime
            // loader — which resolves registered platform modules and `@/components/<id>` siblings —
            // never by the preview sandbox, so `looks_buildable_module` (which condemns every `@/`
            // import, correctly for the sandbox) is simply the wrong question here. Asking it produced a
            // warning that named sixteen perfectly resolvable specifiers on `fleetpage` and told the
            // reader it had been "stored as a SPEC, not as compilable code" — of the record that renders
            // the Fleet page in the running app.
            let role = item.get("role").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
            if role == "page" {
                if !crate::graph_health::renders_at_runtime(src_text)
                    && !FORCE_WRITE.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed)
                {
                    return Err(format!(
                        "{}: refusing to store a `role: page` record that cannot render — {}. \
                         A page record IS the page; there is no source file behind it, so this would ship \
                         a blank screen. Fix the source, or pass --force to store it as a deliberate spec.",
                        item_label(item),
                        crate::graph_health::runtime_module_defects(src_text).join("; "),
                    ));
                }
                // It renders (or --force). Fall THROUGH to the syntax check rather than `continue`ing:
                // under the old shape a page's source skipped that check entirely, which is exactly the
                // #3470 inversion — the source least like a preview module got the least validation.
            } else {
                eprintln!("{}", unbuildable_module_warning(item, src_text));
                continue;
            }
        }
        if let Err(msg) = crate::syntax::check_module_syntax(src_text) {
            return Err(format!(
                "{}: {msg} — its srcText looks like a module but won't build. Fix it, or author it from a raw file to avoid shell-escaping corruption.",
                item_label(item)
            ));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The stderr advisory (#3470) for a non-empty `srcText` that `looks_buildable_module` rejected. Names
/// every reason `module_defects` found and says plainly what just got stored, so "this is a spec, not
/// code" is something the writer sees AT WRITE TIME instead of discovering days later as a `doctor`
/// finding. Returns the message rather than printing it so the wording is under test, like the batch
/// result. (Only called on the not-a-module branch, where the defect list is non-empty by construction.)
fn unbuildable_module_warning(item: &serde_json::Value, src_text: &str) -> String {
    format!(
        "warning: component '{}' has a srcText that is NOT a buildable module: {} — it is stored as a SPEC, not as compilable code, so the Design Studio preview will show no implementation and `bsc ui doctor` will report it. Author a self-contained module (inline or vendor what it imports) if you meant to ship code.",
        item_label(item),
        crate::graph_health::module_defects(src_text).join("; ")
    )
}

/// The human handle for a record in a write-time message — its `name`, else its `id`, else the generic
/// noun. One helper so the syntax REJECTION and the not-a-module WARNING point at the same string.
fn item_label(item: &serde_json::Value) -> &str {
    item.get("name")
        .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)
        .or_else(|| item.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str))
        .unwrap_or("component")
}

/// Non-blocking write-time advisory (#3065) for a component's INLINE animation defs. A component's
/// `animations` entries may each be a kit-animation NAME (a string — always fine, a ref into the kit's
/// library) OR an INLINE def object (a full `KitAnimation` used directly for component-specific one-off
/// motion, validated exactly like `bsc ui kit define-animation`). An inline def that fails the motion
/// grammar — or an entry that is neither a string nor an object — is WARNED about on stderr (naming the
/// component id), but NEVER rejected: the render compiler guards every field at render, and dropping a
/// whole component over one bad anim is too heavy. Purely advisory — it never changes the batch result.
fn warn_component_animations(item: &serde_json::Value) {
    let Some(anims) = item.get("animations").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_array) else {
        return;
    };
    let id = item
        .get("id")
        .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)
        .or_else(|| item.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str))
        .unwrap_or("component");
    for entry in anims {
        if entry.is_string() {
            continue; // a NAME ref into the kit's animations library — always fine.
        }
        if entry.is_object() {
            if let Err(msg) = validate_animation(entry) {
                eprintln!(
                    "warning: component '{id}' has an invalid inline animation: {msg} — it will be dropped at render (fix it, or reference a kit animation by name)."
                );
            }
        } else {
            eprintln!(
                "warning: component '{id}' has an `animations` entry that is neither a name (string) nor an inline def (object) — it will be ignored."
            );
        }
    }
}

/// Non-blocking write-time advisory (#3709) for a JS unicode/hex escape (`\uXXXX`, `\u{…}`, `\xHH`)
/// sitting in JSX-TEXT / code position — OUTSIDE any string literal, template, or comment. JSX children
/// text is not a JS string, so a bare escape typed directly between tags is never interpreted: the browser
/// renders the literal `backslash-u-…` characters, not the glyph. It passes the syntax check (valid JS) and
/// stores clean, so ONLY a screenshot catches it — a semantic-but-not-syntactic defect the build can't see.
/// WARN (naming the leaked escapes + the fix — a real UTF-8 char, or a JS string like `{"·"}`), but
/// NEVER reject: the record is valid JS. Purely advisory, like [`warn_component_animations`].
fn warn_jsx_text_escapes(item: &serde_json::Value) {
    let src_text = item.get("srcText").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
    let leaks = crate::graph_health::jsx_text_escape_leaks(src_text);
    if leaks.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    // Unique escapes, first-seen order, capped so a component riddled with them stays one readable line.
    let mut seen = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
    let uniq: Vec<&str> =
        leaks.iter().filter(|e| seen.insert(e.as_str())).map(String::as_str).collect();
    let shown = uniq.iter().take(5).copied().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
    let more = if uniq.len() > 5 { format!(", +{} more", uniq.len() - 5) } else { String::new() };
    eprintln!(
        "warning: component '{}' has {} unicode escape(s) in JSX-text position ({shown}{more}) — a JS escape typed directly between JSX tags renders as the literal backslash-text, NOT the glyph. Use a real UTF-8 character, or wrap it in a JS string like {{\"\\u00b7\"}}.",
        item_label(item),
        leaks.len(),
    );
}

/// Resolve the COMPONENT store with the same flag → env (`BSC_COMPONENT_DIR`) → default
/// (`~/.base-studio-code/components/`) precedence as the shared store CLI, for the custom reads.
/// `crossgraph [--dir D] [--pretty]` — the cross-pillar reference meter (see
/// [`crate::crossgraph`] for why it derives rather than stores).
fn cmd_crossgraph(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut pretty) = (None::<String>, false);
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other => {
                return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}' — usage: bsc ui crossgraph [--dir D] [--pretty]"))
            }
        }
    }
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let components: Vec<serde_json::Value> = store
        .list()
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|raw| serde_json::from_str(raw).ok())
        .collect();
    // The LIVE algorithms store, not the packaged seed: the meter must report what this machine
    // actually holds, and a seed-only read would miss every curated record.
    let implementations = bsc_graph::implementations();
    let out = crate::crossgraph::report(&components, &implementations);
    println!("{}", if pretty {
        serde_json::to_string_pretty(&out).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
    } else {
        serde_json::to_string(&out).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
    });
    Ok(())
}

/// PUBLIC so an in-process reader outside this crate can resolve the library the same way the CLI
/// does — the fleet reads it to render a feature's required COMPONENTS beside its algorithms, and a
/// second resolution path would be a second answer to "where is the store".
pub fn open_component_store(dir: &Option<String>) -> Result<bsc_json_store::Store, String> {
    let dir = bsc_cli_util::resolve_store_path(dir, COMPONENT_SPEC.dir_env, || {
        bsc_util::bsc_base_dir()
            .map(|b| b.join(COMPONENT_SPEC.dir_segment))
            .ok_or_else(|| "could not resolve a home directory; set HOME/USERPROFILE".to_string())
    })?;
    let store = bsc_json_store::Store::new(dir, "component");
    crate::graph_health::set_provided_specifiers(provided_specifiers(&store));
    Ok(store)
}

/// Where a materialization writes the record's CLOSURE — a mirror of `src/` that the generated config
/// aliases `@` to. Underscore-led so it sorts away from the record's own files and can never collide
/// with a real `src/` top-level dir.
const MIRROR_DIR: &str = "_closure";

/// A string as a JSON/JS literal — the generated config is source, so every path it embeds goes through
/// the same escaping the store's own JSON does rather than being pasted between quotes.
fn json_str(s: &str) -> String {
    serde_json::Value::String(s.to_owned()).to_string()
}

/// Materialize ONE component record into `out` and, when `run`, execute its paired tests there.
///
/// The algorithms twin (`bsc graph test`) is the template, and most of the design is settled by it: one
/// record per directory, the record's OWN `vitest.config.ts` so vitest cannot walk up and borrow the
/// repo's aliases and setup file, the module file named after its ORIGINAL basename so the paired test's
/// `./Thing` import resolves, and a refusal — never a vacuous pass — when a record has no paired test.
///
/// One difference from that twin: a component test normally RENDERS, so `jsdom` is the common case here
/// rather than the exception. `@testing-library` is HARNESS — present in the image, and exactly what the
/// isolation rule already allows a record's test to use.
///
/// A second difference, and the reason a composing record can be verified at all: the record does not go
/// in ALONE — its transitive RECORD closure ([`crate::closure`]) is written beside it into a `_closure/`
/// mirror of `src/` that `@` is aliased to. Components compose components, so one-record materialization
/// verified only leaves. An import that resolves to no record is still left out and still fails.
fn materialize_component_test(
    comp: &serde_json::Value,
    out: &str,
    run: bool,
    index: Option<&crate::closure::Index<'_>>,
) -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> {
    let id = comp.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
    let tests = comp.get("tests").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_array).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
    if tests.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!(
            "'{id}' has no paired test — nothing to run. A test that reaches other app modules is not \
             paired onto the record; it belongs on an edge."
        ));
    }
    let src_text = comp.get("srcText").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
    // The ORIGINAL basename, not the record id: a paired test imports `./WorkerModals`, and
    // `worker-modals` would not resolve.
    // BLANK IS MISSING. A retired record carries `src: ""` alongside a real `srcRetired`, and treating
    // the empty string as present produced an empty stem — a component written to `.tsx` and its test to
    // `.test.tsx`, so the test's `./Dropdown` import resolved to nothing and every run failed to collect.
    let non_blank = |k: &str| {
        comp.get(k).and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).map(str::trim).filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
    };
    let stem = non_blank("src")
        .or_else(|| non_blank("srcRetired"))
        .and_then(|p| p.rsplit('/').next())
        .map(|f| f.trim_end_matches(".tsx").trim_end_matches(".ts").to_string())
        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
        .or_else(|| non_blank("name").map(str::to_owned))
        .unwrap_or_else(|| id.to_string());
    let dir = std::path::Path::new(out);
    std::fs::create_dir_all(dir).map_err(|e| format!("cannot create {out}: {e}"))?;
    let module = dir.join(format!("{stem}.tsx"));
    std::fs::write(&module, src_text).map_err(|e| format!("cannot write the component: {e}"))?;
    let mut written = vec![module.to_string_lossy().into_owned()];
    for (i, t) in tests.iter().enumerate() {
        let src = t.get("src").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
        let name = if i == 0 { format!("{stem}.test.tsx") } else { format!("{stem}.{i}.test.tsx") };
        let p = dir.join(&name);
        std::fs::write(&p, src).map_err(|e| format!("cannot write {name}: {e}"))?;
        written.push(p.to_string_lossy().into_owned());
    }
    // A component that needs a DOM should SAY so by reaching for testing-library or `document`; one that
    // does not should never silently receive a DOM it never declared it needed.
    let needs_dom = tests.iter().any(|t| {
        t.get("src")
            .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)
            .is_some_and(|src| src.contains("@testing-library") || src.contains("document"))
    });
    let env = if needs_dom { "jsdom" } else { "node" };
    // The jest-dom MATCHERS are harness, like testing-library itself: `toHaveTextContent` and friends are
    // registered by the repo's `src/test/setup.ts`, which this run deliberately does not load. Without
    // them a rendering record fails with `Invalid Chai property: toHaveTextContent` — a missing matcher,
    // not a broken component. Supplying them here keeps the withheld thing APP CONTEXT (aliases, the
    // store, other modules) rather than the test toolkit.
    let setup = if needs_dom {
        // The `/vitest` entrypoint, not the bare one: the bare import registers against a GLOBAL
        // `expect`, which exists in the repo's suite only because its config sets `globals: true`.
        // Here it produced `ReferenceError: expect is not defined` — again a harness gap reading as a
        // broken record.
        std::fs::write(
            dir.join("setup.ts"),
            "import \"@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest\";\n\
             import { cleanup } from \"@testing-library/react\";\n\
             import { afterEach } from \"vitest\";\n\
             // RTL auto-registers cleanup only when `globals` is on, which this config deliberately is\n\
             // not. Without it every render in a file accumulates and the second test sees the first\n\
             // one's DOM — \"Found multiple elements with the role button\", which reads as a broken\n\
             // component and is a missing afterEach.\n\
             afterEach(cleanup);\n",
        )
            .map_err(|e| format!("cannot write the test setup: {e}"))?;
        written.push(dir.join("setup.ts").to_string_lossy().into_owned());
        ", setupFiles: [\"./setup.ts\"]"
    } else {
        ""
    };
    // The record's DECLARED dependency graph, written into a mirror of `src/`. The record's own code is
    // what is walked — a record whose IMPORTS reach sideways is only revealed by materializing (and
    // running) it, never by reading its test.
    let provides = non_blank("provides");
    // `--no-closure` (index: None) is the STRICT form the runner used to be: nothing but the record. A
    // pass there proves it is a LEAF — kept because that is the RETIRABILITY signal, and it answers a
    // different question from "are this record's dependencies records".
    let cl = index
        .map(|ix| crate::closure::resolve_closure(src_text, id, provides, ix))
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let mirror = dir.join(MIRROR_DIR);
    for m in &cl.members {
        let p = mirror.join(&m.rel);
        if let Some(parent) = p.parent() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).map_err(|e| format!("cannot create {}: {e}", parent.display()))?;
        }
        std::fs::write(&p, &m.source).map_err(|e| format!("cannot write {}: {e}", m.rel))?;
        written.push(p.to_string_lossy().into_owned());
    }
    // ABSOLUTE, forward-slashed. A relative replacement would be re-resolved against the IMPORTER
    // rather than this config, so `@/x` inside a mirror member two levels down would miss.
    let abs = |p: &std::path::Path| -> String {
        let a = if p.is_absolute() {
            p.to_path_buf()
        } else {
            std::env::current_dir().map(|c| c.join(p)).unwrap_or_else(|_| p.to_path_buf())
        };
        a.to_string_lossy().replace('\\', "/")
    };
    let resolve_block = if index.is_none() {
        // No alias at all, so `@/…` resolves to nothing — exactly the contract before the closure.
        String::new()
    } else {
