            bsc_util::emit_ui_activity_in("component", &row.id, &kit);
        }
    }

    if json {
        let out = serde_json::json!({
            "corpus": { "records": store_texts, "files": files, "roots": roots },
            "examined": examined,
            "withUsage": with_usage,
            "unused": unused,
            "applied": apply,
            "assessed": assessed,
            "rows": report.rows.iter().map(|r| serde_json::json!({
                "id": r.id, "name": r.name, "kit": r.kit, "used": r.used,
                "sources": r.sources.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
            })).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        });
        let text = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&out) } else { serde_json::to_string(&out) };
        println!("{}", text.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
        return Ok(());
    }

    // The corpus is printed FIRST and always. A usage number whose scope the reader has to infer is the
    // failure mode this verb exists to end, not one to reproduce in its own output.
    println!("corpus: {store_texts} record(s) + {files} file(s) from {} root(s){}", roots.len(),
        if roots.is_empty() { " — records only; pass --root to add a tree" } else { "" });
    for r in &roots {
        println!("  root: {r}");
    }
    println!("examined {examined} component(s): {with_usage} with usage, {unused} with none");
    for row in report.rows.iter().filter(|r| r.used > 0).take(40) {
        let srcs: Vec<&str> = row.sources.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();
        println!("  {:>4}  {} ({})  [{}]", row.used, row.name, row.id, srcs.join(" · "));
    }
    if with_usage > 40 {
        println!("  … {} more with usage (use --json for all)", with_usage - 40);
    }
    if apply {
        println!("applied: wrote `used` to {examined} record(s); `usageAssessed` to the {assessed} with evidence of use");
        println!(
            "  the other {unused} keep NO assessment on purpose — a scan proves USE, never DISUSE, so \
             they stay reported and unprunable rather than becoming deletable by default"
        );
    } else {
        println!("(read only — pass --apply to write `used`, and `usageAssessed` for the {with_usage} with evidence)");
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Walk `root` for TS/TSX/JS/JSX sources, handing each `(path, text)` to `f`. A missing root is an
/// ERROR, not an empty walk: a mistyped `--root` that silently contributes nothing would report every
/// component in that tree as unused, and `--apply` would then mark them assessed.
fn walk_source_files(
    root: &std::path::Path,
    f: &mut impl FnMut(&std::path::Path, String),
) -> Result<(), String> {
    if !root.exists() {
        return Err(format!("--root '{}' does not exist — a root that contributes nothing would report its components unused", root.display()));
    }
    let mut stack = vec![root.to_path_buf()];
    while let Some(dir) = stack.pop() {
        let entries = match std::fs::read_dir(&dir) {
            Ok(e) => e,
            Err(_) => continue,
        };
        for entry in entries.flatten() {
            let p = entry.path();
            let name = entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
            if p.is_dir() {
                // Never walk into a build output or a dependency tree — they hold megabytes of code that
                // says nothing about whether THIS library's components are used.
                if !matches!(name.as_str(), "node_modules" | "target" | "dist" | ".git" | ".bsc-records") {
                    stack.push(p);
                }
            } else if matches!(
                p.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()),
                Some("ts" | "tsx" | "js" | "jsx")
            ) {
                if let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(&p) {
                    f(&p, text);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// `bsc ui used-by <id>` / `--all` (#3584) — the graph-usage read (composes-inverse). A READ verb, never
/// scope-gated. Single form: one component's composers + count. `--all`: every component ranked by usage,
/// most-used first (`--kit` scopes to one kit) — the whole-library "what is load-bearing" view.
fn cmd_used_by(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut json, mut pretty, mut all, mut kit_filter, mut id) =
        (None::<String>, false, false, false, None::<String>, None::<String>);
    // `--src` adds the LITERAL reference count beside the composes-inverse one. The two together are what
    // separates a MISSING composes edge (count 0, references > 0) from a real dead root (both 0) — the
    // call every `doctor` dangling-branch/orphan finding needs before anything is deleted.
    let mut src = false;
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--json" => json = true,
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            "--all" => all = true,
            "--src" => src = true,
            "--kit" => kit_filter = it.next().cloned(),
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            other if id.is_none() => id = Some(other.to_string()),
            other => return Err(format!("unexpected argument '{other}'")),
        }
    }
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
        store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok()).collect();
    let idx = used_by_index(&comps);
    let count_of = |c: &serde_json::Value| -> usize {
        let key = (
            c.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string(),
            c.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string(),
        );
        idx.get(&key).map_or(0, Vec::len)
    };

    if all {
        // Whole-library ranking, most-used first (id tiebreak for order-stability).
        let mut rows: Vec<serde_json::Value> = comps
            .iter()
            .filter(|c| kit_filter.as_deref().is_none_or(|k| c.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(k)))
            .map(|c| {
                let mut row = serde_json::json!({
                    "id": c.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or(""),
                    "name": c.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or(""),
                    "kit": c.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or(""),
                    "count": count_of(c),
                });
                if src {
                    let cid = c.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
                    let nm = c.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
                    row["srcCount"] = serde_json::json!(src_reference_rows(&comps, cid, nm).len());
                }
                row
            })
            .collect();
        rows.sort_by(|a, b| {
            b["count"].as_u64().cmp(&a["count"].as_u64()).then_with(|| a["id"].as_str().cmp(&b["id"].as_str()))
        });
        if json {
            let out = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&rows) } else { serde_json::to_string(&rows) };
            println!("{}", out.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
        } else {
            println!("components by graph usage (composes-inverse), most-used first:");
            if src {
                println!("  {:>3}  {:>3}  component", "use", "src");
            }
            for r in &rows {
                if src {
                    // A `0  N` row is the interesting one: nothing composes it, yet N components name it.
                    println!(
                        "  {:>3}  {:>3}  {} ({})",
                        r["count"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0),
                        r["srcCount"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0),
                        r["name"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
                        r["kit"].as_str().unwrap_or("")
                    );
                } else {
                    println!("  {:>3}  {} ({})", r["count"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0), r["name"].as_str().unwrap_or(""), r["kit"].as_str().unwrap_or(""));
                }
            }
        }
        return Ok(());
    }

    let id = id.ok_or("usage: bsc ui used-by <id> [--json]  |  bsc ui used-by --all [--kit K]")?;
    let target = comps
        .iter()
        .find(|c| c.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(id.as_str()))
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("no component with id '{id}' (see `bsc ui list --raw`)"))?;
    let key = (
        target.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string(),
        target.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string(),
    );
    let composers = idx.get(&key).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
    let src_refs = if src { src_reference_rows(&comps, &id, &key.1) } else { Vec::new() };
    let mut out = serde_json::json!({
        "id": id,
        "name": key.1,
        "kit": key.0,
        "usedBy": composers,
        "count": composers.len(),
    });
    if src {
        out["srcRefs"] = serde_json::Value::Array(src_refs.clone());
        out["srcCount"] = serde_json::json!(src_refs.len());
    }
    if json {
        let text = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&out) } else { serde_json::to_string(&out) };
        println!("{}", text.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    } else if composers.is_empty() {
        println!("'{}' ({}) is composed by NOTHING in its kit — an orphan candidate (used-by 0).", key.1, key.0);
        if src {
            // THE DISTINCTION THIS FLAG EXISTS FOR: composed by nothing, yet literally referenced, means a
            // MISSING `composes` edge — not a dead root, and not safe to delete.
            if src_refs.is_empty() {
                println!("  …and no literal srcText reference either — a genuine dead root.");
            } else {
                println!(
                    "  …but {} component(s) literally reference it: {} — a MISSING `composes` edge, not a dead root.",
                    src_refs.len(),
                    src_refs.iter().filter_map(|r| r["name"].as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")
                );
            }
        }
    } else {
        println!("'{}' ({}) is composed by {} component(s): {}", key.1, key.0, composers.len(), composers.join(", "));
        if src {
            println!("  literal srcText references: {}", src_refs.len());
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Every OTHER live component whose `srcText`/`source` literally mentions `name`, with the mention kinds
/// broken out — the shared body of `bsc ui refs` and `bsc ui used-by --src`.
///
/// ONE IMPLEMENTATION ON PURPOSE. `used-by` reads the DECLARED composes graph, so a component genuinely
/// used in another's JSX but never added to `composes` reads as an orphan there, indistinguishable from a
/// dead root — which is exactly the call `doctor`'s dangling-branch/orphan findings need made. A second,
/// cruder matcher is why the earlier attempt at this was not landed, so both verbs go through
/// [`crate::usage_scan::name_mentions`] AND through this one loop.
fn src_reference_rows(comps: &[serde_json::Value], id: &str, name: &str) -> Vec<serde_json::Value> {
    let mut hits: Vec<serde_json::Value> = Vec::new();
    if name.is_empty() {
        return hits;
    }
    for c in comps {
        let cid = c.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
        if cid == id || cid.is_empty() {
            continue; // never a reference to itself
        }
        if c.get("suppressed").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_bool) == Some(true) {
            continue; // a tombstone's content is gone; it can only ever dilute
        }
        let mut text = String::new();
        for f in ["srcText", "source"] {
            if let Some(t) = c.get(f).and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) {
                text.push_str(t);
                text.push('\n');
            }
        }
        if text.trim().is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let mentions = crate::usage_scan::name_mentions(&text, name);
        if mentions.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let kind = |k: crate::usage_scan::MentionKind| {
            mentions.iter().filter(|m| std::mem::discriminant(*m) == std::mem::discriminant(&k)).count()
        };
        hits.push(serde_json::json!({
            "id": cid,
            "name": c.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or(""),
            "kit": c.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or(""),
            "jsx": kind(crate::usage_scan::MentionKind::JsxTag),
            "importClause": kind(crate::usage_scan::MentionKind::ImportClause),
            "bare": kind(crate::usage_scan::MentionKind::Bare),
            "total": mentions.len(),
        }));
    }
    hits.sort_by(|a, b| {
        b["total"].as_u64().cmp(&a["total"].as_u64()).then_with(|| a["id"].as_str().cmp(&b["id"].as_str()))
    });
    hits
}

/// `bsc ui refs <id>` (#113) — literal srcText cross-references to a component's NAME, across every
/// OTHER live component in the store. The complement to `used-by`: `used-by` reads the DECLARED
/// composes graph, so a component actually used in another's JSX/import but never added to `composes`
/// reads as an orphan there, indistinguishable from a genuinely dead root. This scans raw srcText for
/// the name itself instead, so the two stop looking identical.
fn cmd_refs(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut json, mut pretty, mut id) = (None::<String>, false, false, None::<String>);
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--json" => json = true,
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            other if id.is_none() => id = Some(other.to_string()),
            other => return Err(format!("unexpected argument '{other}'")),
        }
    }
    let id = id.ok_or("usage: bsc ui refs <id> [--json] [--pretty]")?;
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
        store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok()).collect();
    let target = comps
        .iter()
        .find(|c| c.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(id.as_str()))
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("no component with id '{id}' (see `bsc ui list --raw`)"))?;
    let name = target.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
    if name.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!("component '{id}' has no name to search for"));
    }

    let hits = src_reference_rows(&comps, &id, &name);

    if json {
        let out = serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "name": name, "refs": hits, "count": hits.len() });
        let text = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&out) } else { serde_json::to_string(&out) };
        bsc_util::emit_line(&text.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    } else if hits.is_empty() {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
            "'{name}' ({id}) — no literal srcText reference found in any other component. Genuinely unreferenced, not just missing a `composes` edge.",
        ));
    } else {
        bsc_util::emit_line(&format!("'{name}' ({id}) is literally referenced in {} component(s):", hits.len()));
        for h in &hits {
            bsc_util::emit_line(&format!(
                "  {} ({})  [jsx {} · import {} · bare {}]",
                h["name"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
                h["id"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
                h["jsx"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0),
                h["importClause"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0),
                h["bare"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0),
            ));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The `bsc ui pattern` verbs (#a-pattern-has-no-id-so-the-only-way-to-author-a-sibling-is-to-copy-one)
/// — a convention with an ID, so authoring the fifth sibling is "add a member to <pattern>" rather than
/// "find one and copy it".
fn cmd_pattern(args: &[String], prog: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    let sub = args.first().map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("");
    if sub.is_empty() || sub == "help" {
        print!("{}", bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "pattern"));
        return Ok(());
    }
    // TWO stores are in play here, so `--dir` cannot mean both. It keeps its usual meaning — the
    // COMPONENT store, which is what conformance is computed against — and the pattern records get
    // their own flag. Sharing one flag would silently look for patterns inside the component dir.
    let (mut dir, mut pattern_dir, mut json, mut pretty) = (None::<String>, None::<String>, false, false);
    let (mut id, mut from, mut name, mut threshold) =
        (None::<String>, None::<String>, None::<String>, crate::patterns::DEFAULT_CONFORMANCE);
    let mut it = args[1..].iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--pattern-dir" => pattern_dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--from" => from = it.next().cloned(),
            "--name" => name = it.next().cloned(),
            "--threshold" => {
                threshold = it.next().and_then(|s| s.parse::<f64>().ok()).ok_or("--threshold needs a number in [0,1]")?;
            }
            "--json" => json = true,
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            other if id.is_none() => id = Some(other.to_string()),
            other => return Err(format!("unexpected argument '{other}'")),
        }
    }
    if !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&threshold) {
        return Err("--threshold must be in [0,1]".to_string());
    }
    let pstore = open_pattern_store(&pattern_dir)?;
    let cstore = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
        cstore.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok()).collect();
    let emit = |v: &serde_json::Value| -> Result<(), String> {
        let t = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(v) } else { serde_json::to_string(v) };
        println!("{}", t.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
        Ok(())
    };
    let read = |id: &str| -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> {
        pstore
            .get(id)?
            .as_deref()
            .and_then(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok())
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("no pattern with id '{id}' (see `bsc ui pattern list`)"))
    };

    match sub {
        "list" => {
            let rows: Vec<serde_json::Value> = pstore
                .list()
                .iter()
                .filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok())
                .map(|p| {
                    let n = crate::patterns::conforming(&p, &comps, true).len();
                    serde_json::json!({
                        "id": p["id"], "name": p["name"],
                        "signatureSource": p["signatureSource"], "members": n,
                    })
                })
                .collect();
            if json {
                return emit(&serde_json::Value::Array(rows));
            }
            if rows.is_empty() {
                println!("No named patterns yet. Find the library's conventions with `bsc ui patterns`, then promote one:");
                println!("  bsc ui pattern new <id> --from <a-member-id>");
                return Ok(());
            }
            for r in &rows {
                println!(
                    "  {:<28} {:>3} members  [{}]  {}",
                    r["id"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
                    r["members"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0),
                    r["signatureSource"].as_str().unwrap_or("?"),
                    r["name"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
                );
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        "get" => {
            let id = id.ok_or("usage: bsc ui pattern get <id>")?;
            let p = read(&id)?;
            let members = crate::patterns::conforming(&p, &comps, true);
            let rows: Vec<serde_json::Value> = members
                .iter()
                .map(|m| serde_json::json!({
                    "id": m.id, "name": m.name, "kit": m.kit, "exemplar": m.exemplar,
                    "basis": m.basis.as_str(),
                    "score": m.score.map(|s| (s * 100.0).round() / 100.0),
                }))
                .collect();
            if json {
                let mut out = p.clone();
                out["members"] = serde_json::Value::Array(rows);
                return emit(&out);
            }
            println!("{}  —  {}", p["id"].as_str().unwrap_or(""), p["name"].as_str().unwrap_or(""));
            let list = |v: &serde_json::Value| {
                v.as_array().map(|a| a.iter().filter_map(|x| x.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")).unwrap_or_default()
            };
            println!("  signature ({}):", p["signatureSource"].as_str().unwrap_or("?"));
            println!("    composes: {}", nonempty(&list(&p["signature"]["composes"])));
            println!("    renders:  {}", nonempty(&list(&p["signature"]["skeleton"])));
            let basis = members.first().map(|m| m.basis.as_str()).unwrap_or("scored");
            println!("\n  {} member(s), matched by {basis}:", members.len());
            for m in &members {
                println!(
                    "    {}{}{}",
                    m.name,
                    if m.exemplar { "  (exemplar)" } else { "" },
                    m.score.map(|s| format!("  {:.0}%", s * 100.0)).unwrap_or_default(),
                );
            }
            if basis == "containment" {
                println!(
                    "\n  NOTE: matched by CONTAINMENT of a declared signature, which is looser than scoring\n  against exemplars — anything holding these parts matches. Promote a real member with\n  `bsc ui pattern new {} --from <id>` to tighten it.",
                    p["id"].as_str().unwrap_or("<id>"),
                );
            }
            println!("\n  To author into this pattern, read an exemplar: `bsc ui get <exemplar-id>`");
            Ok(())
        }
        "new" => {
            let id = id.ok_or("usage: bsc ui pattern new <id> --from <member-id> [--name \"...\"]")?;
            let from = from.ok_or(
                "bsc ui pattern new needs --from <member-id>: a pattern is PROMOTED from a cluster `bsc ui patterns` found, and any one member names it",
            )?;
            if pstore.get(&id)?.is_some() {
                return Err(format!("a pattern with id '{id}' already exists — `bsc ui pattern get {id}`, or pick another id"));
            }
            // The cluster holding <from> IS the pattern. Reusing the sweep means a promoted pattern's
            // members are the cluster that was reported, not a differently-drawn set.
            let clusters = crate::similarity::shape_clusters(&comps, threshold, 2);
            let cluster = clusters
                .iter()
                .find(|c| {
                    c["members"].as_array().is_some_and(|a| {
                        a.iter().any(|m| m["id"].as_str() == Some(from.as_str()))
                    })
                })
                .ok_or_else(|| format!(
                    "'{from}' is not in any cluster at threshold {threshold} — nothing to promote. Check `bsc ui patterns --threshold {threshold}`, or lower the bar."
                ))?;
            let member_ids: Vec<&str> =
                cluster["members"].as_array().into_iter().flatten().filter_map(|m| m["id"].as_str()).collect();
            let members: Vec<serde_json::Value> = comps
                .iter()
                .filter(|c| member_ids.contains(&c.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("")))
                .cloned()
                .collect();
            let display = name.unwrap_or_else(|| id.clone());
            let rec = crate::patterns::derive(&id, &display, &members, threshold);
            pstore.set(&id, &serde_json::to_string(&rec).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?)?;
            if json {
                return emit(&rec);
            }
            println!("{id}  —  promoted from the cluster containing '{from}' ({} exemplars)", members.len());
            println!("  bsc ui pattern get {id}");
            Ok(())
        }
        "remove" => {
            let id = id.ok_or("usage: bsc ui pattern remove <id>")?;
            read(&id)?; // a removal of nothing is an error, not a silent success
            pstore.remove(&id)?;
            println!("{id} removed");
            Ok(())
        }
        "of" => {
            // The REVERSE lookup: which convention does this record already belong to? The read a
            // session makes when it has a component in hand, not a pattern.
            let id = id.ok_or("usage: bsc ui pattern of <component-id>")?;
            if !comps.iter().any(|c| c.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(id.as_str())) {
                return Err(format!("no component with id '{id}' (see `bsc ui list --raw`)"));
            }
            let hits: Vec<serde_json::Value> = pstore
                .list()
                .iter()
                .filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok())
                .filter_map(|p| {
                    let m = crate::patterns::conforming(&p, &comps, true);
                    m.iter().find(|c| c.id == id).map(|c| serde_json::json!({
                        "pattern": p["id"], "name": p["name"], "basis": c.basis.as_str(),
                        "score": c.score.map(|s| (s * 100.0).round() / 100.0), "exemplar": c.exemplar,
                    }))
                })
                .collect();
            if json {
                return emit(&serde_json::Value::Array(hits));
            }
            if hits.is_empty() {
                println!("'{id}' belongs to no named pattern.");
                println!("  If it should: `bsc ui similar {id} --shape` to see what it is built like,");
                println!("  then `bsc ui pattern new <pattern-id> --from {id}` to name the convention.");
                return Ok(());
            }
            for h in &hits {
                println!(
                    "  {} ({}){}",
                    h["pattern"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
                    h["basis"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
                    if h["exemplar"].as_bool().unwrap_or(false) { "  — an exemplar" } else { "" },
                );
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        other => Err(format!("unknown `pattern` command '{other}' — try list | get | new | remove | of")),
    }
}

fn nonempty(s: &str) -> String {
    if s.is_empty() { "—".to_string() } else { s.to_string() }
}

fn open_pattern_store(dir: &Option<String>) -> Result<bsc_json_store::Store, String> {
    let dir = bsc_cli_util::resolve_store_path(dir, "BSC_COMPONENT_PATTERN_DIR", || {
        bsc_util::bsc_base_dir()
            .map(|b| b.join("patterns"))
            .ok_or_else(|| "could not resolve a home directory; set HOME/USERPROFILE".to_string())
    })?;
    Ok(bsc_json_store::Store::new(dir, "pattern"))
}

/// `bsc ui patterns` — the whole-library shape sweep
/// (#shape-similarity-is-pairwise-so-a-pattern-can-only-be-confirmed-never-found).
///
/// `similar --shape` needs a seed, so it can only CONFIRM a pattern someone already suspects. This
/// returns the equivalence classes themselves. Prints the threshold and the counts before the rows —
/// a sweep whose bar is invisible reads as "this is everything".
fn cmd_patterns(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut json, mut pretty, mut kit_filter) = (None::<String>, false, false, None::<String>);
    let (mut threshold, mut min_size) = (PATTERN_THRESHOLD, 2usize);
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--kit" => kit_filter = it.next().cloned(),
            "--threshold" => {
                threshold = it.next().and_then(|s| s.parse::<f64>().ok()).ok_or("--threshold needs a number in [0,1]")?;
            }
            "--min" => {
                min_size = it.next().and_then(|s| s.parse::<usize>().ok()).filter(|n| *n >= 2)
                    .ok_or("--min needs an integer of 2 or more (a cluster of one is not a pattern)")?;
            }
            "--json" => json = true,
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other => return Err(format!("unexpected argument '{other}'")),
        }
    }
    if !(0.0..=1.0).contains(&threshold) {
        return Err("--threshold must be in [0,1]".to_string());
    }
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> = store
        .list()
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok())
        .filter(|c| kit_filter.as_deref().is_none_or(|k| c.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(k)))
        .collect();
    let clusters = crate::similarity::shape_clusters(&comps, threshold, min_size);
    if json {
        let out = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&clusters) } else { serde_json::to_string(&clusters) };
        println!("{}", out.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
        return Ok(());
    }
    let clustered: usize = clusters.iter().filter_map(|c| c["size"].as_u64()).sum::<u64>() as usize;
    println!(
        "{} structural pattern(s) over {} record(s) — {} of {} scanned are in one, at threshold {threshold:.2} (min {min_size}).",
        clusters.len(),
        clustered,
        clustered,
        comps.len(),
    );
    if clusters.is_empty() {
        println!("Nothing clusters at that bar. Lower --threshold to see looser groupings.");
        return Ok(());
    }
    for c in &clusters {
        let sig = &c["signature"];
        let list = |v: &serde_json::Value| {
            v.as_array().map(|a| a.iter().filter_map(|x| x.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")).unwrap_or_default()
        };
        let (composes, skeleton) = (list(&sig["composes"]), list(&sig["skeleton"]));
        let cohesion = c["cohesion"].as_f64().unwrap_or(0.0);
        println!(
            "\n  {} members · cohesion {:.0}%{}",
            c["size"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0),
            cohesion * 100.0,
            // Connected components chain; below the bar the group is related, not uniform.
            if cohesion + 1e-9 < threshold { "  ← CHAINED (some members are not alike)" } else { "" },
        );
        println!("    composes: {}", if composes.is_empty() { "—".into() } else { composes });
        println!("    renders:  {}", if skeleton.is_empty() { "—".into() } else { skeleton });
        let names: Vec<&str> =
            c["members"].as_array().into_iter().flatten().filter_map(|m| m["name"].as_str()).collect();
        println!("    {}", names.join(", "));
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// `bsc ui exports` (#a-record-holds-one-item-not-a-module-of-them) — a record's PUBLIC SURFACE, grouped
/// into the ITEMS its exports name.
///
/// The read behind the library's one-record-one-item rule, and the one nothing else could answer:
/// `bsc ui get --field /srcText` hands back the whole module and `bsc ui doctor` reports only the sharp
/// end of it. `--all` is the unbounded ranking — deliberately no threshold, because the interesting tail
/// (a component plus one domain type) is exactly the part a bar would hide.
fn cmd_exports(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut json, mut pretty, mut all, mut kit_filter, mut id) =
        (None::<String>, false, false, false, None::<String>, None::<String>);
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--json" => json = true,
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            "--all" => all = true,
            "--kit" => kit_filter = it.next().cloned(),
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            other if id.is_none() => id = Some(other.to_string()),
            other => return Err(format!("unexpected argument '{other}'")),
        }
    }
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
        store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok()).collect();
    let str_of = |c: &serde_json::Value, k: &str| {
        c.get(k).and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string()
    };
    // The surface of ONE record, plus the fields a caller needs to identify it.
    let surface_of = |c: &serde_json::Value| {
        let src = str_of(c, "srcText");
        let name = str_of(c, "name");
        let defined: std::collections::BTreeSet<String> =
            crate::graph_health::top_level_components(&src).into_iter().collect();
        let s = crate::exports::surface(&src, &name, &defined);
        (name, s)
    };

    if all {
        let mut rows: Vec<serde_json::Value> = comps
            .iter()
            .filter(|c| kit_filter.as_deref().is_none_or(|k| str_of(c, "kitId") == k))
            .filter(|c| !str_of(c, "srcText").trim().is_empty())
            .map(|c| {
                let (name, s) = surface_of(c);
                serde_json::json!({
                    "id": str_of(c, "id"),
                    "name": name,
                    "kit": str_of(c, "kitId"),
                    "items": s.items.len(),
                    "exports": s.exports.len(),
                    "foreign": s.foreign().iter().map(|e| e.name.clone()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
                    "foreignComponents": s.foreign_components().iter().map(|e| e.name.clone()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
                })
            })
            .collect();
        rows.sort_by(|a, b| {
            b["items"].as_u64().cmp(&a["items"].as_u64()).then_with(|| a["id"].as_str().cmp(&b["id"].as_str()))
        });
        if json {
            let out = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&rows) } else { serde_json::to_string(&rows) };
            println!("{}", out.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
        } else {
            println!("records by ITEM count (a name and its decorations are one item), most-first:");
            for r in &rows {
                let fc = r["foreignComponents"].as_array().map_or(0, Vec::len);
                println!(
                    "  {:>3} items  {:>3} exports  {}{} ({})",
                    r["items"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0),
                    r["exports"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0),
                    r["name"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
                    if fc > 0 { format!("  ← {fc} foreign component(s)") } else { String::new() },
                    r["kit"].as_str().unwrap_or(""),
                );
            }
        }
        return Ok(());
    }

    let id = id.ok_or("usage: bsc ui exports <id> [--json]  |  bsc ui exports --all [--kit K]")?;
    let target = comps
        .iter()
        .find(|c| str_of(c, "id") == id)
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("no component with id '{id}' (see `bsc ui list --raw`)"))?;
    let (name, s) = surface_of(target);
    let out = serde_json::json!({
        "id": id,
        "name": name,
        "kit": str_of(target, "kitId"),
        "items": s.items,
        "exports": s.exports.iter().map(|e| serde_json::json!({
            "name": e.name, "item": e.item, "component": e.component, "foreign": e.foreign,
        })).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        "foreignComponents": s.foreign_components().iter().map(|e| e.name.clone()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    });
    if json {
        let text = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&out) } else { serde_json::to_string(&out) };
        println!("{}", text.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    } else if s.exports.is_empty() {
        println!("'{name}' exports NOTHING readable — a spec-only record, a built-in whose source is packaged elsewhere, or a module whose only export is `export * from`.");
    } else {
        println!("'{}' — {} export(s) naming {} item(s):", name, s.exports.len(), s.items.len());
        for e in &s.exports {
            println!(
                "  {:<28} item={:<20}{}{}",
                e.name,
                e.item,
                if e.component { "  component" } else { "" },
                if e.foreign { "  FOREIGN" } else { "" },
            );
        }
        let fc = s.foreign_components();
        if !fc.is_empty() {
            println!(
                "\n{} component(s) beyond `{}` live here: {} — each is reachable by import but has no record, never previews, and is never a `composes` edge.",
                fc.len(),
                name,
                fc.iter().map(|e| e.name.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", "),
            );
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The `doctor --fix` optimize action (#2679, #3089 merge) — the curator's mechanical, SAFE graph
/// optimization as a COMMAND (epic #3087: 'keep the graph minimal' is a tool, not hand-organization).
/// Two lossless steps, dry-run unless `apply`:
///   1. MERGE byte-identical duplicates (`graph_health::merge_plan`) — fold each group into the
///      most-`used` canonical, repointing composers; only byte-identical, never a same-`wraps` dup. A
///      removed dup that is itself `builtin: true` is retired via [`retire_component`] — a suppression
///      tombstone, not a bare delete — so it does not reappear on the next hydrate (#96).
///   2. PRUNE the GUARDED dead roots (`graph_health::prune_plan`) — orphan/dead-root only, never a
///      `used > 0`, and never a `page` / packaged built-in / anything at all while the usage index is
///      unpopulated (#3087). A guarded candidate is still reported, just never auto-removed.
///
/// Cycles + same-`wraps` (differing-source) duplicates need the curator's SEMANTIC call, so they're only
/// surfaced as a note — never auto-resolved here.
///
/// `usage_reference` is what the prune guard's `usage_index_populated` check is judged against — pass
/// `comps` itself when there's no separate enrichment (every direct caller before #3888) or the
/// UN-enriched store read when `comps`' `used` has been widened by `usage_sources::enrich_used` for
/// finding-suppression purposes (`cmd_doctor`): see [`crate::graph_health::prune_plan_with`] for why
/// those two must never be the same list once one of them is ephemeral.
fn doctor_fix(
    store: &bsc_json_store::Store,
    comps: &[serde_json::Value],
    usage_reference: &[serde_json::Value],
    apply: bool,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let plan = crate::graph_health::merge_plan(comps);
    // Dead roots to prune, minus anything a merge already removes (never double-handle an id).
    let merged_ids: std::collections::BTreeSet<String> =
        plan.groups.iter().flat_map(|g| g.removed.iter().map(|(id, _)| id.clone())).collect();
    let prune_plan = crate::graph_health::prune_plan_with(comps, usage_reference);
    let prunable: Vec<_> =
        prune_plan.prune.into_iter().filter(|p| !merged_ids.contains(&p.id)).collect();
    let skipped = prune_plan.skipped;
    let cycles = crate::graph_health::analyze(comps).iter().filter(|f| f.category == "cycle").count();
    let manual_note = || {
        if cycles > 0 {
            println!("  ({cycles} cycle(s) need a manual break; same-`wraps` duplicates need the curator's semantic call — see `bsc ui doctor`).");
        }
    };
    // #3087: the guards are LOUD — a withheld candidate is named with the guard that saved it, so the
    // report never silently shrinks and a genuine dead page/seed is still visible to the human.
    let guard_note = || {
        if skipped.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        println!(
            "  {} dead-root finding(s) HELD BACK by the prune guards (#3087) — still reported by `bsc ui doctor`, never auto-removed:",
            skipped.len()
        );
        for s in &skipped {
            println!("    · {} ({}) — {}", s.name, s.id, s.guard);
        }
    };

    if plan.groups.is_empty() && prunable.is_empty() {
        if skipped.is_empty() {
            println!("✓ nothing to auto-optimize — no byte-identical duplicates and no dead roots.");
        } else {
            println!("✓ nothing SAFE to auto-optimize — no byte-identical duplicates, and every dead-root candidate is guarded.");
        }
        guard_note();
        manual_note();
        return Ok(());
    }

    if !apply {
        if !plan.groups.is_empty() {
            println!("DRY RUN — {} byte-identical duplicate group(s) WOULD be merged (pass --yes to apply):", plan.groups.len());
            for g in &plan.groups {
                let names: Vec<&str> = g.removed.iter().map(|(_, n)| n.as_str()).collect();
                println!("  merge {} → {} ({})", names.join(", "), g.canonical_name, g.canonical_id);
            }
            if !plan.repoints.is_empty() {
                println!("  ({} composer(s) would repoint to the canonical)", plan.repoints.len());
            }
        }
        if !prunable.is_empty() {
            println!("DRY RUN — {} dead node(s) WOULD be pruned:", prunable.len());
            for p in &prunable {
                println!("  - {} ({}) — {}", p.name, p.id, p.reason);
            }
        }
        guard_note();
        manual_note();
        return Ok(());
    }

    // APPLY — merge first (repoint composers, then drop the dups), then prune dead roots. A repoint IS
    // a record edit, so stamp it (#3164): bump rev + updatedAt + updatedBy (writer from $BSC_UI_WRITER,
    // else "unknown"), like every other `bsc ui` write.
    let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(None);
    for (id, rec) in &plan.repoints {
        stamped_set(store, id, rec.clone(), &writer)?;
    }
    // A removed dup can itself be a packaged BUILTIN (two builtins can ship byte-identical `srcText`) —
    // `retire_component` needs to know which, to tombstone rather than bare-delete it (#96).
    let builtin_by_id: std::collections::BTreeMap<&str, bool> = comps
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|c| {
            c.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).map(|id| {
                (id, c.get("builtin").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_bool) == Some(true))
            })
        })
        .collect();
    let mut merged = 0usize;
    let mut skipped_claims = 0usize;
    for g in &plan.groups {
        for (id, name) in &g.removed {
            let builtin = builtin_by_id.get(id.as_str()).copied().unwrap_or(false);
            // A refused retirement SKIPS this pair and says why. It must not `?` out: the repoints above
            // are already written, so aborting here leaves the store half-folded — references pointing at
            // the survivor while the record they came from is still live. One unsafe pair is not a reason
            // to abandon the safe ones, and a silent skip is not an option either (#no-silent-caps).
            match retire_component(store, id, builtin, Some(&g.canonical_id)) {
                Ok(what) => {
                    println!("merged {name} ({id}) → {} [{}]", g.canonical_name, what.as_str());
                    merged += 1;
                }
                Err(why) => {
                    println!("SKIPPED {name} ({id}) → {}: {why}", g.canonical_name);
                    skipped_claims += 1;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    let mut pruned = 0usize;
    for p in &prunable {
        store.remove(&p.id)?;
        println!("pruned {} ({})", p.name, p.id);
        pruned += 1;
    }
    if skipped_claims > 0 {
        println!(
            "{skipped_claims} merge(s) SKIPPED — each would have orphaned a specifier something still imports. \
             Re-point those importers (or give the survivor the claim) and re-run."
        );
    }
    println!("optimized: merged {merged} duplicate(s), pruned {pruned} dead node(s). Re-run `bsc ui doctor` — an optimization can surface more.");
    guard_note();
    Ok(())
}

/// The escape-hatch clause every rule message carries — MUST stay byte-identical to
/// `src/features/components/lib/rules.ts` `ESCAPE_HATCH` (the two generators are one contract).
const ESCAPE_HATCH: &str = "If truly required, add `// eslint-disable-next-line <rule> -- <reason>`.";

/// `eslint-preset [--kit K] [--pretty]` — read the component store + emit the kit's lint rules as an
/// eslint config. The deterministic, agent-reachable twin of the frontend `toEslintPreset` (rules.ts);
/// the planner runs it to bake enforcement into a generated app.
fn cmd_eslint_preset(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut kit, mut dir, mut pretty) = (None::<String>, None::<String>, false);
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--kit" => kit = it.next().cloned(),
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    let store = match dir {
        Some(d) => bsc_json_store::Store::new(d, "component"),
        None => bsc_json_store::Store::open_default("components", "component")?,
    };
    let comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
        store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str(j).ok()).collect();
    let scoped: Vec<&serde_json::Value> = comps
        .iter()
        .filter(|c| match kit.as_deref() {
            Some(k) => c.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str) == Some(k),
            None => true,
        })
        .collect();
    let preset = eslint_preset(&scoped);
    let json = if pretty {
        serde_json::to_string_pretty(&preset)
    } else {
        serde_json::to_string(&preset)
    };
    println!("{}", json.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// One resolved lint rule (derived-from-`wraps` or authored), before it's rendered to eslint config.
struct Rule {
    kind: String,
    target: String,
    use_: String,
    message: Option<String>,
}

/// Collect a scoped set of components into their deduped lint rules — derived (`wraps`) first, then
/// authored `rules` (which OVERRIDE a derived rule for the same kind+target). A `BTreeMap` keys by
/// `kind:target` so the output is deterministic (stable generation).
fn collect_rules(components: &[&serde_json::Value]) -> Vec<Rule> {
    use serde_json::Value;
    let mut by_key: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, Rule> = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
    for c in components {
        if let Some(w) = c.get("wraps").and_then(Value::as_str).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()) {
            let name = c.get("name").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
            by_key.insert(
                format!("forbid-element:{w}"),
                Rule { kind: "forbid-element".into(), target: w.into(), use_: name, message: None },
            );
        }
    }
    for c in components {
        if let Some(rules) = c.get("rules").and_then(Value::as_array) {
            for r in rules {
                let kind = r.get("kind").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
                let target = r.get("target").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
                if target.is_empty() || !matches!(kind, "forbid-element" | "forbid-import") {
                    continue;
                }
                by_key.insert(
                    format!("{kind}:{target}"),
                    Rule {
                        kind: kind.into(),
                        target: target.into(),
                        use_: r.get("use").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default().into(),
                        message: r.get("message").and_then(Value::as_str).map(String::from),
                    },
                );
            }
        }
    }
    by_key.into_values().collect()
}

fn rule_message(r: &Rule) -> String {
    if let Some(m) = &r.message {
        return m.clone();
    }
    let base = if r.kind == "forbid-element" {
        format!("Use the kit's <{}> instead of a raw <{}>.", r.use_, r.target)
    } else {
        format!("Import {} from the kit instead of \"{}\".", r.use_, r.target)
    };
    format!("{base} {ESCAPE_HATCH}")
}

/// Compile a scoped component set into `{ rules: { … } }` — mirrors `toEslintPreset` in rules.ts.
fn eslint_preset(components: &[&serde_json::Value]) -> serde_json::Value {
    use serde_json::{json, Value};
    let mut syntax: Vec<Value> = vec![json!("error")];
    let mut import_paths: Vec<Value> = Vec::new();
    for r in &collect_rules(components) {
        if r.kind == "forbid-element" {
            syntax.push(json!({
                "selector": format!("JSXOpeningElement[name.name='{}']", r.target),
                "message": rule_message(r),
            }));
        } else {
            import_paths.push(json!({ "name": r.target, "message": rule_message(r) }));
        }
    }
    let mut rules = serde_json::Map::new();
    if syntax.len() > 1 {
        rules.insert("no-restricted-syntax".into(), Value::Array(syntax));
    }
    if !import_paths.is_empty() {
        rules.insert("no-restricted-imports".into(), json!(["error", { "paths": import_paths }]));
    }
    json!({ "rules": Value::Object(rules) })
}

/// `usage list|add|remove` — the kit-usage consumer index (#2277). Defaults to `list`. A flat edge
/// store (crate::usage), not a per-record CRUD, so it's handled here rather than via the shared store CLI.
fn cmd_usage(args: &[String], prog: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    let json = args.iter().any(|a| a == "--json");
    let positional: Vec<&str> = args.iter().filter(|a| !a.starts_with("--")).map(String::as_str).collect();
    match positional.first().copied().unwrap_or("list") {
        "list" => {
            let edges = crate::usage::load();
            if json {
                let arr: Vec<serde_json::Value> = edges
                    .iter()
                    .map(|u| serde_json::json!({ "id": u.id, "projectKey": u.project_key, "kitId": u.kit_id }))
                    .collect();
                println!("{}", serde_json::to_string(&arr).unwrap_or_else(|_| "[]".into()));
            } else if edges.is_empty() {
                println!("(no kit usage)");
            } else {
                for u in &edges {
                    println!("{}\t{} uses {}", u.id, u.project_key, u.kit_id);
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        "add" => {
            let usage_err = || format!("usage: {prog} usage add <projectKey> <kitId>");
            let project_key = positional.get(1).ok_or_else(usage_err)?;
            let kit_id = positional.get(2).ok_or_else(usage_err)?;
            println!("{}", crate::usage::add(project_key, kit_id)?);
            Ok(())
        }
        "remove" => {
            let id = positional.get(1).ok_or_else(|| format!("usage: {prog} usage remove <id>"))?;
            crate::usage::remove(id)?;
            if !json {
                println!("removed {id}");
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        other => Err(format!(
            "unknown usage command '{other}'\n\n{}",
            bsc_cli_util::help_for(prog, TAGLINE, COMPONENT_COMMANDS, "usage")
        )),
    }
}

// ── preview observability (#3165) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Two custom verbs make the Design Studio's build-and-iframe preview inspectable from a session's shell:
//   • `preview-props` prints the schema-derived sample props the harness passes a component, per state —
//     the pure sampler (`crate::preview_props`) mirrors the TS `samplePropValue`/`bootstrapSource`, pinned
//     to it by a shared golden fixture (both sides assert it).
//   • `preview-error` / `preview-errors` are the write/read of a durable JSONL log the frontend appends to
//     when the sandboxed iframe posts `{__preview:"error"}` (`crate::preview_errors`) — so a preview
//     runtime throw is observable, not just an ephemeral in-pane banner.

/// `preview-props <id> [--state S] [--dir D] [--pretty]` (#3165) — print the schema-derived sample props
/// the live preview harness passes <id>'s component, per data-state. A read verb (never scope-gated).
fn cmd_preview_props(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut pretty, mut state, mut id) = (None::<String>, false, None::<String>, None::<String>);
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--state" => state = it.next().cloned(),
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            positional => id = Some(positional.to_string()),
        }
    }
    let id = id.ok_or("usage: preview-props <id> [--state loaded|empty|loading] [--pretty]")?;
    if let Some(s) = &state {
        if !matches!(s.as_str(), "loaded" | "empty" | "loading") {
            return Err(format!("unknown state '{s}' — one of loaded | empty | loading"));
        }
    }
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let raw = store.get(&id)?.ok_or_else(|| format!("no component '{id}'"))?;
    // #3545: inspecting a component's preview props FOCUSES it in the Design Studio (a `ui-focus`, so the
    // preview follows Claude's working focus). A read → no re-hydrate. No-op off a designer session.
    bsc_util::emit_ui_focus("component", &id);
    let rec: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let name = rec.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or(&id);
    let role = rec.get("role").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
    let props = crate::preview_props::props_from_record(&rec);
    let src = crate::preview_props::source_from_record(&rec);
    let mut states = crate::preview_props::preview_props_states(name, &props, &src);
    // --state narrows the states object to just the one requested (the shape stays `{ <state>: {…} }`).
    if let Some(s) = &state {
        let picked = states.get(s).cloned().unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null);
        states = serde_json::json!({ s: picked });
    }
    let out = serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "name": name, "role": role, "states": states });
    let json = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&out) } else { serde_json::to_string(&out) };
    println!("{}", json.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// `preview-errors [-n N] [--pretty]` (#3165) — tail the last N captured preview runtime errors. Read-only.
/// `scan-cache [get|put|clear]` — the preview sweep's durable memory.
///
/// `get` prints the whole map so the frontend can seed BOTH halves in one read: the signatures it may
/// skip, and the statuses that badge the graph before anything is rebuilt.
///
/// `put` reads a JSON object of `{ <id>: { sig, status, stateBlanks } }` and MERGES it, because the sweep
/// flushes in batches and each write carries only what it just finished.
fn cmd_scan_cache(args: &[String], prog: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    let pretty = args.iter().any(|a| a == "--pretty");
    let verb = args.iter().find(|a| !a.starts_with('-')).map(String::as_str).unwrap_or("get");
    match verb {
        "get" => {
            // Through the SHARED emitter, not `println!`
            // (#the-scan-cache-read-is-the-last-boot-spawn): this read is answered by the warm `bsc
            // serve` child, which captures a request's output off the same stdout it speaks its
            // protocol on. `emit_line` is byte-identical to the `println!` it replaces when nothing
            // is capturing — which is what keeps the served and one-shot answers interchangeable, and
            // it is the same helper this crate's other JSON read already uses. `put`/`clear` below
            // are WRITES and stay one-shot, so their printing is left alone.
            let all = serde_json::Value::Object(crate::scan_cache::load());
            bsc_util::emit_line(&if pretty {
                serde_json::to_string_pretty(&all).unwrap_or_else(|_| "{}".into())
            } else {
                serde_json::to_string(&all).unwrap_or_else(|_| "{}".into())
            });
            Ok(())
        }
        "put" => {
            use std::io::Read;
            let mut buf = String::new();
            std::io::stdin().read_to_string(&mut buf).map_err(|e| format!("reading stdin: {e}"))?;
            let parsed: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(buf.trim())
                .map_err(|e| format!("{prog} scan-cache put: stdin is not JSON: {e}"))?;
            let serde_json::Value::Object(entries) = parsed else {
                return Err(format!("{prog} scan-cache put: expected a JSON OBJECT of {{ id: entry }}"));
            };
            let n = entries.len();
            crate::scan_cache::put(entries)?;
            println!("{n}");
            Ok(())
        }
        "clear" => {
            crate::scan_cache::clear()?;
            println!("cleared");
            Ok(())
        }
        other => Err(format!("{prog} scan-cache: unknown verb '{other}' (get | put | clear)")),
    }
}

fn cmd_preview_errors(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut n, mut pretty) = (20usize, false);
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "-n" | "--limit" => {
                n = it.next().and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).ok_or("-n needs a number")?;
            }
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other if other.starts_with('-') => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            other => return Err(format!("unexpected argument '{other}'")),
        }
    }
    let arr = serde_json::Value::Array(crate::preview_errors::tail(n));
    let json = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&arr) } else { serde_json::to_string(&arr) };
    println!("{}", json.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// `preview-error <id>` (#3165) — append a preview-error record (message read from stdin) to the durable
/// log `preview-errors` tails. A diagnostic append, so NOT ui-scope gated.
fn cmd_preview_error(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    // #3737: `preview-error clear <id>` clears a stale render-error directly (without re-writing the
    // component), for when the recorded error no longer reflects the current source. Everything else is
    // the RECORD form: `preview-error <id>` with the message on stdin.
    if args.first().map(String::as_str) == Some("clear") {
        let id = args.get(1).ok_or("usage: preview-error clear <id>")?;
        crate::preview_errors::clear(id)?;
        println!("{id}");
        return Ok(());
    }
    let id = args
        .iter()
        .find(|a| !a.starts_with("--"))
        .ok_or("usage: preview-error <id>   # error message / stack trace on stdin (or `clear <id>`)")?;
    // REFUSE AN ID THAT IS NOT A COMPONENT, and do it BEFORE touching stdin
    // (#preview-error-list-silently-records-a-component-named-list).
    //
    // The listing verb is `preview-errors` — PLURAL — so the natural-looking `preview-error list` parses
    // as "record an error for the component `list`", then BLOCKS on stdin (ten minutes, in the run that
    // found this) and, on an empty stdin, silently appends a junk row for a component that does not
    // exist. That row lands in the very log someone reads to decide whether a render error is stale,
    // which is the question requests #57 and #60 are about — a bad place to be quietly wrong.
    //
    // Validating first is what removes the hang: a mistyped verb fails immediately instead of waiting
    // for input that is never coming. The frontend only ever records against a real component, so this
    // refuses nothing legitimate. `clear` is handled above and stays unvalidated on purpose — an
    // already-junk row must always be clearable, including one written before this check existed.
    // A store that cannot be opened at all is NOT treated as "unknown id" — the record path must keep
    // working when the store is unreachable, exactly as it did before this check.
    let known: Option<Vec<String>> = open_component_store(&None).ok().map(|s| {
        s.list()
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok())
            .filter_map(|v| v.get("id").and_then(|x| x.as_str()).map(str::to_string))
            .collect()
    });
    if let Some(ids) = known {
        if !ids.iter().any(|k| k == id) {
            return Err(format!(
                "preview-error: no component '{id}' — nothing to record against.\n\
                 To LIST captured errors use the plural verb: `bsc ui preview-errors`.\n\
                 To clear a stale one: `bsc ui preview-error clear <id>`."
            ));
        }
    }
    let mut message = String::new();
    std::io::stdin().read_to_string(&mut message).map_err(|e| format!("cannot read stdin: {e}"))?;
    crate::preview_errors::record(id, message.trim())?;
    println!("{id}");
    Ok(())
}

// ── component animations (#2869, epic #2865) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// The AUTHORING surface for the motion an LLM defines as DATA on a `ComponentRecord.animations` (the
// render engine is `src/shared/ui/kit/animations.ts`). Because this compiles LLM-authored data into
// live CSS, the validator is a CLOSED SAFETY GRAMMAR that MUST mirror animations.ts exactly:
//   SAFE_IDENT  /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/   — the animation name
//   SAFE_STOP   /^(from|to|\d{1,3}%)$/ — every keyframe stop selector
//   SAFE_PROP   /^[a-z-]+$/           — every declaration property
//   UNSAFE_VALUE /[;{}<>\\]|url\(|expression\(|@import|\/\*/i — refused in any value (case-insensitive)
// The render engine SKIPS anything failing these (defense in depth); the authoring path REJECTS it
// with a clear message so a designer fixes it at write time instead of shipping silently-dropped motion.

/// A safe CSS identifier — `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$` (mirrors animations.ts `SAFE_IDENT`).
fn is_safe_ident(s: &str) -> bool {
    let mut chars = s.chars();
    match chars.next() {
        Some(c) if c.is_ascii_lowercase() => {}
        _ => return false,
    }
    chars.all(|c| c.is_ascii_lowercase() || c.is_ascii_digit() || c == '-')
}

/// A keyframe stop selector — `from`, `to`, or a 1–3 digit percentage (mirrors `SAFE_STOP`).
fn is_safe_stop(s: &str) -> bool {
    if s == "from" || s == "to" {
        return true;
    }
    match s.strip_suffix('%') {
        Some(num) => (1..=3).contains(&num.len()) && num.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()),
        None => false,
    }
}

/// A CSS declaration property — `^[a-z-]+$`, non-empty (mirrors `SAFE_PROP`).
fn is_safe_prop(s: &str) -> bool {
    !s.is_empty() && s.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_lowercase() || c == '-')
}

/// A safe CHILD selector for the applying rule (#3054) — ONLY selector-safe characters, so it cannot
/// break out of the selector position into a declaration / new rule / comment (no `{ } ; < \ /`).
/// Mirrors animations.ts `SAFE_SELECTOR` (classes, tags, `#`ids, `>`/space/`+`/`~` combinators,
/// `[attr="v"]`, `:nth-child(2n)`, `,` lists, `*`).
fn is_safe_selector(s: &str) -> bool {
    !s.is_empty()
        && s.chars().all(|c| {
            c.is_ascii_alphanumeric()
                || matches!(
                    c,
                    ' ' | '.' | '_' | '#' | '>' | '[' | ']' | '=' | '"' | '\'' | '-' | ':' | '(' | ')'
                        | ',' | '*' | '+' | '~'
                )
        })
}

/// A declaration/duration/easing VALUE that cannot end the declaration or inject CSS — non-empty and
/// free of any `UNSAFE_VALUE` sequence (case-insensitive), mirroring animations.ts `safeValue`.
fn is_safe_value(v: &str) -> bool {
    if v.is_empty() {
        return false;
    }
    if v.chars().any(|c| matches!(c, ';' | '{' | '}' | '<' | '>' | '\\')) {
        return false;
    }
    let lower = v.to_ascii_lowercase();
    !(lower.contains("url(")
        || lower.contains("expression(")
        || lower.contains("@import")
        || lower.contains("/*"))
}

/// Validate one authored animation object against the closed motion grammar (the port of
/// animations.ts's guards, but REJECTING rather than skipping). Returns a clear, specific error naming
/// the first problem. Pure → unit-tested directly.
fn validate_animation(anim: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<(), String> {
    use serde_json::Value;
    let obj = anim.as_object().ok_or("animation must be a JSON object")?;

    let name = obj
        .get("name")
        .and_then(Value::as_str)
        .ok_or("animation `name` is required (a string)")?;
    if !is_safe_ident(name) {
        return Err(format!(
            "animation name '{name}' must be a safe CSS identifier [a-z][a-z0-9-]*"
        ));
    }

    let keyframes = obj
        .get("keyframes")
        .and_then(Value::as_object)
        .ok_or("animation `keyframes` is required (an object of stop → declarations)")?;
    if keyframes.is_empty() {
        return Err("animation `keyframes` must have at least one stop".into());
    }
    let mut valid_stops = 0usize;
    for (stop, decls) in keyframes {
        if !is_safe_stop(stop) {
            return Err(format!(
                "keyframe stop '{stop}' must be `from`, `to`, or a 1–3 digit percentage (e.g. `50%`)"
            ));
        }
        let decls = decls
            .as_object()
            .ok_or_else(|| format!("keyframe '{stop}' must map properties to values (an object)"))?;
        let mut valid_decls = 0usize;
        for (prop, value) in decls {
            if !is_safe_prop(prop) {
                return Err(format!("declaration property '{prop}' must match [a-z-]+"));
            }
            let v = value
                .as_str()
                .ok_or_else(|| format!("declaration '{prop}' value must be a string"))?;
            if !is_safe_value(v) {
                return Err(format!(
                    "declaration '{prop}: {v}' carries an unsafe value (no ; {{ }} < > \\ url( expression( @import /*)"
                ));
            }
            valid_decls += 1;
        }
        if valid_decls > 0 {
            valid_stops += 1;
        }
    }
    if valid_stops == 0 {
        return Err("animation `keyframes` must have at least one stop with a declaration".into());
    }

    // Optional duration/easing/delay/stagger: motion-token refs or literals, checked against the value
    // grammar. `delay` (#3056) is an animation-level time slotted after easing in the shorthand;
    // `stagger` (#3055) is a per-matched-element delay STEP (needs a `selector`, guarded below).
    for key in ["duration", "easing", "delay", "stagger"] {
        if let Some(v) = obj.get(key) {
            let s = v.as_str().ok_or_else(|| format!("animation `{key}` must be a string"))?;
            if !is_safe_value(s) {
                return Err(format!("animation `{key}` value '{s}' carries an unsafe value"));
            }
        }
    }

    // Optional trigger: one of the closed set.
    if let Some(t) = obj.get("trigger") {
        let s = t.as_str().ok_or("animation `trigger` must be a string")?;
        if !matches!(s, "mount" | "hover" | "always" | "exit") {
            return Err(format!(
                "animation `trigger` '{s}' must be one of mount | hover | always | exit"
            ));
        }
    }

    // Optional selector (#3054): scope the applying rule to a CHILD element — a closed selector grammar.
    if let Some(v) = obj.get("selector") {
        let s = v.as_str().ok_or("animation `selector` must be a string")?;
        if !is_safe_selector(s) {
            return Err(format!(
                "animation `selector` '{s}' must use only selector-safe characters (letters, digits, space . _ # > [ ] = \" ' - : ( ) , * + ~)"
            ));
        }
    }

    // Semantic guard (#3055): a `stagger` STEP cascades the delay across the elements a `selector`
    // matches, so it's meaningless on the root — reject a `stagger` with no `selector` at write time.
    if obj.contains_key("stagger") && !obj.contains_key("selector") {
        return Err(
            "animation `stagger` requires a `selector` — it steps the delay across the matched child elements".into(),
        );
    }

    // Optional set (#3054): STATIC declarations applied on the rule (transform-origin/box, etc.), each
    // checked against the same property + value grammar as a keyframe declaration.
    if let Some(v) = obj.get("set") {
        let set = v
            .as_object()
            .ok_or("animation `set` must map properties to values (an object)")?;
        for (prop, value) in set {
            if !is_safe_prop(prop) {
                return Err(format!("`set` property '{prop}' must match [a-z-]+"));
            }
            let s = value
                .as_str()
                .ok_or_else(|| format!("`set` value for '{prop}' must be a string"))?;
            if !is_safe_value(s) {
                return Err(format!("`set` declaration '{prop}: {s}' carries an unsafe value"));
            }
        }
    }

    Ok(())
}

/// Validate + upsert `anim` into component `id`'s `animations` array by `name` (replace same-named,
/// else append), writing the record back. Errors when the component is absent or its record is not a
/// JSON object. Pure of stdin/print so tests drive it directly.
fn upsert_animation(
    store: &bsc_json_store::Store,
    id: &str,
    anim: &serde_json::Value,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    validate_animation(anim)?;
    let name = anim.get("name").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or_default();
    let mut record = load_component_object(store, id)?;
    let obj = record.as_object_mut().expect("load_component_object guarantees an object");
    let arr = obj
        .entry("animations")
        .or_insert_with(|| serde_json::Value::Array(Vec::new()));
    let list = arr
        .as_array_mut()
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("record '{id}' `animations` is not an array"))?;
    match list
        .iter_mut()
        .find(|a| a.get("name").and_then(|n| n.as_str()) == Some(name))
    {
        Some(slot) => *slot = anim.clone(),
        None => list.push(anim.clone()),
    }
    // Stamp the write like every other `bsc ui` mutation (#3164): bump rev + updatedAt + updatedBy
    // (writer from $BSC_UI_WRITER, else "unknown" — the animation verbs take no --by).
    stamped_set(store, id, record, &crate::record::resolve_writer(None))
}

/// Remove the animation named `name` from component `id`, writing the record back. Errors when the
/// component is absent OR it has no animation with that name (so a typo surfaces, not a silent no-op).
fn remove_named_animation(store: &bsc_json_store::Store, id: &str, name: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut record = load_component_object(store, id)?;
    let obj = record.as_object_mut().expect("load_component_object guarantees an object");
    let removed = match obj.get_mut("animations").and_then(|a| a.as_array_mut()) {
        Some(list) => {
            let before = list.len();
            list.retain(|a| a.get("name").and_then(|n| n.as_str()) != Some(name));
            before != list.len()
        }
        None => false,
    };
    if !removed {
        return Err(format!("component '{id}' has no animation named '{name}'"));
    }
    // Stamp the write like every other `bsc ui` mutation (#3164).
    stamped_set(store, id, record, &crate::record::resolve_writer(None))
}

/// The component's `animations` array (an empty array when the field is absent). Errors when the
/// component id has no stored record.
fn animations_of(store: &bsc_json_store::Store, id: &str) -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> {
    let record = load_component_object(store, id)?;
    Ok(record
        .get("animations")
        .cloned()
        .unwrap_or_else(|| serde_json::Value::Array(Vec::new())))
}

/// Load component `id`'s stored record as a JSON object, or a clear error when it's absent / malformed.
/// Resolve a component HANDLE to the id the store is keyed by: the id itself when one exists, else the
/// unique record whose `name` matches case-insensitively.
///
/// Designer request #91 filed a broken-`composes` bug that was not one, on the strength of
/// `bsc ui get deploytoggle` answering `null`. The record was there the whole time — id `toggle`, name
/// `DeployToggle`, composed by ten components resolving by NAME exactly as the edge builders do. Lowercasing
/// a name and trying it as an id is the obvious guess, and the store answered a confident-looking falsehood,
/// so a correct graph got reported as broken. Resolving the guess is cheaper than the report it prevents.
///
/// The id WINS when both could match, because the store is keyed by id and that is the identity every other
/// verb takes. An ambiguous name is refused rather than resolved to whichever record sorts first — picking
/// one silently is how the next false report gets filed.
fn resolve_component_handle(store: &bsc_json_store::Store, handle: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    if store.get(handle)?.is_some() {
        return Ok(handle.to_string());
    }
    let mut by_name: Vec<String> = store
        .list()
        .iter()
        .filter_map(|raw| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(raw).ok())
        .filter(|v| {
            v.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).is_some_and(|n| n.eq_ignore_ascii_case(handle))
        })
        .filter_map(|v| v.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).map(str::to_string))
        .collect();
    by_name.sort();
    by_name.dedup();
    match by_name.len() {
        0 => Err(format!(
            "no record '{handle}' in the store — author it first with `bsc ui set` (or `bsc ui kit set`)"
        )),
        1 => Ok(by_name.remove(0)),
        n => Err(format!(
            "'{handle}' is the NAME of {n} components, not an id — pass one of: {}",
            by_name.join(", ")
        )),
    }
}

fn load_component_object(store: &bsc_json_store::Store, id: &str) -> Result<serde_json::Value, String> {
    let id = &resolve_component_handle(store, id)?;
    let raw = store
        .get(id)?
        .ok_or_else(|| format!("no record '{id}' in the store — author it first with `bsc ui set` (or `bsc ui kit set`)"))?;
    let record: serde_json::Value =
        serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|e| format!("stored record '{id}' is not valid JSON: {e}"))?;
    if !record.is_object() {
        return Err(format!("stored record '{id}' is not a JSON object"));
    }
    Ok(record)
}

/// Parse the shared `--dir`/`--pretty` flags + the trailing positionals from an animation-verb's args.
/// Unknown flags error specifically; each caller pulls the `<component-id>` (+ `<name>`) it needs and
/// emits its own usage line when a positional is missing.
/// [`parse_anim_args`] plus `--superseded-by <id>` — the suppress-only flag
/// (#a-tombstone-can-name-what-superseded-it). Kept separate rather than widening `parse_anim_args`,
/// which a dozen other verbs share: an unknown flag must stay an ERROR everywhere else, so
/// `bsc ui define-animation --superseded-by x` still refuses.
struct SuppressArgs {
    positionals: Vec<String>,
    dir: Option<String>,
    superseded_by: Option<String>,
    force: bool,
}

fn parse_suppress_args(args: &[String]) -> Result<SuppressArgs, String> {
    let mut passthrough: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut superseded_by = None::<String>;
    let mut force = false;
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        if a == "--force" {
            force = true;
        } else if a == "--superseded-by" {
            let v = it
                .next()
                .cloned()
                .ok_or("--superseded-by needs a component id")?;
            if v.trim().is_empty() {
                return Err("--superseded-by needs a component id".into());
            }
            superseded_by = Some(v);
        } else {
            passthrough.push(a.clone());
        }
    }
    let (positionals, dir, _pretty) = parse_anim_args(&passthrough)?;
    Ok(SuppressArgs { positionals, dir, superseded_by, force })
}

fn parse_anim_args(args: &[String]) -> Result<(Vec<String>, Option<String>, bool), String> {
    let (mut dir, mut pretty) = (None::<String>, false);
    let mut positionals: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            positional => positionals.push(positional.to_string()),
        }
    }
    Ok((positionals, dir, pretty))
}

/// `define-animation <component-id> [--pretty]` (#2869) — read + validate an animation from stdin and
/// upsert it onto the component; print the stored animation. A ui-scope mutation (gated in `run`).
fn cmd_define_animation(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (pos, dir, pretty) = parse_anim_args(args)?;
    let id = pos
        .first()
        .ok_or("usage: bsc ui define-animation <component-id>   # animation JSON on stdin")?;
    let mut raw = String::new();
    std::io::stdin().read_to_string(&mut raw).map_err(|e| format!("cannot read stdin: {e}"))?;
    let anim: serde_json::Value =
        serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|e| format!("animation is not valid JSON: {e}"))?;
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    upsert_animation(&store, id, &anim)?;
    bsc_util::emit_ui_activity("component", id);
    let out = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&anim) } else { serde_json::to_string(&anim) };
    println!("{}", out.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// `list-animations <component-id> [--pretty]` (#2869) — print the component's animations array. Read-only.
fn cmd_list_animations(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (pos, dir, pretty) = parse_anim_args(args)?;
    let id = pos.first().ok_or("usage: bsc ui list-animations <component-id>")?;
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let anims = animations_of(&store, id)?;
    let out = if pretty { serde_json::to_string_pretty(&anims) } else { serde_json::to_string(&anims) };
    println!("{}", out.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    Ok(())
}

/// `remove-animation <component-id> <name> [--pretty]` (#2869) — drop a named animation. A ui-scope
/// mutation (gated in `run`); errors when the component or the named animation is absent.
fn cmd_remove_animation(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    const USAGE: &str = "usage: bsc ui remove-animation <component-id> <name>";
    let (pos, dir, _pretty) = parse_anim_args(args)?;
    let id = pos.first().ok_or(USAGE)?;
    let name = pos.get(1).ok_or(USAGE)?;
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    remove_named_animation(&store, id, name)?;
    bsc_util::emit_ui_activity("component", id);
    println!("removed animation '{name}' from '{id}'");
    Ok(())
}

/// `kit define-animation <kit-id>` (#2942) — read + validate an animation from stdin and upsert it into
/// the KIT's motion library by name (the kit owns the def; components reference it by name). Prints the
/// stored animation. A ui-scope mutation (gated in `run`).
fn cmd_kit_define_animation(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (pos, dir, pretty) = parse_anim_args(args)?;
    let id = pos
        .first()
        .ok_or("usage: bsc ui kit define-animation <kit-id>   # animation JSON on stdin")?;
    let mut raw = String::new();
