            put("parent", serde_json::json!({ "id": "parent", "name": "Parent", "kitId": "base-studio-code", "role": "composite", "composes": ["Child"] }));

            // A READ never emits — nothing changed for the Studio to reload.
            run(vec!["usage-scan".into(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()], "bsc ui").expect("read");
            assert!(!act.is_file() || std::fs::read_to_string(&act).unwrap().is_empty(), "a read must not touch the activity log");

            run(vec!["usage-scan".into(), "--apply".into(), "--dir".into(), dir], "bsc ui").expect("apply");
            let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&act).unwrap();
            assert!(
                text.contains("\tui-touch\tcomponent\tchild") && text.contains("\tbase-studio-code"),
                "the rescued (now-used) record touches, carrying its kit: {text:?}",
            );
            assert!(
                text.contains("\tui-touch\tcomponent\tparent"),
                "every applied record touches, not just the one that changed orphan status: {text:?}",
            );

            std::env::remove_var("BSC_UI_ACTIVITY_LOG");
            std::env::remove_var("BSC_AUDIT_PANE");
            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&act);
        });
    }

    /// `--apply` writes, so it must be scope-gated like every other write — while the READ stays
    /// available to a read-scoped session, because the diagnosis is the useful half.
    #[test]
    fn usage_scan_is_a_read_until_apply() {
        let a = |args: &[&str]| args.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        assert!(!is_scoped_mutation(&a(&["usage-scan"])), "the scan is a read");
        assert!(!is_scoped_mutation(&a(&["usage-scan", "--kit", "k"])), "still a read");
        assert!(is_scoped_mutation(&a(&["usage-scan", "--apply"])), "--apply writes");
        assert!(is_scoped_mutation(&a(&["usage-scan", "--kit", "k", "--apply"])), "wherever the flag sits");
        assert!(COMPONENT_COMMANDS.iter().any(|c| c.name == "usage-scan"), "registered in the catalog");
        assert!(run(vec!["usage-scan".into(), "help".into()], "bsc ui").is_ok(), "help reachable");
    }

    #[test]
    fn merge_will_not_orphan_a_specifier_something_still_imports() {
        let store = tmp_component_store("merge-orphan");
        let dir = store.dir().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        let put = |id: &str, v: serde_json::Value| store.set(id, &v.to_string()).unwrap();
        // The real shape: a MODULE record answering a specifier, the component harvested from the same
        // file, and a page that imports the specifier.
        put("mod", serde_json::json!({
            "id": "mod", "name": "CardModule", "kitId": "k", "role": "composite", "builtin": true,
            "provides": "@/features/x/Card", "srcText": "export const Card = () => null;", "composes": [],
        }));
        put("harv", serde_json::json!({
            "id": "harv", "name": "Card", "kitId": "k", "role": "primitive", "builtin": true,
            "provides": "@/components/harv", "srcText": "export const Card = () => null;", "composes": [],
        }));
        put("page", serde_json::json!({
            "id": "page", "name": "Page", "kitId": "k", "role": "page", "builtin": true,
            "srcText": "import { Card } from \"@/features/x/Card\";", "composes": ["CardModule"],
        }));

        // REFUSED — the survivor already claims a different specifier, so it cannot inherit this one.
        let err = run(
            vec!["merge".into(), "mod".into(), "harv".into(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()],
            "bsc ui",
        )
        .expect_err("merging away a live claim onto a survivor that holds another must refuse");
        assert!(err.contains("@/features/x/Card"), "the refusal names the specifier at risk: {err}");
        assert!(err.contains("one record cannot answer both"), "{err}");
        // ... and NOTHING was written. A refusal that half-applies is worse than no guard at all.
        let still = stored(&store, "mod");
        assert!(still.get("suppressed").is_none(), "the refused record must be untouched: {still}");
        assert_eq!(still["provides"], "@/features/x/Card", "and must keep its claim: {still}");

        // The survivor with NO claim INHERITS it instead — the consolidation still lands, and the
        // importer keeps resolving. This is the path that makes the guard usable rather than a wall.
        put("free", serde_json::json!({
            "id": "free", "name": "FreeCard", "kitId": "k", "role": "primitive", "builtin": true,
            "srcText": "export const Card = () => null;", "composes": [],
        }));
        run(vec!["merge".into(), "mod".into(), "free".into(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()], "bsc ui")
            .expect("a survivor with no claim inherits and the merge lands");
        assert_eq!(
            stored(&store, "free")["provides"], "@/features/x/Card",
            "the survivor inherited the claim, so the importer still resolves",
        );
        assert_eq!(stored(&store, "mod")["suppressed"], serde_json::Value::Bool(true));

        // A claim NOTHING imports is not a hazard — orphaning it costs nothing and must stay quiet, or
        // the guard would block every ordinary consolidation in the library.
        put("lonely", serde_json::json!({
            "id": "lonely", "name": "Lonely", "kitId": "k", "role": "primitive", "builtin": true,
            "provides": "@/nobody/imports/this", "srcText": "export const L = () => null;", "composes": [],
        }));
        put("keep", serde_json::json!({
            "id": "keep", "name": "Keep", "kitId": "k", "role": "primitive", "builtin": true,
            "srcText": "export const K = () => null;", "composes": [],
        }));
        run(vec!["merge".into(), "lonely".into(), "keep".into(), "--dir".into(), dir], "bsc ui")
            .expect("an unimported claim is not a hazard");
        assert_eq!(stored(&store, "lonely")["suppressed"], serde_json::Value::Bool(true));
    }

    /// #102: 32 ids reported `"removed"` were all still gettable. They were TOMBSTONED, by design — the
    /// word was the defect. A caller cannot tell a delete from a tombstone if both are called removed.
    #[test]
    fn merge_reports_a_tombstone_as_a_tombstone_and_a_delete_as_a_delete() {
        // The report object, which is the contract a caller parses.
        let t = merge_report("builtin-dup", "survivor", "k", &["page".to_string()], Retired::Tombstoned);
        assert_eq!(t["retired"], "tombstoned", "a builtin is tombstoned, and must say so: {t}");
        assert_eq!(
            t["removed"], serde_json::Value::Null,
            "`removed` must be null for a record that still answers `bsc ui get`: {t}",
        );
        let r = merge_report("user-dup", "survivor", "k", &[], Retired::Removed);
        assert_eq!(r["retired"], "removed", "a non-builtin is deleted outright: {r}");
        assert_eq!(r["removed"], "user-dup", "and `removed` names it: {r}");

        // ... and the STORE agrees with the word, which is the half #102 actually checked.
        let store = tmp_component_store("merge-retired-word");
        let dir = store.dir().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        let put = |id: &str, v: serde_json::Value| store.set(id, &v.to_string()).unwrap();
        put("survivor", serde_json::json!({ "id": "survivor", "name": "Survivor", "kitId": "k", "role": "composite" }));
        put("builtin-dup", serde_json::json!({
            "id": "builtin-dup", "name": "BuiltinDup", "kitId": "k", "role": "composite", "builtin": true,
        }));
        put("user-dup", serde_json::json!({ "id": "user-dup", "name": "UserDup", "kitId": "k", "role": "composite" }));

        run(vec!["merge".into(), "builtin-dup".into(), "survivor".into(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()], "bsc ui")
            .expect("merge lands");
        assert!(store.get("builtin-dup").unwrap().is_some(), "`tombstoned` means it still answers `get`");

        run(vec!["merge".into(), "user-dup".into(), "survivor".into(), "--dir".into(), dir], "bsc ui")
            .expect("merge lands");
        assert!(store.get("user-dup").unwrap().is_none(), "`removed` means it is genuinely gone");
    }

    #[test]
    fn merge_of_a_builtin_from_writes_a_suppression_tombstone_not_a_bare_delete() {
        let store = tmp_component_store("merge-builtin");
        let dir = store.dir().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        store.set(
            "settings-accentcolorcard",
            &serde_json::json!({
                "id": "settings-accentcolorcard", "name": "AccentColorCard", "kitId": "k",
                "role": "composite", "builtin": true, "composes": []
            })
            .to_string(),
        )
        .unwrap();
        store.set(
            "settings-appearancecard",
            &serde_json::json!({ "id": "settings-appearancecard", "name": "AppearanceCard", "kitId": "k", "role": "composite" })
                .to_string(),
        )
        .unwrap();

        run(
            vec!["merge".into(), "settings-accentcolorcard".into(), "settings-appearancecard".into(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()],
            "bsc ui",
        )
        .expect("merge lands");

        // NOT gone — a tombstone occupies the id, which is what stops the seed-reconcile re-adding it.
        let tomb = stored(&store, "settings-accentcolorcard");
        assert_eq!(tomb["suppressed"], serde_json::Value::Bool(true), "merging a builtin away tombstones it: {tomb}");
        assert_eq!(tomb["supersededBy"], "settings-appearancecard", "the tombstone names what replaced it: {tomb}");
        // The survivor is untouched by the retirement.
        assert!(store.get("settings-appearancecard").unwrap().is_some());

        // Merging away a NON-builtin (the existing behavior) still deletes outright — no stray tombstone.
        store.set("dup", &serde_json::json!({ "id": "dup", "name": "Dup", "kitId": "k", "role": "composite" }).to_string()).unwrap();
        run(vec!["merge".into(), "dup".into(), "settings-appearancecard".into(), "--dir".into(), dir], "bsc ui").expect("merge lands");
        assert!(store.get("dup").unwrap().is_none(), "a non-builtin merge is still a bare delete");
    }

    // ── #4107 slice B, FINISHED: the `group` -> `folder` rename ──

    /// The inverse of the test this replaces. `record_folder_reads_the_legacy_group_key` pinned the
    /// COMPATIBILITY SHIM — "every READ must accept both names" — which was right while 351 records
    /// predated the rename. `bsc ui refolder` has since migrated the last of them and the packaged seed
    /// never carried the legacy key, so the shim is gone and this pins its absence.
    ///
    /// It is pinned rather than merely deleted because a silently-returning alias is exactly how the two
    /// names stayed alive: `bsc ui list` projected through it while `bsc ui get --field folder` read the
    /// raw record, so the two disagreed for a year and each looked correct on its own.
    #[test]
    fn record_folder_no_longer_reads_the_legacy_group_key() {
        use serde_json::json;
        assert_eq!(record_folder(&json!({ "folder": "shared/ui" })), Some("shared/ui"));
        assert_eq!(
            record_folder(&json!({ "group": "shared/ui" })), None,
            "the legacy key is NOT read — a record still on it is unfoldered, which is what makes the \
             migration observable instead of silently permanent"
        );
        assert_eq!(record_folder(&json!({ "folder": "new/path", "group": "old/path" })), Some("new/path"));
        assert_eq!(record_folder(&json!({})), None);
        // An empty value is "absent", never a `""` bucket — the record convention the doc pins.
        assert_eq!(record_folder(&json!({ "folder": "" })), None);
    }

    /// `refolder` migrates a SRCLESS record carrying the legacy key by VALUE — the case that kept the
    /// shim load-bearing. `folder` derives from `src`, so a record with none was skipped outright, and
    /// every one of the 19 components still on `group` at 2026-08-25 was srcless: the only verb that
    /// could finish the rename structurally could not touch the records that needed it.
    #[test]
    fn refolder_migrates_a_srcless_legacy_record_by_value() {
        let dir = tmp_store_dir("refolder-legacy");
        let store = bsc_json_store::Store::new(std::path::PathBuf::from(&dir), "component");
        // srcless + legacy key: its folder is CURATED, so no `src` could reproduce it.
        store.set("endedconsole", r#"{"id":"endedconsole","name":"EndedConsole","group":"app/console"}"#).unwrap();
        // has src: re-derivation, the unchanged path.
        store.set("btn", r#"{"id":"btn","name":"Btn","src":"src/shared/ui/controls/Btn.tsx"}"#).unwrap();

        run(vec!["refolder".into(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()], "bsc ui").unwrap();

        let ended: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&store.get("endedconsole").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(ended["folder"], "app/console", "the curated value is CARRIED, not re-derived");
        assert!(ended.get("group").is_none(), "the legacy key is cleared, so the two cannot drift");

        let btn: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&store.get("btn").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(btn["folder"], "shared/ui/controls", "a record WITH src still derives");
    }

    /// A record with neither `src` nor the legacy key is left alone — the 9 suppression TOMBSTONES in the
    /// live store are exactly this shape, and a tombstone is not a component that lost its folder.
    #[test]
    fn refolder_leaves_a_tombstone_alone() {
        let dir = tmp_store_dir("refolder-tombstone");
        let store = bsc_json_store::Store::new(std::path::PathBuf::from(&dir), "component");
        store.set("windowcontrols", r#"{"id":"windowcontrols","suppressed":true}"#).unwrap();
        run(vec!["refolder".into(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()], "bsc ui").unwrap();
        let t: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&store.get("windowcontrols").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert!(t.get("folder").is_none(), "a tombstone gains no folder");
        assert_eq!(t["suppressed"], true, "and is otherwise untouched");
    }

    /// A refolder pass must MIGRATE a legacy record, not just re-derive it: it writes `folder` and drops
    /// `group`, so the record ends up with exactly one name for its folder.
    #[test]
    fn refolder_migrates_a_legacy_record_off_the_group_key() {
        use serde_json::json;
        let dir = tmp_store_dir("refolder-legacy");
        let store = open_component_store(&Some(dir.clone())).unwrap();
        store
            .set(
                "button",
                &json!({ "id": "button", "name": "Button", "kitId": "harvested", "role": "primitive",
                         "group": "shared/ui/controls", "src": "src/shared/ui/controls/Button.tsx" })
                .to_string(),
            )
            .unwrap();

        run(vec!["refolder".into(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()], "bsc ui").unwrap();

        let rec: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&store.get("button").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(rec.get("folder").and_then(|v| v.as_str()), Some("shared/ui/controls"));
        assert!(rec.get("group").is_none(), "the legacy key is dropped, so the two can never drift");
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod list_kit_tests {
    use super::*;

    /// A store seeded with two kits, so the filter has something real to separate.
    fn seeded() -> (tempdir_shim::Dir, String) {
        let dir = tempdir_shim::Dir::new("bsc-4158");
        let store = open_component_store(&Some(dir.path())).unwrap();
        store.set("a1", r#"{"id":"a1","name":"A1","kitId":"alpha"}"#).unwrap();
        store.set("a2", r#"{"id":"a2","name":"A2","kitId":"alpha"}"#).unwrap();
        store.set("b1", r#"{"id":"b1","name":"B1","kitId":"beta"}"#).unwrap();
        let p = dir.path();
        (dir, p)
    }

    #[test]
    fn list_kit_selects_only_that_kit_and_tolerates_an_unknown_one() {
        // #4158 / designer request #44: comparing two kits' membership used to need a full-store dump
        // and a grep of the auto-persisted tool-output file.
        let (_d, path) = seeded();
        let ids = |kit: &str| -> Vec<String> {
            let store = open_component_store(&Some(path.clone())).unwrap();
            store
                .list()
                .iter()
                .filter(|j| {
                    serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j)
                        .ok()
                        .and_then(|v| v.get("kitId").and_then(|k| k.as_str().map(str::to_owned)))
                        .as_deref()
                        == Some(kit)
                })
                .filter_map(|j| bsc_json_store::cli::id_field(j))
                .collect()
        };
        let mut alpha = ids("alpha");
        alpha.sort();
        assert_eq!(alpha, vec!["a1", "a2"]);
        assert_eq!(ids("beta"), vec!["b1"]);
        // An unknown kit is an EMPTY list, not an error — asking about a kit with no components is a
        // legitimate question, and erroring would make "is it empty?" unanswerable.
        assert!(ids("nope").is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn list_kit_requires_a_value() {
        // A bare `--kit` has nothing to filter on; failing loudly beats silently listing everything.
        assert!(cmd_list_kit(&["--kit".to_string()]).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn list_kit_rejects_an_unknown_flag() {
        // Mirrors `list --shape`'s contract, so the two interceptions behave the same way.
        assert!(cmd_list_kit(&["--kit".into(), "alpha".into(), "--nope".into()]).is_err());
    }
}

/// The SUBJECT axis (`the-graphs-cannot-be-searched-by-the-axes-they-store`).
///
/// `feature` says which worker may WRITE a component; `tags` says what it is ABOUT — and a worker
/// looking for what it NEEDS is asking the second question, which this store could not answer at all.
#[cfg(test)]
mod list_tags_tests {
    use super::*;

    /// Three components: two share a tag, one of those carries a second, one is UNTAGGED — the last is
    /// what proves the filter is additive rather than sweeping.
    fn seeded() -> (tempdir_shim::Dir, String) {
        let dir = tempdir_shim::Dir::new("bsc-tags");
        let store = open_component_store(&Some(dir.path())).unwrap();
        store.set("chart-a", r#"{"id":"chart-a","name":"ChartA","kitId":"alpha","tags":["chart","compact"]}"#).unwrap();
        store.set("chart-b", r#"{"id":"chart-b","name":"ChartB","kitId":"alpha","tags":["chart"]}"#).unwrap();
        store.set("plain", r#"{"id":"plain","name":"Plain","kitId":"alpha"}"#).unwrap();
        let p = dir.path();
        (dir, p)
    }

    fn ids(dir: &str, tags: &str) -> Vec<String> {
        let (r, out) = bsc_util::capture_output(|| {
            cmd_list_tags(&["--tags".into(), tags.into(), "--dir".into(), dir.into()])
        });
        r.unwrap();
        let mut v: Vec<String> = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(out.trim())
            .unwrap()
            .as_array()
            .unwrap()
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|i| i.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).map(str::to_owned))
            .collect();
        v.sort();
        v
    }

    #[test]
    fn list_tags_is_an_and_and_never_sweeps_in_the_untagged() {
        let (_d, path) = seeded();

        // One tag selects both carriers…
        assert_eq!(ids(&path, "chart"), vec!["chart-a".to_string(), "chart-b".to_string()]);
        // …a SECOND tag NARROWS. This separates AND from OR: a union would return both here, so the
        // flag would widen as a caller tried to refine — the opposite of what naming a tag means.
        assert_eq!(ids(&path, "chart,compact"), vec!["chart-a".to_string()]);
        // Order does not matter — it is a set intersection, not a prefix.
        assert_eq!(ids(&path, "compact,chart"), vec!["chart-a".to_string()]);
        // A tag NOTHING carries returns NOTHING. The algorithms twin of this flag used to return the
        // WHOLE store here, with no error, and a caller could not tell that from a hit.
        assert!(ids(&path, "totally-absent").is_empty());
        // The UNTAGGED component is in the store and is never a match — the filter hides only what it
        // was asked to hide, the same purely-additive rule `--feature` follows.
        let store = open_component_store(&Some(path.clone())).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(store.list().len(), 3, "the untagged record really is in the store");
        assert!(!ids(&path, "chart").contains(&"plain".to_string()));
        // Whitespace around a tag is the shape a shell hands over; it must not defeat the match.
        assert_eq!(ids(&path, " chart , compact "), vec!["chart-a".to_string()]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn list_tags_composes_with_kit_rather_than_replacing_it() {
        let (_d, path) = seeded();
        let store = open_component_store(&Some(path.clone())).unwrap();
        store.set("beta-chart", r#"{"id":"beta-chart","name":"BetaChart","kitId":"beta","tags":["chart"]}"#).unwrap();

        let (r, out) = bsc_util::capture_output(|| {
            cmd_list_tags(&["--tags".into(), "chart".into(), "--kit".into(), "beta".into(), "--dir".into(), path.clone()])
        });
        r.unwrap();
        let v: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(out.trim()).unwrap();
        let got: Vec<&str> = v.as_array().unwrap().iter().filter_map(|i| i["id"].as_str()).collect();
        assert_eq!(got, vec!["beta-chart"], "every filter on the verb INTERSECTS: {v}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn list_tags_refuses_an_empty_search_rather_than_listing_everything() {
        let (_d, path) = seeded();
        // A bare `--tags`, and a value that trims to nothing, are the two ways a caller ends up asking
        // for "no tags at all". Answering with the whole store is exactly the silent-ignore this item
        // exists to remove, so both are errors.
        assert!(cmd_list_tags(&["--tags".into(), "--dir".into(), path.clone()]).is_err());
        assert!(cmd_list_tags(&["--tags".into(), " , ".into(), "--dir".into(), path.clone()]).is_err());
        assert!(cmd_list_tags(&["--tags".into(), "chart".into(), "--nope".into(), "--dir".into(), path]).is_err());
    }

    #[test]
    fn tags_reports_the_vocabulary_most_used_first() {
        let (_d, path) = seeded();
        let (r, out) = bsc_util::capture_output(|| cmd_tags(&["--dir".into(), path.clone()]));
        r.unwrap();
        let v: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(out.trim()).unwrap();
        let rows = v.as_array().unwrap();
        // Only the tags that EXIST, each with its real count — the untagged component contributes none.
        assert_eq!(rows.len(), 2, "two distinct tags: {v}");
        assert_eq!(rows[0], serde_json::json!({ "tag": "chart", "count": 2 }), "most-used leads");
        assert_eq!(rows[1], serde_json::json!({ "tag": "compact", "count": 1 }));
        // Scoped to a kit that holds nothing yields an EMPTY vocabulary, not every tag in the store.
        let (r, out) = bsc_util::capture_output(|| cmd_tags(&["--kit".into(), "nope".into(), "--dir".into(), path]));
        r.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(out.trim()).unwrap(), serde_json::json!([]));
    }
}

/// A minimal scoped temp dir for the tests above — the crate has no dev-dependency on `tempfile`.
#[cfg(test)]
mod preview_error_guard_tests {
    use super::*;


    /// `used-by --src` exists to separate a MISSING `composes` edge from a real dead root, and the whole
    /// signal collapses if a name in PROSE counts. `name_mentions` already classifies comments and string
    /// literals out; this pins that the verb's count inherits it, because the earlier attempt at this
    /// feature shipped a second, cruder matcher and was rejected for exactly that.
    #[test]
    fn src_references_ignore_a_name_in_a_comment_or_a_string_literal() {
        let comps = vec![
            serde_json::json!({ "id": "target", "name": "ActionRow", "kitId": "k" }),
            serde_json::json!({
                "id": "prose", "name": "Prose", "kitId": "k",
                // Both mentions are inert: one comment, one string.
                "srcText": "// ActionRow is described here\nconst label = \"ActionRow\";\n",
            }),
        ];
        assert!(
            src_reference_rows(&comps, "target", "ActionRow").is_empty(),
            "a name in prose is not a reference"
        );

        // NON-VACUITY: a real JSX use and a real import DO count, so the emptiness above is about the
        // classification rather than the scan finding nothing at all.
        let comps = vec![
            serde_json::json!({ "id": "target", "name": "ActionRow", "kitId": "k" }),
            serde_json::json!({
                "id": "user", "name": "User", "kitId": "k",
                "srcText": "import { ActionRow } from \"@/x\";\nexport const U = () => <ActionRow />;\n",
            }),
        ];
        let rows = src_reference_rows(&comps, "target", "ActionRow");
        assert_eq!(rows.len(), 1, "{rows:?}");
        assert_eq!(rows[0]["id"].as_str(), Some("user"));
        assert!(rows[0]["total"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0) >= 2, "jsx + import: {:?}", rows[0]);
    }

    /// It never counts a component against ITSELF, and never counts a tombstone — a suppressed record's
    /// content is gone, so it can only dilute.
    #[test]
    fn src_references_skip_self_and_suppressed_records() {
        let comps = vec![
            serde_json::json!({
                "id": "target", "name": "ActionRow", "kitId": "k",
                "srcText": "export const ActionRow = () => <ActionRow />;\n",
            }),
            serde_json::json!({
                "id": "dead", "name": "Dead", "kitId": "k", "suppressed": true,
                "srcText": "export const D = () => <ActionRow />;\n",
            }),
        ];
        assert!(src_reference_rows(&comps, "target", "ActionRow").is_empty());
    }

    /// #preview-error-list-silently-records-a-component-named-list — the exact shape that produced this.
    ///
    /// The listing verb is `preview-errors` (PLURAL). `preview-error list` therefore parses as "record an
    /// error for the component `list`", and before this guard it blocked on stdin and then appended a junk
    /// row for a component that does not exist — into the very log a designer reads to decide whether a
    /// render error is stale.
    ///
    /// The assertion is that it is REFUSED **and never reads stdin**: this test would hang rather than fail
    /// if the validation moved back below the read, which is the failure mode that cost ten minutes.
    #[test]
    fn preview_error_refuses_an_id_that_is_not_a_component() {
        let dir = tempdir_shim::Dir::new("bsc-preview-error-guard");
        std::env::set_var("BSC_COMPONENT_DIR", dir.path());
        let err = cmd_preview_error(&["list".to_string()]).unwrap_err();
        std::env::remove_var("BSC_COMPONENT_DIR");
        assert!(err.contains("no component 'list'"), "{err}");
        assert!(err.contains("preview-errors"), "names the plural listing verb: {err}");
    }

    /// `clear` stays reachable for ANY id — including a junk row written before the guard existed. If the
    /// guard applied to clear too, an already-bad row would be permanently unclearable.
    #[test]
    fn clear_is_not_gated_by_the_component_check() {
        let dir = tempdir_shim::Dir::new("bsc-preview-error-clear");
        std::env::set_var("BSC_COMPONENT_DIR", dir.path());
        let r = cmd_preview_error(&["clear".to_string(), "not-a-component".to_string()]);
        std::env::remove_var("BSC_COMPONENT_DIR");
        assert!(r.is_ok(), "clear must work for any id: {r:?}");
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tempdir_shim {
    pub struct Dir(std::path::PathBuf);
    impl Dir {
        pub fn new(tag: &str) -> Self {
            let p = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
                "{tag}-{}-{}",
                std::process::id(),
                std::time::SystemTime::now()
                    .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
                    .map(|d| d.as_nanos())
                    .unwrap_or(0)
            ));
            std::fs::create_dir_all(&p).ok();
            Self(p)
        }
        pub fn path(&self) -> String {
            self.0.to_string_lossy().into_owned()
        }
    }
    impl Drop for Dir {
        fn drop(&mut self) {
            std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0).ok();
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod feature_tests {
    use super::*;

    /// A store shaped like the real one at the split: a baseline, two features, the shell, and a
    /// HOLLOW record (no folder, no kitId, no name) — 44 of 448 live records look exactly like that,
    /// and they are the reason this backfill reports rather than defaults.
    fn seeded() -> (tempdir_shim::Dir, String) {
        let dir = tempdir_shim::Dir::new("bsc-domains");
        let store = open_component_store(&Some(dir.path())).unwrap();
        store.set("button", r#"{"id":"button","name":"Button","kitId":"k","folder":"shared/ui/controls"}"#).unwrap();
        store.set("glancepage", r#"{"id":"glancepage","name":"GlancePage","kitId":"k","folder":"features/glance"}"#).unwrap();
        store.set("settingscard", r#"{"id":"settingscard","name":"Card","kitId":"k","folder":"features/settings/cards"}"#).unwrap();
        store.set("rail", r#"{"id":"rail","name":"Rail","kitId":"k","folder":"app/chrome"}"#).unwrap();
        store.set("hollow", r#"{"id":"hollow"}"#).unwrap();
        let p = dir.path();
        (dir, p)
    }

    fn run_features(path: &str, extra: &[&str]) -> serde_json::Value {
        // Drive the mapping the command drives, over the same store, so the assertions are about the
        // backfill's DECISIONS rather than about stdout capture.
        let store = open_component_store(&Some(path.to_string())).unwrap();
        let apply = extra.contains(&"--apply");
        let mut changed = Vec::new();
        let mut unmapped = Vec::new();
        let mut by: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, usize> = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();
        let mut updated = Vec::new();
        for raw in store.list() {
            let rec: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&raw).unwrap();
            let id = rec.get("id").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
            let folder = record_folder(&rec).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
            let old = rec.get("feature").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
            match crate::feature_from_folder(&folder) {
                None => unmapped.push(id),
                Some(new) => {
                    *by.entry(new.clone()).or_default() += 1;
                    if old != new {
                        changed.push(id.clone());
                        // The DELTA, exactly as the command sends it — see the null-clear note there.
                        updated.push(serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "feature": new }));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        if apply && !updated.is_empty() {
            let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(None);
            let plan = WritePlan { replace: false, clear: &[] };
            set_stamped(&store, &updated, None, &writer, "component", Some("features"), plan).unwrap();
        }
        changed.sort();
        unmapped.sort();
        serde_json::json!({ "changed": changed, "unmapped": unmapped, "byDomain": by })
    }

    #[test]
    fn maps_the_baseline_the_shell_and_each_feature() {
        let (_d, p) = seeded();
        let r = run_features(&p, &[]);
        assert_eq!(r["byDomain"]["core"], 1, "shared/** is the baseline");
        assert_eq!(r["byDomain"]["shell"], 1, "app/** is the shell, NOT the baseline");
        assert_eq!(r["byDomain"]["glance"], 1);
        assert_eq!(r["byDomain"]["settings"], 1, "the feature is the segment after `features/`");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_hollow_record_is_reported_unmapped_and_never_given_a_default() {
        // THE POINT OF THE REPORT. 44 live records carry no folder, kitId or name. Bucketing them
        // under core (or anything) would hide a data-quality problem inside a migration.
        let (_d, p) = seeded();
        let r = run_features(&p, &[]);
        assert_eq!(r["unmapped"].as_array().unwrap(), &[serde_json::json!("hollow")]);
        assert!(!r["changed"].as_array().unwrap().contains(&serde_json::json!("hollow")));
        for d in ["core", "shell", "glance", "settings"] {
            assert_eq!(r["byDomain"][d], 1, "an unmapped record inflated no domain");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn reports_without_writing_until_apply() {
        let (_d, p) = seeded();
        run_features(&p, &[]);   // no --apply
        let store = open_component_store(&Some(p.clone())).unwrap();
        let rec: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&store.get("button").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert!(rec.get("feature").is_none(), "a report must not write — --apply is the write");
    }

    #[test]
    fn apply_writes_the_feature_and_re_running_is_a_no_op() {
        let (_d, p) = seeded();
        let first = run_features(&p, &["--apply"]);
        assert_eq!(first["changed"].as_array().unwrap().len(), 4);
        let store = open_component_store(&Some(p.clone())).unwrap();
        let rec: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&store.get("glancepage").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(rec["feature"], "glance");
        // Idempotence is what makes the backfill safe to re-run after adjudicating the unmapped ones.
        let second = run_features(&p, &["--apply"]);
        assert!(second["changed"].as_array().unwrap().is_empty(), "second run changed nothing");
        assert_eq!(second["unmapped"].as_array().unwrap(), &[serde_json::json!("hollow")]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_stored_null_field_survives_the_backfill() {
        // REGRESSION. The backfill first resubmitted the whole round-tripped record. The write MERGES,
        // so that looked equivalent — but a resubmitted explicit `null` reads as a CLEAR, so every null
        // field a record carried was deleted by a command that only meant to ADD one.
        //
        // Caught on the real store, not here: 448 records went in and 401 fields came out where 402
        // should have, and the missing one was `terminalhost.provides`, a stored null. A store-wide key
        // count is what found it; no per-record assertion would have.
        let dir = tempdir_shim::Dir::new("bsc-domains-null");
        let store = open_component_store(&Some(dir.path())).unwrap();
        store
            .set("nullish", r#"{"id":"nullish","name":"N","kitId":"k","folder":"features/glance","provides":null}"#)
            .unwrap();
        let p = dir.path();
        run_features(&p, &["--apply"]);
        let store = open_component_store(&Some(p)).unwrap();
        let rec: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&store.get("nullish").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(rec["feature"], "glance", "the field it meant to add is added");
        assert!(
            rec.as_object().unwrap().contains_key("provides"),
            "a stored null must SURVIVE — the backfill adds a field, it never clears one"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_backfill_leaves_folder_untouched() {
        // `folder` is derived from `src` and read by emit + regroup. If the backfill moved it, every
        // `bsc ui regroup` would undo this work — which is the whole reason domain is a second field.
        let (_d, p) = seeded();
        run_features(&p, &["--apply"]);
        let store = open_component_store(&Some(p)).unwrap();
        let rec: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&store.get("settingscard").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(rec["folder"], "features/settings/cards", "folder is untouched");
        assert_eq!(rec["feature"], "settings");
    }

    #[test]
    fn feature_rides_the_lean_list_projection() {
        // "What is in this feature" has to be answerable from `list` alone, without --full.
        assert!(COMPONENT_SPEC.meta_fields.contains(&"feature"));
        assert!(COMPONENT_SPEC.meta_fields.contains(&"folder"), "beside folder, not instead of it");
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod required_by_tests {
    use super::*;

    /// A component set carrying `requiredBy` is validated at the write, not trusted.
    ///
    /// The field is the USAGE mirror of a plan feature's `requires`: which features, in which projects,
    /// need this component. It is a LIST because the relation is many-to-many in both directions —
    /// several features across several projects legitimately need the same button.
    #[test]
    fn a_qualified_required_by_is_accepted() {
        let item = serde_json::json!({
            "id": "button", "name": "Button", "srcText": "export const Button=()=>null;",
            "requiredBy": ["studio-code:glance", "my-app:settings"],
        });
        assert!(validate_component_batch(&[item]).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_bare_slug_is_refused_at_the_write() {
        // The whole reason entries are qualified: nothing stops two projects both having `settings`,
        // so a bare slug names no one feature. Refusing here is what keeps the stored field unambiguous.
        let item = serde_json::json!({
            "id": "button", "name": "Button", "srcText": "export const Button=()=>null;",
            "requiredBy": ["settings"],
        });
        let err = validate_component_batch(&[item]).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("<projectKey>:<feature>"), "{err}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_non_array_required_by_is_refused_rather_than_coerced() {
        let item = serde_json::json!({
            "id": "button", "name": "Button", "srcText": "export const Button=()=>null;",
            "requiredBy": "studio-code:glance",
        });
        assert!(validate_component_batch(&[item]).is_err(), "a bare string is not the list shape");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_record_with_no_required_by_is_unaffected() {
        // The field is OPTIONAL — most records have no declared user, and absence is not a defect.
        let item = serde_json::json!({
            "id": "button", "name": "Button", "srcText": "export const Button=()=>null;",
        });
        assert!(validate_component_batch(&[item]).is_ok());
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod feature_backfill_preserves_tests {
    use super::*;

    /// REGRESSION. The backfill derives `feature` from `folder`, and the first version OVERWROTE a
    /// value already set. That silently undid curation on every invocation: `toggle` was placed in
    /// `core` by hand (it is `DeployToggle`, and four other features compose it) and the very next
    /// `bsc ui features --apply` put it back under `planner`, because its folder says planner.
    ///
    /// The two-field split is what makes that placement legitimate — `folder` stays the provenance the
    /// file was lifted from, `feature` says who owns the record — so the backfill must treat the
    /// derivation as a starting point and never as an authority. The algorithms backfill had this
    /// property from the start; the graphs disagreeing about it is what made the loss possible.
    #[test]
    fn a_hand_placed_feature_survives_a_re_run() {
        let dir = tempdir_shim::Dir::new("bsc-feature-preserve");
        let store = open_component_store(&Some(dir.path())).unwrap();
        store
            .set("toggle", r#"{"id":"toggle","name":"DeployToggle","kitId":"k","folder":"features/planner/bodies","feature":"core"}"#)
            .unwrap();
        store.set("card", r#"{"id":"card","name":"Card","kitId":"k","folder":"features/glance"}"#).unwrap();

        let store = open_component_store(&Some(dir.path())).unwrap();
        let mut placed = Vec::new();
        for raw in store.list() {
            let rec: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&raw).unwrap();
            let id = rec.get("id").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
            let folder = record_folder(&rec).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
            let old = rec.get("feature").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
            if !old.is_empty() {
                continue; // the rule under test
            }
            if let Some(new) = crate::feature_from_folder(&folder) {
                placed.push((id, new));
            }
        }
        assert_eq!(placed, vec![("card".to_string(), "glance".to_string())], "only the unplaced one moves");
    }
}


#[cfg(test)]
mod feature_rule_gate {
    use bsc_util::feature_rule::{violations, Violation};

    /// Edges deliberately kept, each with the decision behind it. EXACT `from -> to` ids.
    ///
    /// Two entries, and both are pages composing another feature's page. Neither is obviously wrong —
    /// a settings section that embeds the tunnel's own panel is reusing the real thing rather than
    /// copying it — but neither is obviously right either, so they are named here rather than made
    /// invisible by a broader rule.
    const ALLOWED: &[&str] = &[
        // The Automations page embeds the MCP page's server list: automations dispatch into panes, and
        // the servers a pane can reach are the MCP feature's roster. The alternative is a second list.
        "automationspage -> mcppage",
        // Settings → Planner embeds the tunnel's settings panel so the pairing UI lives in one place.
        "settings-planner -> tunnelsettings",
    ];

    /// Every packaged component record, read from the seed tree the app ships.
    fn packaged_components() -> Vec<serde_json::Value> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        for root in bsc_util::packaged::data_dirs() {
            let dir = root.join("components").join("app");
            if !dir.is_dir() {
                continue;
            }
            let mut stack = vec![dir];
            while let Some(d) = stack.pop() {
                let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(&d) else { continue };
                for e in entries.flatten() {
                    let p = e.path();
                    if p.is_dir() {
                        stack.push(p);
                    } else if p.extension().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) == Some("json") {
                        if let Ok(s) = std::fs::read_to_string(&p) {
                            if let Ok(v) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&s) {
                                out.push(v);
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            if !out.is_empty() {
                break; // the first data dir that HAS the tree wins, matching `packaged::read`
            }
        }
        out
    }

    /// THE OWNERSHIP RULE over the packaged component seed.
    ///
    /// A component's `composes` names other components BY NAME, not by id, so the resolution differs
    /// from the algorithms graph — which is exactly why `bsc_util::feature_rule` takes already-resolved
    /// edges and leaves the addressing to each caller.
    #[test]
    fn the_ownership_rule_holds_across_the_component_library() {
        let recs = packaged_components();
        assert!(!recs.is_empty(), "no packaged component records found — the gate would be vacuous");

        // name -> (feature, id). A record with no name cannot be a `composes` target.
        let by_name: std::collections::HashMap<String, (String, String)> = recs
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|r| {
                let name = r.get("name")?.as_str()?.trim();
                if name.is_empty() {
                    return None;
                }
                let id = r.get("id")?.as_str()?.to_string();
                let f = r.get("feature").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or_default().to_string();
                Some((name.to_string(), (f, id)))
            })
            .collect();

        let mut edges: Vec<(String, String, String, String)> = Vec::new();
        for r in &recs {
            let Some(from_id) = r.get("id").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) else { continue };
            let from_f = r.get("feature").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or_default();
            let Some(cs) = r.get("composes").and_then(|v| v.as_array()) else { continue };
            for t in cs.iter().filter_map(|v| v.as_str()) {
                // A `composes` naming a component the seed does not hold is `bsc ui doctor`'s finding.
                let Some((to_f, to_id)) = by_name.get(t) else { continue };
                edges.push((from_id.to_string(), from_f.to_string(), to_id.clone(), to_f.clone()));
            }
        }

        let v: Vec<Violation> = violations(&edges, ALLOWED);
        assert!(
            v.is_empty(),
            "{} ownership violation(s) in the component library:\n{}",
            v.len(),
            v.iter().map(Violation::describe).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\n")
        );
    }

    /// COVERAGE — the rule may only skip a record whose feature is unknown, so how many are unknown is
    /// part of what the gate asserts.
    ///
    /// THIS GATE SHIPPED VACUOUS ONCE AND WAS PULLED FOR IT. When it was first written, 0 of 306
    /// packaged component files carried `feature`, so it classified ZERO edges and passed — a test that
    /// could only pass, which is worse than no test at all. Asserting coverage is what makes the
    /// difference between "the rule holds" and "the rule saw nothing".
    #[test]
    fn every_packaged_component_is_placed_so_the_rule_covers_the_library() {
        let recs = packaged_components();
        assert!(!recs.is_empty(), "no packaged component records found");
        let unplaced: Vec<&str> = recs
            .iter()
            .filter(|r| r.get("feature").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or_default().trim().is_empty())
            .filter_map(|r| r.get("id").and_then(|v| v.as_str()))
            .collect();
        assert!(
            unplaced.is_empty(),
            "{} packaged component(s) carry no `feature`, so the ownership rule cannot see their \
             edges: {:?}",
            unplaced.len(),
            &unplaced[..unplaced.len().min(10)]
        );
    }

    /// The gate must be able to FAIL. A rule whose test can only pass is a comment.
    #[test]
    fn the_rule_reports_a_planted_baseline_violation() {
        let planted = vec![(
            "planted".to_string(),
            "core".to_string(),
            "some-glance-thing".to_string(),
            "glance".to_string(),
        )];
        let v = violations(&planted, ALLOWED);
        assert_eq!(v.len(), 1, "a core -> feature edge must be reported");
        assert!(v[0].describe().contains("core/planted -> glance/some-glance-thing"));
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod feature_confinement_tests {
    use super::*;

    /// A confined session writes only its own feature's COMPONENTS
    /// (`a-worker-writes-only-its-own-feature`).
    ///
    /// Driven through `set_stamped` — the funnel every component write lands in — rather than through
    /// a verb, because that is where the guard is and why: `ui set` takes its records from stdin, so
    /// the id is not in argv and a dispatch-level check could not see it.
    /// A scratch component store. Its own rather than the sibling module's `tmp_component_store`,
    /// which is private to that module — copying four lines beats making a test helper public.
    fn scratch(tag: &str) -> bsc_json_store::Store {
        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
        static N: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
            "bsc-confine-{tag}-{}-{}",
            std::process::id(),
            N.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)
        ));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        bsc_json_store::Store::new(dir, "component")
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_confined_session_writes_only_its_own_features_components() {
        let store = scratch("confine");
        let rec = |id: &str, feature: &str| {
            serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "name": id, "kitId": "k", "feature": feature })
        };
        // Authored UNCONFINED, which is how a designer or the seed reconcile works.
        for (id, f) in [("mine", "glance"), ("theirs", "planner"), ("shared", "core")] {
            set_stamped(&store, &[rec(id, f)], None, "seed", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();
        }

        bsc_cli_util::with_features(Some("glance"), || {
            // Its own lane: allowed.
            set_stamped(&store, &[rec("mine", "glance")], None, "w", "component", None, WritePlan::default())
                .expect("a worker writes its own feature's components");

            // Another lane, and the shared baseline: refused.
            for (id, owner) in [("theirs", "planner"), ("shared", "core")] {
                let err = set_stamped(&store, &[rec(id, owner)], None, "w", "component", None, WritePlan::default())
                    .expect_err("must be refused");
                assert!(err.contains("writes only"), "`{id}`: {err}");
                assert!(err.contains(owner), "…naming its owner: {err}");
            }

            // THE LAUNDERING MOVE: claiming another lane's record for your own. The STORED feature
            // governs, so a payload saying `glance` cannot take `core`'s component.
            let err = set_stamped(&store, &[rec("shared", "glance")], None, "w", "component", None, WritePlan::default())
                .expect_err("a claim must not launder a write");
            assert!(err.contains("core"), "the STORED owner decides: {err}");

            // A NEW record must claim a lane this session may write.
            assert!(
                set_stamped(&store, &[serde_json::json!({ "id": "fresh", "name": "Fresh", "kitId": "k" })], None, "w", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).is_err(),
                "a new component with no feature is refused",
            );
            set_stamped(&store, &[rec("fresh", "glance")], None, "w", "component", None, WritePlan::default())
                .expect("…and lands when it claims a lane it may write");
        });

        // UNCONFINED is unchanged.
        bsc_cli_util::with_features(None, || {
            set_stamped(&store, &[rec("shared", "core")], None, "lib", "component", None, WritePlan::default())
                .expect("an unconfined session writes the shared baseline");
        });
    }
}

//! The component-library CLI (#2281) — the shim over the shared verbatim-JSON-per-id store CLI
//! ([`bsc_json_store::cli`], #2158). TWO collections: the **components**
//! (`~/.base-studio-code/components/<id>.json`) and the **kits** (`~/.base-studio-code/kits/<id>.json`),
//! each list/get/set/remove-able from a session's own shell — the same store the desktop Component
//! Library pane reads/writes and an agent reaches to reuse a proven component instead of re-inventing it.
//!
//! **Mounted under `bsc ui` (#2469)** — the one UI-design-surface command: `bsc ui <cmd>` operates on
//! components; `bsc ui kit <cmd>` operates on kits (`bsc_ui::cli` delegates the store verbs here via
//! [`run`], composing [`command_docs`] into its merged help tree). `bsc component …` remains a thin
//! DEPRECATED alias for one release (the umbrella `bsc` prints a stderr pointer, then delegates here
//! unchanged — the #1721 `bsc plan integration` → `bsc data connector` pattern). Per-command help
//! (#1762):
//!   bsc ui help          # the merged UI-surface commands
//!   bsc ui kit help      # kit commands
//!   bsc ui set help      # detailed help for ONE command
//!
//! Each collection resolves via `--dir <path>` or its env var, defaulting to `~/.base-studio-code/<seg>/`.

/// The data-shape vocabulary (#2475 + `series` #3517) — the seven canonical shapes a feature's data
/// can take, each with the one-line description `bsc ui shapes` prints. A component's optional `shapes`
/// JSON field stamps the shapes it is an IDEAL rendering for; the CLI computes the index from those
/// fields verbatim (no Rust schema — the store stays verbatim JSON). Mirrors `DataShape` in
/// `src/features/designs/lib/model.ts`.
const DATA_SHAPES: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
    ("list", "a flat, ordered collection of homogeneous items"),
    ("linked-list", "a sequence whose items chain by explicit next/prev links"),
    ("tree", "a hierarchy — every item nests under a single parent"),
    ("graph", "nodes joined by arbitrary edges (many-to-many)"),
    ("table", "homogeneous records with fixed, aligned columns"),
    ("key-value", "one record's named fields — a label → value map"),
    ("series", "an ordered axis + one or more aligned numeric value series — a time-series (LineArea · Bars · Spark)"),
];

Restores `srcText` to a version the change log retained (`prevSrc`, see `bsc ui log`). With no --to it
undoes the LAST write that moved the source; `--to <rev>` restores the source as the record held it at
that revision.

WHY IT EXISTS. Recovery from a bad write used to be \"re-seed from the packaged seed\", which is no
recovery at all for a record that has no seed — and 25 of 47 `role: page` records had none. A designer
session that rewrote five rendering-critical records at 01:39 left three of them with the broken version
as the only copy that had ever existed, because the log recorded THAT `srcText` changed and never what it
was. This is the way back.

The revert is itself a WRITE: it stamps a new rev and its own history entry (noting where it came from),
so the version it replaced becomes revertible in turn and a mistaken revert is not a second unrecoverable
act. It restores ONLY `srcText` — every other field is left exactly as it stands, so a revert of a bad
source never also rewinds a good `composes` edit.

A revision whose source has aged past the retention cap is REFUSED, naming the revisions that are still
reachable. It never falls back to a nearer version: silently reverting to bytes the record never held at
the revision you asked for is worse than refusing. A ui-scope MUTATION.",

  bsc ui set --replace …                                                                # verbatim WHOLE-record write (see below)
  bsc ui set --force …                                                                  # store a `role: page` the gate would refuse (a deliberate spec)

Upserts each component by its (required, non-empty) \"id\" field. Prints the id(s) written — how an
agent (or the pane) authors/updates a component in the shared kit.

A write is a MERGE (#4197): the fields you send are overlaid on the STORED record, and every field you
did NOT send is PRESERVED. So `{\"id\":\"fleetpage\",\"srcText\":\"…\"}` changes the source and leaves the
kit, role, `composes` edges, `src`/`folder` provenance and `props` exactly as they were. This matches
`bsc graph impl set` (#4154) — the two stores answer a partial write identically. It used to REPLACE,
which silently deleted every field a write did not restate; that cost a 16-entry reorg on the algorithms
side, and here it can be unrecoverable (`fleetpage` has had no source file since #3636, so the record is
the only copy of that UI).

Removal is therefore EXPLICIT, two equivalent ways: --clear a,b removes those fields, or send JSON
`null` as the field's value. `id` can never be removed (it is the store key). Each removal is recorded
in the change history as `dropped` — separate from `changed` — so `bsc ui log <id>` tells a write that
DELETED fields from one that merely edited them.

--replace opts back into the verbatim whole-record write for a caller that genuinely holds the whole
record: the app's write-through bridge, `bsc ui import`, and the seed reconcile's authoritative reset
(which a merge would stop from ever converging back on the seed). It is the ONLY mode that can still
delete a field by omission, so it WARNS on stderr naming each one. --clear with --replace is refused.

--file <name> reads the SAME payload from a bare-named file in the session's $BSC_SCRATCH dir instead
of stdin (#3373). It exists because a heredoc cannot be permitted in a restricted session: newlines are
command separators, so the JSON body parses as its own (unmatchable) subcommands. The name must be
BARE — no '/', '\\', '..' or ':' — and $BSC_SCRATCH must be set, or the flag is refused.

Every write STAMPS provenance (#3164): it auto-bumps the record's `rev` integer, sets `updatedAt`
(ISO-8601 UTC), and records `updatedBy` — the writer tag from `--by <tag>`, else $BSC_UI_WRITER, else
\"unknown\". --if-version <n> is OPTIMISTIC CONCURRENCY: the write is REJECTED (non-zero exit, nothing
stored) unless the record's CURRENT rev is exactly <n> — so a background rewrite can't silently clobber
your edit. Read a record's current rev with `bsc ui log <id>`; --if-version takes a single record on stdin.

An optional `group` field is the component's FOLDER PATH within the kit — a nested, `/`-delimited path
(`shared/ui/controls`, `features/github`) that organizes the kit like a completed project's folders
(#3579). Orthogonal to `role` (the arch tier), organizational only (`composes` still resolves across the
whole kit). `bsc ui refolder` re-derives it from `src` for the whole store; the harvest seeds it too.",

        name: "backing",
        summary: "which component record backs a file — and the gate that keeps edits going to the record",
        usage: "USAGE:
  bsc ui backing <path> [--json|--pretty]   # the record(s) whose `src` names this file
  bsc ui backing gate <path>...             # exit 1 if ANY path is record-backed (the landing gate)
  bsc ui backing audit [--json|--pretty]    # records whose `src` names a file that is NOT here (#4223)
  bsc ui backing reconcile [--json] [--apply] [--annotate] [--retire]
                                            # the SEED-side provenance reconcile (#records)

The graph is the source of truth and a component's file is the EMITTED ARTIFACT, so a fix belongs in the
record: edit it with `bsc ui set`, then `bsc ui emit component <id> <dir>` and the file follows. Editing
the file directly loses the change — the record keeps the old body and the app renders the record (#4193).

`backing <path>` answers whether a file has a record before you touch it. It reads the store's own `src`
provenance, so it covers EVERY component, not only the pages in the migration catalogue. Prints
`{ path, backed, records: [{ id, kitId, src }] }`.

`backing gate <path>...` is the landing check: run it over the files your change touches (e.g.
`git diff --name-only`). It exits 1 and names the record + the two fix commands for every backed path, and
exits 0 when none are backed. Rejecting rather than warning is deliberate — a warning here becomes noise.

`backing reconcile` is the SEED half, and it is a DIFFERENT POPULATION from `audit`: `audit` reads the
STORE (what the running app renders), this reads `data/components/app/**` (what ships to a fresh install),
and the store carries harvested and de-seeded records the seed has never held — so a fix to one leaves the
other wrong. It is the gate in front of the whole file-retirement track: deleting a migrated file whose
record is the OLDER copy is a silent revert of real work, and when the two disagreed the FILE was the newer
copy in NINE OF NINE cases measured (#4235).

Six verdicts — `ok` · `null-src` (no `src` at all, the convention for a record with no file counterpart) ·
`stale-pointer` (`src` names a file that is not here) · `moved` (`src` resolves, but the record's SYMBOL is
not in it — re-point, do not refresh) · `drifted` (symbol present, bodies disagree) · `intentional`
(drifted, with an evidenced `srcDivergence` saying why, so the reason lives where a future sweep reads it).

It REPORTS on every run and writes only under a flag: `--apply` re-points what is UNAMBIGUOUS and never
guesses, `--annotate` records why a difference is by construction, `--retire` moves `src` to `srcRetired`
where the file is gone and nothing matches. So the same command answers \"what is wrong\" and \"fix what can
be fixed mechanically\", and answers the first one again afterwards.

SCOPE: components only. An algorithm record is a function LIFTED OUT of a file and several share one
`src` (#4192), so a path-based gate cannot be honest about them yet.",

    CmdDoc {
        name: "test",
        summary: "materialize a record + its CLOSURE + its paired tests into an EMPTY dir and run them there — a pass proves every dependency is a record or the declared platform",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui test <id> --out <dir> [--run]         # one record + its closure
  bsc ui test --all --out <dir> [--run]        # every record carrying a paired test, each in its own dir
  bsc ui test <id> --out <dir> --records-only  # is every dependency a RECORD yet? (migration progress)
  bsc ui test <id> --out <dir> --no-closure    # the STRICT form: the record utterly alone
  bsc ui test <id> --out <dir> --repo <dir>    # where the boundary's real files live (default: cwd)

The components twin of `bsc graph test`. Materializing OUT OF THE REPO is what makes the run mean
something: inside the repo every import resolves whether the record declares it or not.

What goes in with the record is its RECORD CLOSURE — every record its code imports, transitively
(materialize-a-records-record-closure). Components COMPOSE components, so a strict one-record
materialization can only ever verify leaves, and most of a UI library is not leaves. The closure resolves
the way the running app resolves: a `@/components/<id>` sibling, then a component whose `provides` is the
specifier, then an algorithm impl's. Members are written into a `_closure/` MIRROR of `src/` that `@` is
aliased to, so each sits at its real position and its own imports resolve with no source rewriting.

The loader's OTHER half comes in too: a dependency may be a record, or a module the PLATFORM REGISTRY
(`platform-modules.json`) declares. The two are supplied differently on purpose — a record is COPIED out
of the store into the mirror, a boundary module is ALIASED to the app's real file, one exact alias per
specifier actually reached. Never a blanket `@` onto `src/`: that would resolve everything and leave the
run proving nothing.

What is withheld is still APP CONTEXT — the repo tree, the app's aliases, the store. An import that is
NEITHER a record nor declared is left out and the run FAILS on it, even when the file is sitting right
there. Every run reports `closure` (records that came in, and from which store), `boundary` (what the app
still supplies from a FILE — this IS the per-record migration list) and `missing`.

The record under test is JUDGED; the boundary is SUPPLIED, not judged. Inside a boundary module the app's
own resolution applies, so its imports are followed whether declared or not, and those are reported with
`registered: false`. Judging the platform's internals would fail records over modules the app resolves
perfectly well — measuring the registry instead of the record.

--records-only empties the registry, so the run answers the MIGRATION question instead: is every one of
this record's dependencies a record YET? That is the progress measure, and it is a different question
from whether the record works.

--no-closure restores the strict one-record form: a pass there proves the record is a LEAF, importing no
other app module at all. That is the RETIRABILITY signal, and it runs opposite to usefulness — the
records that verify alone are the primitives everything imports.

The directory gets its own `vitest.config.ts`, or vitest walks UP, finds the repo's, and lends the record
the aliases and setup file isolation exists to withhold. The component file takes its ORIGINAL basename,
because the paired test imports it the way it always did (`./WorkerModals`, not `worker-modals`).
`environment` follows the test — jsdom when it reaches for @testing-library or `document`, node otherwise.

A record with NO paired test is refused rather than reported green: a vacuous pass would claim `verified`
about a record nothing checks. A test that reaches other app modules is not paired onto the record at all
— it belongs on an edge. `--all` exits non-zero when any record fails, and COUNTS the ones it skipped.",

    CmdDoc {
        name: "doctor",
        summary: "graph-health report — orphans, dead branches, duplicates, cycles, unbuildable + self-referential components (#2678)",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui doctor [--kit K] [--json] [--pretty]              # the health report (read-only)
  bsc ui doctor --category cat[,cat…] [--kit K] [--json]   # NARROW the report to one or more categories (#114)
  bsc ui doctor --sound-kit id@version [--json]            # judge @bsc/sounds/… against a PINNED sound kit (#3412)
  bsc ui doctor --motion [--kit K] [--json]                # ALSO run the four mechanical MOTION checks (#3163)
  bsc ui doctor --runtime [--kit K] [--json]               # ALSO report what the app OBSERVED while running
  bsc ui doctor --imports [--kit K] [--json]               # ALSO walk each record's import CLOSURE for a symbol the target never exports (#149)
  bsc ui doctor --fix [--kit K] [--yes]                    # OPTIMIZE: merge byte-identical dups + prune dead roots (dry-run unless --yes)

--category (#114) narrows the report to the named categories after every lens has contributed — so it
composes with --motion/--runtime/--imports rather than pre-empting them. Comma-separated for more than
one (`--category dangling-branch,orphan`); an unknown category name simply matches nothing, same as an
unknown --kit. Use it to check one category's status out of a 200+ finding report without a helper
script or re-parsing --json by hand.

--sound-kit (#3412) names the project's PINNED sound kit (its blueprint's `soundKit`, as `id@version` in the
`bsc sound release` store), so a `@bsc/sounds/<cue>` reference is judged against the kit the project actually
adopted — the same target the Design Studio's preview resolves. Omit it for an unpinned project and the
packaged default kit is used. A ref the store does not hold is a hard ERROR, never a quiet fall back to the
default: a pinned project reported against the starter kit would call broken sound references clean.

--motion (#3163) ADDS four mechanical animation checks to the report: MOTION-DEAD-SELECTOR (an animation
`selector` whose class hook the component's source never renders — it matches nothing), MOTION-DASH-NO-
PATHLENGTH (a stroke-dash(offset|array) keyframe on a component that sets no `pathLength` — a draw needs a
known path length), MOTION-TRANSFORM-ATTR (a CSS `transform` keyframe on a component using an SVG
`transform=` ATTRIBUTE — the two don't compose), and MOTION-NAME-COLLISION (an inline animation NAME
declared by 2+ components in the same kit — their keyframes clobber). They scan each component's INLINE
animation defs (a name-ref string points at the kit's shared library and is not checked).

--runtime (#doctor-reads-the-runtime) ADDS the findings this report structurally cannot reach, read from
runtime.db — what the RUNNING app observed rather than what the graph's shape implies. RUNTIME-DECLINED (the
loader refused the record and served the bundled platform module instead — the record is inert while the app
looks fine), RUNTIME-NEVER-RAN (no attestation at all; the honest superset of ORPHAN, which only sees
`composes` edges), RUNTIME-STALE (the record's current source has never run — an unexercised edit is where a
broken record hides), RUNTIME-FELL-BACK (an older version rendered instead), RUNTIME-RENDER-THREW (mounted,
then threw), RUNTIME-RECOMPILE-LOOP and RUNTIME-SLOW-COMPILE. With no attestations recorded it emits ONE
finding saying so rather than calling every record dead — an empty store means nothing was MEASURED, which
is not the same as nothing having run.

--imports (bsc request #149) ADDS UNRESOLVED-IMPORT-SYMBOL: `unresolvable-import` above only asks whether a
`@/…` specifier resolves to SOME record; this asks the sharper question — once it resolves, does the target
actually EXPORT the name being imported? Follows `export * from` barrels (and `export type * from`) through
the SAME resolution chain `bsc ui test`'s closure walker uses (sibling by id → component `provides` → algorithm
impl `provides`), and reads every comma-separated declarator in a `const`/`let`/`var` export, not just the
first — a checker that stops at either of those reports a record clean on exactly the drift that breaks it at
runtime with no typecheck error and no failing test (tsc/vitest compile the SEED file; the app loads the STORE
record, and the two can drift apart). Skips a specifier that resolves to no record at all — that gap is
UNRESOLVABLE-IMPORT's finding, not this one's, so the two never double-report the same defect.

Traverses each kit's composition graph (nodes = components, edges = `composes`) and reports the
dead/duplicated design a growing kit accumulates: CYCLE (a composes loop), DANGLING-BRANCH (an unused
root that still pulls in dependencies), DUPLICATE (two components wrapping the same intrinsic, or
byte-identical source), NO-IMPLEMENTATION (a component the Design Studio preview can't build — a spec,
not code; a built-in whose real source lives in the packaged artifact is NOT flagged), and ORPHAN (an
isolated, never-referenced primitive/composite). \"Unused\" = no composer AND used = 0; a page/layout
with used > 0 is a legit entry point, never flagged. Ranked most-severe-first; --kit scopes to one
kit; --json emits the findings array (LLM-consumable).

PROPS-METADATA-MISMATCH (#88) diffs each record's `props` against the prop signature parsed from its own
source, naming the missing and extra props. The preview's sample-data synthesizer reads `props` and
NOTHING else, so an EMPTY `props: []` on a component with a real typed signature silently leaves it
nothing to sample and the component renders with every prop undefined. Run kit-wide, it partitions a
render-error backlog into the crashes a `props` edit fixes and the ones that need a real change. It
reports only what it can read off the source — an imported props type or a `memo(…)` wrapper yields
nothing rather than a guess — and cedes the \"metadata names props the source never uses at all\" case to
UNWIRED-PROP, which already owns it.

DANGLING-COMPOSES-REFERENCE (#89) is the standard the designer doc always stated and nothing checked: a
`composes` entry naming no component in the kit, by name OR id. Both edge builders DROP an unresolved
name, so the graph reads as complete while the reference names nothing. One finding per MISSING
component, listing every composer — the fix is one record, not one per site — and it distinguishes the
two cases, whose fixes are opposites: the name exists NOWHERE (a forward reference to an extraction
never done ⇒ author the canonical record it already names) versus the name exists in ANOTHER kit
(`composes` only resolves within one kit ⇒ reach the record that exists; do not write a second copy).
Neither fix is a merge: `bsc ui dupes` used to report such a pair as a near-duplicate whose \"merge X
into Y\" the preview sandbox makes impossible, so that proposal now leads with the extraction instead.

SKIPS-FAMILY-SHELL (#87) is the question `dupes`/`similar` structurally cannot answer: which members of a
FAMILY do not compose the shell primitive the rest of it does. A family is a folder or a trailing-
PascalCase-word group of 6+ in one kit; a shell is any component 85%+ of that family composes AND its kit
composes widely (10+ composers), and the finding names the minority — at most three, or it is a split
rather than an outlier. Fuzzy name + prop-contract distance CANNOT see this: a toggle card has
`enabled`/`onToggle` and an info card has `value`/`label`, so siblings sharing a shell never meet in a
dupes report. It is a REPORT, not a rule — an outlier may be a deliberate exception.

--fix is the mechanical, SAFE OPTIMIZE (#3089): (1) MERGE byte-identical-source duplicates — fold each
group into the most-`used` canonical and repoint composers to it (lossless; only byte-identical, never a
same-`wraps` dup; a merged-away `builtin: true` dup gets a suppression tombstone instead of a bare delete,
same as `bsc ui merge`, so it survives the next hydrate — #96), then (2) PRUNE the GUARDED dead roots — the
ROOT of each orphan/dangling-branch finding (never a used > 0 node). DRY RUN by default (prints what WOULD
change); pass --yes to apply. Cycles and same-`wraps` (differing-source) duplicates are NOT auto-resolved —
they need a semantic call. Branch descendants are left for the next pass (one might be shared) — re-run to
clean them.

The PRUNE GUARDS (#3087) — the dead-root heuristic is a good REPORT and a dangerous auto-DELETE, so three
classes of candidate are named, then held back: a `page` (a page is a root BY DEFINITION — nothing composes
a page, so the heuristic condemns the whole pages tier), a `builtin: true` packaged seed (shipped on
purpose; the seed reconcile re-adds it), and EVERY candidate while the usage index is unpopulated (no
component in scope carries used > 0, so `used = 0` means UNKNOWN, not unused). A held-back candidate is
still REPORTED by `bsc ui doctor` — only the automatic removal is withheld. #2678/#2679/#3089/#3087.",

    CmdDoc {
        name: "dupes",
        summary: "the whole-library duplicate report — exact + fuzzy NEAR-duplicates (name + contract distance), propose-only (#3544)",
        usage: "\
USAGE:
  bsc ui dupes [--kit K] [--threshold 0..1] [--explain] [--json] [--pretty]

The DEDUP surface. Reports the EXACT `duplicate` findings the per-kit analyzer emits (two components sharing
a `wraps` intrinsic, or byte-identical source) PLUS the FUZZY near-duplicates it structurally misses —
`Donut`≈`DonutChart`, `Bars`≈`BarChart`, `Legend`≈`ChartLegend`, and cross-kit `Card`/`Grid`/`KeyValueList`
repeats a growing multi-kit library accumulates. Each near-duplicate is scored by NAME distance (normalized
token-set + edit distance; `Chart`/`View`/`Bsc` affixes stripped, names singularized) and CONTRACT/body
distance, combined 0.5·name + 0.5·contract. Cross-kit by design — the whole point is consolidating
overlapping kits into one.

CONTRACT TERMS (#4138): prop-signature · source shingles · `src` (same file — a strong PRIOR, not a verdict:
several components are legitimately extracted from one module) · `folder` · `composes` · `shapes` ·
`whenUse`/`whenNot` guidance · variants · tags · colocated `tests` · `wraps` · role. A term with NO signal on
either side is DROPPED, never scored 0 — two prop-less primitives must not read as identical for both
lacking props.

A pair is contract-scored when its NAME is near OR it shares a hard co-location signal (same `src`, folder,
`wraps`, `provides`, shape or test file). Before #4138 a dissimilar name alone skipped the pair entirely, so
`Donut` vs `PieChart` — the duplicates you cannot grep for — were invisible unless byte-identical.

Also reports `provides-collision`: several records overriding ONE platform specifier. Not a similarity
score — the loader resolves it to one record, so the rest are dead overrides that still read as live.

SUPPRESSED RECORDS ARE NOT SCORED, here or in `bsc ui similar`. A tombstone keeps its id and loses every
content field, so every contract term drops for want of signal and NAME similarity alone is left carrying
the pair — and ids retired together are named alike by construction. Left in, one batch consolidation
mints a mutually near-duplicate clique out of the records it just retired: the live store's largest
cluster was 31 `settings-*card` tombstones proposing the consolidation that produced them, with 41 of the
store's 58 tombstones somewhere in the report, sitting on top of the live clusters. Asking about a
tombstone BY id still answers — it is ranked against the live library, and `similar` says the record is
retired so a thin result is not read as `nothing resembles it`.

A SHARED FORWARD REFERENCE is not shared code (#89). `composes` is a raw string-set match that never asks
whether a name resolves, so two records both naming a component nobody has authored score 1.0 on that term.
Where that fabricated agreement is the only thing carrying a pair over the bar, the pair is DROPPED — the
signal is `bsc ui doctor`'s `dangling-composes-reference`, not a duplicate. Where the pair stands on real
evidence anyway (same `src`, same folder, overlapping bodies), it is still reported, but the proposal leads
with AUTHORING the record both already name: that extraction is the consolidation, and a literal merge is
not available, because the preview sandbox forbids the first-party import it would need.

--explain prints each pair's per-term contributions (`term=value×weight→contribution`) and the terms dropped
for lack of signal, so the ranking is auditable and the weights are tunable against real output.

--threshold tunes the fuzzy bar (default 0.55); --kit scopes to ONE kit (which drops cross-kit near-dups);
--json emits the findings array (LLM-consumable), each `{ category, severity, kit, nodeIds, nodeNames, why,
suggestedAction }`. PROPOSE-ONLY: there is no `--fix` here — a near-duplicate is a WEAKER signal than a
byte-identical dup and the merge is a semantic call, so use these proposals to guide a manual/designer merge.
Inspect one component's neighborhood with `bsc ui similar <id>`. #3544.",

settings cards composing [Card, ToggleRow] around one skeleton score 34% blended and never meet.

Each cluster carries three things beyond its member list:

              them. A member list says WHICH records are alike; the signature says WHAT they are, which

  cohesion    the WEAKEST pairwise score inside the cluster. Connected components CHAIN — A~B and B~C

              an exact equivalence class.

(default 2; a pair is a legitimate pattern-of-two); --kit scopes; --json emits the clusters; --pretty
indents. The threshold and the counts are always PRINTED before the rows, because a sweep whose bar is
invisible reads as `this is everything`.

Suppressed records are excluded, as everywhere on this surface. A READ — never scope-gated.

NOT a dedup proposal. Two records sharing a shape are usually SUPPOSED to: that is what a pattern is.

  bsc ui pattern of <component-id> [--json]
  bsc ui pattern remove <id>

`bsc ui patterns` (plural) FINDS the library's structural conventions. This names one. A cluster is a
report — recomputed every sweep, with nothing to point at — so the only way to author into an existing
convention is to find a sibling and copy it, which is how the convention drifts and how a fifth copy
gets written by a session that believed it was writing a first.

settings-toggle-card`, and a pattern you are INSTANTIATING is not one you can duplicate.
