/// Gather the authored motion (kit libraries + component INLINE defs) into flat AnimationDefs and compile
/// them to CSS (#3163). KIT-level animations emit un-namespaced (`bsc-<kit>-<name>`); a component's inline
/// animations are NAMESPACED by the owning component (`bsc-<kit>-<component>-<name>`) so two components'
/// same-named animations don't collide. A name-ref string on a component points at the kit's shared
/// library (already emitted from the kit pass), so only object entries are taken here. `kit` scopes to one
/// kit id. Pure over the two stores → driven directly by tests.
fn collect_motion_css(
    kit: Option<&str>,
    kit_store: &bsc_json_store::Store,
    comp_store: &bsc_json_store::Store,
) -> String {
    let scoped = |kit_id: &str| kit.is_none_or(|k| k == kit_id);
    let mut defs: Vec<serde_json::Value> = Vec::new();

    // KIT-level motion libraries → `bsc-<kit>-<name>` (no component namespace).
    for raw in kit_store.list() {
        let Ok(k) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&raw) else {
            continue;
        };
        let kit_id = k.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
        if !scoped(kit_id) {
            continue;
        }
        if let Some(anims) = k.get("animations").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_array) {
            for a in anims {
                if let Some(def) = crate::motion::anim_def(a, kit_id, None) {
                    defs.push(def);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // COMPONENT INLINE motion → namespaced by the owning component (#3163).
    for raw in comp_store.list() {
        let Ok(c) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&raw) else {
            continue;
        };
        let kit_id = c.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
        if !scoped(kit_id) {
            continue;
        }
        let name = c.get("name").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
        if let Some(anims) = c.get("animations").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_array) {
            for a in anims {
                if a.is_object() {
                    if let Some(def) = crate::motion::anim_def(a, kit_id, Some(name)) {
                        defs.push(def);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    crate::motion::compile_animations_css(&defs)
}

/// `kit emit-motion-css [--kit K]` (#3163) — compile the authored motion (kit libraries + component inline
/// defs) to CSS and print it, so an author can SEE the keyframes/rules/delays instead of guessing from the
/// data. A custom READ over BOTH the kit and component stores (never scope-gated). `--dir`/`--component-dir`
/// override the two store paths (for tests).
fn cmd_emit_motion_css(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut kit, mut kit_dir, mut comp_dir) = (None::<String>, None::<String>, None::<String>);
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--kit" => kit = it.next().cloned(),
            "--dir" => kit_dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--component-dir" => comp_dir = it.next().cloned(),
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            other => return Err(format!("unexpected argument '{other}'")),
        }
    }
    let kit_store = open_kit_store(&kit_dir)?;
    let comp_store = open_component_store(&comp_dir)?;
    println!("{}", collect_motion_css(kit.as_deref(), &kit_store, &comp_store));
    Ok(())
}

// ── granular writes (#3162) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// `set-src` / `patch` / `get --field`: edit or read ONE field of a component record without a
// whole-record round-trip (and its ~10KB stdin ceiling). Every WRITE path still runs the `set` write-
// time JSX syntax gate (`validate_component_batch`, #2928) so a granular write can't smuggle in a
// module `srcText` that won't build. The core mutations (`replace_src` / `apply_patch`) are pure of
// stdin/print so tests drive them directly; the `cmd_*` wrappers add arg/stdin parsing + the ui-scope
// gate (honored BEFORE stdin/the store are touched, like `doctor --fix`).

/// Normalize a user-supplied JSON pointer: a leading `/` is optional for ergonomics, so `name` and
/// `/name` both address the top-level `name` field (the empty string stays empty — the whole doc).
///
/// Rejects a pointer that git-bash's MSYS path conversion has REWRITTEN. Any argument starting with `/`
/// is treated by MSYS as a unix path and rewritten to the git install root — so `--field /name` reaches
/// the process as `C:/Program Files/Git/name`. The old failure was `no field 'C:/Program Files/Git/name'`,
/// which reads as a missing field and sent a caller hunting for the wrong thing; the studio sessions run
/// in git-bash, so every pointer they passed the documented way silently mis-addressed (#3383).
///
/// We ERROR rather than recover: the mangled form is `<install-root><pointer>` and the root's length is
/// not knowable in-process, so stripping it would be a guess at WHICH field was meant — and a wrong guess
/// on `patch` writes the wrong field. A drive-letter prefix is an unambiguous tell (no legitimate pointer
/// token starts with `C:`), so this only ever fires on genuine damage, and it names the fix.
fn normalize_pointer(p: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    let b = p.as_bytes();
    if b.len() >= 3 && b[0].is_ascii_alphabetic() && b[1] == b':' && (b[2] == b'/' || b[2] == b'\\') {
        // Deliberately NOT reconstructing the intended pointer: the mangled form is
        // `<install-root><pointer>` and the root's length is unknowable here, so any tail we picked
        // would be a guess — and naming the wrong field on `patch` steers a wrong WRITE. State the
        // rule instead; the caller knows which field they meant.
        return Err(format!(
            "'{p}' is not a JSON pointer — a leading '/' was rewritten by git-bash path conversion.\n\
             Re-run WITHOUT the leading slash (`name`, `animations/1`), not with it (`/name`). The \
             leading '/' is optional everywhere a pointer is taken, and the slash-free form is never \
             rewritten.\n\
             Do NOT prefix the command with MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 — a restricted session cannot run an \
             environment-variable assignment."
        ));
    }
    Ok(if p.is_empty() || p.starts_with('/') { p.to_string() } else { format!("/{p}") })
}

/// Set `value` at the RFC-6901 JSON pointer `pointer` within `root`, replacing (or inserting, for an
/// object key or an array append slot) exactly that one field. The pointer's PARENT container must
/// already exist — this is a granular field write, not a deep-create. An array token is a numeric index
/// (which may equal the length to append) or `-` (push). Escapes: `~1`→`/`, `~0`→`~`. Pure → unit-tested.
fn set_at_pointer(root: &mut serde_json::Value, pointer: &str, value: serde_json::Value) -> Result<(), String> {
    use serde_json::Value;
    let tokens: Vec<String> = if pointer.is_empty() {
        Vec::new()
    } else {
        pointer[1..].split('/').map(|t| t.replace("~1", "/").replace("~0", "~")).collect()
    };
    let Some((last, parents)) = tokens.split_last() else {
        // An empty pointer would replace the whole record — refuse (patch is a FIELD write).
        return Err("a JSON pointer must name at least one field (e.g. `/name`)".to_string());
    };
    // Walk to the parent container; each intermediate level must already exist.
    let mut cur = root;
    for tok in parents {
        cur = match cur {
            Value::Object(map) => map
                .get_mut(tok)
                .ok_or_else(|| format!("no object key '{tok}' along the pointer '{pointer}'"))?,
            Value::Array(arr) => {
                let i: usize =
                    tok.parse().map_err(|_| format!("pointer token '{tok}' is not a valid array index"))?;
                arr.get_mut(i).ok_or_else(|| format!("array index {i} out of range along '{pointer}'"))?
            }
            _ => return Err(format!("pointer '{pointer}' descends into a non-container at '{tok}'")),
        };
    }
    // Set the final token on the parent container.
    match cur {
        Value::Object(map) => {
            map.insert(last.clone(), value);
            Ok(())
        }
        Value::Array(arr) => {
            if last == "-" {
                arr.push(value);
                return Ok(());
            }
            let i: usize = last
                .parse()
                .map_err(|_| format!("pointer token '{last}' is not a valid array index (or `-` to append)"))?;
            match i.cmp(&arr.len()) {
                std::cmp::Ordering::Less => {
                    arr[i] = value;
                    Ok(())
                }
                std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => {
                    arr.push(value);
                    Ok(())
                }
                std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => Err(format!(
                    "array index {i} is out of range (len {}) — a patch cannot leave holes",
                    arr.len()
                )),
            }
        }
        _ => Err(format!("cannot set '{last}': the parent along '{pointer}' is not an object or array")),
    }
}

/// The writer that most recently authored a record's `srcText`, read from its change history — `None`
/// when the record has no history, or no entry ever touched `srcText` (nothing recorded to protect).
///
/// A `created` entry counts. `changed_fields` records the first write as `["created"]` rather than
/// listing the fields, so a record AUTHORED with its `srcText` and never rewritten would otherwise read
/// as unattributed and be left unguarded — which is exactly the newly-authored Design Studio record
/// this is meant to protect. The branch this is recovered from stopped at `srcText` entries and had
/// that hole.
fn last_src_writer(record: &serde_json::Value) -> Option<String> {
    let authored_src = record
        .get(crate::record::SRC_TEXT)
        .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)
        .is_some_and(|s| !s.trim().is_empty());
    record
        .get(crate::record::HISTORY)
        .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_array)?
        .iter()
        .rev()
        .find(|e| {
            e.get("changed").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_array).is_some_and(|a| {
                a.iter().any(|v| {
                    v.as_str() == Some(crate::record::SRC_TEXT)
                        || (authored_src && v.as_str() == Some("created"))
                })
            })
        })
        .and_then(|e| e.get("by").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str))
        .map(str::to_owned)
}

/// Refuse an UNATTRIBUTED `srcText` write (`writer == "unknown"` — no `--by`, no `$BSC_UI_WRITER`) that
/// would replace content someone DID attribute to themselves.
///
/// This is the half [`refuse_buildable_regression`] cannot see. That guard asks whether the new source
/// still BUILDS, so an overwrite that happens to stay buildable — most of them — passes it cleanly while
/// still destroying someone's work with no record of who did it. `kitsharemodal` rev4-6 and
/// `consolepage` rev11-12 were both lost exactly that way: writer `"unknown"`, no note, both restored by
/// hand from `prevSrc` (bsc request #119).
///
/// Deliberately narrow, because a false refusal on a legitimate automated write would be a daily tax:
/// an attributed writer of ANY name passes, a write over previously-unattributed source passes (there is
/// no one to protect), identical content passes (nothing is lost), and `--force` passes. What is left is
/// precisely "an anonymous write is about to destroy a named author's source".
fn refuse_anonymous_src_overwrite(
    id: &str,
    prior: &serde_json::Value,
    new_src: &str,
    writer: &str,
    force: bool,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    if force || writer != "unknown" {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let Some(prior_writer) = last_src_writer(prior) else { return Ok(()) };
    if prior_writer == "unknown" {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let prior_src =
        prior.get(crate::record::SRC_TEXT).and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
    if prior_src == new_src {
        return Ok(()); // identical content — nothing would be lost
    }
    Err(format!(
        "'{id}': refusing an UNATTRIBUTED write over srcText last authored by '{prior_writer}' — this is \
         exactly the shape that silently regressed a designer's preview fix back to unbuildable app \
         source (bsc request #119). Identify the write (--by <tag>, or $BSC_UI_WRITER), or pass --force \
         if this really should overwrite '{prior_writer}'s source."
    ))
}


/// Refuse to regress a PREVIEW-BUILDABLE `srcText` (the Design Studio preview sandbox can compile and
/// mount it — [`crate::graph_health::looks_buildable_module`]) into one it cannot, on a record that
/// carries no `provides`. `provides` is what turns "the preview sandbox can't build this" from a defect
/// into a deliberate module-lift outcome (#43) — and a record with none yet is exactly the state
/// `bsc ui set-src` leaves it in for the first of `lift-component-module.mjs`'s two writes (`set-src` the
/// faithful module, THEN `set --provides` in a second call). Un-refused, nothing marked that in-between
/// state as a real regression rather than corruption: the write-time gate only WARNS on an unbuildable
/// non-page `srcText` (`validate_component_batch`), so the first write landed silently and the record
/// stayed exactly there whenever the follow-up `set --provides` call never ran (or targeted the wrong
/// id) — which is how a designer-authored preview stub (bsc request #119: `KitShareModal`/`ConsolePage`)
/// got silently clobbered back to raw `@/…`-importing app source no preview could render.
///
/// `--force` ([`FORCE_WRITE`], the same escape `set` already has for the page-role refusal) is the
/// deliberate override — e.g. a genuine module lift that sets `provides` in a LATER call, same as the
/// script does today.
fn refuse_buildable_regression(old_record: &serde_json::Value, new_src: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    let provides = old_record.get("provides").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
    if !provides.trim().is_empty() {
        return Ok(()); // already a module record — `provides` beats the preview sandbox (#43)
    }
    let old_src = old_record.get("srcText").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
    if !crate::graph_health::looks_buildable_module(old_src) {
        return Ok(()); // nothing buildable was there to protect
    }
    if crate::graph_health::looks_buildable_module(new_src) {
        return Ok(()); // still buildable — not a regression
    }
    if FORCE_WRITE.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let id = old_record.get("id").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or("<no id>");
    Err(format!(
        "'{id}': refusing to overwrite a srcText the Design Studio preview can BUILD with one it can't ({}). \
         This record carries no `provides`, so nothing marks the new source as a deliberate module lift \
         rather than a silent regression (bsc request #119). Set `provides` in the SAME write if this is a \
         real module lift, or pass --force to store it anyway.",
        crate::graph_health::module_defects(new_src).join("; ")
    ))
}

/// Replace ONLY component `id`'s `srcText` with `src`, leaving every other field untouched, then run the
/// SAME write-time JSX syntax gate as `set` (#2928) before writing. The write funnels through
/// [`stamped_set`] so it bumps `rev`/`updatedAt`/`updatedBy` like every other `bsc ui` mutation (#3164).
/// Errors when the component is absent. Pure of stdin/print so tests drive it directly.
pub fn replace_src(
    store: &bsc_json_store::Store,
    id: &str,
    src: &str,
    by: Option<&str>,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut record = load_component_object(store, id)?;
    let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(by);
    refuse_anonymous_src_overwrite(
        id,
        &record,
        src,
        &writer,
        FORCE_WRITE.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
    )?;
    refuse_buildable_regression(&record, src)?;
    record
        .as_object_mut()
        .expect("load_component_object guarantees an object")
        .insert("srcText".to_string(), serde_json::Value::String(src.to_string()));
    validate_component_batch(std::slice::from_ref(&record))?;
    stamped_set(store, id, record, &writer)?;
    // #3737: `set-src` invalidates the last render — clear any stale `render-error` so `bsc ui doctor`
    // doesn't keep reporting the pre-edit throw (batch `set` already does this, #43; set-src/patch didn't,
    // which is how the #11/#21 stale errors survived). Best-effort; a no-op unless this id has an error.
    let _ = crate::preview_errors::clear(id);
    Ok(())
}

/// Drop `provides` from component `id` — the DISARM half of a records-carry-relative-imports repair.
///
/// A record that diverges from the live file it names is not the whole module, so its `provides` is a
/// false claim; and because a record's `provides` BEATS the platform registry, leaving it in place while
/// repairing its imports would turn a preview-shaped derivative into a working, LIVE override of the
/// module it derives from. That is why the repair drops the claim FIRST and rewrites second — the other
/// order leaves a window, and the app is running while this happens.
///
/// Goes through [`stamped_set`] like every other mutation, so the drop is stamped and appears in
/// `bsc ui log` rather than being an untraceable edit.
pub fn clear_provides(
    store: &bsc_json_store::Store,
    id: &str,
    by: Option<&str>,
    note: Option<&str>,
) -> Result<bool, String> {
    let mut record = load_component_object(store, id)?;
    {
        let obj = record.as_object_mut().expect("load_component_object guarantees an object");
        if obj.remove("provides").is_none() {
            return Ok(false); // nothing claimed — not an error, just nothing to disarm
        }
    }
    let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(by);
    // Mirrors `stamped_set`, but carries the NOTE: why a claim was dropped is the part a reader needs
    // months later, and `stamped_set` has no channel for it.
    let prior = current_record(store, id)?;
    crate::record::stamp_with_history(
        &mut record,
        &prior,
        &writer,
        &crate::record::now_iso(),
        note,
    );
    store.set(id, &serde_json::to_string(&record).map_err(|e| format!("set: {e}"))?)?;
    Ok(true)
}

/// Set `value` at `pointer` on component `id`'s record, then run the `set` syntax gate (#2928) — so a
/// `patch /srcText …` can't smuggle in a module that won't build. The write funnels through
/// [`stamped_set`] so it bumps `rev`/`updatedAt`/`updatedBy` like every other `bsc ui` mutation (#3164).
/// Errors when the component (or the pointer's parent) is absent. Pure of stdin/print so tests drive it.
fn apply_patch(
    store: &bsc_json_store::Store,
    id: &str,
    pointer: &str,
    value: serde_json::Value,
    by: Option<&str>,
) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut record = load_component_object(store, id)?;
    let pointer = normalize_pointer(pointer)?;
    let writer = crate::record::resolve_writer(by);
    if pointer == "/srcText" {
        if let serde_json::Value::String(new_src) = &value {
            refuse_anonymous_src_overwrite(
                id,
                &record,
                new_src,
                &writer,
                FORCE_WRITE.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
            )?;
            refuse_buildable_regression(&record, new_src)?;
        }
    }
    set_at_pointer(&mut record, &pointer, value)?;
    validate_component_batch(std::slice::from_ref(&record))?;
    stamped_set(store, id, record, &writer)?;
    // #3737: a component patch invalidates the last render — clear any stale `render-error` (see `replace_src`).
    let _ = crate::preview_errors::clear(id);
    Ok(())
}

/// Render ONE resolved field value for `get --field` to the string to emit: `raw` unwraps a string (no
/// quotes/escaping) so a shell capture is clean — a non-string value still prints as compact JSON;
/// otherwise JSON (pretty indents). The raw string is EMITTED via the shared [`bsc_cli_util::print_raw`]
/// (#3166) by the caller, so `--field --raw` is byte-identical to the whole-record `--raw`. Pure → unit-tested.
fn field_output(value: &serde_json::Value, raw: bool, pretty: bool) -> Result<String, String> {
    if raw {
        return Ok(match value {
            serde_json::Value::String(s) => s.clone(),
            other => serde_json::to_string(other).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?,
        });
    }
    if pretty {
        serde_json::to_string_pretty(value).map_err(|e| e.to_string())
    } else {
        serde_json::to_string(value).map_err(|e| e.to_string())
    }
}

/// The two flags the granular `srcText` writes (`set-src`, `patch`) accept beyond `parse_anim_args`:
/// `--force` (armed into [`FORCE_WRITE`], the same escape `set` has for the page-role refusal) and
/// `--by <tag>` (the writer, matching `bsc ui set --by`).
///
/// Parsed HERE rather than by widening [`parse_anim_args`], which a dozen other verbs share and whose
/// strict unknown-flag errors must stay strict — the same reasoning `SuppressArgs` already follows.
struct SrcWriteArgs {
    /// Everything `parse_anim_args` should still see.
    rest: Vec<String>,
    /// `--by <tag>`, or `None` to fall back to `$BSC_UI_WRITER` and then `"unknown"`.
    by: Option<String>,
}

/// Pull `--force` and `--by <tag>` out of an args list, arming [`FORCE_WRITE`] for the former and
/// returning the rest for [`parse_anim_args`]. A `--by` with no value is an ERROR rather than a silent
/// no-op: a write that MEANT to identify itself and silently did not is the failure this whole guard
/// exists to stop, so it must not be reachable by a typo.
fn parse_src_write_args(args: &[String]) -> Result<SrcWriteArgs, String> {
    let mut rest = Vec::with_capacity(args.len());
    let mut by = None;
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--force" => FORCE_WRITE.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
            "--by" => {
                let v = it.next().ok_or("--by needs a value: --by <tag>")?;
                if v.trim().is_empty() || v.starts_with("--") {
                    return Err("--by needs a value: --by <tag>".to_string());
                }
                by = Some(v.clone());
            }
            _ => rest.push(a.clone()),
        }
    }
    Ok(SrcWriteArgs { rest, by })
}

/// `set-src <id> [--dir D] [--force]` (#3162) — replace ONLY component <id>'s `srcText` from stdin. A
/// ui-scope MUTATION: the write-scope is honored BEFORE stdin/the store are touched (so a read-scoped
/// session refuses immediately without blocking on stdin). `--force` is the escape for
/// [`refuse_buildable_regression`] (bsc request #119).
fn cmd_set_src(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let parsed = parse_src_write_args(args)?;
    let (pos, dir, _pretty) = parse_anim_args(&parsed.rest)?;
    let id = pos
        .first()
        .ok_or("usage: bsc ui set-src <id> [--by <tag>] [--force]   # the new srcText on stdin")?;
    bsc_cli_util::require_write_scope("ui")?;
    let mut src = String::new();
    std::io::stdin().read_to_string(&mut src).map_err(|e| format!("cannot read stdin: {e}"))?;
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    replace_src(&store, id, &src, parsed.by.as_deref())?;
    bsc_util::emit_ui_activity("component", id);
    println!("{id}");
    Ok(())
}

/// `patch <id> <json-pointer> <value> [--dir D] [--force]` (#3162) — set ONE field by JSON pointer,
/// parsing <value> as JSON (else a bare string). A ui-scope MUTATION (gated before the store is touched).
/// `--force` is the escape for [`refuse_buildable_regression`] when `<json-pointer>` is `/srcText`.
fn cmd_patch(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    const USAGE: &str = "usage: bsc ui patch <id> <json-pointer> <value> [--by <tag>] [--force]";
    let parsed = parse_src_write_args(args)?;
    let (pos, dir, _pretty) = parse_anim_args(&parsed.rest)?;
    let id = pos.first().ok_or(USAGE)?;
    let pointer = pos.get(1).ok_or(USAGE)?;
    let raw_value = pos.get(2).ok_or(USAGE)?;
    bsc_cli_util::require_write_scope("ui")?;
    // JSON when it parses, else a bare string (so `/name Button` stores "Button" without the quotes).
    let value: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(raw_value)
        .unwrap_or_else(|_| serde_json::Value::String(raw_value.clone()));
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    apply_patch(&store, id, pointer, value, parsed.by.as_deref())?;
    bsc_util::emit_ui_activity("component", id);
    println!("{id}");
    Ok(())
}

/// `get <id> [--field <json-pointer>] [--raw] [--dir D] [--pretty] [--out <name>]` — the read verbs this
/// crate intercepts (the shared store CLI rejects the extra flags). Prints the whole record, or ONE
/// `--field` resolved by JSON pointer (#3162), to stdout — OR, with `--out <name>`, writes the exact same
/// bytes into `$BSC_SCRATCH/<name>` (#3713) and prints that path. A read verb (never scope-gated); errors
/// when the component OR the `--field` is absent.
///
/// **Why `--out` exists:** a restricted studio session truncates large stdout (~30KB) and spills the
/// remainder to a path OUTSIDE the confinement, which the FS hook then blocks Read/Grep from opening — so a
/// large `srcText` (e.g. a 538-line page) can't be reviewed via stdout at all. `--out` lands it in the
/// scratch dir, a confinement-allowed path the session Reads in full regardless of size.
fn cmd_get(args: &[String]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let (mut id, mut dir, mut field, mut out, mut kit) =
        (None::<String>, None::<String>, None::<String>, None::<String>, None::<String>);
    let (mut raw, mut pretty) = (false, false);
    let mut it = args.iter();
    while let Some(a) = it.next() {
        match a.as_str() {
            "--dir" => dir = it.next().cloned(),
            "--field" => field = it.next().cloned(),
            "--out" => out = it.next().cloned(),
            "--kit" => kit = it.next().cloned(),
            "--raw" => raw = true,
            "--pretty" => pretty = true,
            other if other.starts_with("--") => return Err(format!("unknown flag '{other}'")),
            positional if id.is_none() => id = Some(positional.to_string()),
            other => return Err(format!("unexpected argument '{other}'")),
        }
    }
    let id = id.ok_or("usage: bsc ui get <id> [--field <json-pointer>] [--kit <kitId>] [--raw] [--out <name>]")?;
    let store = open_component_store(&dir)?;
    let record = load_component_object(&store, &id)?;
    // #3729: `--kit <kitId>` disambiguates. The store is keyed by id ALONE, so there is exactly ONE
    // record per id — this asserts WHICH kit it belongs to (a designer who harvested a same-named
    // component into another kit believed two coexisted). Errors, naming the ACTUAL kit, on a mismatch.
    if let Some(want_kit) = &kit {
        let actual = record.get("kitId").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str).unwrap_or_default();
        if actual != want_kit {
            return Err(format!(
                "component '{id}' is in kit '{actual}', not '{want_kit}' — the store is keyed by id, so there is exactly one '{id}' (the last write wins)"
            ));
        }
    }
    // The value to render: one `--field`, else the whole record. `field_output` handles both a scalar
    // field and a whole object uniformly (raw string-unwraps, else compact/pretty JSON).
    let text = match &field {
        Some(f) => {
            let value = record
                .pointer(&normalize_pointer(f)?)
                .ok_or_else(|| format!("no field '{f}' in component '{id}'"))?;
            field_output(value, raw, pretty)?
        }
        None => {
            // A whole-record read follows Claude's working focus in the studio (#3545), matching the
            // plain `get <id>`; a `--field` read does not (it's an inspection of one attribute).
            bsc_util::emit_ui_focus("component", &id);
            field_output(&record, raw, pretty)?
        }
    };
    match out {
        // Spill to the sealed scratch dir — same bytes stdout would carry: raw ⇒ the #3166 LF-only,
        // CR-stripped, single-trailing-LF form; non-raw ⇒ the value + one newline (like `println!`).
        Some(name) => {
            let path = bsc_cli_util::resolve_scratch_out(&name)?;
            let bytes = if raw { bsc_cli_util::raw_line(&text) } else { format!("{text}\n") };
            std::fs::write(&path, bytes.as_bytes())
                .map_err(|e| format!("cannot write --out {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
            // Report the absolute path so the session knows exactly what to Read next.
            println!("{}", path.display());
        }
        None if raw => {
            // Compose with the shared #3166 raw printer so `--field --raw` behaves IDENTICALLY to the
            // whole-record `--raw`: LF-only (CR-stripped), bytes-direct (no locale layer), one trailing LF.
            bsc_cli_util::print_raw(&text);
        }
        None => println!("{text}"),
    }
    Ok(())
}

    /// #3606 — export dumps the store to a folder tree nested by `folder`, import loads it back, and the
    /// round-trip is lossless; a kit BUNDLE ({components:[…]}, e.g. react-ui.json) is exploded on import.
    #[test]
    fn export_import_round_trips_a_folder_tree_and_explodes_a_bundle() {
        let base = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("bsc-comp-io-roundtrip-{}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&base);
        let store_dir = base.join("store");
        let tree = base.join("tree");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&store_dir).unwrap();
        let store = bsc_json_store::Store::new(store_dir.clone(), "component");
        // One nested-by-FOLDER component, one unfoldered. (This fixture used the legacy `group` key
        // until finish-the-4107-group-to-folder-shim removed the alias that made it resolve.)
        store.set("card", r#"{"id":"card","name":"Card","folder":"ui/data","srcText":"export const Card=()=>null;"}"#).unwrap();
        store.set("loose", r#"{"id":"loose","name":"Loose","srcText":"export const Loose=()=>null;"}"#).unwrap();

        // export → files nest by the `group` folder path; ungrouped sits at the root.
        cmd_export(&["--dir".into(), store_dir.to_string_lossy().into_owned(), tree.to_string_lossy().into_owned()]).unwrap();
        assert!(tree.join("ui/data/card.json").exists(), "grouped component nests by its folder path");
        assert!(tree.join("loose.json").exists(), "ungrouped component sits at the tree root");

        // wipe the store, then import the tree back — lossless.
        store.remove("card").unwrap();
        store.remove("loose").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(store.list().len(), 0, "store cleared before re-import");
        cmd_import(&["--dir".into(), store_dir.to_string_lossy().into_owned(), tree.to_string_lossy().into_owned()]).unwrap();
        let card: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&store.get("card").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(card["folder"], "ui/data", "the foldered record imported back verbatim");
        assert_eq!(card["srcText"], "export const Card=()=>null;");
        assert!(store.get("loose").unwrap().is_some(), "the ungrouped record imported back too");

        // a kit bundle file is exploded — every component inside it is imported.
        std::fs::write(tree.join("bundle.json"), r#"{"id":"kit","components":[{"id":"x","name":"X"},{"id":"y","name":"Y"}]}"#).unwrap();
        cmd_import(&["--dir".into(), store_dir.to_string_lossy().into_owned(), tree.to_string_lossy().into_owned()]).unwrap();
        assert!(store.get("x").unwrap().is_some() && store.get("y").unwrap().is_some(), "the bundle's components were exploded in");
        assert!(store.get("kit").unwrap().is_none(), "the bundle wrapper itself is NOT stored as a component");

        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&base);
    }

    /// The component half of the stateful-shadow refusal. `bsc graph impl set` has enforced this since

    /// component records — so this tier was ungoverned entirely.
    #[test]
    fn validate_component_batch_refuses_a_stateful_record_that_provides_a_registered_specifier() {
        // A specifier the manifest really registers, so the test moves with the manifest instead of
        // asserting against a name invented here.
        let spec = "@/shared/lib/a11y/announcer";
        assert!(
            bsc_graph::is_registered_platform_module(spec),
            "fixture assumes {spec} is registered; update the fixture if the manifest changed"
        );

        let stateful = serde_json::json!({
            "id": "announcer-shadow", "name": "Announcer", "provides": spec,
            "srcText": "import { create } from \"zustand\";\nexport const useAnnouncer = create((set) => ({ msg: \"\" }));\n",
        });
        let err = validate_component_batch(std::slice::from_ref(&stateful)).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("announcer-shadow"), "names the record; got: {err}");
        assert!(err.contains("useAnnouncer"), "names the STATE, not just the rule; got: {err}");

        // The same record without the claim is fine — the refusal is about the specifier, not the state.
        let mut no_claim = stateful.clone();
        no_claim["provides"] = serde_json::Value::String(String::new());

        // which is why 315 pure shadows are deliberately allowed to stand.
        let pure = serde_json::json!({
            "id": "pure-shadow", "name": "Pure", "provides": spec,
            "srcText": "export const label = (s: string) => s.trim();\n",
        });
        assert!(validate_component_batch(std::slice::from_ref(&pure)).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_import_no_record_publishes_warns_at_write_time() {
        // DESIGNER REQUEST #73. `@/components/<id>` resolves ONLY when the target declares
        // `provides: "@/components/<id>"` — the id alone is not a specifier. roledot published nothing,
        // so the write was accepted and `bsc navigate` refused to build it two tool-calls later.
        let dir = tmp_store_dir("unresolvable-import");
        let store = bsc_json_store::Store::new(dir, "component");
        // A target that publishes its specifier, and one that does not.
        store
            .set("roledot", r#"{"id":"roledot","name":"RoleDot","kitId":"harvested","src":"kitChrome.tsx"}"#)
            .unwrap();
        store
            .set(
                "statusdot",
                r#"{"id":"statusdot","name":"StatusDot","kitId":"harvested","provides":"@/components/statusdot"}"#,
            )
            .unwrap();

        let importer = |spec: &str| {
            serde_json::json!({
                "id": "pane", "name": "Pane", "kitId": "harvested",
                "srcText": format!("import {{ X }} from \"{spec}\";\nexport function Pane() {{ return <X/>; }}"),
            })
        };

        let ws = unresolvable_component_imports(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&importer("@/components/roledot")));
        assert_eq!(ws.len(), 1, "the unpublished import warns: {ws:?}");
        assert!(ws[0].contains("@/components/roledot"), "names the specifier: {}", ws[0]);
        // The suggested fix must be a command that RUNS. `bsc ui set` takes its record on stdin and
        // has no `--provides` flag, so the plausible-looking `bsc ui set <id> --provides <spec>` fails
        // with BOTH `unknown flag` and `unexpected argument` — the first draft of this warning shipped
        // exactly that, and a warning naming a broken command is worse than no warning.
        assert!(
            ws[0].contains(r#"{"id":"roledot","provides":"@/components/roledot"}"#) && ws[0].contains("| bsc ui set"),
            "suggests the stdin merge-write, the only form that works: {}",
            ws[0]
        );
        assert!(!ws[0].contains("--provides"), "must not suggest a flag `set` does not have: {}", ws[0]);

        // The target publishes it ⇒ silent. This is the half that proves the check is not just
        // "warn on every @/components import".
        assert!(
            unresolvable_component_imports(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&importer("@/components/statusdot"))).is_empty(),
            "a published specifier is silent"
        );

        // A PLATFORM module is the declared boundary and is never a component specifier — it must not
        // be scanned at all, or every record in the store would warn.
        let platform = serde_json::json!({
            "id": "pane", "name": "Pane", "kitId": "harvested",

    #[test]
    fn a_provides_component_with_at_imports_is_syntax_checked_not_warned_as_unbuildable() {
        use serde_json::json;
        // #43: a graph-source component (carries `provides`) has its `@/` imports resolved by the runtime
        // loader — so the gate must NOT emit the false "unresolved first-party @/" advisory for it, and
        // instead runs the real syntax check. A valid one passes.
        let ok = json!({ "id":"box", "name":"Box", "provides":"@/shared/ui/layout/Box",
            "srcText":"import { space } from \"@/shared/ui/layout/space\";\nexport function Box(){ return null; }" });
        assert!(validate_component_batch(std::slice::from_ref(&ok)).is_ok(), "a valid provides-component with @/ imports passes");
        // ...and a CORRUPT one is now caught (before #43 the `@/` import made `looks_buildable_module` false,
        // which skipped syntax-checking entirely, so it stored silently).
        let corrupt = json!({ "id":"box2", "name":"Box2", "provides":"@/shared/ui/layout/Box",
            "srcText":"import { x } from \"@/x\";\nexport const s = [1,2].join(\"\n\");" });
        let err = validate_component_batch(std::slice::from_ref(&corrupt)).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("Box2"), "a corrupt provides-component is caught, not silently stored: {err}");

    /// #3470 — the two edge rows of the issue's table. The gate used to be INVERTED at its edges: a
    /// `srcText` that keeps its `@/` imports made `looks_buildable_module` false, which skipped the
    /// syntax check ENTIRELY, so the source least like a module got the least validation and stored with
    /// zero complaint. Both rows still STORE (a spec-only record is legitimate) — the fix is that the
    /// outcome is now stated.
    #[test]
    fn a_srctext_that_is_not_a_buildable_module_is_reported_never_silently_skipped() {
        use serde_json::json;

        // ROW 3 — keeps its `@/` imports. Warned, with the reason NAMING the import and saying what was
        // stored; still accepted. Unchanged by #3849: this is the PREVIEW's oracle, and in the preview
        // sandbox a `@/` import genuinely does not resolve.
        let spec = json!({
            "id": "card", "name": "Card",
            "srcText": "import { Button } from \"@/shared/ui/controls/Button\";
export const Card = () => <Button />;",
        });
        let src = spec["srcText"].as_str().unwrap();
        assert!(!crate::graph_health::looks_buildable_module(src), "row 3 is not a PREVIEW module…");
        // …but the LOADER resolves it fine, which is the distinction #3849 turns on.
        assert!(crate::graph_health::renders_at_runtime(src), "…yet it renders at runtime");
        let warning = unbuildable_module_warning(&spec, src);
        assert!(warning.contains("Card"), "names the component: {warning}");
        assert!(warning.contains("@/shared/ui/controls/Button"), "names the import: {warning}");
        assert!(warning.contains("SPEC"), "states what was stored: {warning}");
        assert!(validate_component_batch(std::slice::from_ref(&spec)).is_ok(), "warn-only — it still stores");

        // ROW 2 — a fragment with no imports IS treated as a module (it has an `export`), so it is NOT
        // warned about and the syntax gate DOES run: a corrupt one is rejected outright.
        let fragment = json!({ "id": "frag", "name": "Frag", "srcText": "export const F = () => <b>hi</b>;" });
        let src = fragment["srcText"].as_str().unwrap();
        assert!(crate::graph_health::looks_buildable_module(src), "a no-import fragment counts as a module");
        assert!(validate_component_batch(std::slice::from_ref(&fragment)).is_ok());
        let corrupt_fragment = json!({ "id": "frag", "name": "Frag", "srcText": "export const s = [1,2].join(\"\n\");" });
        assert!(
            validate_component_batch(std::slice::from_ref(&corrupt_fragment)).is_err(),
            "the syntax gate still runs for a no-import fragment",
        );

        // A record with no srcText at all is neither warned about nor gated.
        let bare = json!({ "id": "c", "name": "C" });
        assert!(validate_component_batch(std::slice::from_ref(&bare)).is_ok());

        // And the #3470 false positive: a component whose only `…` is UI copy is a real module — it must
        // NOT be accused of being a sketch; it goes through the syntax gate like any other module.
        let copy = json!({ "id": "sel", "name": "Select", "srcText": "export const S = () => <input placeholder=\"Select…\" />;" });
        let src = copy["srcText"].as_str().unwrap();
        assert!(crate::graph_health::looks_buildable_module(src), "an ellipsis in COPY is not an elision");
        assert!(validate_component_batch(std::slice::from_ref(&copy)).is_ok());
    }

    /// #3849 — the false-positive classes the issue names, each as a fixture, because the gate below
    /// REJECTS a page and a gate built on a liar just teaches everyone to pass `--force`.
    #[test]
    fn the_buildability_check_does_not_fire_on_its_three_known_false_positives() {
        // 1 — `…` (U+2026) inside STRING LITERALS. The three strings from the issue, verbatim.
        for copy in [
            "export const A = () => <input placeholder=\"Search name, description, tools…\" />;",
            "export const B = () => <button>Set scope…</button>;",
            "export const C = () => <button>Add to group…</button>;",
        ] {
            assert!(
                crate::graph_health::looks_buildable_module(copy),
                "an ellipsis in UI copy is prose, not an elision marker: {copy}",
            );
        }

        // 2 — `...` SPREAD syntax, which is code, not prose standing in for omitted code.
        let spread = "export const D = (p) => <div {...p} style={{ ...p.style, top: 0 }} />;";
        assert!(crate::graph_health::looks_buildable_module(spread), "spread is not an elision: {spread}");

        // 3 — a REGISTERED platform import. The one measured live: restoring `fleetpage` from the
        // recovery archive warned about sixteen specifiers the runtime resolves fine.
        let platform = "import { Button } from \"@/shared/ui/controls/Button\";\n\
                        import { Card } from \"@/shared/ui/data/Card\";\n\
                        export const E = () => <Card><Button /></Card>;";
        assert!(crate::graph_health::renders_at_runtime(platform), "registered platform imports resolve");

        // …and a SIBLING record import, which `resolveGraphSource` vendors from the store by id.
        let sibling = "import { Health } from \"@/components/fleet-health\";\nexport const F = () => <Health />;";
        assert!(crate::graph_health::renders_at_runtime(sibling), "`@/components/<id>` resolves by id");

        // The check must still CATCH the real thing, or none of the above is worth anything.
        let real_elision = "export const G = () => {\n  const rows = [\n    …\n  ];\n  return <div>{rows}</div>;\n};";
        assert!(!crate::graph_health::looks_buildable_module(real_elision), "a mid-code elision is still caught");
        let unresolvable = "import { X } from \"@/features/nowhere/X\";\nexport const H = () => <X />;";
        assert!(!crate::graph_health::renders_at_runtime(unresolvable), "an unregistered import is still caught");
    }

    /// #3849 — the gate itself: a `role: page` that cannot render is REFUSED, because a page record IS
    /// the page (there is no `.tsx` behind `fleetpage`), so storing a broken one ships a blank screen.
    /// Every other role stays permissive, and `--force` remains for a deliberate spec.
    #[test]
    fn a_page_record_that_cannot_render_is_refused_while_other_roles_still_store() {
        use serde_json::json;
        let broken = "import { X } from \"@/features/nowhere/X\";\nexport const P = () => <X />;";

        let page = json!({ "id": "p", "name": "P", "role": "page", "srcText": broken });
        let err = validate_component_batch(std::slice::from_ref(&page)).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("cannot render"), "states the refusal: {err}");
        assert!(err.contains("@/features/nowhere/X"), "names the specific cause: {err}");
        assert!(err.contains("--force"), "names the escape: {err}");

        // The SAME source under any other role is advisory, exactly as before.
        let primitive = json!({ "id": "q", "name": "Q", "role": "primitive", "srcText": broken });
        assert!(validate_component_batch(std::slice::from_ref(&primitive)).is_ok(), "non-page still stores");

        // A page whose imports RESOLVE is not refused — the gate must not fire on the common case.
        let ok_page = json!({
            "id": "r", "name": "R", "role": "page",
            "srcText": "import { Card } from \"@/shared/ui/data/Card\";\nexport const R = () => <Card />;",
        });
        assert!(validate_component_batch(std::slice::from_ref(&ok_page)).is_ok(), "a resolvable page stores");

        // …and `--force` stores the broken page deliberately.
        FORCE_WRITE.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
        let forced = validate_component_batch(std::slice::from_ref(&page));
        FORCE_WRITE.store(false, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
        assert!(forced.is_ok(), "--force stores it as a deliberate spec");
    }

    #[test]
    fn validate_component_batch_never_rejects_over_inline_animations() {
        use serde_json::json;
        // #3065: a component's `animations` entries may be a kit-animation NAME (string) OR an INLINE
        // def object (validated like `bsc ui kit define-animation`). A VALID inline def + a name ref is
        // clean — the batch passes.
        let good = json!({
            "id": "spark", "name": "Sparkline",
            "animations": [
                "fade-in", // a NAME ref into the kit's library
                { "name": "draw", "keyframes": { "from": { "opacity": "0" }, "to": { "opacity": "1" } } }
            ],
        });
        assert!(validate_component_batch(std::slice::from_ref(&good)).is_ok());

        // An INVALID inline def (an unsafe `url(...)` keyframe value + a bad-ident name) and a
        // non-string/non-object entry are NON-BLOCKING — the batch STILL writes (the warnings are a
        // stderr side-effect; the render compiler drops the bad fields). Rejecting a whole component
        // over one bad anim is too heavy.
        let bad = json!({
            "id": "spark2", "name": "Sparkline2",
            "animations": [
                { "name": "draw", "keyframes": { "from": { "opacity": "url(evil)" } } },
                { "name": "BAD NAME", "keyframes": { "from": { "opacity": "0" } } },
                42
            ],
        });
        assert!(
            validate_component_batch(std::slice::from_ref(&bad)).is_ok(),
            "an invalid inline animation must WRITE (warn-only), never reject the component",
        );

        // A component whose `animations` are all NAME refs (the pre-#3065 shape) is untouched + clean,
        // and one with a corrupt inline def alongside a corrupt-module srcText still fails ONLY on the
        // srcText (the srcText Err semantics are unchanged by the animations advisory).
        let names_only = json!({ "id": "c", "name": "C", "animations": ["fade-in", "pop"] });
        assert!(validate_component_batch(std::slice::from_ref(&names_only)).is_ok());
        let bad_src_and_anim = json!({
            "id": "d", "name": "DChart",
            "srcText": "export const s = [1,2].join(\"\n\");",
            "animations": [{ "name": "BAD NAME", "keyframes": {} }],
        });
        let err = validate_component_batch(std::slice::from_ref(&bad_src_and_anim)).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("DChart") && err.contains("unterminated string literal"), "srcText Err unchanged; got: {err}");
    }

    /// Serializes the tests that mutate the process-wide `$BSC_SCOPES` / `$BSC_UI_ACTIVITY_LOG` env
    /// (the scope-gate test and the #2525 emit test): parallel threads share the process env, so an
    /// unguarded scope flip would make a concurrent gated mutation flakily refuse or misroute a
    /// `ui-touch`. Poisoning is ignored (one test's assert failure must not cascade).
    static ENV_LOCK: std::sync::Mutex<()> = std::sync::Mutex::new(());

    /// A fresh (created, empty) scratch store dir so the shape-verb tests never touch the user's
    /// real `~/.base-studio-code/components` store.
    /// #4246 — `bsc ui parity` compares what the app RENDERS (the store) against what it SHIPS (the
    /// seed folder). Three guards already watch the graph and every one of them reads the seed, so a
    /// record whose store copy drifted renders source nothing has ever compared against anything.
    #[test]
    fn parity_reports_store_vs_seed_and_only_gates_under_strict() {
        let dir = tmp_store_dir("parity");
        let seed = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("bsc-parity-seed-{}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&seed);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&seed).unwrap();

        // Three seed records: one the store matches, one it has drifted from, one it has never seen.
        for (id, role, src) in [
            ("agree", "page", "export const A = 1;"),
            ("drifted", "page", "export const B = 1; // the SEED copy, longer"),
            ("never-hydrated", "page", "export const C = 1;"),
        ] {
            std::fs::write(
                seed.join(format!("{id}.json")),
                serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "name": id, "role": role, "srcText": src }).to_string(),
            )
            .unwrap();
        }
        // The store holds two of them, and its `drifted` copy is NOT the seed's.
        let store = open_component_store(&Some(dir.clone())).unwrap();
        for (id, src) in [("agree", "export const A = 1;"), ("drifted", "export const B = 1;")] {
            let payload = serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "name": id, "role": "page", "srcText": src }).to_string();
            store.set(id, &payload).unwrap();
        }

        let seed_s = seed.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        // Default: REPORTS, exits Ok. A guard that lands red protects nothing (see `record-link-debt`).
        cmd_parity(&[seed_s.clone(), "--role".into(), "page".into(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()]).unwrap();

        // --strict is the gate, for a caller that has adjudicated the known set.
        let err = cmd_parity(&[
            seed_s.clone(), "--role".into(), "page".into(), "--strict".into(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone(),
        ])
        .unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("differs from what ships"), "names the failure: {err}");
        assert!(err.contains("bsc ui parity"), "names how to see them: {err}");

        // A role filter that matches nothing leaves nothing to compare — and must not then "pass" by
        // vacuity under --strict, which would make `--role` a way to silence the gate.
        cmd_parity(&[
            seed_s.clone(), "--role".into(), "primitive".into(), "--strict".into(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone(),
        ])
        .expect("no records in scope is not a drift");

        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&seed);
    }

    /// #139/#158 — `sync-seed` writes a store record's CURRENT body back into its packaged seed file, by
    /// id, stripping the store-only bookkeeping (`history`/`rev`/`updatedAt`/`updatedBy`/`builtin`/
    /// `seedHash`/`used`/`usageAssessed`/`version`) no seed file has ever carried — the gap `bsc ui
    /// export`'s own doc note names (it dumps a record verbatim, so its output can't be dropped straight
    /// into the packaged tree).
    #[test]
    fn sync_seed_writes_store_back_into_the_matching_seed_file_by_id() {
        let dir = tmp_store_dir("sync-seed");
        let seed = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("bsc-sync-seed-{}", std::process::id()));
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&seed);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&seed).unwrap();

        // Three seed files: one the store agrees with, one the store has drifted from (carrying store
        // bookkeeping a seed never had), one the store has never seen.
        for (id, src) in [
            ("agree", "export const A = 1;"),
            ("drifted", "export const B = 1; // the SEED copy, stale"),
            ("seed-only", "export const C = 1;"),
        ] {
            std::fs::write(
                seed.join(format!("{id}.json")),
                serde_json::json!({ "id": id, "name": id, "role": "primitive", "srcText": src }).to_string(),
            )
            .unwrap();
        }

        let store = open_component_store(&Some(dir.clone())).unwrap();
        store.set("agree", &serde_json::json!({ "id": "agree", "name": "agree", "role": "primitive", "srcText": "export const A = 1;" }).to_string()).unwrap();
        store
            .set(
                "drifted",
                &serde_json::json!({
                    "id": "drifted", "name": "drifted", "role": "primitive",
                    "srcText": "export const B = 1; // the STORE copy, current",
                    "history": [{ "rev": 1 }], "rev": 4, "updatedAt": "2026-08-01T00:00:00Z",
                    "updatedBy": "designer", "builtin": true, "seedHash": "abc123", "used": true,
                    // #158: `usage-scan --apply` stamps these two onto a store record — the strip list
                    // was short by exactly them, so a sync after either had run wrote them into the seed.
                    "usageAssessed": true, "version": "",
                })
                .to_string(),
            )
            .unwrap();
        store.set("store-only", &serde_json::json!({ "id": "store-only", "name": "store-only", "role": "primitive", "srcText": "export const D = 1;" }).to_string()).unwrap();

        let seed_s = seed.to_string_lossy().into_owned();

        // Dry run (no --apply): reports the would-be sync, touches nothing on disk.
        let (r, out) = bsc_util::capture_output(|| {
            cmd_sync_seed(&["agree".into(), "drifted".into(), "seed-only".into(), "store-only".into(), "ghost".into(), "--seed-dir".into(), seed_s.clone(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()])
        });
        r.unwrap();
        let report: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(out.trim()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(report["applied"], false);
        let synced: Vec<&str> = report["synced"].as_array().unwrap().iter().map(|v| v["id"].as_str().unwrap()).collect();
        assert_eq!(synced, vec!["drifted"], "only the genuinely diverged id needs writing");
        assert_eq!(report["upToDate"], serde_json::json!(["agree"]));
        assert_eq!(report["missingFromSeed"], serde_json::json!(["store-only"]), "in the store, no seed file — a PROMOTION, not a sync");
        assert_eq!(report["missingFromStore"], serde_json::json!(["seed-only", "ghost"]));
        let drifted_seed_untouched: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&std::fs::read_to_string(seed.join("drifted.json")).unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(drifted_seed_untouched["srcText"], "export const B = 1; // the SEED copy, stale", "dry run wrote nothing");

        // --apply writes the store's CURRENT body, minus store-only bookkeeping.
        cmd_sync_seed(&["drifted".into(), "--seed-dir".into(), seed_s.clone(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone(), "--apply".into()]).unwrap();
        let written: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&std::fs::read_to_string(seed.join("drifted.json")).unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(written["srcText"], "export const B = 1; // the STORE copy, current");
        for field in SEED_BOOKKEEPING_FIELDS {
            assert!(written.get(*field).is_none(), "seed must not carry store bookkeeping field '{field}': {written}");
        }
        // #158 regression: named explicitly (not just via the const above) so a future shrink of
        // SEED_BOOKKEEPING_FIELDS can't silently re-open the gap these two were filed for.
        assert!(written.get("usageAssessed").is_none(), "usage-scan's stamp must not leak into the seed: {written}");
        assert!(written.get("version").is_none(), "the store-only version key must not leak into the seed: {written}");

        // A second sync of the now-synced id is a no-op — reported up to date, not re-written.
        let (r, out) = bsc_util::capture_output(|| {
            cmd_sync_seed(&["drifted".into(), "--seed-dir".into(), seed_s.clone(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()])
        });
        r.unwrap();
        let report: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(out.trim()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(report["upToDate"], serde_json::json!(["drifted"]));
        assert_eq!(report["synced"], serde_json::json!([]));

        assert!(cmd_sync_seed(&["agree".into(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()]).is_err(), "--seed-dir is required");
        assert!(cmd_sync_seed(&["--seed-dir".into(), seed_s.clone(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()]).is_err(), "at least one id is required");

        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&seed);
    }

    /// #162 (request from kevin) — `promote` writes a genuinely NEW store record into its own file
    /// under the packaged seed, the case `sync-seed` explicitly declines ("an id with no matching seed
    /// file needs PROMOTING, not syncing"). Before this there was no path from a store-only component
    /// to git except hand-writing the seed json.
    #[test]
    fn promote_writes_a_new_record_into_a_new_seed_file_nested_by_folder() {

        // One seed file already exists (`already-seeded`); the store also holds a genuinely NEW record

        std::fs::write(
            seed.join("already-seeded.json"),
            serde_json::json!({ "id": "already-seeded", "name": "already-seeded", "role": "primitive" }).to_string(),
        )
        .unwrap();

        let store = open_component_store(&Some(dir.clone())).unwrap();
        store
            .set(
                "already-seeded",
                &serde_json::json!({
                    "id": "already-seeded", "name": "already-seeded", "role": "primitive",
                    "srcText": "export const A = 2; // store has since drifted",
                })
                .to_string(),
            )
            .unwrap();
        store
            .set(
                "new-one",
                &serde_json::json!({
                    "id": "new-one", "name": "NewOne", "role": "composite",
                    "srcText": "export const B = 1;", "folder": "features/studio-sessions",
                    // Store bookkeeping a seed file never carries — must be stripped on the way out.
                    "history": [{ "rev": 1 }], "rev": 3, "updatedAt": "2026-08-28T00:00:00Z",
                    "updatedBy": "designer", "builtin": false, "seedHash": "xyz", "used": true,
                    "usageAssessed": true, "version": "",
                })
                .to_string(),
            )
            .unwrap();
        store
            .set(
                "rootless",
                &serde_json::json!({ "id": "rootless", "name": "Rootless", "role": "primitive", "srcText": "export const C = 1;" })
                    .to_string(),
            )
            .unwrap();

        let seed_s = seed.to_string_lossy().into_owned();

        // Dry run (no --apply): reports what WOULD be written, touches nothing on disk.
        let (r, out) = bsc_util::capture_output(|| {
            cmd_promote(&[
                "new-one".into(), "already-seeded".into(), "rootless".into(), "ghost".into(),
                "--seed-dir".into(), seed_s.clone(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone(),
            ])
        });
        r.unwrap();
        let report: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(out.trim()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(report["applied"], false);
        let promoted: Vec<&str> = report["promoted"].as_array().unwrap().iter().map(|v| v["id"].as_str().unwrap()).collect();
        assert!(promoted.contains(&"new-one") && promoted.contains(&"rootless"), "promoted: {promoted:?}");
        assert_eq!(report["alreadySeeded"], serde_json::json!(["already-seeded"]), "an id with a seed file is refused, not overwritten");
        assert_eq!(report["missingFromStore"], serde_json::json!(["ghost"]));
        assert!(!seed.join("features/studio-sessions/new-one.json").exists(), "dry run wrote nothing");
        assert_eq!(
            std::fs::read_to_string(seed.join("already-seeded.json")).unwrap(),
            serde_json::json!({ "id": "already-seeded", "name": "already-seeded", "role": "primitive" }).to_string(),
            "an already-seeded id is untouched even in the report-only pass",
        );

        // --apply actually writes: nested by `folder` for `new-one`, at the seed-dir root for the
        // folder-less `rootless`.
        cmd_promote(&["new-one".into(), "rootless".into(), "--seed-dir".into(), seed_s.clone(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone(), "--apply".into()]).unwrap();
        let new_one_path = seed.join("features/studio-sessions/new-one.json");
        assert!(new_one_path.exists(), "new-one lands nested under its `folder`");
        let written: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&std::fs::read_to_string(&new_one_path).unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(written["srcText"], "export const B = 1;");
        assert_eq!(written["folder"], "features/studio-sessions");
        for field in SEED_BOOKKEEPING_FIELDS {
            assert!(written.get(*field).is_none(), "seed must not carry store bookkeeping field '{field}': {written}");
        }
        assert!(seed.join("rootless.json").exists(), "a folder-less record lands at the seed-dir root");

        // Promoting it again now reports `alreadySeeded` — the file it just created is a real seed file.
        let (r, out) = bsc_util::capture_output(|| {
            cmd_promote(&["new-one".into(), "--seed-dir".into(), seed_s.clone(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()])
        });
        r.unwrap();
        let report: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(out.trim()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(report["alreadySeeded"], serde_json::json!(["new-one"]));
        assert_eq!(report["promoted"], serde_json::json!([]));

        assert!(cmd_promote(&["new-one".into(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()]).is_err(), "--seed-dir is required");
        assert!(cmd_promote(&["--seed-dir".into(), seed_s.clone(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()]).is_err(), "at least one id is required");

        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&seed);
    }

    /// `write-gate-blind-to-merge-writes` — the page gate must judge what will be STORED.
    ///
    /// A write MERGES by default (#4197), so the ordinary payload is `{id, srcText}` and carries no
    /// `role`. Validating the raw payload judged a page by a field it never restated, so every partial
    /// write slipped past #3849's gate — and a `role: page` that cannot render could be stored by any of
    /// them. Found by using the gate on a real six-page push, which warned at `githubpage` (a page) with
    /// the PREVIEW oracle's message.
    #[test]
    fn the_page_gate_judges_the_merged_record_not_the_payload() {
        let dir = tmp_store_dir("gate-merge");
        let store = open_component_store(&Some(dir.clone())).unwrap();
        // A stored PAGE, currently fine.
        store
            .set(
                "p",
                &serde_json::json!({
                    "id": "p", "name": "P", "role": "page",
                    "srcText": "import { Card } from \"@/shared/ui/data/Card\";
export const P = () => <Card />;"
                })
                .to_string(),
            )
            .unwrap();

        // The ordinary merge payload: NO role. Its source cannot resolve, so the page gate must refuse.
        let broken = serde_json::json!({
            "id": "p",
            "srcText": "import { X } from \"@/features/nowhere/X\";
export const P = () => <X />;"
        });
        let merged = {
            let prior: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&store.get("p").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
            crate::record::merge_over(&prior, &broken, &[])
        };
        assert_eq!(merged.get("role").and_then(|v| v.as_str()), Some("page"), "the merge restores the role");
        let err = validate_component_batch(std::slice::from_ref(&merged)).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("cannot render"), "the gate fires on the MERGED record: {err}");

        // …and on the raw payload it does not, which is the bug being fixed. Kept as the contrast: if
        // this ever starts failing, the gate has begun reading something other than `role` and the
        // reasoning above no longer holds.
        assert!(
            validate_component_batch(std::slice::from_ref(&broken)).is_ok(),
            "the RAW payload has no role — judged as a non-page, which is exactly why validation moved",
        );
    }

    fn tmp_store_dir(tag: &str) -> String {
        let d = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("bsc-component-cli-test-{tag}-{}", std::process::id()));
        // Start EMPTY (#3382). `process::id()` is unique among LIVE processes, not over time — the OS
        // recycles pids — and this fixture never cleaned up, so a later run that drew a recycled pid
        // inherited the previous run's store. That surfaced as `a fresh record's first write is rev 1`
        // failing with rev 3: the record was already there at rev 2. Same shape as the env race this
        // issue fixes (state outliving the test that wrote it), different channel — the filesystem.
        // Every tag is used by exactly one test, so wiping here cannot disturb a sibling.
        //
        // BOTH paths must go. The SQLite backend keys off the SIBLING `<dir>.db`, not a file inside
        // `<dir>` (`db_path_for` in bsc-json-store), so removing only the directory leaves the actual
        // database — which is exactly why the first attempt at this fix changed nothing.
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&d);
        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(format!("{}.db", d.to_string_lossy()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&d).unwrap();
        d.to_string_lossy().into_owned()
    }

    /// The whole point of the closure (materialize-a-records-record-closure): a COMPOSING record — the
    /// 108-of-116 failure shape — materializes with the record it imports beside it, at that record's
    /// REAL position under a `_closure/` mirror, with `@` aliased there. Asserted on the files, because
    /// the walker being right and the materialization being right are two different things: the first
    /// batch of this work resolved perfectly and still wrote a config vitest could not use.
    #[test]
    fn materialize_writes_the_record_closure_into_a_mirror_and_aliases_at_to_it() {
        let out = tmp_store_dir("closure-mirror");
        let comps = vec![serde_json::json!({
            "id": "ui-empty-state", "name": "EmptyState", "provides": "@/shared/ui/feedback/EmptyState",
            "src": "src/shared/ui/feedback/EmptyState.tsx",
            "srcText": "export function EmptyState() { return null; }",
        })];
        let plat = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
        let index = crate::closure::Index::new(&comps, &[], &plat, None);
        let root = serde_json::json!({
            "id": "activityfeed", "name": "ActivityFeed", "src": "src/shared/ui/data/ActivityFeed.tsx",
            "srcText": "import { EmptyState } from \"@/shared/ui/feedback/EmptyState\";\n\
                        export const ActivityFeed = EmptyState;",
            "tests": [{ "src": "import { ActivityFeed } from \"./ActivityFeed\";\n" }],
        });
        let v = materialize_component_test(&root, &out, false, Some(&index)).unwrap();

        let member = std::path::Path::new(&out).join(MIRROR_DIR).join("shared/ui/feedback/EmptyState.tsx");
        assert!(member.is_file(), "the imported record is written at its real position in the mirror");
        assert_eq!(
            std::fs::read_to_string(&member).unwrap(),
            "export function EmptyState() { return null; }",
            "VERBATIM — a member that differs from the store would make a failure the runner's, not the record's"
        );
        let cfg = std::fs::read_to_string(std::path::Path::new(&out).join("vitest.config.ts")).unwrap();
        assert!(cfg.contains("resolve: { alias: ["), "the config aliases, or the mirror is unreachable");
        assert!(
            cfg.contains(&format!("{}/{MIRROR_DIR}", out.replace('\\', "/"))),
            "`@` points at THIS record's mirror by absolute path — a relative one re-resolves against the \
             importer, so a member two levels down would miss: {cfg}"
        );
        assert!(v["missing"].as_array().unwrap().is_empty(), "every import was a record");
        assert_eq!(v["closure"][0]["origin"], "component");
        assert_eq!(v["closure"][0]["path"], "shared/ui/feedback/EmptyState.tsx");
    }

    /// `--no-closure` is the STRICT contract the runner used to have, kept because a pass there proves
    /// the record is a LEAF — the retirability signal. It must emit NO alias at all: an `@` pointing at
    /// an empty mirror would still resolve nothing, but a future member landing there would silently
    /// turn the strict run into a closure run.
    #[test]
    fn no_closure_writes_the_record_utterly_alone_with_no_alias() {
        let out = tmp_store_dir("closure-strict");
        let root = serde_json::json!({
            "id": "activityfeed", "name": "ActivityFeed", "src": "src/shared/ui/data/ActivityFeed.tsx",
            "srcText": "import { EmptyState } from \"@/shared/ui/feedback/EmptyState\";\nexport const A = EmptyState;",
            "tests": [{ "src": "import { A } from \"./ActivityFeed\";\n" }],
        });
        let v = materialize_component_test(&root, &out, false, None).unwrap();
        assert!(!std::path::Path::new(&out).join(MIRROR_DIR).exists(), "no mirror at all");
        let cfg = std::fs::read_to_string(std::path::Path::new(&out).join("vitest.config.ts")).unwrap();
        assert!(!cfg.contains("resolve:"), "no alias, so `@/…` resolves to nothing: {cfg}");
        assert!(
            cfg.contains("--no-closure"),
            "and the config SAYS which contract it was written under — a header describing an alias it \
             does not carry sends a reader hunting a resolution bug that is the strict mode working: {cfg}"
        );
        assert!(v["closure"].as_array().unwrap().is_empty());
        assert!(v["missing"].as_array().unwrap().is_empty(), "strict mode makes no claim about what is missing");
    }

    #[test]
    fn components_and_kits_persist_to_sqlite_db_files_not_legacy_json() {
        // Regression proof for #2984 (epic #2982): the shared-store SQLite migration (#2983) is
        // transparent to this crate. A component (and a kit) written through the crate's OWN store-open
        // path must land in the sibling `<base>/<segment>.db` SQLite file — NOT the pre-migration legacy
        // `<base>/<segment>/<id>.json` per-id file.
        let base = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("bsc-component-sqlite-{}", std::process::id()));
        // Start from a clean slate so a prior run can't pre-seed the db (making "exists" trivially true)
        // or leave a stray legacy file (making "no legacy json" trivially false).
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&base);
        let comp_dir = base.join("components");
        let kit_dir = base.join("kits");

        // Open both collections through the crate's own resolution. A `--dir` override wins over the env
        // (`resolve_store_path`), so this is deterministic: components at `<base>/components`, kits at
        // `<base>/kits`.
        let comps = open_component_store(&Some(comp_dir.to_string_lossy().into_owned())).unwrap();
        let kits = open_kit_store(&Some(kit_dir.to_string_lossy().into_owned())).unwrap();

        // Write one record into each collection…
        comps
            .set("button", r#"{"id":"button","name":"Button","kitId":"react-ui","role":"control"}"#)
            .unwrap();
        kits.set("react-ui", r#"{"id":"react-ui","name":"React UI","stack":"react"}"#).unwrap();

        // …and read them back verbatim (the round-trip the desktop library + a live session rely on).
        assert_eq!(
            comps.get("button").unwrap().as_deref(),
            Some(r#"{"id":"button","name":"Button","kitId":"react-ui","role":"control"}"#),
            "component round-trips through the SQLite store",
        );
        assert_eq!(
            kits.get("react-ui").unwrap().as_deref(),
            Some(r#"{"id":"react-ui","name":"React UI","stack":"react"}"#),
            "kit round-trips through the SQLite store",
        );

        // The SQLite backing is the sibling `<base>/<segment>.db`, and it exists after the write.
        assert_eq!(comps.db_path(), base.join("components.db").as_path());
        assert_eq!(kits.db_path(), base.join("kits.db").as_path());
        assert!(comps.db_path().exists(), "components persist to components.db");
        assert!(kits.db_path().exists(), "kits persist to kits.db");

        // No legacy per-id JSON file was written. `Store::file` computes exactly the pre-migration
        // `<segment>/<id>.json` path the SQLite backend replaced — assert it was never created.
        let legacy_comp = comps.file("button").unwrap();
        let legacy_kit = kits.file("react-ui").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(legacy_comp, comp_dir.join("button.json"));
        assert_eq!(legacy_kit, kit_dir.join("react-ui.json"));
        assert!(!legacy_comp.exists(), "no legacy components/<id>.json — the record lives in SQLite");
        assert!(!legacy_kit.exists(), "no legacy kits/<id>.json — the record lives in SQLite");

        // The db files (+ their WAL/SHM siblings) live inside `base`, so this clears everything.
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&base);
    }

    /// #the-scan-cache-read-is-the-last-boot-spawn — `ui scan-cache get` is answered by the WARM
    /// `bsc serve` child, which captures a request's output off the same stdout it speaks its
    /// protocol on. This branch printed with a raw `println!`, which would have written straight into
    /// that protocol stream and corrupted every later response on the child. The claim under test is
    /// "its output is CAPTURABLE", not "it prints the right thing" — so it fails the moment someone
    /// reaches for `println!` here again.
    ///
    /// `put`/`clear` are deliberately NOT covered: they are writes, are never served, and keep their
    /// own printing.
    #[test]
    fn scan_cache_get_output_is_capturable_by_the_warm_serve_loop() {
        let dir = tempdir_shim::Dir::new("bsc-scan-cache-capture");
        let cache = format!("{}/component-scan.json", dir.path());
        std::fs::write(&cache, r#"{"widget":{"sig":"abc","status":"ok"}}"#).unwrap();
        // The store honours $BSC_SCAN_CACHE, so the test never touches the real one. That var is
        // process-global and this is the ONLY test in the crate that sets it — `scan_cache::tests`
        // drive the path-injectable `load_from`/`put_to` instead. The CLI path resolves its own file,
        // so the env var is the only injection point available here.
        std::env::set_var("BSC_SCAN_CACHE", &cache);

        let (r, captured) =

        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(

        std::fs::write(
            &store_path,
            r#"{"implementations":[
                {"id":"dup-a.ts","tech":"typescript","role":"algorithm","name":"dup","code":"export function dup(){}"},

        let a = |args: &[&str]| args.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        // The mutating shapes (#2470) — gated on both collections + the animation writers (#2869).
        assert!(is_scoped_mutation(&a(&["set"])));

        ] {
