    /// A minimal valid animation object (a mount fade-in referencing the motion tokens).
    fn valid_anim(name: &str) -> serde_json::Value {
        serde_json::json!({
            "name": name,
            "keyframes": { "from": { "opacity": "0" }, "to": { "opacity": "1" } },
            "duration": "var(--dur-base)",
            "easing": "var(--ease-standard)",
            "trigger": "mount",
        })
    }

    #[test]
    fn validate_animation_accepts_a_well_formed_definition() {
        assert!(validate_animation(&valid_anim("fade-in")).is_ok());
        // Minimal: just a name + one keyframe stop with one declaration (defaults fill the rest).
        assert!(validate_animation(&serde_json::json!({
            "name": "pulse",
            "keyframes": { "50%": { "transform": "scale(1.05)" } },
        }))
        .is_ok());
        // Optional selector / set / delay (#3054/#3056): a child selector, static decls, and a delay.
        assert!(validate_animation(&serde_json::json!({
            "name": "icon-spin",
            "keyframes": { "to": { "transform": "rotate(90deg)" } },
            "selector": ".icon > svg:nth-child(2n)",
            "set": { "transform-origin": "center", "transform-box": "fill-box" },
            "delay": "120ms",
        }))
        .is_ok());
        // Optional stagger (#3055): a per-element delay step is valid WITH a selector.
        assert!(validate_animation(&serde_json::json!({
            "name": "wave",
            "keyframes": { "to": { "opacity": "1" } },
            "selector": ".cell",
            "stagger": "14ms",
        }))
        .is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn validate_animation_rejects_each_grammar_violation() {
        // Bad name (uppercase / leading digit / injection char).
        for bad in ["Fade", "1fade", "fade_in", "fade in", ""] {
            let a = serde_json::json!({ "name": bad, "keyframes": { "to": { "opacity": "1" } } });
            let err = validate_animation(&a).unwrap_err();
            assert!(err.contains("name"), "bad name '{bad}' rejected: {err}");
        }
        // Bad keyframe stop.
        let err = validate_animation(&serde_json::json!({
            "name": "x", "keyframes": { "start": { "opacity": "1" } }
        }))
        .unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("stop"), "{err}");
        // Bad property.
        let err = validate_animation(&serde_json::json!({
            "name": "x", "keyframes": { "to": { "Opacity": "1" } }
        }))
        .unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("property"), "{err}");
        // Unsafe value (declaration-ending / injection).
        for bad in ["1; } body { color: red", "url(evil.png)", "1 /* x */", "expression(alert(1))"] {
            let a = serde_json::json!({ "name": "x", "keyframes": { "to": { "opacity": bad } } });
            let err = validate_animation(&a).unwrap_err();
            assert!(err.contains("unsafe"), "unsafe value '{bad}' rejected: {err}");
        }
        // Unsafe duration / easing.
        let err = validate_animation(&serde_json::json!({
            "name": "x", "keyframes": { "to": { "opacity": "1" } }, "duration": "1s; color: red"
        }))
        .unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("duration"), "{err}");
        // Empty / non-object keyframes.
        assert!(validate_animation(&serde_json::json!({ "name": "x", "keyframes": {} })).is_err());
        assert!(validate_animation(&serde_json::json!({ "name": "x", "keyframes": "nope" })).is_err());
        // Missing name / keyframes.
        assert!(validate_animation(&serde_json::json!({ "keyframes": { "to": { "opacity": "1" } } })).is_err());
        assert!(validate_animation(&serde_json::json!({ "name": "x" })).is_err());
        // Unknown trigger.
        let err = validate_animation(&serde_json::json!({
            "name": "x", "keyframes": { "to": { "opacity": "1" } }, "trigger": "click"
        }))
        .unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("trigger"), "{err}");
        // `exit` (#3057) is a valid trigger — accepted (its rule/keyframes compile; runtime is a follow-up).
        assert!(validate_animation(&serde_json::json!({
            "name": "x", "keyframes": { "to": { "opacity": "1" } }, "trigger": "exit"
        }))
        .is_ok());
        // Injection selector (#3054) — a breakout attempt in the child selector is rejected.
        for bad in ["a{}b", "a;b", "</style>", "svg/*x*/"] {
            let a = serde_json::json!({
                "name": "x", "keyframes": { "to": { "opacity": "1" } }, "selector": bad
            });
            let err = validate_animation(&a).unwrap_err();
            assert!(err.contains("selector"), "bad selector '{bad}' rejected: {err}");
        }
        // Unsafe `set` property / value (#3054).
        let err = validate_animation(&serde_json::json!({
            "name": "x", "keyframes": { "to": { "opacity": "1" } }, "set": { "Bad-Prop": "center" }
        }))
        .unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("set"), "{err}");
        let err = validate_animation(&serde_json::json!({
            "name": "x", "keyframes": { "to": { "opacity": "1" } }, "set": { "transform-origin": "center; }evil{" }
        }))
        .unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("set") && err.contains("unsafe"), "{err}");
        // Unsafe delay (#3056).
        let err = validate_animation(&serde_json::json!({
            "name": "x", "keyframes": { "to": { "opacity": "1" } }, "delay": "1s; color: red"
        }))
        .unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("delay"), "{err}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn doctor_fix_merges_byte_identical_dups_and_repoints_composers() {
        let dir = tmp_store_dir("doctor-merge");
        let store = bsc_json_store::Store::new(dir, "component");
        let src = "export function Button(){ return <button/>; }";
        // The canonical (most-used) + a byte-identical dup + a page that composes the DUP.
        store.set("btn", &serde_json::json!({ "id": "btn", "name": "Button", "kitId": "k", "role": "primitive", "used": 9, "composes": [], "srcText": src, "source": src }).to_string()).unwrap();
        store.set("btn2", &serde_json::json!({ "id": "btn2", "name": "Btn2", "kitId": "k", "role": "primitive", "used": 1, "composes": [], "srcText": src, "source": src }).to_string()).unwrap();
        store.set("page", &serde_json::json!({ "id": "page", "name": "Page", "kitId": "k", "role": "page", "used": 2, "composes": ["Btn2"], "srcText": "p", "source": "export const C=()=>null;" }).to_string()).unwrap();

        let comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> = store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str(j).ok()).collect();

        // Dry run touches nothing.
        doctor_fix(&store, &comps, &comps, false).unwrap();
        assert!(store.get("btn2").unwrap().is_some(), "a dry run removes nothing");

        // Apply: the byte-identical dup is merged away; the canonical survives; the composer repoints.
        doctor_fix(&store, &comps, &comps, true).unwrap();
        assert!(store.get("btn2").unwrap().is_none(), "the byte-identical dup is merged away");
        assert!(store.get("btn").unwrap().is_some(), "the most-used canonical survives");
        let page: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&store.get("page").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(page["composes"], serde_json::json!(["Button"]), "the composer repointed Btn2 → Button");
    }

    /// as the REMOVED (non-canonical) side of a group — two packaged builtins can ship identical
    /// `srcText`. That removal must tombstone, not bare-delete, or the seed-reconcile brings it straight
    /// back on the next hydrate.

    /// #3087 end-to-end: `--fix --yes` APPLIED against a store shaped like the live one must leave the
    /// pages tier and the packaged viz seeds standing, while still pruning a genuine user orphan.
    #[test]
    fn doctor_fix_apply_never_removes_a_page_or_a_builtin_seed() {
        let dir = tmp_store_dir("doctor-guards");
        let store = bsc_json_store::Store::new(dir, "component");
        let module = "export const C=()=>null;";
        let set = |id: &str, rec: serde_json::Value| store.set(id, &rec.to_string()).unwrap();
        // Every candidate is `usageAssessed` — a detector looked and found no usage — so the PAGE and
        // BUILTIN guards are what hold each one back, not the never-determined one. Since #3888 slice 1
        // that judgement is per node: a `used > 0` component elsewhere no longer lifts it for all.
        set("btn", serde_json::json!({ "id": "btn", "name": "Button", "kitId": "k", "role": "primitive", "used": 7, "composes": [], "srcText": "b", "source": module }));
        // A page: a root by definition, composing its section component → "dangling-branch".
        set("invoicespage", serde_json::json!({ "id": "invoicespage", "name": "InvoicesPage", "kitId": "k", "role": "page", "used": 0, "usageAssessed": true, "composes": ["DataTable"], "srcText": "p", "source": module }));
        set("table", serde_json::json!({ "id": "table", "name": "DataTable", "kitId": "k", "role": "composite", "used": 0, "composes": [], "srcText": "t", "source": module }));
        // A packaged viz seed: isolated ON PURPOSE (#3194/#3242) → "orphan".
        set("algocells", serde_json::json!({ "id": "algocells", "name": "AlgoCells", "kitId": "k", "role": "primitive", "used": 0, "usageAssessed": true, "builtin": true, "composes": [], "srcText": "a", "source": module }));
        // A genuine user orphan — the case `--fix` exists for.
        set("ghost", serde_json::json!({ "id": "ghost", "name": "Ghost", "kitId": "k", "role": "primitive", "used": 0, "usageAssessed": true, "composes": [], "srcText": "g", "source": module }));
        // A record that CLAIMS a specifier: measured, unused, composed by nothing — and still never
        // pruned, because an importer resolves that name and nothing here can see it (guard 4).
        set("claimer", serde_json::json!({ "id": "claimer", "name": "Claimer", "kitId": "k", "role": "composite", "used": 0, "usageAssessed": true, "provides": "@/features/x/Card", "composes": [], "srcText": "c", "source": module }));

        let comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> = store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str(j).ok()).collect();
        doctor_fix(&store, &comps, &comps, true).unwrap();

        assert!(store.get("invoicespage").unwrap().is_some(), "a page is a root by definition — never pruned");
        assert!(store.get("algocells").unwrap().is_some(), "a packaged builtin seed is never pruned");
        assert!(store.get("claimer").unwrap().is_some(), "a record claiming a specifier is never pruned");
        assert!(store.get("ghost").unwrap().is_none(), "a genuine user orphan still prunes");
    }

    /// #114 end-to-end: filed by the react designer, who needed to isolate one category (e.g.
    /// `dangling-branch`) out of a 200+ finding report without a helper script. Builds a store shaped to
    /// trip TWO distinct categories — an orphan primitive and a dangling-branch root — and checks the
    /// SAME retain the CLI applies (findings.retain(|f| wanted.contains(&f.category))) narrows the
    /// combined report to just the requested one(s), composing with what every lens already contributed.
    #[test]
    fn doctor_category_filter_narrows_the_report_to_the_named_categories() {
        let dir = tmp_store_dir("doctor-category-filter");
        let store = bsc_json_store::Store::new(dir, "component");
        // A single-export default module — `export const C=…` shared across records tripped a spurious
        // `multi-export` finding on every one of them (the record id and the export name disagree), which
        // drowned out the two categories this fixture is built to isolate.
        let module = "export default () => null;";
        // An isolated primitive nothing composes ⇒ "orphan".
        store
            .set(
                "ghost",
                &serde_json::json!({ "id": "ghost", "name": "Ghost", "kitId": "k", "role": "primitive", "used": 0, "composes": [], "srcText": "g", "source": module }).to_string(),
            )
            .unwrap();
        // An unused root that still composes a dependency ⇒ the whole branch is "dangling-branch".
        store
            .set(
                "root",
                &serde_json::json!({ "id": "root", "name": "Root", "kitId": "k", "role": "composite", "used": 0, "composes": ["Leaf"], "srcText": "r", "source": module }).to_string(),
            )
            .unwrap();
        store
            .set(
                "leaf",
                &serde_json::json!({ "id": "leaf", "name": "Leaf", "kitId": "k", "role": "primitive", "used": 0, "composes": [], "srcText": "l", "source": module }).to_string(),
            )
            .unwrap();

        let comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> = store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str(j).ok()).collect();
        let all = crate::graph_health::analyze(&comps);
        // The fixture really does trip both categories, or the filter below would prove nothing.
        assert!(all.iter().any(|f| f.category == "orphan"), "{all:?}");
        assert!(all.iter().any(|f| f.category == "dangling-branch"), "{all:?}");

        let wanted = parse_category_arg("orphan");
        let mut narrowed = all.clone();
        narrowed.retain(|f| wanted.iter().any(|c| c == f.category));
        assert!(narrowed.iter().all(|f| f.category == "orphan"), "{narrowed:?}");
        assert!(!narrowed.is_empty());

        // A category present in no lens narrows to empty, same as an unknown `--kit`.
        let wanted = parse_category_arg("no-such-category");
        let mut none = all.clone();
        none.retain(|f| wanted.iter().any(|c| c == f.category));
        assert!(none.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn normalize_pointer_adds_an_optional_leading_slash() {
        assert_eq!(normalize_pointer("/name").unwrap(), "/name");
        assert_eq!(normalize_pointer("name").unwrap(), "/name");
        assert_eq!(normalize_pointer("props/0/req").unwrap(), "/props/0/req");

    // #3383: git-bash rewrites any arg starting with `/` to the git install root, so the DOCUMENTED
    // `--field /name` reached the process as `C:/Program Files/Git/name` and failed as a missing field.
    // Every studio session runs in git-bash, so this hit every pointer they passed the documented way.
    #[test]
    fn normalize_pointer_rejects_an_msys_mangled_pointer_and_names_the_fix() {
        for mangled in [
            "C:/Program Files/Git/name",
            "C:/Program Files/Git/animations/1",
            r"D:\msys64\name",
        ] {
            let err = normalize_pointer(mangled).expect_err("a drive-letter prefix is never a pointer");
            assert!(err.contains("git-bash path conversion"), "explains the cause: {err}");
            // Names the SLASH-FREE form to use, not just the failure.
            assert!(err.contains("WITHOUT the leading slash"), "names the fix: {err}");
            // It must NOT invent a field name — the intended pointer is unrecoverable here, and a
            // guessed one would steer a wrong WRITE on `patch`.
            assert!(!err.contains("use `"), "never guesses the field: {err}");
            // ...and steers off the workaround a restricted session cannot run.
            assert!(err.contains("MSYS_NO_PATHCONV"), "warns off the env prefix: {err}");
        }
        assert!(normalize_pointer("C:/Program Files/Git/name").unwrap_err().contains("`name`"));
    }

    // A pointer that merely CONTAINS a colon is untouched — only a leading `X:/` or `X:\` is MSYS damage.
    #[test]

    #[test]
    fn set_at_pointer_sets_replaces_appends_and_errors_on_a_missing_parent() {
        use serde_json::json;
        let mut v = json!({ "name": "Old", "props": [{ "name": "a", "req": false }] });
        // Replace an existing object key + a nested array-element field.
        set_at_pointer(&mut v, "/name", json!("New")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(v["name"], "New");
        set_at_pointer(&mut v, "/props/0/req", json!(true)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(v["props"][0]["req"], true);
        // Insert a NEW object key (the field didn't exist yet).
        set_at_pointer(&mut v, "/group", json!("forms")).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(v["group"], "forms");
        // Append to an array by index == len, and via the `-` push token.
        set_at_pointer(&mut v, "/props/1", json!({ "name": "b" })).unwrap();
        set_at_pointer(&mut v, "/props/-", json!({ "name": "c" })).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(v["props"][1]["name"], "b");
        assert_eq!(v["props"][2]["name"], "c");
        // RFC-6901 escapes: ~1 → / and ~0 → ~.
        set_at_pointer(&mut v, "/a~1b", json!(1)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(v["a/b"], 1);
        // Errors: a missing intermediate parent, an out-of-range index (no holes), the whole-doc
        // pointer (a patch is a FIELD write), and descending into a non-container.
        assert!(set_at_pointer(&mut v, "/missing/deep", json!(1)).is_err());
        assert!(set_at_pointer(&mut v, "/props/9", json!(1)).is_err());
        assert!(set_at_pointer(&mut v, "", json!(1)).is_err());
        assert!(set_at_pointer(&mut v, "/name/x", json!(1)).is_err());
    }

    /// bsc request #119: `refuse_buildable_regression` is what makes `set-src`/`patch /srcText` refuse
    /// exactly the write that clobbered `KitShareModal`/`ConsolePage` — a `provides`-less record whose
    /// `srcText` the Design Studio preview sandbox could BUILD, overwritten with one it cannot.
    #[test]
    fn refuse_buildable_regression_blocks_only_a_provides_less_buildable_to_unbuildable_write() {
        use serde_json::json;
        let buildable = "export const Button = () => null;";
        let unbuildable = "import { X } from \"@/store\";\nexport const Button = () => X;";

        // The core case: no `provides`, buildable -> unbuildable is refused, and the error names both
        // the request and the escape.
        let bare = json!({ "id": "consolepage", "srcText": buildable });
        let err = refuse_buildable_regression(&bare, unbuildable).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("consolepage"), "{err}");
        assert!(err.contains("#119"), "{err}");
        assert!(err.contains("--force"), "{err}");
        assert!(err.contains("provides"), "{err}");

        // A record that already CARRIES `provides` is a module lift, not a preview stub — the preview
        // sandbox no longer decides buildability for it (#43), so the same regression is fine.
        let with_provides = json!({ "id": "c", "srcText": buildable, "provides": "@/components/c" });
        assert!(refuse_buildable_regression(&with_provides, unbuildable).is_ok());

        // Nothing buildable was there to protect — the prior copy was ALREADY unbuildable (e.g. a raw
        // seed transcription that was never fixed), so there is no regression to guard against.
        let already_broken = json!({ "id": "d", "srcText": unbuildable });
        assert!(refuse_buildable_regression(&already_broken, unbuildable).is_ok());

        // The new source is STILL buildable — not a regression at all.
        let still_good = "export const Button2 = () => null;";
        assert!(refuse_buildable_regression(&bare, still_good).is_ok());

        // `--force` is the deliberate override, same escape `set` already has for the page-role refusal.
        FORCE_WRITE.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
        let forced = refuse_buildable_regression(&bare, unbuildable);
        FORCE_WRITE.store(false, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
        assert!(forced.is_ok(), "--force stores the regression deliberately");
    }

    /// The guard is wired into the actual write paths, not just the pure predicate: `set-src` refuses
    /// the regression, leaves the store untouched, and `--force` overrides it.
    #[test]
    fn set_src_refuses_a_buildable_to_unbuildable_regression_unless_forced() {

        assert_eq!(rec["srcText"], buildable, "the refused write left srcText untouched");

        assert!(replace_src(&store, "consolepage", unbuildable, None).is_ok(), "provides beats the preview sandbox");

        // And `--force` overrides it even without `provides`, on a fresh record.
        store.set("kitsharemodal", r#"{"id":"kitsharemodal","name":"KitShareModal","srcText":"export const K = () => null;"}"#).unwrap();
        FORCE_WRITE.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
        let forced = replace_src(&store, "kitsharemodal", unbuildable, None);
        FORCE_WRITE.store(false, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);

    }

    /// #119 — the half `refuse_buildable_regression` cannot see. That guard asks whether the NEW source
    /// still builds, so an anonymous overwrite that happens to stay buildable sails through it while
    /// still destroying a named author's work. `kitsharemodal` rev4-6 and `consolepage` rev11-12 were
    /// both lost that way. Every source here is buildable, precisely so the other guard stays silent
    /// and this one is the only thing under test.
    #[test]
    fn an_unattributed_write_cannot_clobber_srctext_someone_signed_for() {
        let dir = tmp_store_dir("anon-src-overwrite");
        let store = bsc_json_store::Store::new(dir, "component");
        let designer_src = "export const KitShareModal = () => null;";
        store
            .set(
                "kitsharemodal",
                &format!(
                    r#"{{"id":"kitsharemodal","name":"KitShareModal","srcText":{},
                        "history":[{{"rev":1,"by":"designer","changed":["srcText"]}}]}}"#,
                    serde_json::to_string(designer_src).unwrap()
                ),
            )
            .unwrap();
        let other = "export const KitShareModal = () => 1;";

        // The filed shape: an anonymous sync overwrites a designer's source.
        let err = replace_src(&store, "kitsharemodal", other, None).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("UNATTRIBUTED"), "{err}");
        assert!(err.contains("designer"), "it must name whose work is at risk: {err}");
        let rec: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&store.get("kitsharemodal").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(rec["srcText"], designer_src, "the refused write left srcText untouched");

        // An ATTRIBUTED write passes — any name, not just the prior one. Identifying yourself is the
        // whole ask; the guard is not an ownership lock.
        replace_src(&store, "kitsharemodal", other, Some("harvester")).unwrap();
        let rec: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&store.get("kitsharemodal").unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(rec["srcText"], other);
        assert_eq!(rec["updatedBy"], "harvester", "--by flows through to the stamp");
    }

    /// The escapes and the non-cases, kept separate so a failure names which rule broke.
    #[test]
    fn the_anonymous_srctext_guard_stays_out_of_the_way_of_everything_else() {
        use serde_json::json;
        let signed = json!({
            "id": "c", "srcText": "export const C = () => null;",
            "history": [{ "rev": 1, "by": "designer", "changed": ["srcText"] }],
        });

        // --force is the deliberate override.
        assert!(refuse_anonymous_src_overwrite("c", &signed, "next", "unknown", true).is_ok());
        // Identical content loses nothing, so there is nothing to refuse.
        assert!(
            refuse_anonymous_src_overwrite("c", &signed, "export const C = () => null;", "unknown", false)
                .is_ok()
        );
        // Nobody to protect: the prior write was itself unattributed.
        let anon = json!({
            "id": "c", "srcText": "x",
            "history": [{ "rev": 1, "by": "unknown", "changed": ["srcText"] }],
        });
        assert!(refuse_anonymous_src_overwrite("c", &anon, "y", "unknown", false).is_ok());
        // No history at all, and history that never moved srcText — nothing recorded to protect.
        assert!(refuse_anonymous_src_overwrite("c", &json!({ "id": "c" }), "y", "unknown", false).is_ok());
        let namesonly = json!({
            "id": "c", "srcText": "x",
            "history": [{ "rev": 1, "by": "designer", "changed": ["name"] }],
        });
        assert!(refuse_anonymous_src_overwrite("c", &namesonly, "y", "unknown", false).is_ok());

        // A `created` entry DOES count when the record carries srcText — a record authored with its
        // source and never rewritten is exactly the newly-authored Design Studio record this protects.
        let created = json!({
            "id": "c", "srcText": "export const C = () => null;",
            "history": [{ "rev": 1, "by": "designer", "changed": ["created"] }],
        });
        assert!(refuse_anonymous_src_overwrite("c", &created, "y", "unknown", false).is_err());
        // ...but not on a record with no source of its own — there was never any srcText authored.
        let created_srcless =
            json!({ "id": "c", "history": [{ "rev": 1, "by": "designer", "changed": ["created"] }] });
        assert!(refuse_anonymous_src_overwrite("c", &created_srcless, "y", "unknown", false).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_src_write_parser_takes_by_and_force_and_refuses_a_valueless_by() {

        assert!(parse_src_write_args(&a(&["btn", "--by"])).is_err(), "a valueless --by must error");
        assert!(
            parse_src_write_args(&a(&["btn", "--by", "--force"])).is_err(),

        assert!(FORCE_WRITE.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed));

    /// REGRESSION, designer request #91. A broken-`composes` bug was filed that was not one, because
    /// `bsc ui get deploytoggle` answered a bare `null` for a record present under id `toggle` with name
    /// `DeployToggle`. The lookup is the bug; the graph was correct.
    #[test]
    fn get_resolves_a_name_as_well_as_an_id_and_refuses_to_answer_null() {
        let dir = tmp_store_dir("get-handle");
        let store = bsc_json_store::Store::new(dir.clone(), "component");
        store.set("toggle", r#"{"id":"toggle","name":"DeployToggle","kitId":"k"}"#).unwrap();
        let go = |a: Vec<&str>| run(a.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect(), "bsc ui");

        // The id path is untouched.
        assert!(go(vec!["get", "toggle", "--dir", &dir]).is_ok());
        // The reporter's EXACT command now resolves — by name, case-insensitively, through both the plain
        // path and the `--field` path.
        assert!(go(vec!["get", "deploytoggle", "--dir", &dir]).is_ok(), "the name resolves");
        assert!(go(vec!["get", "DeployToggle", "--dir", &dir]).is_ok());
        assert!(go(vec!["get", "deploytoggle", "--field", "id", "--dir", &dir]).is_ok(), "and with --field");

        // A genuine miss is an ERROR, not `null` on stdout — that silence is what made the graph look broken.
        let err = go(vec!["get", "nosuchthing", "--dir", &dir]).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("nosuchthing"), "{err}");

        // An id BEATS a name of the same spelling: the store is keyed by id, so that is the identity every
        // other verb takes, and resolving to the other record would be a silent switcheroo.
        store.set("deploytoggle", r#"{"id":"deploytoggle","name":"Something Else","kitId":"k"}"#).unwrap();
        let resolved = resolve_component_handle(&store, "deploytoggle").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(resolved, "deploytoggle", "the id wins over a same-spelled name");

        // An AMBIGUOUS name is refused, naming the candidates — picking one silently is how the next false
        // report gets filed.
        store.set("toggle2", r#"{"id":"toggle2","name":"DeployToggle","kitId":"k"}"#).unwrap();
        let err = resolve_component_handle(&store, "DeployToggle").unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("toggle") && err.contains("toggle2"), "names both candidates: {err}");
    }

    /// A scratch COMPONENT store over a fresh temp dir, for the stamping tests.
    fn tmp_component_store(tag: &str) -> bsc_json_store::Store {
        bsc_json_store::Store::new(tmp_store_dir(tag), "component")
    }

    /// Parse a stored record's verbatim JSON back to a `Value` (the read-back the assertions use).
    fn stored(store: &bsc_json_store::Store, id: &str) -> serde_json::Value {
        serde_json::from_str(&store.get(id).unwrap().unwrap()).unwrap()
    }

    /// The record #4197 exists for: a PAGE whose source file no longer exists (`fleetpage`, deleted by
    /// #3636), so the store holds the only copy of that UI and a dropped field is unrecoverable.
    fn fleetpage_record() -> serde_json::Value {
        serde_json::json!({
            "id": "fleetpage", "name": "FleetPage", "kitId": "base-studio-code", "role": "page",
            "composes": ["Row", "Card"], "src": "src/features/planner/fleet/Fleet.tsx",
            "folder": "features/planner/fleet", "srcText": "old",
            "props": { "title": "string" },
        })
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_partial_write_merges_and_preserves_every_field_it_omitted() {
        // THE regression test for #4197. `set` used to REPLACE, so the write below — the exact shape the
        // worker protocol tells a fleet worker to make for a record-backed component file (#4193) —
        // deleted the record's kit, role, composes edges, provenance and props. Against the old
        // behaviour every `preserved` assertion fails; against the merge (the #4154 semantics, now shared
        // with `bsc graph impl set`) only `srcText` moves.
        let store = tmp_component_store("merge-partial");
        let rich = fleetpage_record();
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rich), None, "seed", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();

        let partial = serde_json::json!({ "id": "fleetpage", "srcText": "new" });
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&partial), None, "worker", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();

        let after = stored(&store, "fleetpage");
        assert_eq!(after["srcText"], "new", "the supplied field is written");
        for (field, expected) in [
            ("name", serde_json::json!("FleetPage")),
            ("kitId", serde_json::json!("base-studio-code")),
            ("role", serde_json::json!("page")),
            ("composes", serde_json::json!(["Row", "Card"])),
            ("src", serde_json::json!("src/features/planner/fleet/Fleet.tsx")),
            ("folder", serde_json::json!("features/planner/fleet")),
            ("props", serde_json::json!({ "title": "string" })),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(after[field], expected, "the write never mentioned {field}, so it is preserved");
        }
        // The history reflects the truth: an EDIT, with nothing dropped.
        let entry = after["history"].as_array().unwrap().last().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(entry["changed"], serde_json::json!(["srcText"]), "only srcText moved: {entry}");
        assert!(entry.get("dropped").is_none(), "a merging write removes nothing: {entry}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn clear_removes_one_field_explicitly_and_leaves_the_rest_alone() {
        // A merge makes removal-by-omission impossible, so removal is EXPLICIT — `--clear a,b`, exactly
        // as `bsc graph impl set` spells it (#4154). The removal is recorded in the history's `dropped`.
        let store = tmp_component_store("merge-clear");
        let rich = fleetpage_record();
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rich), None, "seed", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();
        let prior = stored(&store, "fleetpage");

        let clear = ["folder".to_string()];
        let edit = serde_json::json!({ "id": "fleetpage", "srcText": "new" });
        let plan = WritePlan { replace: false, clear: &clear };
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&edit), None, "designer", "component", None, plan).unwrap();

        let after = stored(&store, "fleetpage");
        assert!(after.get("folder").is_none(), "the cleared field is gone");
        assert_eq!(after["src"], "src/features/planner/fleet/Fleet.tsx", "its neighbours are untouched");
        assert_eq!(after["composes"], serde_json::json!(["Row", "Card"]));
        let entry = after["history"].as_array().unwrap().last().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(entry["dropped"], serde_json::json!(["folder"]), "the removal is legible in `bsc ui log`: {entry}");
        // An asked-for removal is NOT warned about — the caller requested it, and warning about a deletion
        // you just asked for is the noise that trains people to ignore the real warning.
        let effective = crate::record::merge_over(&prior, &edit, &clear);
        assert!(destructive_write_warning("fleetpage", "component", &prior, &effective, &clear).is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_replace_write_still_replaces_and_warns_about_every_field_it_deletes() {
        // `--replace` is the ONE remaining way to delete by omission — it exists for the app bridge,
        // `bsc ui import`, and the seed reconcile's authoritative reset (#3723), which a merge would stop
        // from ever converging. Because it can still lose data, it says so, naming each field.
        let store = tmp_component_store("replace-warns");
        let rich = fleetpage_record();
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rich), None, "seed", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();
        let prior = stored(&store, "fleetpage");

        let partial = serde_json::json!({ "id": "fleetpage", "srcText": "new" });
        let plan = WritePlan { replace: true, clear: &[] };
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&partial), None, "bridge", "component", None, plan).unwrap();
        let after = stored(&store, "fleetpage");
        assert!(after.get("kitId").is_none() && after.get("composes").is_none(), "--replace really replaces");

        let msg = destructive_write_warning("fleetpage", "component", &prior, &partial, &[])
            .expect("a partial --replace over a rich record is destructive");
        for field in ["composes", "folder", "kitId", "name", "props", "role", "src"] {
            assert!(msg.contains(field), "the warning names {field}: {msg}");
        }
        // …and NOT the server-managed fields, which every write re-stamps regardless of the payload.
        // Reporting those would fire on every single write and train the reader to ignore it.
        for noise in ["rev", "updatedAt", "updatedBy", "history"] {
            assert!(!msg.contains(&format!(" {noise},")) && !msg.contains(&format!(" {noise}.")),
                "the warning does not cry wolf about {noise}: {msg}");
        }
    }

        // gone and there is nothing for `--clear` to remove. Refusing beats silently honouring one — and
        // the refusal lands BEFORE stdin is touched, so it never half-writes.
        let args: Vec<String> =
            ["--replace", "--clear", "folder"].iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
        let err = cmd_set(&args, open_component_store, validate_component_batch, "component").unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("--clear and --replace contradict"), "names the conflict: {err}");
        // `--clear` still needs its value — a bare flag is a usage error, not an empty clear list.
        let bare: Vec<String> = vec!["--clear".to_string()];
        assert!(cmd_set(&bare, open_component_store, validate_component_batch, "component")
            .unwrap_err()
            .contains("--clear needs a comma-separated field list"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_destructive_write_is_recorded_in_the_history_separately_from_edits() {
        // `changed` already counts a removal, but files it next to ordinary edits — so `bsc ui log` could
        // not tell "deleted half the record" from "fixed a typo". `dropped` is what makes that legible,
        // and it is ABSENT on a non-destructive write so existing entries keep their shape.
        let store = tmp_component_store("drop-history");
        let rich = serde_json::json!({
            "id": "card", "name": "Card", "kitId": "react-ui", "role": "composite", "composes": ["Row"],
        });
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rich), None, "seed", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();
        let first: serde_json::Value = stored(&store, "card");
        let entry = first["history"].as_array().unwrap().last().unwrap();
        assert!(entry.get("dropped").is_none(), "a create drops nothing: {entry}");

        let partial = serde_json::json!({ "id": "card", "name": "Card" });
        let plan = WritePlan { replace: true, clear: &[] };
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&partial), None, "designer", "component", None, plan).unwrap();
        let after: serde_json::Value = stored(&store, "card");
        let entry = after["history"].as_array().unwrap().last().unwrap();
        let dropped: Vec<&str> =
            entry["dropped"].as_array().unwrap().iter().map(|v| v.as_str().unwrap()).collect();
        assert_eq!(dropped, vec!["composes", "kitId", "role"]);
        // …and the fields really are gone from the stored record — the warning describes a real deletion,
        // it does not merely predict one.
        assert!(after.get("composes").is_none() && after.get("role").is_none());
    }

    /// The valid-JSX source the write-time syntax gate accepts, parameterised so two revisions differ.
    fn page_src(marker: &str) -> String {
        format!("export function GraphPrimitive() {{ return <div>{marker}</div>; }}\n")
    }

    #[test]
    fn revert_restores_the_source_a_bad_write_replaced() {
        // THE incident, end to end through the store. `graphprimitive` had no packaged seed, so once the
        // designer overwrote it at 01:39 the broken version was the only copy that had ever existed.
        let store = tmp_component_store("revert-restores");
        let good = serde_json::json!({
            "id": "graphprimitive", "name": "GraphPrimitive", "kitId": "base-studio-code",
            "role": "primitive", "provides": "@/shared/ui/spec/graphPrimitive", "srcText": page_src("good"),
        });
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&good), None, "seed", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();
        let broken = serde_json::json!({ "id": "graphprimitive", "srcText": page_src("broken") });
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&broken), None, "designer", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(stored(&store, "graphprimitive")["srcText"], page_src("broken"));

        cmd_revert(&["graphprimitive".into(), "--dir".into(), store.dir().to_string_lossy().to_string(), "--by".into(), "rescue".into()]).unwrap();

        let after = stored(&store, "graphprimitive");
        assert_eq!(after["srcText"], page_src("good"), "the source the bad write replaced is back");
        assert_eq!(after["rev"], serde_json::json!(3), "a revert is a WRITE — it stamps forward, never rewinds rev");
        assert_eq!(after["updatedBy"], "rescue");
        // Every other field is untouched — a revert of a bad SOURCE must not also rewind good metadata.
        assert_eq!(after["provides"], "@/shared/ui/spec/graphPrimitive");
        assert_eq!(after["role"], "primitive");
        // ...and the version it replaced is itself revertible now, so a mistaken revert is not terminal.
        let entry = after["history"].as_array().unwrap().last().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(entry["prevSrc"], page_src("broken"));
        assert!(entry["note"].as_str().unwrap().starts_with("revert: srcText restored to rev 1"), "{entry}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn revert_to_an_explicit_rev_and_a_refusal_when_it_is_out_of_reach() {
        let store = tmp_component_store("revert-to-rev");
        let mut rec = serde_json::json!({ "id": "kitrenderer", "srcText": page_src("v0") });
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rec), None, "seed", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();
        for i in 1..=(crate::record::PREV_SRC_CAP + 2) {
            rec = serde_json::json!({ "id": "kitrenderer", "srcText": page_src(&format!("v{i}")) });
            set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rec), None, "designer", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();
        }
        let dir = store.dir().to_string_lossy().to_string();
        let latest = crate::record::read_rev(&stored(&store, "kitrenderer"));

        // An explicit --to inside the retained window lands on exactly that revision's source.
        cmd_revert(&["kitrenderer".into(), "--to".into(), (latest - 2).to_string(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()]).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(stored(&store, "kitrenderer")["srcText"], page_src(&format!("v{}", latest - 3)));

        // Past the content cap it REFUSES, and names what is still reachable — it never silently lands on
        // a nearer version, which would report success while restoring bytes that revision never held.
        let err = cmd_revert(&["kitrenderer".into(), "--to".into(), "1".into(), "--dir".into(), dir]).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("no longer retained"), "{err}");
        assert!(err.contains("revertible revisions:"), "the refusal says what IS possible: {err}");
    }

        let err = cmd_revert(&["nosuch".into(), "--dir".into(), store.dir().to_string_lossy().to_string()]).unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("nothing to revert"), "{err}");
    }

        let rec = serde_json::json!({ "id": "button", "name": "Button", "kitId": "react-ui" });

        // First write of a brand-new record → rev 1, updatedBy = the writer, updatedAt an ISO stamp.
        let ids = set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rec), None, "alice", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(ids, vec!["button".to_string()]);

        // Stamping never disturbs the domain fields.

        // A second write of the same id bumps from the STORED rev (1 → 2), even though the payload carries none.
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rec), None, "bob", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();
        let s = stored(&store, "button");

        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rec), None, "x", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap(); // → rev 1

        // --if-version 0 is STALE (current rev is 1): rejected with a clear message, nothing overwritten.
        let err = set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rec), Some(0), "x", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap_err();

        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rec), Some(1), "x", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(stored(&store, "chip")["rev"], serde_json::json!(2));

        // --if-version guards a SINGLE record — a batch with a lone version number is a usage error.
        let batch = vec![serde_json::json!({ "id": "a" }), serde_json::json!({ "id": "b" })];
        let err = set_stamped(&store, &batch, Some(1), "x", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap_err();

        // The lean projection is byte-for-byte the same — the stamp fields don't leak into it, the axes still
        // project. `domain` reads as "" here because this fixture predates the FEATURE axis: `lean_meta`
        // renders an ABSENT meta field as the empty string rather than omitting it, so a record with no
        // domain still has the same SHAPE as one that has it. That is what keeps a consumer parsing a
        // fixed set of keys instead of branching on presence.
        let meta = bsc_json_store::cli::lean_meta(&store.get("card").unwrap().unwrap(), COMPONENT_SPEC.meta_fields);
        assert_eq!(
            meta,
            serde_json::json!({ "id": "card", "name": "Card", "kitId": "react-ui", "role": "layout", "folder": "pages", "feature": "", "shapes": ["list"] })
        );
        // get / list / list --full still run clean end-to-end over a stamped store.
        assert!(run(vec!["get".into(), "card".into(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()], "bsc ui").is_ok());
        assert!(run(vec!["list".into(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()], "bsc ui").is_ok());
        assert!(run(vec!["list".into(), "--full".into(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()], "bsc ui").is_ok());
        // doctor still parses the stamped records (the extra fields don't perturb graph health).
        assert!(run(vec!["doctor".into(), "--dir".into(), dir], "bsc ui").is_ok());
    }

        // #4072 — the Design Studio hydrated its graph with `--full`: 1.72 MB over 321 components, of
        // which 77.6% is `srcText` that no node reads, and the page blocked up to 8s on it. The graph
        // projection must carry the node card + `composes` (edges) and NOTHING heavy.
        let store = tmp_component_store("graphproj");

        let rec = serde_json::json!({
            "id": "card", "name": "Card", "kitId": "react-ui", "role": "layout", "folder": "pages",
            "used": 12, "composes": ["Box", "Text"],
            // The weight the projection exists to leave behind:
            "srcText": "export function Card() { /* … a great many bytes … */ }",
            "tests": ["a", "b"], "history": [{ "rev": 1 }], "props": { "title": "string" },
        });
        set_stamped(&store, std::slice::from_ref(&rec), None, "designer", "component", None, WritePlan::default()).unwrap();

        let g = bsc_json_store::cli::lean_meta(&store.get("card").unwrap().unwrap(), COMPONENT_SPEC.graph_fields);

            })
        );
        // The heavy fields are absent, not merely empty — that is the whole point.
        for heavy in ["srcText", "tests", "history", "props"] {

        }

    #[test]
    fn pattern_promotes_a_cluster_then_answers_membership_both_ways() {
        let store = tmp_component_store("pattern-c");
        let pdir = tmp_component_store("pattern-p");
        let (cd, pd) = (store.dir().to_string_lossy().into_owned(), pdir.dir().to_string_lossy().into_owned());
        let card = |id: &str, name: &str| {
            serde_json::json!({
                "id": id, "name": name, "kitId": "react-ui", "role": "composite", "composes": ["Card", "ToggleRow"],
                "srcText": format!("export const {name} = () => <Card title=\"x\"><ToggleRow on={{a}} onToggle={{b}} title=\"t\"/></Card>;"),
            })
        };
        for r in [card("a", "AlphaCard"), card("b", "BetaCard"), card("c", "GammaCard")] {
            store.set(r["id"].as_str().unwrap(), &r.to_string()).unwrap();
        }
        let d = |extra: &[&str]| {
            extra.iter().map(|s| s.to_string())
                .chain(["--dir".into(), cd.clone(), "--pattern-dir".into(), pd.clone()])
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        };
        // An empty store lists cleanly and points at how to fill it, rather than printing nothing.
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "list"]), "bsc ui").is_ok());
        // Promotion needs --from: there is no positional cluster index, because one would go stale.
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "new", "settings-toggle-card"]), "bsc ui").is_err(), "--from is required");
        let err = run(d(&["pattern", "new", "p", "--from", "ghost"]), "bsc ui").unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("not in any cluster"), "{err}");

        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "new", "settings-toggle-card", "--from", "a", "--name", "Settings toggle card"]), "bsc ui").is_ok());
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "new", "settings-toggle-card", "--from", "a"]), "bsc ui").is_err(), "id collision refused");
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "get", "settings-toggle-card", "--json", "--pretty"]), "bsc ui").is_ok());
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "list", "--json"]), "bsc ui").is_ok());

        // The stored record is derived, carries its exemplars, and does NOT carry a member list.
        let rec: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(pdir.get("settings-toggle-card").unwrap().unwrap().as_str()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(rec["signatureSource"], "derived");
        assert_eq!(rec["exemplars"].as_array().map(Vec::len), Some(3));
        assert!(rec.get("members").is_none(), "membership is computed, never frozen into the record");

        // The reverse lookup, both outcomes.
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "of", "a", "--json"]), "bsc ui").is_ok());
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "of", "ghost"]), "bsc ui").is_err(), "an absent component names itself");
        store.set("chart", &serde_json::json!({
            "id": "chart", "name": "Chart", "kitId": "react-ui", "composes": ["Axis"],
            "srcText": "export const Chart = () => <Axis scale={s}/>;",
        }).to_string()).unwrap();
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "of", "chart"]), "bsc ui").is_ok(), "belonging to none is an answer, not an error");

        // A newly authored sibling is a member with NO edit to the pattern — the point of computing it.
        store.set("new", &card("new", "TelemetryCard").to_string()).unwrap();
        let comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
            store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str(j).ok()).collect();
        let members = crate::patterns::conforming(&rec, &comps, true);
        assert!(members.iter().any(|m| m.id == "new"), "the new sibling joined: {:?}", members.iter().map(|m| &m.id).collect::<Vec<_>>());
        assert!(!members.iter().any(|m| m.id == "chart"), "the unrelated record did not");

        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "remove", "settings-toggle-card"]), "bsc ui").is_ok());
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "remove", "settings-toggle-card"]), "bsc ui").is_err(), "removing nothing is an error");
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "--nope"]), "bsc ui").is_err(), "unknown flag");
        assert!(run(d(&["pattern", "wat"]), "bsc ui").is_err(), "unknown subcommand");
        assert!(run(vec!["pattern".into(), "help".into()], "bsc ui").is_ok(), "help reachable");
        assert!(COMPONENT_COMMANDS.iter().any(|c| c.name == "pattern"), "the verb is documented");
    }

                "srcText": "export const Widget = () => <div />;",
            }),
            // References Widget in JSX, and separately imports it — but never lists it in `composes`.
            serde_json::json!({
                "id": "page", "name": "Page", "kitId": "react-ui", "role": "composite", "composes": [],
                "srcText": "import { Widget } from \"@/x/Widget\";\nexport const Page = () => <Widget />;",
            }),
            // Shares no reference at all.
            serde_json::json!({
                "id": "unrelated", "name": "Unrelated", "kitId": "react-ui", "role": "primitive", "composes": [],
                "srcText": "export const Unrelated = () => <span />;",
            }),
        ] {
            store.set(rec["id"].as_str().unwrap(), &rec.to_string()).unwrap();
        }
        let d = |extra: &[&str]| {
            extra.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).chain(["--dir".to_string(), dir.clone()]).collect::<Vec<_>>()
        };

        // `used-by` sees NOTHING — there is no `composes` edge — which is exactly the false "orphan"
        // #113 filed against. `used-by` itself prints via plain `println!`, so its human output is not
        // capturable here; going straight at the composes-inverse index proves the same fact.
        let comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
            store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(j).ok()).collect();
        let idx = used_by_index(&comps);
        assert!(
            !idx.contains_key(&("react-ui".to_string(), "Widget".to_string())),
            "used-by is blind to the JSX reference: no `composes` edge names Widget"
        );

        // `refs` finds it: `page` shows both a JSX hit and an import-clause hit, `unrelated` does not appear.
        let (r, out) = bsc_util::capture_output(|| run(d(&["refs", "widget", "--json"]), "bsc ui"));
        r.unwrap();
        let v: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(out.trim()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(v["name"], "Widget");
        assert_eq!(v["count"], 1);
        assert_eq!(v["refs"][0]["id"], "page");
        assert_eq!(v["refs"][0]["jsx"], 1);
        assert_eq!(v["refs"][0]["importClause"], 1);

        // The text form names the referencer and never mentions `unrelated`.
        let (r, out) = bsc_util::capture_output(|| run(d(&["refs", "widget"]), "bsc ui"));
        r.unwrap();
        assert!(out.contains("Page"), "{out}");
        assert!(!out.contains("Unrelated"), "{out}");

        // A component nothing references at all — the genuinely-dead case `refs` exists to confirm.
        let (r, out) = bsc_util::capture_output(|| run(d(&["refs", "unrelated"]), "bsc ui"));
        r.unwrap();
        assert!(out.contains("no literal srcText reference found"), "{out}");

        assert!(run(vec!["refs".into(), "help".into()], "bsc ui").is_ok(), "help reachable");
        let err = run(d(&["refs", "ghost"]), "bsc ui").unwrap_err();
        assert!(err.contains("no component with id 'ghost'"), "{err}");

        // A READ — in the catalog, never a scoped mutation, and runs under a read-only ui scope.
        assert!(COMPONENT_COMMANDS.iter().any(|c| c.name == "refs"));
        assert!(!is_scoped_mutation(&["refs".to_string(), "widget".to_string()]), "refs is a read");
        bsc_cli_util::with_scopes(Some(r#"{"ui":"read"}"#), || {
            assert!(run(d(&["refs", "widget"]), "bsc ui").is_ok(), "refs works read-scoped");
        });
    }

    /// Designer request #96: `bsc ui merge` folding a `builtin: true` duplicate away must STICK — a
    /// bare `store.remove` leaves the id looking merely absent, and the frontend seed-reconcile treats
    /// "absent" as "never seeded", bringing the packaged builtin right back on the next hydrate. Merging
    /// a builtin `from` must instead write the same suppression tombstone `bsc ui suppress` does.
    /// 2026-08-24: a designer session merged 34 module records away and orphaned 34 specifiers, taking
    /// Settings, Glance and Accessibility off the store's resolution graph. `suppress` refuses exactly
    /// this; `merge` reached the same tombstone through `retire_component`, which had none of the check.
    /// The write half, which is what decides whether anything can be DELETED.
    ///
    /// A scan can prove USE. It cannot prove DISUSE — and this one was wrong about that twice while it
    /// was being written: with three sources, `--apply` on the real store authorized deleting `App`,
    /// `GraphComponent` and `ThemeProvider`. So `usageAssessed` is written only where usage was FOUND.
    #[test]
    fn usage_scan_writes_used_for_all_but_asserts_assessment_only_where_it_found_use() {
        let store = tmp_component_store("usage-scan-apply");
        let dir = store.dir().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
        let put = |id: &str, v: serde_json::Value| store.set(id, &v.to_string()).unwrap();
        put("child", serde_json::json!({ "id": "child", "name": "Child", "kitId": "k", "role": "primitive", "composes": [] }));
        put("parent", serde_json::json!({ "id": "parent", "name": "Parent", "kitId": "k", "role": "composite", "composes": ["Child"] }));
        put("lonely", serde_json::json!({ "id": "lonely", "name": "Lonely", "kitId": "k", "role": "primitive", "composes": [] }));

        // A READ never writes. If it did, every `doctor` run would quietly license the next prune.
        run(vec!["usage-scan".into(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()], "bsc ui").expect("read");
        let before = stored(&store, "child");
        assert!(before.get("usageAssessed").is_none(), "a read must not write: {before}");
        assert!(before.get("used").is_none(), "…anything at all: {before}");

        run(vec!["usage-scan".into(), "--apply".into(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()], "bsc ui").expect("apply");
        let child = stored(&store, "child");
        assert_eq!(child["used"], 1, "composed once: {child}");
        assert_eq!(child["usageAssessed"], serde_json::Value::Bool(true), "evidence of use ⇒ assessed");

        // `lonely` gets the COUNT (it is real information) but NOT the assessment — so `doctor --fix`
        // still holds it back, and doctor still reports it. "We found no reference" is not "it is dead".
        let lonely = stored(&store, "lonely");
        assert_eq!(lonely["used"], 0, "the count is written for everyone: {lonely}");
        assert!(
            lonely.get("usageAssessed").is_none(),
            "no evidence ⇒ NO assessment, or the scan would be licensing its own blind spots: {lonely}",
        );
        let comps: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
            store.list().iter().filter_map(|j| serde_json::from_str(j).ok()).collect();
        let plan = crate::graph_health::prune_plan(&comps);
        assert!(
            !plan.prune.iter().any(|p| p.id == "lonely"),
            "and it is therefore still unprunable: {:?}",
            plan.prune,
        );

        // A mistyped --root is an ERROR, never an empty walk: a root contributing nothing would report
        // every component in that tree unused, and --apply would then act on it.
        let err = run(
            vec!["usage-scan".into(), "--root".into(), "/no/such/tree-xyz".into(), "--dir".into(), dir],
            "bsc ui",
        )
        .expect_err("a missing root must refuse");
        assert!(err.contains("does not exist"), "{err}");
    }

    /// #110: `usage-scan --apply` is a real mutation path (it flips `used`/`usageAssessed`, which is
    /// exactly what moves a record off `doctor`'s orphan/dangling-branch findings) but it wrote through
    /// `stamped_set` directly and never called `emit_ui_activity`, unlike every other write verb (`set`,
    /// `remove`, `rename`, `merge`, `import`, …). The Design Studio's live-focus poll (`useUiActivity`)
    /// re-hydrates the library on a `ui-touch` line and nothing else — so a component `usage-scan --apply`
    /// rescued from a false orphan kept showing the stale badge in the running app until a full relaunch,
    /// because the ONE signal that tells it to reload never fired. Filed as request 110 (DeployToggle).
    #[test]
    fn usage_scan_apply_emits_a_ui_touch_per_written_record_so_the_studio_rehydrates() {
        let _guard = ENV_LOCK.lock().unwrap_or_else(|p| p.into_inner());
        bsc_cli_util::with_scopes(None, || {
            let act = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("bsc-component-uiact-usagescan-{}.log", std::process::id()));
            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&act);
            std::env::set_var("BSC_UI_ACTIVITY_LOG", &act);
            std::env::set_var("BSC_AUDIT_PANE", "design-studio:designer");

            let store = tmp_component_store("usage-scan-emit");
            let dir = store.dir().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
            let put = |id: &str, v: serde_json::Value| store.set(id, &v.to_string()).unwrap();
            put("child", serde_json::json!({ "id": "child", "name": "Child", "kitId": "base-studio-code", "role": "primitive", "composes": [] }));
            put("parent", serde_json::json!({ "id": "parent", "name": "Parent", "kitId": "base-studio-code", "role": "composite", "composes": ["Child"] }));

            // A READ never emits — nothing changed for the Studio to reload.
            run(vec!["usage-scan".into(), "--dir".into(), dir.clone()], "bsc ui").expect("read");
            assert!(!act.is_file() || std::fs::read_to_string(&act).unwrap().is_empty(), "a read must not touch the activity log");

            run(vec!["usage-scan".into(), "--apply".into(), "--dir".into(), dir], "bsc ui").expect("apply");
            let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&act).unwrap();
            assert!(
                text.contains("\tui-touch\tcomponent\tchild") && text.contains("\tbase-studio-code"),
                "the rescued (now-used) record touches, carrying its kit: {text:?}",
            );
            assert!(
                text.contains("\tui-touch\tcomponent\tparent"),
                "every applied record touches, not just the one that changed orphan status: {text:?}",
            );

            std::env::remove_var("BSC_UI_ACTIVITY_LOG");
            std::env::remove_var("BSC_AUDIT_PANE");
            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&act);
        });
    }
